sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. A^avorN , He made an incision in the foot of the camel [ in order to know and trace the footprints ]; as also ↓ A^v~rhu . (M.) And A^avara AlbaEiyri He made a mark upon the bottom of the camel's foot with the iron instrument called miy^ovarap in order that the footprints upon the ground might be known: (T, TT:) or he scraped the inner [i. e. under ] part of the camel's foot with that instrument in order that the footprints might be traced. (S.) -A2- A^avara AlHadiyva , (T, S, M, A, &c.,) Eani Alqawomi , (M,) aor. (S, M, Msb, K) and , (M, K,) inf. n. sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taA^oviyrN , He, or it, made, (Msb,) or left, (M, K,) or caused to remain, (S,) an impression, or a mark, or trace, upon him, or it. (S, * M, Msb, K. *) It is said of a sword, [meaning It made, or left, a mark, or scar, upon him, or it, ] and in like manner of a blow. (T, TA.) [Whence,] A^av~ara fiY EiroDihi cross; [ He scarred his honour ]. (K in art. wx$ .) You say also, A^av~ara biwajohihi wabijabiynihi Als~ujuwdu [ Prostration in prayer made, or left, a mark, or marks, upon his face and upon his forehead ]. (T, * TA.) See also 1, first sentence. -A2- He, or it, made an impression, or produced an effect, upon him, or it; impressed, affected, or influenced, him, or it. (The Lexicons passim.) -A3- A^av~ara ka*aA bika*aA , (T, TT,) or ↓ A=vara , (K,) He, or it, made such a thing to be followed by such a thing. (T, TT, K. *)

sourceDefinition: , (AZ, T, S, A, L, K, &c.,) said by Yaakoob to be the only form known to As, (S,) and ↓ A^avarN , which is a form used by poetic licence, (M, L,) and ↓ A^vorapN , (M, L, K,) and ↓ A^uvurN , (M,) and ↓ A^uvurN , which is in like manner a sing., not a pl., (T, L,) and ↓ A^vorapN , (El-Leblee,) and ↓ A^aviyro , (K,) The diversified wavy marks, streaks, or grain, of a sword; syn. firinodN ; (As, T, S, M, A, L, K;) and tasalosulN ; and diybaAjapu ; (AZ, T;) and its lustre, or glitter: (M, L:) pl. [of the first] A^uvuro : (T, M, L, K:) the pl. of A^uvorapN is A^uvarN . (El-Leblee.) Khufáf Ibn-Nudbeh Es-Sulamee says, [describing swords,] jalaAhaA AlS~ayoqaluwna faA_axolaSuwhaA xifaAfAF kul~uhaA yatoqiY biA^avori [ The furbishers polished them, and freed them from impurities, making them light: each of them preserving itself from the evil eye by means of its lustre ]: i. e., each of them opposes to thee its firinod : (S, L:) yatoqiY is a contraction of yat~aqiY ; and the meaning is, when a person looks at them, their bright rays meet his eye, so that he cannot continue to look at them. (L.)

definition: A remain, or relic, of a thing;
sourceDefinition: A remain, or relic, of a thing; (M, Msb, K;) as of a house; as also ↓ A^avaArapN : (Msb:) a trace remaining of a thing; and of the stroke, or blow, of a sword: (S:) see also A^uvorN : a sign, mark, or trace; opposed to the Eayon , or thing itself: (TA:) a footstep, vestige, or track; a footprint; the impression, or mark, made by the foot of a man [ &c. ] upon the ground; as also ↓ A_ivorN : and an impress, or impression, of anything: (El-Wá'ee:) pl. A=vaArNH (M, Msb, K) and A_uvuwrN . (M, K.) [The sing. is also frequently used in a pl. sense: and the former of these pls. is often used to signify Remains, or monuments, or memorials, of anti- quity, or of any past time. ] It is said in a prov., laA A^aTolubu A^avarFA baEoda EayonK I will not seek a trace, or vestige, [or, as we rather say in English, a shadow, ] after suffering a reality, or substance, to escape me: or, as some relate it, laA taTolubo seek not thou. (Har pp. 120 and 174.) And one says, qaTaEa All~`hu A^avarahu [ May God cut short his footsteps ]: meaning may God render him crippled: for when one is crippled, his footsteps cease. (TA.) definition: The [ kind of trees termed ] HamoD ;
sourceDefinition: The [ kind of trees termed ] HamoD ; (AHn, K;) as also ↓ A_irokN : (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) and (K) certain trees of the kind termed HayoD , (T, S, Msb, K,) well known, bearing what resemble bunches of grapes, (T, TA,) and of which sticks for cleaning the teeth are made, (AHn, Aboo-Ziyád, Msb, K,) that is, of its branches, (AHn, Aboo-Ziyád, Msb,) and of its roots, which latter are more esteemed for this purpose: (Aboo-Ziyád:) it is the best of the trees of which the branches are used for this purpose, and the best of those upon which beasts feed with respect to the odour of the milk [ yielded by those beasts ]: (AHn:) or one of the large thorny trees, upon which camels feed: the milk of [ the camels that feed upon ] it is the best of milk: and it is not allowable to prohibit the public from feeding their beasts upon it: (Mgh:) or a kind of tall, smooth, or soft, tree, abounding with leaves and branches, the wood of which is weak, and which has a fruit in bunches, or racemes, called bariyr , one [ bunch ] of which will fill the hand: (Msb:) n. un. with p : (S, Msb:) pl. (of the n. un., T) A^urukN (T, K) and A^araAy^iku , (IB, K,) which is a form sometimes used, and is also pl. of the n. un. (IB.) ― -b2- A piece of land (K, TA) in which are trees of the kind thus called. (TA.)

definition: A raised couch ( sariyr ) in a Hajalap , (K, and Jel in xviii.
sourceDefinition: A raised couch ( sariyr ) in a Hajalap , (K, and Jel in xviii. 30,) which is a tent, or pavilion, or chamber, ( byt ,) adorned with cloths and curtains, [or a kind of curtained canopy or alcove or the like, ] for a bride; (Jel ubi suprà;) a raised couch ( sryr ) in a Hajalap , and having before it a curtain; when alone, not thus called: (TA:) or a bed, or thing spread upon the ground to sit or lie upon, in a Hajalap : (Zj, TA:) or a raised couch ( sryr ), absolutely, whether in a Hjlp or not: (TA:) or [in the CK “ and ”] anything upon which one reclines such as is termed sariyr or mnaS~ap or firaA$ : (K, TA:) or [in some copies of the K “ and ”] a raised couch ( sryr ) ornamentally furnished and decorated, in a [ tent, or pavilion, or the like, such as is termed ] qub~ap , or in a chamber, or an apartment, bayot , [or by this may be meant here a tent of any kind, though I think that in this instance it more probably denotes an inner apartment, or an alcove, ]) which, when there is not in it a sryr , is termed Hajalap : (S, Sgh, K:) accord. to Er-Rághib, so named because originally made of [the wood of] the A^araAk ; or because it is a place of abode; from A^arak biAlmakaAni “ be abode in the place: ” (TA:) pl A^araAy^iku (S, K) and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ A^ariykN . (K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. A^aTiyTN (S, K) and A^aT~N , (TA,) It produced, made, gave, emitted, or uttered, a sound, noise, voice, or cry; (S, K;) [and particularly, it creaked; and it moaned; ] said of a camel's saddle, (S, * K, [in the CK, Alr~ajulu is put by mistake for Alr~aHolu ]) [and particularly of a new camel's saddle,] and the like, (K,) such as a [plaited or woven girth called] nisoE and of everything of which the sound resembles that of a new camel's saddle, (TA,) and of a palm-trunk, and of a tree of the kind called sidor , (S TA,) or of the kind called saroH , (TA,) and of a cane or reed on the occasion of its being straightened, [in which instance it is said to be tropical, but if so it is tropical in several other instances,] and of a bow, (TA,) and of the belly by reason of emptiness, (S,* TA,) and, in a trad. of Aboo-Dharr, (tropical:) of heaven, or the sky, notwithstanding there being [really] no A^aTiyT in this instance, for it is meant to denote [the presence of] multitude, and confirmation of the majesty of God. (TA.) [It is also said of other things, as will be shown by phrases here following, and by explanations of A^aTiyTN below.] You also say, A^aT~ati AlA_ibilu , (K,) aor. as above, inf. n. A^aTiyTN , (TA,) The camels moaned by reason of fatigue, or uttering their yearning cry to their young, (K, TA,) and sometimes by reason of fulness of their udders with milk. (TA.) And laA A=tiyka maA A^aT~ati AlA_ibilu I will not come to thee as long as camels utter cries [or moan ] by reason of the heaviness of their loads. (S.) And laA A^afoEalu *`lika maA A^aT~ati AlA_ibilu , meaning I will not do that ever. (TA.) And maA lanaA baEiyrN yay^iT~u We have not a camel that moans, or cries; meaning we have not any camel; for the camel cannot but do so. (TA, from a trad.) [See also A^aTiyTN , below.] And A^aT~ato lahu raHimiY (tropical:) [ My feeling of relationship, or sympathy of blood, ] became affected with tenderness, or compassion, and became moved, [or rather pleaded, ] for him [or in his favour ]: (K, TA:) and hence ↓ Alt~aA^aT~uTu [inf. n. of the verb in the syn. phrase taA^aT~aTato lahu raHimiY ]. (Sgh, TA.) And A^aT~ato bika Alr~aHimu [ The feeling of relationship, or sympathy of blood, pleaded, or hath pleaded, in thee; ] i. e., inclined thee to favour. (Ham p. 765.) [See another ex. voce HaAs~apN .]

sourceDefinition: [as explained in what here follows seems to be properly an inf. n., though, like all inf. ns., it may be used as a subst.:] The sounding, or the like, or the sound, or the like, [and particularly the creaking, or creaking sound, and the moaning, or moaning sound, ] of a camel's saddle (S, K, TA) when new; (TA;) and so ↓ A^aT~N of the litters and saddles of camels when the riders are heavy thereon; and the former, also, of a door; said, in a trad., of the gate of paradise, by reason of its being crowded; (TA;) and of a plaited or woven thong when stretching; (Ez-Zejjájee, TA;) and of the back [when strained]; (K;) and of the bowels, (TA,) and of the belly, or inside, by reason of hunger, (K,) or by reason of vehement hunger; (TA;) and of camels, (S, K,) by reason of their burdens, (K,) or by reason of the heaviness of their burdens; (S;) and the prolonging of the cries of camels: (TA:) but 'Alee Ibn- Hamzeh says that the cry of camels is termed rugaA='N , and that A^aTiyTN signifies the sounding, or sound, of their bellies, or insides, by reason of repletion from drinking. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Hunger, (K, TA,) itself, as well as the sound of the bowels or belly by reason thereof: from EzZejjájee. (TA.)

definition: is a particle of determination: (Mughnee &c.
sourceDefinition: is a particle of determination: (Mughnee &c.:) or, accord. to some, it is a conjunct noun, and this is the correct opinion; but some say it is a conjunct particle; and some, a particle of determination: (I 'AK p. 40:) [it is equivalent to our article The ;] as in Alr~ajulu [ The man ]: (S and K in art. lwm , and I 'Ak p. 48:) accord. to Kh, [what is termed] the determinative is Aalo [altogether, and therefore it is called by some “the determinative alif and lám“]; but accord. to Sb, it is the l alone; [wherefore it is called by some, as in the S &c., “the lám of determination;”;] so that accord. to Kh, the hemzeh is a hemzeh of disjunction; but accord. to Sb, it is a hemzeh of conjunction: (I 'Ak ubi suprà:) [J says,] the l being quiescent, the conjunctive A is prefixed to it in order that it may commence therewith; but when it is conjoined with what precedes it, the A is dropped, as in lilr~ajuli . (S in art. lwm .) Sometimes the Arabs suppress hemzeh after it; and sometimes they also suppress the A of the article itself: thus, for AlA^aHomaru , they say AlaHomaru , and laHomaru . (Zj, cited in TA in art. Ayk .) In the dial. of some of the people of El-Yemen, (TA in art. Am , q. v.,) or in the dial. of Himyer, (TA in art. Tyb ,) Amo is used in the sense of Al . (Mughnee.)

definition: Anything which has a quality requiring it to be regarded as sacred, or inviolable;
sourceDefinition: Anything which has a quality requiring it to be regarded as sacred, or inviolable; which has some right pertaining to it: and thus used in particular senses here following. (R, TA.) ― -b2- Relationship; or nearness with respect to kindred; (Fr, T, S, M, R, K;) as also ↓ A_il~apN , (Fr, T, K,) of which the pl. is A_ilalN . (K.) So in the Kur [ix. 8], laA yaroqubuwA fiykumo A_il~aA (Fr, T) They will not regard, with respect to you, relationship; (Bd, Jel;) accord. to some. (Bd.) And so in a trad. of 'Alee, yaxuwnu AlEahoda wa yaqoTaEu AlA_il~a [ He is unfaithful to the covenant, and cuts the tie of relationship ]. (TA.) Hassán Ibn-Thábit says, laEamoruka A_in~a A_il~aka mino qurayo$K kaA_il~i Als~aqobi mino raA^oli Aln~aEaAmi [ By thy life, thy relationship to Kureysh is like the relationship of the young camel to the young of the ostrich ]. (S.) ― -b3- Good origin. (K.) So, accord. to some, in a saying of Aboo-Bekr, which see below. (TA.) ― -b4- I. q. maEodinN , (K,) or maEodinN SaHiyHN [as meaning A place, or person, whence a thing, or person, originates, free from imperfection, or from everything that would induce doubt or suspicion or evil opinion ]. (El-Muärrij, TA: [in which the verse of Hassán cited above is given as an ex. of this signification.]) ― -b5- A compact, or covenant; or one by which a person becomes responsible for the safety, or safe-keeping, of a person or thing; syn. EahodN : (AO, Aboo-Is- hák, T, S, M, R, K:) a confederacy, or league; syn. HilofN ; (Aboo-Is-hák, T, M, K;) and so, accord. to some, in the Kur ubi suprà: (Bd:) a covenant between two parties by which either is bound to protect the other; syn. juwaArN : (Aboo-Is-hák, T, R:) a promise, or an assurance, of security or safety; or indemnity; syn. A^amaAnN ; (K;) a meaning which it has, accord. to some, in the verse of the Kur cited above. (TA.) Hence, wafiY~u AlA_ili A fulfiller, performer, or keeper, of the compact, or covenant. sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor , (T, M, Msb,) inf. n. A^am~N , (T, S, M, Msb,) He tended, repaired, betook himself, or directed his course, to, or towards, him, or it; aimed at, sought, endeavoured after, pursued, or endeavoured to reach or attain or obtain, him, or it; intended it, or purposed it; syn. qaSadahu , (Lth, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and tawax~aAhu , (T,) and taEam~adahu , (Mgh,) and tawaj~aha A_ilayohi ; (TA;) as also ↓ A^am~amahu , and ↓ tA^m~mhu , (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ Ay^tm~hu , (M, K,) and ↓ yam~am~hu , (T, M, K,) and ↓ tayam~amahu ; (T, M, Mgh, K;) the last two being formed by substitution [of Y for A^ ]. (M.) Hence, yaAAall~`hu A^um~anaA bixayorK [ O God, bring us good ]. (JK in art. Alh , and Bd in iii. 25.) And laA^am~a maA huwa , occurring in a trad., meaning He has indeed betaken himself to, or pursued, the right way: or it is used in a pass. sense, as meaning he is in the way which ought to be pursued. (TA.) And rasuwla All~`hi ↓ AnoTalaqotu A^ataA^am~amu , in another trad., I went away, betaking myself to the Apostle of God. (TA.) (K.) ― -b2- See also 8. -A2- A^am~ahu , (S, M, Mgh, &c.,) aor. , (M, Mgh,) inf. n. definition: is a conjunction, (S, M, K,) connected with what precedes it (Msb, Mughnee) so that neither what precedes it nor what follows it is independent, the one of the other.
sourceDefinition: is a conjunction, (S, M, K,) connected with what precedes it (Msb, Mughnee) so that neither what precedes it nor what follows it is independent, the one of the other. (Mughnee.) It denotes interrogation; (M, K;) or is used in a case of interrogation, (S, Msb,) corresponding to the interrogative A^a , and meaning A^aY~ , (S,) or, as Z says, A^aY~u AlA^amorayoni kaAy^inN ; [for an explanation of which, see what follows;] (Mughnee;) or, [in other words,] corresponding to the interrogative A^a , whereby, and by A^amo , one seeks, or desires, particularization: (Mughnee:) it is as though it were an interrogative after an interrogative. (Lth, T.) Thus you say, A^azayudN fiY Ald~aAri A^amo EamorNw [ Is Zeyd in the house, or 'Amr? ]; (S, Mughnee;) i. e. which of them two ( A^ay~uhumaA ) is in the house? (S;) therefore what follows Am and what precedes it compose one sentence; and it is not used in commanding nor in forbidding; and what follows it must correspond to what precedes it in the quality of noun and of verb; so that you say, A^azayodN qaAy^imN A^amE qaAEidN [ Is Zeyd standing, or sitting? ] and A^aqaAma zayodN A^amo qaEada [ Did Zeyd stand, or sit? ]. (Msb.) It is not to be coupled with A^a after it: you may not say, A^aEinodaka zayodN A^amo A^aEinodaka EamorNw . (S.) ― -b2- As connected in like manner with what goes before, it is preceded by A^a denoting equality [by occurring after sawaA='N &c.], and corresponds thereto, as in [the Kur lxiii. 6,] sawaA='u Ealayohimo A^asotagofarota lahumN lamN tasotagufiro lahumN [It will be equal to them whether thou beg forgiveness for them or do not beg forgiveness for them ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- It is also unconnected with what precedes it, (S, Msb, Mughnee,) implying always digression, (Mughnee,) preceded by an enunciative, or an interrogative, (S, Msb, Mughnee,) other than A^a , (Mughnee,) or by A^a not meant [really] as an interrogative but to denote disapproval, (Mughnee,) and signifies balo , (Lth, Zj, T, S, M, Mughnee, K,) or balo and A^a together, (Msb,) and this is its meaning always accord. to all the Basrees, but the Koofees deny this. (Mughnee.) Thus, using it after an enunciative, you say, A_in~ahaA laA_ibilN A^amo $aA='N [ Verily they are camels: nay, or nay but, they are sheep, or goats: or nay, are they sheep, or goats? ]: (S Msb, Mughnee:) this being said when one looks at a bodily form, and imagines it to be a number of camels, and says what first occurs to him; then the opinion that it is a number of sheep or goats suggests itself to him, and he turns from the first idea, and says, A^amo $aA='N , meaning balo , because it is a digression from what precedes it; though what follows bl is [properly] a thing known certainly, and what follows Am is opined. (S, TA.) And using it after an interrogative in this case, you say, halo zyodN munoTaliqN A^amo EamorNw [ Is Zeyd going away? Nay rather, or, or rather, is 'Amr? ]: you digress from the question respecting Zeyd's going away, and make the question to relate to 'Amr; so that Am implies indecisive opinion, and interrogation, and digression. (S.) And thus using it, you say, halo zayodN qaAma A^amo EamorNw [ Did Zeyd stand? Nay rather, or or rather, did 'Amr? ]. (Msb.) And an ex. of the same is the saying [in the Kur xiii. 17], halo yasotawiY AloA^aEomaY waAlobaSiyru A^amo halo tasotawiY AlZ~ulumaAtu waAln~uwru [ Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or rather are darkness and light equal? ]. (Mughnee.) And an ex. of it preceded by A^a used to denote disapproval is the saying [in the Kur vii. 194], A^alahumo A^arojulN yamo$uwna bihaA A^amo lahumo A^ayodK yaboTi$uwna bihaA [ Have they feet, to walk therewith? Or have they hands to assault therewith? ]: for A^a is here equivalent to a negation. (Mughnee.) [It has been shown above that] A^amo is sometimes introduced immediately before halo : (S, K:) but IB says that this is when hl occurs in a phrase next before it; [as in the ex. from the Kur xiii. 17, cited above;] and in this case, the interrogative meaning of Am is annulled; it being introduced only to denote a digression. (TA.) ― -b4- It is also used as a simple interrogative; accord. to the assertion of AO; in the sense of halo ; (Mughnee;) or in the sense of the interrogative A^a ; (Lth, T, K) as in the saying, A^amo Einodaka gadaA='i HaADirN , meaning Hast thou a morning-meal ready? a good form of speech used by the Arabs; (Lth, T;) and allowable when preceded by another phrase. (T.) ― -b5- And sometimes it is redundant; (AZ, T, S, Mughnee, K) in the dial. of the people of El-Yemen; (T;) as in the saying, yaA dahona A^amo maA kaAna ma$oyiY rqaSaA balo qado takuwnu mi$oyatiY tawaq~uSaA (T, S, * [in the latter, yA hinodu , and only the former hemistich is given,]) meaning O Dahnà, (the curtailed form dahona being used for dahonaA=' ,) my walking was not, as now in my age, [a feeble movement like] dancing: but in my youth, my manner of walking used to be a bounding: (T:) this is accord. to the opinion of AZ: but accord. to another opinion, Am is here [virtually] conjoined with a preceding clause which is suppressed; as though the speaker had said, yaA dahona A^akaAna ma$oyiY raqaS~aA A^amo maA kaAna ka*lika . (A 'Hát, TA.) -A2- It is also used (T, Mughnee) in the dial. of the people of El-Yemen, (T,) or of Teiyi and Himyer, (Mughnee,) in the sense of Al , (T,) to render a noun determinate. (Mughnee.) So in the trad., layosa mina Amobir~ AmoSiyAmu fiY Amosafari , (T, Mughnee,) i. e. Alayosa mina Albir~i AlS~iyaAmu fiY Als~afari [ Fasting in journeying is not an act of obedience to God]. (T, and M in art. br .) So too in the trad., AaloA=na TaAba AmoDarobu Now fighting has become lawful; as related accord. to the dial. of Himyer, for AlD~arobu . (TA in art. Tyb .) It has been said that this form Am is only used in those cases in which the l of the article does not become incorporated into the first letter of the noun to which it is prefixed; as in the phrase, xu*i Alr~umoHa waArokabi Amofarasa [ Take thou the spear, and mount the mare, or horse ], related as heard in El-Yemen; but this usage may be peculiar to some of the people of that country; not common to all of them; as appears from what we have cited above. (Mughnee.) -A3- A^ama for A^amaA , before an oath: see art. AmA . -A4- And A^ama All~`hi and A^amu All~`hi &c.: see A^ayomunu All~`hi , in art. ymn .

definition: A mother (T, S, M, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: A mother (T, S, M, Msb, K, &c.) [of a human being and] of any animal; (IAar, T;) as also ↓ A_im~N , (Sb, M, Msb, K) and ↓ A_um~apN , (T, M, Msb, K,) and ↓ A^um~ahapN , (S, M, Msb, K,) which last is the original form (S, Msb) accord. to some, (Msb,) or the h in this is augmentative (M, Msb) accord. to others: (Msb:) the pl. is A^um~ahaAtN (Lth, T, S, M, Msb, K) and A^um~aAtN ; (S, M, Msb, K;) or the former is applied to human beings, and the latter to beasts; (T, S;) or the former to rational beings, and the latter to irrational; (M, K;) or the former is much applied to human beings, and the latter to others, for the sake of distinction; (Msb;) but the reverse is sometimes the case: (IB:) IDrst and others hold the latter to be of weak authority: (TA:) the dim. of A^um~N is ↓ A^umayomapN (T, S, K) accord. to some of the Arabs; but correctly, [accord. to those who hold the original form of A^um~N to be A^um~ahapN ,] it is ↓ A^umayomihapN . (Lth, T, TA. [In a copy of the T, I find this latter form of the dim. written Amyhp .]) ― -b2- A^um~a laka denotes dispraise; (S;) being used by the Arabs as meaning Thou hast no free, or ingenuous, mother; because the sons of female slaves are objects of dispraise with the Arabs; and is only said in anger and reviling: (A Heyth, T:) or, as some say, it means thou art one who has been picked up as a foundling, having no Known mother: (TA:) [or] it is also sometimes used in praise; (A 'Obeyd, T, S, K;) and is used as an imprecation without the desire of its being fulfilled upon the person addressed, being said in vehemence of love; [lit. meaning mayest thou have no mother! ], like vakilatoka A^um~uka , and laA A^abaA laka , [and qaAtalaka All~`hu ,] &c. (Har p. 165.) ― -b3- Some elide the A of A^um~ ; as in the saying of 'Adee Ibn—Zeyd. A^ay~uhaA AlEaAy^ibu Einodim~a zayodK [ O thou who art blaming in my presence the mother of Zeyd ]; meaning, EinodiY A^um~a zayodK ; the Y of EndY being also elided on account of the occurrence of two quiescent letters [after the elision of the A of A^um~ ]: (Lth, T, S:) and as in the phrase wayolum~ihi , (S,) which means wayolN liA^um~ihi . (S, and K in art. wyl , q. v.) ― -b4- humaA A^um~aAk~ means They two are thy two parents: or thy mother and thy maternal aunt. (K.) [But] fad~aAhu biA^um~ayohi is said to mean [ He expressed a wish that he (another) might be ransomed with ] his mother and his grandmother. (TA.) ― -b5- One says also, laA tafoEaliY ↓ yaA A^um~ati [ O my mother, do not thou such a thing], and [in like manner] yaA A^abati AfoEalo ; making the sign of the fem. gender a substitute for the [pronominal] affix Y ; and in a case of pause, you say yaA A^um~aho . (S.) ― -b6- And one says, maA A^um~iY waA^um~uhu , and maA $akoliY wa$akoluhu , meaning [ What relationship have I to him, or it? or what concern have I with him, or it? or] what is my case and [what is] his or its, case? because of his, or its, remoteness from me: whence, (T,) wamaA A^um~iY waA^um~u AlwaHo$i lam~aA tafar~aEa fiY mafaAriqiYa Aloma$iybu [ And what concern have I with the wild animals when hoariness hath spread in the places where my hair parts? ]; (T, S;) i. e. maA A^anaAwaTalabu AlwaHo$i baEoda maA kabirotu [i. e. maA A^moriy waTalabu AlwaHo$i : in one copy of the S, waTalaba , i. e. with wa as a prep. denoting concomitance, and therefore governing the accus. case: both readings virtually meaning what concern have I with the pursuing of the wild animals after I have grown old? ]: he means, the girls: and the mention of A^um~ in the verse is superfluous. (S.) ― -b7- A^um~N also relates to inanimate things that have growth; as in A^um~u Al$~ajarapi [ The mother of the tree ]; and A^um~u Aln~axolapi [ the mother of the palm-tree ]; and A^um~u Almawozipa [ the mother of the banana-tree; of which see an ex. in art. mwz ]; and the like. (M, TA.) ― -b8- And it signifies also The source, origin, foundation, or basis, (S, M, Msb, K,) of a thing, (S, Msb, [in the former of which, this is the first of the meanings assigned to the word,]) or of anything; (M, K) its stay, support, or efficient cause of subsistence. (M, K.) ― -b9- Anything to which other things are collected together, or adjoined: (IDrd, M, K:) anything to which the other things that are next thereto are collected together, or adjoined: (Lth, T:) the main, or chief, part of a thing; the main body thereof: and that which is a compriser, or comprehender, of [other] things: (Ham p. 44:) the place of collection, comprisal, or comprehension, of a thing; the place of combination thereof. (En-Nadr, T.) ― -b10- And hence, (IDrd, M,) The head, or chief, of a people, or company of men; (IDrd, S, M, K;) because others collect themselves together to him: (IDrd, TA:) so in the phrase A^um~u EiyaAlK [lit. the mother of a household ], in a poem of Esh-Shenfarà: (IDrd, M:) or in this instance, it has the signification next following, accord. to Esh-Sháfi'ee. (T.) ― -b11- A man who has the charge of the food and service of a people, or company of men; accord. to EshSháfi'ee: (T:) or their servant. (K.) ― -b12- A man's aged wife. (IAar, T, K.) ― -b13- A place of habitation or abode. (K.) So in the Kur [ci. 6], faA^um~uhu haAwiyapN His place of habitation or abode [shall be] the fire [of Hell]: (Bd, Jel, TA:) or, as some say, the meaning is A^um~u raA^osihi haAwiyapN fiyhaA [ his brain shall fall into it, namely, the fire of Hell]. (TA.) ― -b14- The ensign, or standard, which an army follows. (S.) [See A^um~u Alr~umoHi , below.] ― -b15- It is said in a trad., respecting the prophets, A^um~ahaA tuhumo $at~aY , meaning that, though their religion is one, their laws, or ordinances, or statutes, are various, or different: or the meaning is, their times are various, or different. (TA in art. $t .) ― -b16- See also A^um~apN , in two places. ― -b17- A^um~ is also prefixed to nouns significant of many things. (M.) [Most of the compounds thus formed will be found explained in the arts. to which belong the nouns that occupy the second place. The following are among the more common, and are therefore here mentioned, with the meanings assigned to them in lexicons in the present art., and arranged in distinct classes.] ― -b18- A^um~u Alr~ajuli The man's wife; and the person who manages the affairs of his house or tent. (TA.) And A^um~u mavowaY Alr~ajuli The man's wife, to whom he betakes himself for lodging, or abode: (T:) the mistress of the man's place of abode. (S, M.) ― -b19- A^um~u EaAmirK The hyena, or female hyena; as also A^um~u EamorKw ; (TA;) and A^um~u AlT~ariyqi . (S, TA. [See also other significations of the first and last below.]) A^um~u HilosK [or A^um~u AlHilosi (as in the S and K in art. Hlas )] The she-ass. (TA.) A^um~u AlbayoDi The female ostrich. (S, K.) ― -b20- A^um~u Alr~aA^usi The brain: (T, M, K:) or the thin skin that is upon it: (IDrd, M, K:) or the bag in which is the brain: (T:) or the skin that comprises the brain; [ the meninx, or dura mater and pia mater; ] (S, Mgh;) which is called A^um~u Ald~imaAgi (S, Msb) likewise. (S.) ― -b21- A^um~u Aln~ujuwmi The Milky way; (S, M, K) because it is the place where the stars are collected together [in great multitude]: (M:) or, as some say, the sun; which is the greatest of the stars. (Ham pp. 43 and 44.) Because of the multitude of the stars in the Milky way, one says, maA A^a$obaha majolisaka biA^um~i Aln~ujuwmi (assumed tropical:) [ How like is thine assembly to the Milky way! ]. definition: A way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like;
sourceDefinition: A way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like; (AZ, S;) as also ↓ A_im~apN : (AZ, S, K:) Fr assigns this meaning to the latter, and that next following to the former: (T:) a way, course, or rule, of life, or conduct; (Fr, T, M, K;) as also ↓ A_im~apN . (M, K.) ― -b2- Religion; as also ↓ A_im~apN : (AZ, S, M, K: [one of the words by which this meaning is expressed in the M and K is $iroEap ; for which Golius found in the K srEp :]) one course, which people follow, in religion. (T.) You say, fulaAnN laA A^um~apa lahu Such a one has no religion; no religious persuasion. (S.) And a poet says, wahalo yasotawiY *uw A^um~apK wakafuwru [ And are one who has religion and one who is an infidel equal? ]. (S.) ― -b3- Obedience [app. to God ]. (T, M, K.) -A2- The people of a [ particular ] religion: (Akh, S:) a people to whom an apostle is sent, (M, K,) unbelievers and believers; such being called his A^um~ap : (M:) any people called after a prophet are said to be his A^um~ap : (Lth, T:) the followers of the prophet: pl. A^umamN . (T, Msb.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 209], kaAna Aln~aAsu A^um~apK wAHidapF , meaning Mankind was [ a people ] of one religion. (Zj, T, TA.) ― -b2- A nation; a people; a race; a tribe, distinct body, or family; (Lth, T, M, K;) of mankind; (Lth, T;) or of any living beings; as also ↓ A^um~N : (M, K:) a collective body [of men or other living beings]; (T, S;) a sing. word with a pl. meaning: (Akh, S:) a kind, genus, or generical class, (T, S, M, K,) by itself, (T,) of any animals, or living beings, (T, S, M, TA,) others than the sons of Adam, (T,) as of dogs, (T, S, M,) and of other beasts, and of birds; (T, M, * TA;) as also ↓ A^um~N ; (M, K;) pl. of the former A^umamN ; (S, M;) which occurs in a trad. as relating to dogs; (S;) and in the Kur vi. 38, as relating to beasts and birds. (T, M, * TA.) ― -b3- A man's people, community, tribe, kinsfolk, or party; (M, K, TA;) his company. (TA.) ― -b4- A generation of men; or people of one time: pl. A^umamN : as in the saying, qado maDato A^umamN Generations of men have passed away. (T.) ― -b5- The creatures of God. (M, K.) You say, maA raA^ayotu mino A^um~api All~`hi A^aHosana minohu [ I have not seen, of the creatures of God, one more beautiful than he ]. (M.) -A3- I. q. A_imaAmN ; (T, M, K;) accord. to A 'Obeyd, applied in this sense to Abraham, in the Kur xvi. 121. (T.) ― -b2- A righteous man who is an object of imitation. (T.) ― -b3- One who follows the true religion, holding, or doing, what is different from, or contrary to, all other religions: (M, K:) [said to be] thus applied to Abraham, ubi suprà. (M.) ― -b4- One who is known for goodness: (Fr, T:) and so explained by Ibn-Mes'ood as applied to Abraham: (TA:) or, so applied, it has the signification next following: (TA:) a man combining all kinds of good qualities: (T, M, K:) or, as some say, repaired to: or imitated. (Bd:) ― -b5- A learned man: (T, M, K:) one who has no equal: (T:) the learned man of his age, or time, who is singular in his learning: (Msb:) and one who is alone in respect of religion. (T.) -A4- See also A_um~N , first sentence. Hence, yaAA^um~ati which see in the same paragraph. -A5- The stature of a man; tallness, and beauty of stature; or justness of stature; syn. qaAmapN ; (T, S, M, Msb, K;) and $aTaATF : (M, TA: [in the K, the signification of na$aATN is assigned to it; but this is evidently a mistake for $aTaATK ; for the next three significations before the former of these words in the K are the same as the next three before the latter of them in the M; and the next five after the former word in the K are the same as the next five after the latter in the M, with only this difference, that one of these five is the first of them in the M and the third of them in the K:]) pl. A^umamN . (T, S, M. *) You say, A_in~ahu laHasanu AlA^um~api , i. e. Al$~aTaATi [ Verily he is beautiful in justness of stature ]. (M.) And El-Aashà says, HisaAnu Alwujuwhi TiwaAlu AlA^umamo [ Beautiful in respect of the faces, ] tall in respect of the statures. (T, S, M. * [In the last, byDu Alwujuwhi .]) ― -b2- The face. (T, M, K.) ― -b3- A^um~apu AlA=wajohi The form of the face: (AZ, T:) or the principal part thereof; (M, K;) the part thereof in which beauty is usually known to lie. (M) You say, A_in~ahu laHasanu A^um~api AlA=wajohi Verily he is beautiful in the form of the face: and A_in~ahu lA=aqabiyHu A^um~api AlA=wajohi verily he is ugly in the form of the face. (AZ, T.) ― -b4- A^um~apu AlT~ariyqi : see A^um~N . -A6- A time; a period of time; a while. (T, S, M, K.) So in the Kur [xii. 45], waAd~akara baEoda A^um~apK [ And he remembered, or became reminded, after a time ]: (S, M:) or, after a long period of time: but some read ↓ A_im~apK , i. e., after favour had been shown him, in his escape: and some read A^amapK , i. e., forgetting. (Bd.) And so in the same [xi. 11], walay^ino A^x~aronaA Eanohumu AlEa*aAba A_ilA=aY A^um~apK maEoduwdap [ And verily, if we kept back from them the punishment ] until a short period of time. (S * Bd.)

You say, maA raA^ayotu mino A^um~api All~`hi A^aHosana minohu [ I have not seen, of the creatures of God, one more beautiful than he ]. (M.) -A3- I. q. A_imaAmN ; (T, M, K;) accord. to A 'Obeyd, applied in this sense to Abraham, in the Kur xvi. 121. (T.) ― -b2- A righteous man who is an object of imitation. (T.) ― -b3- One who follows the true religion, holding, or doing, what is different from, or contrary to, all other religions: (M, K:) [said to be] thus applied to Abraham, ubi suprà. (M.) ― -b4- One who is known for goodness: (Fr, T:) and so explained by Ibn-Mes'ood as applied to Abraham: (TA:) or, so applied, it has the signification next following: (TA:) a man combining all kinds of good qualities: (T, M, K:) or, as some say, repaired to: or imitated. (Bd:) ― -b5- A learned man: (T, M, K:) one who has no equal: (T:) the learned man of his age, or time, who is singular in his learning: (Msb:) and one who is alone in respect of religion. (T.) -A4- See also A_um~N , first sentence. (M) You say, A_in~ahu laHasanu A^um~api AlA=wajohi Verily he is beautiful in the form of the face: and A_in~ahu lA=aqabiyHu A^um~api AlA=wajohi verily he is ugly in the form of the face. definition: The location that is before;
sourceDefinition: The location that is before; (M, Msb, * K;) contr. of AlwaraA='u . (M, K.) It is used [absolutely] as a noun, and adverbially, (M, Msb, * K,) necessarily prefixed to another noun: (Mgh:) and is fem., (Ks, M,) and sometimes mase.: (M, K:) or it is mase., and sometimes fem. as meaning the jihap : or, as Zj says, they differ as to making it masc. and making it fem. (Msb.) You say, kunotu A^amaAmahu I was before him, in respect of place. (S.) In the saying of Mohammad, to Usámeh, AlSlaApu A^amaAmaka , the meaning is The time of prayer [ is before thee ], or the place thereof; and by the prayer is meant the prayer of sunset. (Mgh.) You also say, A^amaAmaka [i. c. Look before thee; meaning beware thou; or take thou note; ] when you caution another, (M, K,) or notify him, of a thing. (M.)

definition: A person, (S, Mgh,) or learned man, (Msb,) whose example is followed, or who is imitated;
sourceDefinition: A person, (S, Mgh,) or learned man, (Msb,) whose example is followed, or who is imitated; (S, Mgh, Msb;) any exemplar, or object of imitation, (T, M, K,) to a people, or company of men, (T,) such as a head, chief, or leader, or some other person, (M, K,) whether they be following the right way or be erring therefrom: (T:) applied alike to a male and to a female: (Mgh, Msb:) applied to a female, it occurs in a phrase in which it is written by some with p : (Mgh:) but this is said to be a mistake: (Msb:) it is correctly without p , because it is a subst., not an epithet: (Mgh, Msb:) or it is allowable with p , because it implies the meaning of an epithet: (Msb:) and ↓ A^um~apN signifies the same: (T, M, K:) the pl. of the former is A^ayim~apo , (T, S, M, K, [but omitted in the CK,]) originally A^aA^omimapN , (T, S,) of the measure A^afEilapN , like A^amovilapN , pl. of mivaAlN , (T,) but as two meems come together, the former is incorporated into the latter, and its vowel is transferred to the hemzeh before it, which hemzeh, being thus pronounced with kesr, is changed into Y ; (T, S; *) or it is thus changed because difficult to pronounce; (M;) or, as Akh says, because it is with kesr and is preceded by another hemzeh with fet-h: (S:) but some pronounce it A^ay^im~apN , (Akh, T, S, M, K,) namely, those who hold that two hemzehs may occur together; (Akh, S;) the Koofees reading it thus in the Kur ix. 12; (M;) but this is anomalous: (M, K:) it is mentioned as on the authority of Aboo-Is-hák, and [Az says,] I do not say that it is not allowable, but the former is the preferable: (T:) or the pl. is A^ay^im~apN , originally A^aA^omimapN like A^amovilapN : one of the two meems being incorporated into the other after the transfer of its vowel to the hemzeh [next before it]; some of the readers of the Kur pronouncing the [said] hemzeh with its true sound; some softening it, agreeably with analogy, in the manner termed bayona bayona ; and some of the grammarians changing it into Y ; but some of them reckon this incorrect, saying that there is no analogical reason for it: (Msb:) and accord. to some, (M,) its pl. is also A_imaAmu , (M, K,) like the sing., (K,) occurring in the Kur xxv. 74; (M;) not of the same category as EadolN (M, K) and riD~aY , (M,) because they sometimes said A_imaAmaAni , but a broken pl.: (M, K: *) or, accord. to A 'Obeyd, it is in this instance a sing. denoting a pl.: (M, S: *) or it is pl. of A=m~N , [which is originally A=mimo ,] like as SiHaAbN is pl. of SaAHibN : (M:) the dim. of A^ayim~apN is ↓ A^uwayom~apo ; or, as El-Mázinee says, ↓ A^uyayom~apN . (S.) ― -b2- AlA_maAmu also signifies The Prophet: (K:) he is called A_imaAmu [ the exemplar, object of imitation, leader, or head, of his nation, or people ]; (T;) or A_imaAmu AlA^m~api [ the exemplar, &c., of the nation, or people ]; (M;) it being incumbent on all to imitate his rule of life or conduct. (T.) ― -b3- The Khaleefeh: (Msb, K:) he is called A_maAmu Alr~aEiy~api [ the exemplar, &c., of the people, or subjects ]. (M.) The title of AlA_maAmu is still applied to the Kings of El-Yemen: Aboo-Bekr says, you say, fulaAnN A_imaAmu Alqawomi , meaning such a one is the first in authority over the people, or company of men: and A_imaAmu Almasolimiyna means the head, chief, or leader, of the Muslims. (TA.) ― -b4- The person whose example is followed, or who is imitated, [i. e. the leader, ] in prayer. (Msb.) ― -b5- [ The leading authority , or head, of a persuasion, or sect. The four A^yim~ap or A^ay^im~ap are the heads of the four principal persuasions, or sects, of the Sunnees; namely, the Hanafees, Sháfi'ees, Málikees, and Hambelees. And the Hanafees call the two chief doctors of their persuasion, after Aboo- Haneefeh, namely, Aboo-Yoosuf and Mohammad, AlA_imaAmaAni The two Imáms. ] ― -b6- The leader of an army. (M, K.) ― -b7- The guide: (K:) he is called A_imaAmu AlA_ibili [ the leader of the travellers ]. (M.) ― -b8- The conductor, or driver, of camels (M, K) is called A_imaAmu AlA_ibili , though he be behind them, because he guides them. (M.) ― -b9- The manager, or conductor, and right disposer, orderer, or rectifier, of anything. (M, K. *) ― -b10- The Kur-án (M, K) is called A_imaAmu Almusolimyna [ the guide of the Muslims ]; (M;) because it is an exemplar. (TA.) [ The model-copy, or standard-copy, of the Kur-án, namely the copy of the Khaleefeh 'Othmán, is particularly called AlA_imaAmu .] ― -b11- [ The scripture of any people: and, without the article, a book, or written record. ] It is said in the Kur [xvii. 73], yawoma nadoEuw kul~a A^unaAsK biA_maAmihimo The day when we shall call every one of mankind with their scripture: or, as some say, with their prophet and their law: or, as some say, with their book in which their deeds are recorded. (T.) It is also said in the Kur [xxxvi. 11], kul~a $ayo'K A^aHoSayonaAhu fiY A_imaAmK mubiynK , meaning, says El-Hasan, [ And everything have we recorded ] in a perspicuous book, or writing; (S, Jel;) i. e., on the Preserved Tablet. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b12- The lesson of a boy, that is learned each day (T, M, K) in the school: (T:) also called Als~abaqu . (TA.) ― -b13- The model, or pattern, of a semblance, or shape. (M, K.) ― -b14- The builder's wooden instrument [or rule ] whereby he makes the building even. (S, K. *) ― -b15- The cord which the builder extends to make even, thereby, the row of stones or bricks of the building; also called Alt~ur~u and AlmiToharu ; (T;) the string which is extended upon, or against, a building, and according to which one builds. (M, K. *) ― -b16- A_imaAmN signifies also A road, or way: (S, [but omitted in some copies,] M, K:) or a manifest road, or way. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [xv. 79], wa A_in~ahumaA labiA_maAmK mubiynK (S, M) And they were both, indeed, in a way pursued and manifest: (M:) or in a way which they travelled in their journeys. (Fr.) ― -b17- The direction ( taloqaA=' ) of the Kibleh. (M, K. *) ― -b18- A tract, quarter, or region, of land, or of the earth. (S.) ― -b19- A string [of a bow or lute &c.]; syn. watarN . (Sgh, K.)

(M;) not of the same category as EadolN (M, K) and riD~aY , (M,) because they sometimes said A_imaAmaAni , but a broken pl.: (M, K: *) or, accord. to A 'Obeyd, it is in this instance a sing. denoting a pl.: (M, S: *) or it is pl. of A=m~N , [which is originally A=mimo ,] like as SiHaAbN is pl. of SaAHibN : (M:) the dim. of A^ayim~apN is ↓ A^uwayom~apo ; or, as El-Mázinee says, ↓ A^uyayom~apN . (S.) ― -b2- AlA_maAmu also signifies The Prophet: (K:) he is called A_imaAmu [ the exemplar, object of imitation, leader, or head, of his nation, or people ]; (T;) or A_imaAmu AlA^m~api [ the exemplar, &c., of the nation, or people ]; (M;) it being incumbent on all to imitate his rule of life or conduct. (T.) ― -b3- The Khaleefeh: (Msb, K:) he is called A_maAmu Alr~aEiy~api [ the exemplar, &c., of the people, or subjects ]. (M.) The title of AlA_maAmu is still applied to the Kings of El-Yemen: Aboo-Bekr says, you say, fulaAnN A_imaAmu Alqawomi , meaning such a one is the first in authority over the people, or company of men: and A_imaAmu Almasolimiyna means the head, chief, or leader, of the Muslims. (TA.) ― -b4- The person whose example is followed, or who is imitated, [i. e. the leader, ] in prayer. (Msb.) ― -b5- [ The leading authority , or head, of a persuasion, or sect. The four A^yim~ap or A^ay^im~ap are the heads of the four principal persuasions, or sects, of the Sunnees; namely, the Hanafees, Sháfi'ees, Málikees, and Hambelees. And the Hanafees call the two chief doctors of their persuasion, after Aboo- Haneefeh, namely, Aboo-Yoosuf and Mohammad, AlA_imaAmaAni The two Imáms. ] ― -b6- The leader of an army. (M, K.) ― -b7- The guide: (K:) he is called A_imaAmu AlA_ibili [ the leader of the travellers ]. (M.) ― -b8- The conductor, or driver, of camels (M, K) is called A_imaAmu AlA_ibili , though he be behind them, because he guides them. (M.) ― -b9- The manager, or conductor, and right disposer, orderer, or rectifier, of anything. (M, K. *) ― -b10- The Kur-án (M, K) is called A_imaAmu Almusolimyna [ the guide of the Muslims ]; (M;) because it is an exemplar. (TA.) [ The model-copy, or standard-copy, of the Kur-án, namely the copy of the Khaleefeh 'Othmán, is particularly called AlA_imaAmu .] ― -b11- [ The scripture of any people: and, without the article, a book, or written record. ] It is said in the Kur [xvii. 73], yawoma nadoEuw kul~a A^unaAsK biA_maAmihimo The day when we shall call every one of mankind with their scripture: or, as some say, with their prophet and their law: or, as some say, with their book in which their deeds are recorded. (T.) It is also said in the Kur [xxxvi. 11], kul~a $ayo'K A^aHoSayonaAhu fiY A_imaAmK mubiynK , meaning, says El-Hasan, [ And everything have we recorded ] in a perspicuous book, or writing; (S, Jel;) i. e., on the Preserved Tablet. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b12- The lesson of a boy, that is learned each day (T, M, K) in the school: (T:) also called Als~abaqu . (TA.) ― -b13- The model, or pattern, of a semblance, or shape. (M, K.) ― -b14- The builder's wooden instrument [or rule ] whereby he makes the building even. (S, K. *) ― -b15- The cord which the builder extends to make even, thereby, the row of stones or bricks of the building; also called Alt~ur~u and AlmiToharu ; (T;) the string which is extended upon, or against, a building, and according to which one builds. (M, K. *) ― -b16- A_imaAmN signifies also A road, or way: (S, [but omitted in some copies,] M, K:) or a manifest road, or way. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [xv. 79], wa A_in~ahumaA labiA_maAmK mubiynK (S, M) And they were both, indeed, in a way pursued and manifest: (M:) or in a way which they travelled in their journeys. (Fr.) ― -b17- The direction ( taloqaA=' ) of the Kibleh. (M, K. *) ― -b18- A tract, quarter, or region, of land, or of the earth. (S.) ― -b19- A string [of a bow or lute &c.]; syn. watarN . (Sgh, K.)

definition: (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ A^um~aAnN (K) [the former a rel.
sourceDefinition: (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ A^um~aAnN (K) [the former a rel. n. from A^um~apN , and thus properly meaning Gentile: whence, in a secondary, or tropical, sense,(assumed tropical:) a heathen; ] (assumed tropical:) one not having a revealed scripture; (Bd in iii. 19 and 69;) so applied by those having a revealed scripture: (Bd in iii.69:) [and particularly] an Arab: (Jel in iii. 69, and Bd and Jel in lxii. 2:) [or] in the proper language [of the Arabs], of, or belonging to , or relating to, the nation ( A^um~ap ) of the Arabs, who did not write nor read: and therefore metaphorically applied to (tropical:) any one not knowing the art of writing nor that of reading: (Mgh:) or (assumed tropical:) one who does not write; (T, M, K;) because the art of writing is acquired; as though he were thus called in relation to the condition in which his mother ( A^um~ahu ) brought him forth: (T:) or (assumed tropical:) one who is in the natural condition of the nation ( AlA^um~ap ) to which he belongs, (Zj, * T, M, * K, *) in respect of not writing, (T,) or not having learned writing; thus remaining in his natural state: (M, K:) or (assumed tropical:) one who does not write well; said to be a rel. n. from A^m~N ; because the art of writing is acquired, and such a person is as his mother brought him forth, in respect of ignorance of that art; or, as some say, from A^um~apu AlEarabi ; because most of the Arabs were of this description: (Msb:) the art of writing was known among the Arabs [in the time of Mohammad] by the people of Et-Táïf, who learned it from a man of the people of El-Heereh, and these had it from the people of El-Ambár. (T.) A^um~iy~uwn laA yaEolamuwna , AlkitaAba , in the Kur ii. 73, means Vulgar persons, [or heathen, ] who know not the Book of the Law revealed to Moses: (Jel:) or ignorant persons, who know not writing, so that they may read that book; or, who know not the Book of the Law revealed to Moses. (Bd.) Mohammad was termed A^um~iY~ [meaning A Gentile, as distinguished from an Israelite: or, accord. to most of his followers, meaning illiterate; ] because the nation ( A^um~ap ) of the Arabs did not write, nor read writing; and [they say that] God sent him as an apostle when he did not write, nor read from a book; and this natural condition of his was one of his miraculous signs, to which reference is made in the Kur [xxix. 47], where it is said, “thou didst not read, before it, from a book, nor didst thou write it with thy right hand:” (T, TA:) but accord. to the more correct opinion, he was not well acquainted with written characters nor with poetry, but he discriminated between good and bad poetry: or, as some assert, he became acquainted with writing after he had been unacquainted therewith, on account of the expression “ before it ” in the verse of the Kur mentioned above: or, as some say, this may mean that he wrote though ignorant of the art of writing, like as some of the kings, being A^um~iy~uwn , write their signs, or marks: (TA:) or, accord. to Jaafar Es-Sádik, he used to read from the book, or scripture, if he did not write. (Kull p. 73.) [Some judicious observations on this word are comprised in Dr. Sprenger's Life of Mohammad (pp. 101-2); a work which, in the portion already published (Part I.), contains much very valuable information.] ― -b2- Also, (K,) or [only] A^um~iY~N , (AZ, T, M,) applied to a man, (AZ, T,) Impotent in speech, ( EayiY~ , in the K incorrectly written gabiY~ , TA,) of few words, and rude, churlish, uncivil, or surly. (AZ, T, M, K.)

definition: (Msb, K) and bab~agaA='u (K, Kzw) [in modern vulgar Arabic babagaAn , The parrot;
sourceDefinition: (Msb, K) and bab~agaA='u (K, Kzw) [in modern vulgar Arabic babagaAn , The parrot; ] a certain well-known bird; (Msb;) a certain green bird, (Sgh, K, TA,) well known; (TA;) the bird called in Persian TuwTiy , beautiful in colour and form, mostly green, but in some instances red, and yellow, and white; having a thick bill and tongue: it hears the speech of men and repeats it, without knowing its meaning; and utters letters rightly: when they desire to teach it, they put a mirror in its cage, so that it sees therein its own form, and they speak to it from behind the mirror, and when it hears, it repeats, desiring to do as its like; and thus it learns quickly: one of the wonders relating to it is [said to be this], that it never drinks water; for if it drank, it would die: (Kzw:) the affix renders fem. the word, but not the thing named thereby, like the p in HamaAmapN and naEaAmapN ; for the word applies to the male and the female, so that one says, babogaA='u *akarN [ a male parrot ] and babogaA='u A^unovaY [ a female parrot ]: and the pl. is babogaAwaAtN [or bab~agaAwaAtN ], like as SaHoraAwatN is pl. of SaHoraA='u . (Msb.)

definition: ― -b2- mubat~alapN , applied to a woman, Beautiful, elegant, or pretty;
sourceDefinition: : see batyilN . ― -b2- mubat~alapN , applied to a woman, Beautiful, elegant, or pretty; (K;) as though her beauty were divided into portions (↓ but~ila , i. e. quT~iEa ,) [ and distributed in due proportions ] upon her limbs: (M, * K:) or perfect in make, (S,) whose flesh is not accumulated, one portion upon another, (S, M, K,) but distinctly disposed; this latter being said by some to be the meaning: (M:) or, accord. to Lh, (M, TA,) having a lankness, or looseness, in her limbs; (M, K, TA;) not having them compressed, one upon another; (M:) or as though the flesh were cut off from them: (TA:) and in like manner, mubat~alN applied to a camel: (M, K:) not applied as an epithet to a man: (S, M, K:) or mubat~alapu Alxaloqi signifies distinct in make from the generality of women; excelling them [ therein ]: (Aboo-Sa'eed, T, TA:) or perfect in make: or having every part beautiful in itself; not dependent [ for its beauty ] upon another part: (T:) or beautiful in make; not with one part falling short of another [ in beauty ]; not being beautiful in the eye and ugly in the nose, nor beautiful in the nose and ugly in the eye; but perfect. (IAar, TA.)

definition: The body, without the head and arms and legs;
sourceDefinition: The body, without the head and arms and legs; (M, Msb, K;) so says Az: (Msb:) or the body without the arms and legs: (Mgh:) or [the part ] from the shoulder-joint to the posteriors [ inclusive ]: (TA [as from the Mgh, in my copy of which it is not found]:) or the jasada [generally meaning the body together with the members ] of a man; (S;) often applied. to the whole of the jasad ; (Az, TA;) and in the Kur x. 92 it is said to mean the body without soul: (S:) pl. A^abodaAnN ; (M, Msb;) whence the phrase, mentioned by Lh, A_in~ahaA laHasanapu AlA^abodaAni [meaning Verily she is beautiful in respect of the body ], as though the term badanN were applied to every portion of her. (M.) $irokapu AlA^abodaAni is originally $irokapN biAlA^abodaAni , meaning Copartnership in bodily labours for the acquirement of gains. (Msb.) ― -b2- And hence, (tropical:) The part of a shirt, (Mgh, Msb,) and of a [garment of the kind called] jub~ap , (Mgh,) that lies against the back and the belly, [i. e. the body thereof,] without the sleeves and the daxaAriyS [or gores with which it is widened ]: (Mgh, Msb:) pl. as above. (Msb.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) A short diroE [or coat of mail ], (S, M, K,) of the measure of the body: (M:) or it is [ a coat of mail ] like a diroE , except that it is short, only such as covers the body, with short sleeves: (T:) or, as some say, any diroE : (M:) and so it is said to mean in the Kur x. 92 by IAar (T) and by Th; (M;) but Akh says that this assertion is of no account: (S:) pl. as above. (M, K.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A small [ garment of the kind called ] jub~ap ; as being likened to a coat of mail. (TA.) ― -b5- Accord. to Kr, (M,) A limb, or member: or, specially, the limbs, or members, of a slaughtered camel: (M, K: [in the latter of which, the former of these two explanations is improperly connected with the first in this paragraph by the conjunction Aw :]) to these he specially applies it in one instance: pl. as above. (M.) ― -b6- Also An old, or aged, man: (K:) or so rajulN badanN . (T, S, M.) [In like manner, ↓ baAdinN and ↓ badinN are said by Golius, as on the authority of the S, to signify annosus et senior, applied to a man, and also to a woman; but this explanation is wrong; and the latter word I do not find in any lexicon.] ― -b7- And An old mountain-goat: (M, K:) or so waEilN badanN : (S:) [in the present day, badan is applied to the wild goat of the Arabian and Egyptian deserts and mountains; the capra jaela of Hamilton Smith; called by some an ibex; as is also tayotal , properly vayotalN :] pl. [of pauc.] A^abodunu (M, K [in the CK, erroneously, A^abodanN ]) and [of mult.] buduwnN , which is extr. [with respect to rule], on the authority of IAar. (M, TA.) The rájiz says, describing a bitch (S, M) and a mountain-goat, (M, TA,) qado qulotu lam~aA badati AlEuqaAbu waDam~ahaA waAlbadana AlHiqaAbN jid~iY likul~i EaAmilK vawaAbu Aalr~aA^osu waAlA^akoruEu waAlA_ihaAbu (S, * M, * TA,) [ I had said, when El-' Ikáb appeared, and El-Hikáb comprised her and the old mountain-goat, “Exert thyself: for every worker there is a recompense: the head and the shanks and the hide shall be thine”]: AlEqAb is the name of a bitch, and AlHqAb is a certain mountain: he says, “Catch thou this goat, and I will make thy recompense to be the head and the shanks and the hide.” (TA.) [Hence Golius has been led to mistake AlHiqaAb for a signification of Albadanu .] ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) The lineage, or parentage, of a man, and his grounds of pretension to respect or honour. (M, K.)

definition: A she-camel, (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and a male camel, (T, M, Mgh, K,) and a cow, (T, S, M, Mgh, * Msb, K,) and a bull, (M, K,) accord.
sourceDefinition: A she-camel, (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and a male camel, (T, M, Mgh, K,) and a cow, (T, S, M, Mgh, * Msb, K,) and a bull, (M, K,) accord. to some, (Msb,) or properly the first of these, (Mgh, Msb,) and the second, (Mgh,) but made by the Sunneh to apply to a cow also, (Mgh, * Msb,) that is slaughtered at Mekkeh, (S,) or that is, (M, K,) or may be, (T,) brought thither for sacrifice; (T, M, K;) so called because they used to fatten them, (S,) or because of their greatness, or bulkiness: (T, Mgh, Msb:) not applied to a sheep or goat: (T, Msb, TA:) En-Nawawee erroneously cites the T as asserting that it is thus applied; misled, it is said, by an omission in his copy: (MF, TA:) pl. badanaAtN , (T, Mgh, Msb,) a pl. of pauc., (Mgh,) and budonN , (T, S, M, Msb,) or budunN , (Mgh, K,) or both, (M, Msb, TA,) the former being a contraction of the latter, which seems to be pl. of badiynN : (Msb:) one should not use badanN as a pl. of badanapN ; though they used to say xa$abN and A^ajamN &c. (M, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (inf. n. taboriyzN , S, K,) He made it apparent, manifest, plain, or evident; he showed, or manifested, it; (S, A, K;) namely, a writing, or book, (A,) or other thing; (S, A;) as also ↓ Abrzhu : (A, Msb:) or AlkitaAba ↓ Abrz signifies he put forth, or produced, the writing, or book; syn. A^axorajahu : (TA:) and [as it often signifies in the present day,] published, it; syn. na$arahu . (K, TA.) [See also 4 below.] It is said in the Kur [xxvi. 91 and lxxix. 36], wa bur~izati AljaHiymu , meaning And Hell shall be uncovered. (A.) ― -b2- br~z raAkibahu He (a horse) saved his rider. (K.) -A2- See also 1. ― -b2- [Hence,] br~z Alfarasu , (S, Msb,) or br~z EalaY Alxayoli , (K,) inf. n. taboriyzN , (Msb,) The horse outstripped (S, Msb, K) the [ other ] horses (Msb, K) in the race-ground: (Msb:) it is said of a horse that outstrips in a race: and, accord. to some, the like is said of whatever outstrips: (TA:) and br~z EalaY AlgaAyapi [ He (a horse) passed beyond the goal ]. (A.) ― -b3- Hence, br~z fiY AlEilomi , inf. n. as above, He surpassed, or excelled, his fellows in knowledge. (Msb.) And [simply] br~z He surpassed his companions (S, K) in excellence, or in courage. (K.) And br~z EalaY A^aqoraAnihi [ He surpassed, or excelled, his fellows, or his opponents ]. (A.) -A3- See also 4, last signification.

definition: A man characterized by pleasing or goodly aspect, and by intelligence: fem.
sourceDefinition: A man characterized by pleasing or goodly aspect, and by intelligence: fem. with p : (S, TA:) or a man of open condition or state: (TA:) or pure in disposition; (TA;) abstaining from what is unlawful and indecorous; (S, A, Msb:) of great dignity or estimation: (Msb:) fem. with p : (A, Msb:) pl. fem. barozaAtN : (A:) or, as also ↓ baroziY~N a man who abstains from what is unlawful and indecorous, and in whose intelligence, (K,) or, as in some copies of the K, in whose excellence, bifaDolihi , but this is app. a mistranscription, or, as some say, in whose abstinence from what is unlawful and indecorous, (TA,) and his judgment, confidence is placed: (K:) and barozapN a woman whose good qualities or actions, or whose beauties, are apparent: (K:) or open in her converse; syn. mutaAjirapN : or, as in some correct lexicons, disdainful of mean things; syn. mutajaAl~apN : or of middle age, ( kaholapN ,) who is not veiled or concealed like young women: (TA:) or of great dignity or estimation: (AO, TA:) or who goes or comes forth to people, and with whom they sit, and of whom they talk, and who abstains from what is unlawful and indecorous, and is intelligent: (TA:) or who abstains from what is unlawful and indecorous, and goes or comes forth to men, and talks with them, and is advanced in age beyond those women who are kept concealed: (Mgh, Msb:) or open in her converse, ( mutajaAhirapN ,) of middle age, ( kaholapN ,) of great dignity or estimation, who goes or comes forth to people, and with whom they sit and talk, and who abstains from what is unlawful and indecorous: (K:) or in whose judgment, and her abstaining from what is unlawful and indecorous, confidence is placed: (TA:) or who does not veil her face from a man and bend her head down towards the ground. (IAar, on the authority of Ibn-EzZubeyr.)

definition: A field, plain, or wide expanse of land, (S, Msb, K,) without trees;
sourceDefinition: A field, plain, or wide expanse of land, (S, Msb, K,) without trees; (Msb;) as also ↓ biraAzN ; but this latter form is rare: (Msb:) or an open tract of land destitute of herbage and trees and without hills or mountains: (Mgh, Msb:) or a place in which is no covert of trees or other things: (Fr, S:) an open place in which is no covert of trees or other things: (Fr, S:) an open place in which is no covert. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xaraja A_ilaY AlbaraAzi (tropical:) He went forth to satisfy a want of nature. (A.) And A_i*aA A^araAda AlbaraAza A^aboEada (tropical:) [ When he desired to satisfy a want of nature, he went far off ]: a trad.; respecting which El-Khattábee says that the relaters of traditions err respecting the word, pronouncing it with kesr, for ↓ biraAzN is an inf. n.: but (SM says that) authorities differ as to this point. (TA.) ― -b3- [It is further said,] baraAzN , (Mgh, Msb,) or ↓ biraAzN (S, K,) is metonymically applied to (tropical:) Excrement; human ordure; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) the feces of food. (S.)

[Hence,] xaraja A_ilaY AlbaraAzi (tropical:) He went forth to satisfy a want of nature. (A.) And A_i*aA A^araAda AlbaraAza A^aboEada (tropical:) [ When he desired to satisfy a want of nature, he went far off ]: a trad.; respecting which El-Khattábee says that the relaters of traditions err respecting the word, pronouncing it with kesr, for ↓ biraAzN is an inf. n.: but (SM says that) authorities differ as to this point. (TA.)
[It is further said,] baraAzN , (Mgh, Msb,) or ↓ biraAzN (S, K,) is metonymically applied to (tropical:) Excrement; human ordure; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) the feces of food. (S.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. ba$amN , He (a man, S, TA, or an animal, Msb) suffered, or became affected with, indigestion, (S, Msb, K,) in consequence of much eating: (Msb:) or he was heavy in consequence of...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. ba$amN , He (a man, S, TA, or an animal, Msb) suffered, or became affected with, indigestion, (S, Msb, K,) in consequence of much eating: (Msb:) or he was heavy in consequence of food: (Ham p. 363:) or he became distressed, or oppressed, by eating much food. (TA.) You say, ba$imotu mina AlT~aEaAmi I suffered indigestion from the food: (S:) or was heavy in consequence of the food. (Ham ubi suprà) And ba$ima AlfaSiylu mino kavorapi $urobi All~abani The young camel suffered indigestion from drinking much milk. (S.) Accord. to IDrd, ba$amN specially relates to beasts: accord. to Kh, it specially arises from greasy food. (Har p. 164.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) He became affected with disgust, aversion, loathing, or nausea. (S, K, TA.) You say, ba$imotu mina AlT~aEaAmi , (S,) or Eani AlTEAm , (TA,) (tropical:) I turned away with disgust from the food; was averse from it; loathed it; nauseated it. (S, TA.) And ba$ima AlfaSiylu Eani All~abani (assumed tropical:) [ The young camel turned away with disgust from the milk; was averse from it; &c.]. (K in art. dqE .)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. baDiyDN (S, K) and buDuwDN and baD~N , (K,) The water flowed by little and little: (S, K:) or exuded upon a rock or the ground. (TA.) And baD~ati Alr~akiy~apu , and baD~ato bimaAy^ihaA , The well had, or yielded, little water; or its water became little. (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting Tabook, waAlEayonu tabiD~u bi$aYo'K mina AlmaA='i [ The source, or spring, yielding scantily somewhat of water ]. (TA.) And you say, baD~ati AlEayonu , aor. as above, inf. n. baD~N and baDiyDN , The eye shed tears. (TA.) And, of a man when you characterise him as patient under affliction, maA tabiD~u Eayonuhu [ His eye does not shed tears ]. (TA.) And baD~ati AlHalamapu The nipple streamed with milk. (TA.) It is said in a trad., maA tabiD~u bibalaAlK Having no milk dropping from it, or her. (TA.) And in another trad., saqaTa mina Alfarasi faA_i*aA huwa jaAlisN waEuroDu wajohihi yabiD~u maA='F A^aSofara [ He fell from the horse, and lo, he was sitting, with the side of his face exuding yellow water ]. (TA.) One should not say, baD~a Als~iqaA='u , nor Alqirobapu : but some say so, urging the authority of Ru-beh. (S.) And you say of a stone, and the like, baD~a , aor. as above, meaning Water flowed from it like sweat; water oozed from it. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence the saying, maA yabiD~u Hajaruhu (assumed tropical:) No good is obtained from him; (TA;) i. q. maA tanodaY SafaAtuhu : (S:) a prov. applied to the niggardly. (S, K.) definition: He clave to the [ balaAT , i.
sourceDefinition: He clave to the [ balaAT , i. e.] earth, or ground; (K;) said of a man: (TA:) he became bankrupt, or insolvent, or reduced to a state of difficulty or poverty, or without any property, and clave to the balaAT : (AHeyth:) he became poor, and his property went away; as also A^uboliTa : (S, K:) so says Ks; and AZ says the like: (S:) or he became poor; or had little property. (TA.) -A2- A^abolaTa All~iS~u Alqawoma The robber left the people, or company of men, upon the surface of the ground, and left them not anything: (Lh, TA:) or simply, left them not anything. (K.) ― -b2- AblT AlmaTaru AlA^aroDa The rain fell upon the balaAT [or surface ] of the earth, (K, TA,) so that no dust was seen upon it. (TA.) ― -b3- See also 1.

definition: [The acorn; ] a certain thing well known; (S;) the fruit, or produce, of a kind of tree, [namely, the oak, ] which is eaten, (Mgh, Msb,) sometimes, (Msb,) and with the bark of which one tans, (Mgh,...
sourceDefinition: [The acorn; ] a certain thing well known; (S;) the fruit, or produce, of a kind of tree, [namely, the oak, ] which is eaten, (Mgh, Msb,) sometimes, (Msb,) and with the bark of which one tans, (Mgh, Msb,) sometimes: (Msb:) or [the oak; or this kind of tree is properly called $ajaru Albal~uwTi ;] a kind of tree; the fruit, or produce, whereof they used as food, in ancient times; cold and dry (K, TA) in the second degree, or, as some say, in the first; or its dryness is in the third degree; or it is hot in the first degree; (TA;) heavy, coarse, (K, TA,) slow of digestion, bad for the stomach, occasioning headache, injurious to the bladder, but rendered good by its being roasted and having sugar added to it; (TA;) suppressing the urine, (K, TA,) and rendering it difficult; preventing exhaustion by loss of blood, and the emission of blood [ from a wound ]; good for hardnesses, with the fat of a kid; preventing the progress of [ the disease in the mouth called ] qulaAE , and frwE [app. a mistake for quruwH , or wounds ], when it is burnt; preventing also excoriation, and poisons, and looseness of the bowels; and very nutritious when easily digested. (TA.) [See also EafoSN . ― -b2- Forskål, in his Flora Aegypt., p. lvi., mentions this name as applied to The common ash-tree; fraxinus excelsior. ] ― -b3- bal~uwTu Almaliki , according to some, The walnut: accord. to others, the $aAhobal~uwT [a Persian word, and also used by Arabs in the present day, applied to the chestnut ]: as is said in the Minháj. (TA.) ― -b4- bal~uwT AlA^aroDi [applied in the present day to The herb germander, or chamædrys; ] a certain plant, the leaves of which resemble the hinodi baA=' [or endive ]: it is diuretic; aperient; and wasting to the spleen. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , (M, Mgh, Msb, K,) [aor. yabiynu ,] inf. n. bayonuwnapN and buyuwnN (M, Mgh, K) and bayonN , (M, K,) It ( a thing ) became separated, severed, disunited, or cut off, (M, Mgh, Msb, K,) Eani Al$~aYo'i from the thing. (Mgh.) And baAnato , (M, K,) or baAnato biAlT~alaAqi , (Msb,) She (a wife) became separated by divorce, (M, Msb, K,) Eani Alr~ajuli from the man. (M, K.) And baAnatN said of a girl, [ She became separated from her parents by marriage; ] she married: (ISh, T:) as though she became at a distance from the house of her father. (ISh, TA.) And baAna , (M,) or baAna bimaAlK , aor. yabiynu , (T,) inf. n. buyuwnN (T, M) and bayonN , (M,) He became separated from his father, or mother, or both, by property [ which he received from him, or her, or them, ] (AZ, T, M,) to be his alone: (AZ, T:) and ElFárisee states, on the authority of AZ, that one] says also, baAna Eanohu and baAnahu [the former app. meaning he became separated thus from him, i. e., from his father; and the latter being syn. with A^abaAnahu , q. v.]. (M.) And baAna AlxaliyTu , inf. n. bayonN and bayonuwnapN , [ The partner, or copartner, or sharer, &c., became separated from the person, or persons, with whom he had been associated. ] (T.) And baAnato yadu Aln~aAqapi Eano janobihaA , inf. n. buyuwnN , [ The fore leg of the she-camel became withdrawn, or apart, from her side. ] (T.) And baAna , (S, M, Msb,) and baAnuwA , (K,) aor. yabiynu , (S,) inf. n. bayonN and bayonuwnapN , (S, M, Msb, K,) He separated himself, or it separated itself; (S; [in one copy of which it is said of a thing;]) and they separated themselves: (K:) or it (a tribe, M, Msb) went, journeyed, went away, or departed; and went, removed, retired, or withdrew itself, to a distance, or far away, or far off. (Msb.) ― -b2- baAna , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. yabiynu , (T, Msb,) inf. n. bayaAnN ; (T, S, Mgh, K;) and ↓ AbAn , (T, S, M, &c.,) inf. n. A_ibaAnapN ; (T, Msb;) and ↓ by~n , (T, S, M, &c.,) inf. n. taboyiynN ; (S;) and ↓ tby~n ; and ↓ AstbAn ; (T, S, M, &c.,) all signify the same; (T, M, Msb;) i. e. It (a thing, T, S, M, Mgh, or an affair, or a case, Msb) was, or became, [ distinct, as though separate from others; and thus,] apparent, manifest, evident, clear, plain, or perspicuous: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) and it was, or became, known. (K.) You say, baAna AlHaq~u [ The truth became apparent, &c.; or known ]; as also ↓ AbAn . (T.) And AlS~uboHu li*iY Eayonayoni ↓ qado bay~ana The dawn has become apparent to him who has two eyes: a prov.: (S, M:) applied to a thing that becomes altogether apparent, or manifest. (Har p. 542.) And it is said in the Kur [ii. 257], Alr~u$odu mina AlgaY~i ↓ qado tabay~ana [ The right belief hath become distinguished from error ]. (TA.) And the lawyers, correctly, use the phrase, kaSawotK laA minohu HuruwfN ↓ yasotabiynu [ Like a sound whereof letters are not distinguishable ]. (Mgh.) ― -b3- [It seems to be indicated in the TA that baAna , aor. yabiynu , inf. n. bayonN and bayonuwnapN , also signifies It was, or became, united, or connected; thus having two contr. meanings; but I have not found the verb used in this sense, though bayonN signifies both disunion and union.] -A2- baAnahu , aor. yabiynu , inf. n. bayonN : see baAnahu , aor. yabuwnu , inf. n. bawonN , in art. bwn . -A3- See also 2, in two places.

sourceDefinition: , intrans., inf. n. taboyiynN : see 1, in two places. ― -b2- You say also, by~n Al$~ajaru The trees, (K,) or the leaves of the trees, (TA,) appeared, when beginning to grow forth. (K, TA.) And by~n Alqaronu (tropical:) The horn came forth. (K, TA.) -A2- by~n binotahu : see 4. ― -b2- by~nhu , (T, Msb, K,) inf. n. taboyiynN (T, S) and ↓ tiboyaAnN (T, S, * K *) and taboyaAnN ; (K;) the second of which three is an anomalous inf. n., (T, S, K,) for by rule it should be of the measure tafoEaAlN ; (T, S;) but taboyaAnN is not known except accord. to the opinion of those who allow the authority of analogy, which opinion is outweighed by the contrary; (TA;) and tiboyaAnN is the only inf. n. of its measure except tiloqaA='N , (T, S,) accord. to the generality of the leading authorities; but some add timovaAlN , as inf. n. of mav~ala ; and El-Hareeree adds to these two, in the Durrah, tinoDaAlN , as inf. n. of naADalahu ; and Esh-Shiháb adds, in the Expos. of the Durrah, ti$oraAbN , as inf. n. of $ariba Alxamora ; asserting ta$oraAbN also to have been heard, agreeably with analogy; [and to these may be added tabokaA='N and timo$aA='N , and perhaps some other instances of the same kind;] but some disallow tifoEaAlN altogether as the measure of an inf. n., saying that the words transmitted as instances thereof are simple substs. used as inf. ns., like TaEaAmN in the place of A_iToEaAmN ; (MF, TA;) and Sb says that tiboyaAnN is not an inf. n.; for, where it so, it would be taboyaAnN ; but it is, from bay~anotu , like gaArapN from A^agarotu ; (M, TA;) [ He made it distinct, as though separate from others; and thus,] he made it (namely, a thing, T, S, Mgh, or an affair, or a case, Msb) apparent, manifest, evident, clear, plain, or perspicuous; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ AbAnhu , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_ibaAnapN ; (Msb;) and ↓ tby~nhu ; (S, * Msb, K;) and ↓ AstbAnhu : (Mgh, Msb, K:) [ by~nhu is the most common in this sense: and often signifies he explained it: and he proved it: ] and ↓ all these verbs signify also he made it known; he notified it: (K:) or ↓ Aisotabanotuhu signifies, (S,) or signifies also, (Mgh,) I knew it, or became acquainted with it, [or distinguished it, ] (S, Mgh,) clearly, or plainly; (Mgh;) and so ↓ tabay~anotuhu ; (S, * Mgh;) [and bay~anotuhu , as appears from an ex. in what follows, from a verse of En-Nábighah:] ↓ binotuhu and ↓ A^abanotuhu and ↓ Aisotabanotuhu and bay~anotuhu all signify the same as ↓ tabay~anotuhu [app. in all the senses of this verb]: (M:) or, of all these verbs, ↓ baAna is only intrans.: (Msb:) and ↓ Aisotabanotuhu signifies I looked at it, or into it, (namely, a thing,) considered it, examined it, or studied it, repeatedly, in order that it might become apparent, manifest, evident, clear, or plain, to me: (T, TA:) and ↓ tby~nhu he looked at it, or into it, (namely, an affair, or a case,) considered it, examined it, or studied it, repeatedly, or deliberately, in order to know its real state by the external signs thereof. (T.) A poet says, wamaA xifotu Hat~aY bay~ana Al$~irobu waAlA^a*aY ↓ bqaAniy^apK A^an~iY mina AlHaY~i A^aboyanu [ And I feared not until the drinking, or the time of drinking, and molestation, made manifest, or plainly showed, by a deep-red ( sun ), that I was separated from the tribe: see qaAniy^N ]. (M.) And it is said in the Kur [xvi. 91], waA^anozalonaA Ealayoka AlkitaAba tiboyaAnFA likul~i $aYo'K [ And we have sent down to thee the Scripture to make manifest everything ]; meaning, we make manifest to thee in the Scripture everything that thou and thy people require [to know] respecting matters of religion. (T.) See also bayaAnN , in the latter half of the paragraph. En-Nábighah says, A_il~aA AlA^awaAriY~a m~aA A^ubay~inuhaA [ Except the places of the confinement of the beasts: with difficulty did I distinguish them ]; meaning ↓ A^atabay~anuhaA . (S.) You say also, maA ↓ tabay~ana yaA^otiyhi , meaning He sought, or endeavoured, to see, or discover, what would happen to him, of good and evil. (M in art. bSr .) [See also 5, below.]

(K, TA.) -A2- by~n binotahu : see 4. ― -b2- by~nhu , (T, Msb, K,) inf. n. taboyiynN (T, S) and ↓ tiboyaAnN (T, S, * K *) and taboyaAnN ; (K;) the second of which three is an anomalous inf. n., (T, S, K,) for by rule it should be of the measure tafoEaAlN ; (T, S;) but taboyaAnN is not known except accord. to the opinion of those who allow the authority of analogy, which opinion is outweighed by the contrary; (TA;) and tiboyaAnN is the only inf. n. of its measure except tiloqaA='N , (T, S,) accord. to the generality of the leading authorities; but some add timovaAlN , as inf. n. of mav~ala ; and El-Hareeree adds to these two, in the Durrah, tinoDaAlN , as inf. n. of naADalahu ; and Esh-Shiháb adds, in the Expos. of the Durrah, ti$oraAbN , as inf. n. of $ariba Alxamora ; asserting ta$oraAbN also to have been heard, agreeably with analogy; [and to these may be added tabokaA='N and timo$aA='N , and perhaps some other instances of the same kind;] but some disallow tifoEaAlN altogether as the measure of an inf. n., saying that the words transmitted as instances thereof are simple substs. used as inf. ns., like TaEaAmN in the place of A_iToEaAmN ; (MF, TA;) and Sb says that tiboyaAnN is not an inf. n.; for, where it so, it would be taboyaAnN ; but it is, from bay~anotu , like gaArapN from A^agarotu ; (M, TA;) [ He made it distinct, as though separate from others; and thus,] he made it (namely, a thing, T, S, Mgh, or an affair, or a case, Msb) apparent, manifest, evident, clear, plain, or perspicuous; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ AbAnhu , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_ibaAnapN ; (Msb;) and ↓ tby~nhu ; (S, * Msb, K;) and ↓ AstbAnhu : (Mgh, Msb, K:) [ by~nhu is the most common in this sense: and often signifies he explained it: and he proved it: ] and ↓ all these verbs signify also he made it known; he notified it: (K:) or ↓ Aisotabanotuhu signifies, (S,) or signifies also, (Mgh,) I knew it, or became acquainted with it, [or distinguished it, ] (S, Mgh,) clearly, or plainly; (Mgh;) and so ↓ tabay~anotuhu ; (S, * Mgh;) [and bay~anotuhu , as appears from an ex. in what follows, from a verse of En-Nábighah:] ↓ binotuhu and ↓ A^abanotuhu and ↓ Aisotabanotuhu and bay~anotuhu all signify the same as ↓ tabay~anotuhu [app. in all the senses of this verb]: (M:) or, of all these verbs, ↓ baAna is only intrans.: (Msb:) and ↓ Aisotabanotuhu signifies I looked at it, or into it, (namely, a thing,) considered it, examined it, or studied it, repeatedly, in order that it might become apparent, manifest, evident, clear, or plain, to me: (T, TA:) and ↓ tby~nhu he looked at it, or into it, (namely, an affair, or a case,) considered it, examined it, or studied it, repeatedly, or deliberately, in order to know its real state by the external signs thereof. (T.) A poet says, wamaA xifotu Hat~aY bay~ana Al$~irobu waAlA^a*aY ↓ bqaAniy^apK A^an~iY mina AlHaY~i A^aboyanu [ And I feared not until the drinking, or the time of drinking, and molestation, made manifest, or plainly showed, by a deep-red ( sun ), that I was separated from the tribe: see qaAniy^N ]. (M.) And it is said in the Kur [xvi. 91], waA^anozalonaA Ealayoka AlkitaAba tiboyaAnFA likul~i $aYo'K [ And we have sent down to thee the Scripture to make manifest everything ]; meaning, we make manifest to thee in the Scripture everything that thou and thy people require [to know] respecting matters of religion. (T.) See also bayaAnN , in the latter half of the paragraph. En-Nábighah says, A_il~aA AlA^awaAriY~a m~aA A^ubay~inuhaA [ Except the places of the confinement of the beasts: with difficulty did I distinguish them ]; meaning ↓ A^atabay~anuhaA . (S.) You say also, maA ↓ tabay~ana yaA^otiyhi , meaning He sought, or endeavoured, to see, or discover, what would happen to him, of good and evil. (M in art. bSr .) [See also 5, below.]
