sourceDefinition: has two contr. significations; (T, S, Msb;) one of which is Separation, or disunion [of companions or friends or lovers]. (T, S, M, Msb, K.) Hence, *aAtu Albayoni as meaning Enmity, and vehement hatred: and the saying liA_iSolaAHi *aAti Albayoni , i. e. For the reforming, or amending, of the bad, or corrupt, state subsisting between the people, or company of men; meaning for the allaying of the discord, enmity, rancour, or vehement hatred: (Msb:) [but this has also the contr. meaning, as will be seen below: and it is explained as having a vague import; for it is said that] fiY A_iSolaAHi *aAti Albayoni means In the reforming, or amending, of the circumstances subsisting between the persons to whom it relates, by frequent attention thereto. (Mgh.) [Hence also,] guraAbu Albayoni [ The raven of separation or disunion; i. e., whose appearance, or croak, is ominous of separation: said by some to be] the grAb termed A^aboqaEu [i. e. in which is blackness and whiteness; or having whiteness in the breast ]; (S, K;) so described by the poet 'Antarah: (S:) or that which is red in the beak and legs; but the black is called AlHaAtimu , because it makes [or shows] separation to be absolutely unavoidable, (Abu-1-Ghowth, S, K,) according to the assertion of the Arabs, i. e., by its croak: (Msb in art. Htm :) [or it is any species of the corvus: ] Hamzeh says, in his Proverbs, that this name attaches to the grAb because, when the people of an abode go away to seek after herbage, it alights in the place of their tents, searching the sweepings: (Har p. 308:) but accord. to the Kádee of Granada, Aboo-'Abd-Allah Esh-Shereef, this appellation, so often occurring in poetry, properly signifies camels that transport people from one district, or country, to another; and he cites the following verses: galiTa Al~a*iyna raA^ayotuhumo bijahaAlapK yaloHawona kul~uhumu guraAbFA yanoEaqu maA Al*~anobu A_il~aA liloA^abaAEiri A_in~ahaA mim~aA yu$at~itu jamoEahumo wayuqar~iqu A_in~a AlguraAba biyumonihi tudonuw Aln~awaY watu$at~itu Al$~amola AljamiyEa AlA^ayonuqu [ Those have erred whom I have seen, with ignorance, all of them blaming a raven croaking: the fault is not imputable save to the camels; for they are of the things that scatter and disperse their congregation: verily the place that is the object of a journey is brought near by the raven's lucky omen; but the she-camels discompose the united state ]: and Ibn-'Abd-Rabbih says, zaEaqa AlguraAbu faqulotu A^ako*abu TaAy^irK A_in l~amo yuSad~iqohu rugaA='u baEiyri [ The raven cried; and I said, A most lying bird, if the grumbling cry of a camel on the occasion of his being laden do not verify it ]. (TA in art. grb .) ― -b2- Also Distance, (S, M, Msb, K,) by the space, or interval, between two things. (Msb.) You say, bayona Albaladayoni bayonN Between the two countries, or towns, &c., is a distance, of space, or interval: (Msb:) and bayonahumaA bayonN Between them two is a distance, with Y when corporeal distance is meant: (Idem in art. bwn :) or A_in~a bayonahumaA labayonN [ Verily between them two is a distance ], not otherwise, in the case of [literal] distance. (S.) And you say also, bayonahumaA bayonN baEiydN (T in art. bwn , S, M *) and bawonN baEiydN (T in art. bwn , S, M, * Msb * in art. bwn ) Between them two [meaning two men] is a [ wide ] distance; (M;) i. e. between their two degrees of rank or dignity, or between the estimations in which they are commonly held: (Msb in art. bwn :) in this case, the latter is the more chaste. (S.) You also say, [using byn to denote An interval of time, ] laqiytuhu buEayodaAti bayonK [ I met him after, or a little after, an interval, or intervals, ] when you have met him after a while, and then withheld yourself from him, and then come to him. (S, M, K. See also baEodu .]) -A2- Also Union [of companions or friends or lovers]; (T, S, M, Msb, K;) the contr. of the first of the significations mentioned above in this paragraph. (T, S, Msb.) [Hence *aAtu Albayoni as meaning The state of union or concord or friendship or love subsisting between a people or between two parties; this being likewise the contr. of a signification assigned to the same expression above: whence the phrase, A_ifosaAdu *aAti Albayoni (occurring in the S and K in art. Abr , and often elsewhere,) The marring, or disturbance, of the state of union or concord &c.: and] hence the saying, saEaY fulaAnN liA_iSolaAHi *aAti Albayoni mino Ea$iyratihi [ Such a one laboured for the improving of the state of union or concord &c. of his kinsfolk; but in this instance, the meaning given in the second sentence of this paragraph seems to be more appropriate]. (Ham p. 569.) ― -b2- *aAtu bayonihimo may also be used as meaning The vacant space ( saAHap ) that is between their houses, or tents. (Ham p. 195.) -A3- bayon is also an adverbial noun, [as such written bayona ,] (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) capable of being used as a noun absolutely: (M, K:) it relates only to that which has space, as a country; or to that which has some number, either two or more, as two men, and a company of men; and denotes [intervention in] the interval between two things, or the middle, or midst, of two things, (Er-Rághib, TA,) or the middle of a collective number: (S:) [thus it signifies Between, and amidst, and among: ] its meaning is [therefore] vague, not apparent unless it is prefixed to two or more [words, or to a word signifying two or more], or to what supplies the place of such a complement: (Msb:) it must necessarily be prefixed, and may not be otherwise than in the manners just explained: (Mgh:) [i. e.] it may not be prefixed to any noun but such as denotes more than one, or to a noun that has another conjoined to it by w , (M,) not by any other conjunction, (M, Msb,) acc0ord. to the usage commonly obtaining. (Msb.) You say bayona Alr~ajulayoni [ Between the two men ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and AlmaAlu bayona Alqawomi [ The property is between the company of men ]: (M, Msb, Er-Rághib: *) and AlmaAlu bayona zayodK waEamorKw [ The property is between Zeyd and 'Amr ]: and huwa bayoniY wabayonahu [ He, or it, is between me and him ]: (M:) and jalasotu bayona Alqawomi I sat in the middle of [or amidst or among ] the company of men: (S, K:) and bayonakumaA AlbaEiyra faxu*aAhu , with AlbEyr in the accus. case, [See between you two the camel, therefore take him ], a saying heard by Ks: (Lin art. End :) and fasada maA bayonahumo [ The state subsisting among them became bad, or marred, or disturbed ]: (S and K in art. myT :) and bayona AlA^ay~aAmi (M and K in art. ndr ) and fiymaA bayona AlA^ay~aAmi (S and Msb in that art.) [ In, or during, the space of ( several ) days ]: and EawaAnN bayona *`lika , in the Kur [ii. 63], is an ex. of its being prefixed to a single word supplying the place of more than one; (Mgh, Msb;) the meaning being, Of middle age, between that which has been mentioned; namely, the faAriD and the bikor . (Bd.) Some allow that two words to the former of which bayona is prefixed may be connected by fa , citing as an evidence the phrase used by Imra-el-Keys, bayona Ald~axuwli faHawomali [as though meaning Between Ed-Dakhool and Howmal ]: but to this it has been replied that Aldxwl is a name applying to several places; so that the phrase [means amidst Ed-Dakhool &c., and] is similar to the saying, AlmaAlu bayona Alqawomi [mentioned above, or jalasotu bayona Alqawomi , also mentioned above]. (Msb.) [You say also, bayona A^aZohurihimo , and bayona Zahorayohimo &c., meaning In the midst of them. (See art. Zhr .) definition: is originally the inf.
sourceDefinition: is originally the inf. n. of baAna as syn. with tabay~ana , and so signifies The being [ distinct or] apparent &c.; (Kull;) or it is a subst. in this sense: (Msb:) or a subst. from bay~ana , [and so signifies the making distinct or apparent &c.,] being like salaAmN and kalaAmN from sal~ama and kal~ama . (Kull.) ― -b2- Hence, conventionally, (Kull,) The means by which one makes a thing [ distinct, ] apparent, manifest, evident, clear, plain, or perspicuous: (S, Er-Rághib, TA, Kull:) this is of two kinds: one is [ a circumstantial indication or evidence; or] a thing indicating, or giving evidence of, a circumstance, or state, that is a result, or an effect, of a quality or an attribute: the other is a verbal indication or evidence, either spoken or written: [see also bay~inapN :] it is also applied to language that discovers and shows the meaning that is intended: and an explanation of confused and vague language: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or the eduction of a thing from a state of dubiousness to a state of clearness: or making the meaning apparent to the mind so that it becomes distinct from other meanings and from what might be confounded with it. (TA.) ― -b3- Also Perspicuity, clearness, distinctness, chasteness, or eloquence, of speech or language: (T, S:) or simply perspicuity thereof: (Har p. 2:) or perspicuity of speech with quickness, or sharpness, of intellect: (M, K:) or perspicuous, or chaste, or eloquent, speech, declaring, or telling plainly, what is in the mind: (Ksh, TA:) or the showing of the intent, or meaning, with the most eloquent expression: it is an effect of understanding, and of sharpness, or quickness, of mind, with perspicuity, or chasteness, or eloquence, of speech: (Nh, TA:) or a faculty, or principles, [ or a science, ] whereby one knows how to express [ with perspicuity of diction ] one meaning in various forms: (Kull:) [some of the Arabs restrict the science of AlbyAn to what concerns comparisons and tropes and metonymies; which last the Arabian rhetoricians distinguish from tropes: and some make it to include rhetoric altogether:] Esh-Shereeshee says, in his Expos. of the Maká- mát [of El-Hareeree] that the difference between bayaAnN and ↓ tiboyaAnN is this: that the former denotes perspicuity of meaning; and the latter, the making the meaning to be understood; and the former is to another person, and the latter to oneself; but sometimes the latter is used in the sense of the former: (TA:) or the former is the act of the tongue, and the latter is the act of the mind: (Har p. 2:) or the former concerns the verbal expression, and the latter concerns the meaning. (Kull.) It is said in a trad., A_in~a mina AlbayaAni siHorFA (S) or lasiHorFA (TA) [ Verily there is a kind of eloquence that is enchantment: see this explained in art. sHr ]. The saying in the Kur [lv. 2 and 3], xalaqa A@loA_inosaAna Eal~amahu A@lobayaAna means He hath created the Prophet: He hath taught him the Kur-án wherein is the manifestation of everything [ needful to be known ]: or He hath created Adam, or man as meaning all mankind: He hath [ taught him speech, and so ] made him to discriminate, and thus to be distinguished from all [ other ] animals: (Zj, T:) or He hath taught him that whereby he is distinguished from other animals, namely, the declaration of what is in the mind, and the making others to understand what he has perceived, for the reception of inspiration, and the becoming acquainted with the truth, and the learning of the law. (Bd.) ― -b4- It is also applied to Verbosity, and the going deep, or being extravagant, in speech, and affecting to be perspicuous, or chaste, therein, or eloquent, and pretending to excel others therein; or some byAn is thus termed; and is blamed in a trad., as a kind of hypocrisy; as though it were a sort of self-conceit and pride. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A well of which the rope does not strike against the sides, because its interior is straight: or that is wide in the upper part, and narrow in the lower: or in which the drawer of water makes the rope to be aloof from its sides, because of its crookedness: (T:) or deep and wide; (S, K;) because the ropes are wide apart from its sides; (S;) as also ↓ baAy^inapN : (S, TA:) or that is wide between the two [ opposite ] sides: (M:) pl. [regularly of the latter epithet] bawaAy^inu . (T, S.)

definition: [ Distinct, as though separate from others;
sourceDefinition: [ Distinct, as though separate from others; and thus,] apparent, manifest, evident, clear, plain, or perspicuous; (T, S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ baAy^inN (T) and ↓ mubiynN : (T, S:) pl. [of mult.] A^aboyinaA='u (S, K) and [of pauc.] bayinapN . (K.) Hence, AlkitaAbu ↓ AlmubiynN [as applied to the Kur, q. v. in xii. 1, &c.,] The clear, plain, or perspicuous, book or writing or scripture: or, as some say, this means the book &c. that makes manifest all that is required [ to be known ]: (T:) or, of which the goodness and the blessing are made manifest: or, that makes manifest the truth as distinguished from falsity, and what is lawful as distinguished from what is unlawful, and that the prophetic office of Mohammad is true, and so are the narratives relating to the prophets: (Zj, T:) or, that makes manifest the right paths as distinguished from the wrong. (M, TA.) And kalaAmN bay~inN Perspicuous, clear, distinct, chaste, or eloquent, language. (T.) ― -b2- A man, or thing, bearing evidence of a quality &c. that he, or it, possesses. (S and K and other Lexicons passim.) ― -b3- A man (M) perspicuous, or clear, or distinct, in speech or language; or chaste therein; or eloquent; (ISh, T, M, K;) fluent, elegant, and elevated, in speech, and having little hesitation therein: (ISh, T:) pl. A^aboyinaA='u (T, M, K) and buyanaA='u and [of pauc.] A^aboyaAnN : (Lh, M, K:) the second of these pls. is anomalous: the last is formed by likening faEiylN to faAEilN : [for bay~inN is a contraction of bayiynN :] but the pl. most agreeable with analogy is bay~inuwna : so says Sb. (M.)

definition: In a state of separation or disunion;
sourceDefinition: In a state of separation or disunion; or separated, severed, disunited, or cut off; (M, * Msb;) as also ↓ A^aboyanu , occurring in a verse cited above, voce bay~ina . [Hence,] AimoraA^apN baAy^inN A woman separated from her husband by divorce; (M, Msb, K;) as also ↓ mubaAnapN : the former without p : (Msb:) like TaAliqN and HaAy^iDN : you say [to a wife] A^anoti baAy^inN [ Thou art separated from me by divorce. ] (Mgh.) ― -b2- TalaAqN baAy^inN is a tropical phrase; and so is TaloqapN baAy^inapN ; (Mgh;) [signifying the same as] taToliyqapN baAy^inapN (S, M, Msb, K) (tropical:) A divorce that is [ as it were ] cut off; i. q. ↓ mubaAnapN [in the second and third of these phrases, and ↓ mubaAnN in the first]: (ISk, Msb:) bAy^np being here used in the sense of a pass. part. n.: (S, Sgh, Msb:) or it [is a possessive epithet, and thus] means having separation: this kind of divorce is one in the case of which the man cannot take back the woman unless by a new contract; (TA;) nor without her consent. (MF in art. bt .) ― -b3- qawosN baAy^inapN , (S, M, K,) and baAy^inN , (M, K,) A bow that is widely separate from its string: (S, M, K:) contr. of baAniyapN ; (S, M;) this signifying one that is so near to its string as almost to stick to it: (S:) each of these denotes what is a fault. (S, M.) ― -b4- biy^orN baAy^inapN : see bayuwnN . ― -b5- naxolapN baAy^inapN A palm-tree of which the racemes have come forth from the spathes, and of which the fruit-stalks have grown long. (AHn, M.) ― -b6- AlbaAy^inu also signifies He who comes to the milch beast [meaning the she-camel, when she is to be milked, ] from her left side; (S, K;) and AlmuEal~iY , he who comes to her from her right side: (S:) or the former, he who stands on the right of the she-camel when she is milked, and holds the milking-vessel, and raises it to the milker, who stands on her left, and is called AlmusotaEoliY : (T:) two persons are engaged in milking the she-camel; one of them holds the milking-vessel on the right side, and the other milks on the left side; and the milker is called AlmusotaEoliY and AlmuEal~iY ; and the holder, AlbAy^n : (M:) pl. buy~anN . (T.) It is said in a prov., Aisotu AlbaAy^ini A^aEorafu , or, as some say, A^aEolamu ; meaning (assumed tropical:) He who has superintended an affair, and exercised himself diligently in the management thereof, is better acquainted with it than he who has not done this. (T. [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 606.]) ― -b7- TawiylN baAy^inN Excessively tall, far above the stature of tall men. (TA.) -A2- See also bay~inN .

definition: A kind of trees (S, M, K) having a small fruit, (S, M,) like that of the xirowaE [or castor-oil plant ], (M,) which, bursting, discloses grains, that are eaten by the people of the desert: (S, M:) as...
sourceDefinition: A kind of trees (S, M, K) having a small fruit, (S, M,) like that of the xirowaE [or castor-oil plant ], (M,) which, bursting, discloses grains, that are eaten by the people of the desert: (S, M:) as the sun declines, it follows it with the [ upper ] sides of its leaves: (M:) its fruit, with Hurof , (K,) i. e. Hab~u Alr~a$aAdi [q. v.], (TA,) and water, drunk, expels worms; and the application of its leaves, with vinegar, in the manner of a poultice, draws forth warts: (K:) n. un. with p : (S, M, K:) AHn says, it is a kind of dust-coloured trees, of those termed A^agolaAv , eaten by ostriches and gazelles, and of those among which gazelles are snared: its grain, when the coverings thereof open, becomes black; and it has a root ( Eiroq ), sometimes made into a zanod [ for producing fire ]: the places where it grows are mostly the sides of valleys: IAar says, the tn~wmp is a tree of the kind called janobap , of large size, in which grow grains like hemp-seed, used for ointment, and as a seasoning, or condiment: it dries up at the beginning of winter, and disappears: all this is from AHn: (M:) A'Obeyd says, it is one of the plants of the earth, in which, and in the fruit whereof, is a blackness: it is eaten by the ostrich: the pl. [or coll. gen. n.] is tan~uwmN : (T: the author of which then adds,) I say, it is a tree which I have seen in the desert: the colour of its leaves inclines to blackness, and it has grains like hemp-seed, or a little larger: I have seen the women of the desert bruise its grains, and express from them a blue oil, in which is a viscosity; and they anoint their hair with it when they comb themselves: AA says, the tn~wm has a grain which is oily and dustcoloured: En-Nadr says, the tn~wmp is of an ill savour, and the beasts do not like it, or eat much of it: (T:) [it is erroneously said in the K, voce Tul~aAmN , to be hemp-seed ( Hab~u Al$~aAhodaAnij ): and] some say that it is the hemp-plant ( $jr Al$hdAnj ). (Ham p. 135.) The sun, when eclipsed, is said in a trad. to have become black, and like a tn~wmp . (T.) And a poet, who married a woman, and found her to be pretty, but with hoary hair, and who had a youthful wife at his abode, likens the hair of the former to the flower of the A^uqoHuwaAn , and black hair to tn~wm ; saying walam~aA raA^ayotu AlA^uqoHuwaAna munaw~irFA walamo A^ara tan~uwmFA ta*ak~arotu manoziliY [ And when I saw the chamomile flowering, and saw not tennoom, I remembered my abode ]. (Ham ubi suprà.)

definition: and ↓ mavoruwdN Bread crumbled, or broken into small pieces, with the fingers, and then moistened with broth: (Msb:) or [simply] broken bread.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ mavoruwdN Bread crumbled, or broken into small pieces, with the fingers, and then moistened with broth: (Msb:) or [simply] broken bread. (S.) ― -b2- Also, the former, (T, A,) and ↓ variydapN (T, M, A, K) and ↓ vurodapN (S, M, A, Msb) and ↓ varuwdapN (M, K) and ↓ mavoruwdapN (K accord. to the TA) and ↓ A^uvorudaAnN , (Fr, M, * K,) Bread, itself, crumbled, or broken into small pieces, with the fingers, (T, * S, * M, A, Msb, K, *) then moistened with broth (T, A, Msb) &c., (T,) and then piled up in the middle of a bowl; (A;) generally having some flesh-meat with it: (L:) or ↓ variydapN signifies a mess, or portion, of variyd [or bread crumbled or broken &c.]; (T;) [and so ↓ varuwdapN , and ↓ mavoruwdapN :] that of Ghassán is said by common consent to have been prepared with marrow, and with eggs, or the yolks of eggs; and there was no kind more delicious than these two kinds. (TA.) The pl. of vrydp is varaAy^idu and vurudN and vurodN ; (A, and Ham p. 524;) the last of which is a contraction of that next preceding it. (Ham ubi suprà.) A poet, as cited by IAar, says, ↓ A^alaA yaA xubozu yaA A@bonapa yavorudaAnK A^abaY AlHuloquwmu baEodaki laA yanaAmu [ Now surely, O bread, O daughter of two preparers of variyd , the throat refuses, after swallowing thee, to rest, by reason of desire for more]: he says that the poet calls the bread after two young men, or slaves, who were preparing vryd , and gives tenween to yvrdAn by a poetic license, instead of saying yavorudaAni , which, as it is [originally] a verbal phrase, he should have said by rule: but the word, as Fr relates it, is ↓ A^uvorudaAnK ; and [ISd says,] I think that this is a determinate subst., for Alv~ariyd or Almavoruwd , and therefore properly imperfectly decl., but here made perfectly decl. by a poetic license. (M.) It is said in a trad. that the excellence of 'Áïsheh above other women is as the excellence of vryd above other kinds of food; but it is said that what is here meant is food prepared with flesh-meat, together with vryd , because this is generally prepared with flesh-meat, and it is said to be one of the two things called laHom . (TA.)

definition: , (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) said in the K to be like saEaY , implying that the aor.
sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) said in the K to be like saEaY , implying that the aor. is , but this is a mistake, (MF, TA,) [for it is well known that] the aor. is , (Msb,) inf. n. vanoYN , (S, M, Msb, &c.,) He doubled it, or folded it; (T;) he turned one part of it upon another; (M, K;) he bent it; (T, S, Mgh, Msb, TA;) he drew, or contracted, one of its two extremities to [or towards ] the other; or joined, or adjoined, one of them to the other; thus bending it; (Mgh;) namely, a stick, or branch, or twig, (Mgh,) or a thing, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) of any kind. (T.) One says of a man with the mention of whom one begins, in relation to an honourable or a praiseworthy quality, or in relation to science or knowledge, bihi tuvonaY AlxanaASiru , (T,) meaning With [the mention of] him, (T, and Msb in art. xSr ,) among others of his class, (Msb ib.,) the little fingers are bent. (T, and Msb ubi suprá. [For the Arabs, in counting with the fingers, first bend the tip of the little finger down to the palm of the hand; then, the tip of the next; and so on; bending the thumb down upon the other fingers for five; and then continue by extending the fingers, one after another, again commencing with the little finger.]) And a poet says, faA_ino Eud~a majodN A^awo qadiymN limaEo$arK faqawomiY bihimo tuvonaY hunaAka lA^aSaAbiEu [ And if glory, or any old ground of pretension to honour, be reckoned as belonging to a body of men, it is my people, with the mention of them, in that case, the fingers are bent ]; meaning that they are reckoned as the best; (IAar, M;) for the best are not many. (M.) One says also, vanaY warikahu fanazala [lit. He bent his hip, and alighted ], meaning he alighted from his beast. (T.) And vanaY rijolahu Eano daAb~atihi , meaning He drew up his leg to his thigh, and alighted. (M.) But qabola A^ano yavoniYa rijolahu , occurring in a trad., means Before he turned his leg from the position in which it was in the pronouncing of the testimony of the faith. (IAth.) vanaY Sadorahu , aor. and inf. n. as above, [lit. He folded his breast, or bosom, ] means (assumed tropical:) he concealed enmity in his breast, or bosom: or he folded up what was in it, in concealment. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [xi. 5], A^alaA A_in~ahumo yavonawna Suduwrahumo , meaning [ Now surely ] they infold and conceal [ in their bosoms ] enmity and hatred: (Fr, T:) or they bend their breasts, or bosoms, and fold up, and conceal, what is therein: (Zj, T:) I'Ab read, Suduwruhumo ↓ tavonawoniY : you say, AivonawonaY Sadoruhu EalaY AlbagoDaA='i , meaning his breast, or bosom, infolded, or concealed, vehement hatred: (T:) or the phrase in the Kur, accord. to the former reading, means they bend, or turn, their breasts, or bosoms, from the truth; they turn themselves away therefrom: or they incline their breasts, or bosoms, to unbelief, and enmity to the Prophet: or they turn their backs: (Bd:) [for] ― -b2- vanaAhu , (T, S, Msb, TA,) aor. as above, (Msb,) and so the inf. n., (T, Msb, TA,) also signifies He turned him, or it, away or back. (T, S, Msb, TA.) Also He turned him, or turned him away or back, (Lth, T, S,) from the course that he desired to pursue, (Lth, T,) or from the object of his want: (S:) or you say, vanaAhu Eano wajohihi , (Mgh,) and Eano HaAjatihi , (TA,) and Eano muraAdihi , (Msb,) he turned him, or turned him away or back, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) from his course, (Mgh,) and from the object of his want, (TA,) and from the object of his desire. (Msb.) One says also, fulaAnN laA yuvonaY Eano qironihi walaA Eano wajohihi [ Such a one will not be turned, or turned away or back, from his antagonist, nor from his course ]. (T.) ― -b3- Also He tied it; or tied it in a knot or knots; or tied it firmly, fast, or strongly. (TA.) You say, vanayotu AlbaEiyra bivinaAyayoni , meaning, accord. to As, as related by A'Obeyd, I bound both the fore legs of the camel with two bonds: but correctly, I bound the two fore legs of the camel with the two ends of a rope; the last word meaning a single rope: (T:) Eaqalotuhu bivanoyayoni means I bound one of his fore shanks to the arm with two ties, or tyings. (T, M.) ― -b4- vanoYN [as inf. n. of vanaY ] also signifies The act of drawing, or joining, or adjoining, one [ thing ] to another; (Lth, T, Mgh;) and so ↓ tavoniyapN [inf. n. of vn~Y ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- A folding: so in the saying, A^anofa*otu ka*aA vinoYa kitaAbiY , (S, TA,) or fiY vinoYi kitaAbiYi (so in a copy of the S,) i. e., fiY Tay~ihi [lit. I sent, or transmitted, such a thing within the folding of my writing, or letter; meaning infolded, or enclosed, in it; and included in it ]. (S, TA.) ― -b3- A duplicature, or fold, of a garment, or piece of cloth: (TA:) or what is turned back of the extremities thereof: (T:) pl. as above: whence, in a trad. of Aboo-Hureyreh, kaAna yavoniyhi Ealayohi A^avonaA='F mino saEatihi [ He used to fold it upon him in folds by reason of its width ]; meaning the garment. (TA.) [Hence the saying,] wakaAna *`lika fiY A^avonaA='i ka*aA , i. e., fY guDuwnihi [lit And that was in the folds, meaning, in the midst, of such a thing, or such an affair, or event ]. (TA.) And jaAw^uwA fiY A^avonaA='i AlA^amori They came in the midst of the affair, or event. (Msb.) [And hence, app.,] maDaY vinoYN mina All~ayol An hour, or a period, or a short portion, of the night passed; (M, K; *) syn. saAEapN , (Th, M, K,) or waqotN . (Lh, M, K.) [See also what is said below respecting its pl. in relation to a night.] ― -b4- Also sing. of A^avonaA='N meaning The parts of a thing that are laid together like the strands of a rope, or that are laid one upon another as layers or strata, or side by side as the things that compose a bundle; ( quwaAhu , and TaAqaAtuhu ; [rendered by Freytag “ virtutes, facultates rei; ”]) and ↓ mavaAnK , of which the sing. is ↓ mavonaApN and ↓ mivonaApN , signifies the same. (M, K.) ― -b5- Also A bending of the neck of a sheep, or goat, not in consequence of disease: (K: but in the M, vanoYN [inf. n. of 1]:) and a serpent's bending, or folding, of itself: (M, K:) and also (thus in the M, but in the K “or”) a curved part of a serpent that has folded itself; (M, K;) pl. A^avonaA='N , (M,) i. e. the folds of a coiled serpent. (T.) The pl. is used metaphorically [as though meaning (tropical:) The turns ] of a night. (M. [But see explanations of the sing. as used in relation to a night in what precedes.] ― -b6- A part that is bent, or folded, or doubled, of a wi$aAH [q. v.]; (TA;) pl. as above: (T, TA:) and so of a rope: (S:) or a portion of the extremity of a rope folded, or doubled, [ so as to form a loop, ] for binding therewith the pastern of the fore leg of a beast, to serve as a tether. (T.) Tarafeh says, laEamoruka A_in~a Almawota maA A^axoTaA^a AlfataY lakaAlT~iwali AlmuroxaY wavinoyaAhu biAloyadi [ By thy life, death, while missing the strong young man, is like the tether that is slackened while the two folded extremities thereof are upon the fore leg, or in the hand: see TiwalN ]: (T, S:) he means that the young man must inevitably die, though his term of life be protracted; like as the beast, though his tether be lengthened and slackened, cannot escape, being withheld by its two extremities: (so in a copy of the T:) or by vnyAh he means its extremity; using the dual form because it is folded, or doubled, upon the pastern, and tied with a double tie: (so in another copy of the T:) or he means, while its two extremities are in the hand of its owner: (EM p. 91:) by mA AxTA^ , he means fiY A_ixoTaAy^ihi , (S in art. Twl ,) or mud~apa A_ixoTaAy^ihi : and the l [prefixed to the k of comparison] is for corroboration. (EM ubi suprá.) You say also, rab~aqa A^avonaA='a AlHaboli , meaning He made loops in the middle of the rope to put upon the necks of the young lambs or kids. (T.) ― -b7- Also A bend, or place of bending, of a valley, (S, M, * K,) and of a mountain: (S:) pl. as above: (M, K:) and ↓ mavaAnK [likewise] signifies the bends of a valley. (T, K.) -A2- A she-camel that has brought forth twice, (S,) or two, (M,) or a second time: (K:) or, as some say, that has brought forth once: but the former is more analogical: (M:) one does not say vilovN [as meaning “ that has brought forth thrice ”], nor use any similar epithet above this: (S, TA:) pl. vunaA='N , like Zuw^aArN pl. of Ziy^orN , accord. to Sb, (M, TA,) and A^avonaA='N accord. to others: (TA:) in like manner it is applied to a woman, (S, M,) metaphorically: (M:) and to the she-camel's second young one: (S, M:) accord. to As, as related by A'Obeyd, a she-camel that has brought forth once: also that has brought forth twice: [so says Az, but he adds,] but what I have heard from the Arabs is this; that they term a she-camel that has brought forth her first young one bikor ; and her first young one, her bikor ; and when she brought forth a second, she is termed vinoYN ; and her young one, her vinoY : and this is what is correct. (T.) [Hence the saying,] maA h`*aA AlA^amoru minoka bikorFA walaA vinoyFA (tropical:) This thing, or affair, is not thy first nor thy second. (A and TA in art. bkr .) ― -b2- See also vunoyaAnN .

definition: The repetition of a thing;
sourceDefinition: The repetition of a thing; doing it one time after another: (Aboo-Sa'eed, TA:) or a thing, or an affair, done twice: (S, Msb, TA:) this is the primary signification: (TA:) and ↓ vunFY signifies the same. (IB, TA.) It is said in a trad., laA vinaY fiY AlS~adaqapi There shall be no repetition in the taking of the poor-rate; (IAth, TA;) [i. e.] the poor-rate shall not be taken twice in one year: (As, Ks, T, S, M, Mgh, K:) or two she-camels shall not be taken in the place of one for the poor-rate: (M, IAth, K: *) or there shall be no retracting of an alms; or no revoking it: (Mgh, K, * TA:) this last is the meaning accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed, (Mgh, TA,) i. e. Ed-Dareeree, (Mgh,) who, in explaining this trad., as relating to the giving an alms to a man and then desiring to take it back, says he does not deny that vinFY has the meaning first assigned to it above in this paragraph. (TA.) ― -b2- See also vunoyAnN : ― -b3- and AivonaAni .

sourceDefinition: a subst. from AisotivonaA='N ; (S, Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ vanowaY ; the former with damm, and the latter with fet-h: (S, Msb:) both are syn. with AisotivonaA='N [used as a subst., meaning An exception ]; (T;) as also ↓ vaniy~apN , (T, K,) or ↓ vunoyapN , (accord. to one copy of the T,) and ↓ mavonawiy~apN : (T:) so in the saying, Halafa yamiynFA layosa fiyhaA vunoyaA and ↓ vunowaY and ↓ vaniy~apN or ↓ vunoyapN and ↓ mavonawiy~apN [ he swore an oath in which there was not an exception ]; for when the swearer says, “ By God I will not do such and such things unless God will otherwise, ” he reverses what he [first] says by God's willing otherwise: (T: [see 10:]) [and so in the saying,] ↓ HalofapN gayoru *aAti mavonawiy~apK a swearing not made lawful [ by an exception ]: (M:) [so too in the saying,] ↓ bayoEN maA fiyhi mavonawiy~apN [and vunoyaA &c.] (K in art. lHj ) a sale in which there is not an exception: (TA in that art.:) or vunoyaA signifies a thing excepted, (M, Mgh, K,) whatever it be; (K) as also ↓ vanowaY , (M, K,) with w substituted for Y , (M,) or ↓ vunowaY , (so in the TA, [but probably through inadvertence,]) and ↓ vaniy~apN , (M, K,) or ↓ vunoyapN . (TA.) In a sale, it is unlawful when it is the exception of a thing unknown; and when one sells a slaughtered camel for a certain price and excepts the head and extremities: (T, TA:) or when an exception is made from things sold without measuring or weighting or numbering: and in a contract with another for labour upon land on the condition of sharing the produce, it is when one excepts a certain measure after the half or the third. (IAth, TA.) The saying of Mo- hammad, mani A@sotavonaY falahu vunoyaAhu means Whoso maketh an exception, his shall be what he excepteth: (M, TA: *) as, for instance, when one says, “ I divorce her thrice, save once: ” or “ I emancipate them, except such a one. ” (TA.) ― -b2- It also means particularly The head and legs of a slaughtered camel; (T, M, * K;) because the seller of the camel used, in the Time of Ignorance, to except them; (T;) and IF adds, but incorrectly, the back-bone: (Sgh, TA:) whence, applied to a she-camel, mu*ak~arapu Alv~unoyaA , (T, M,) meaning Resembling the make of the male in [ the largeness of ] her head and legs; (Th, M;) or jumaAliy~apu Alv~unoyaA , having thick legs, like those of the male camel in thickness. (T.) [Also, app., The exception, or omission, of a day, in irrigation: see 3 in art. vlv , and vilovN in the same art.] And ↓ vaniy~apN signifies also A palm-tree that is excepted from a bargain. (M, K.) And The martyrs whom God has excepted from those who shall fall down dead or swooning: (M, K:) these, accord. to Kaab, are A@ll~`hi fiY AlA^aroDi ↓ vaniy~pu [ those whom God has excepted on the earth ]; (T, M;) alluded to in the Kur [xxxix. 68], where it is said, “ And the horn shall be blown, and those who are in the heavens and those on the earth shall fall down dead, or swooning, except those whom God shall please [to except]. ” (T.)

definition: The second chief;
sourceDefinition: The second chief; the person who comes second as a chief; (A'Obeyd, T;) the person who is [ next ] below the say~id , (S, M, K, [in some copies of the K, erroneously, syl ,]) in rank; (S;) as also ↓ vinFY (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, K) and ↓ vunFY (A'Obeyd, T, S, K) and ↓ vinoYN : (K:) pl. (of the first, S) vinoyapN [which is also a sing., mentioned above]. (S, K.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce bado'N .] ― -b2- A man having no judgment nor intelligence, or understanding. definition: The cord, or rope, with which a camel's fore shank and his arm are bound together;
sourceDefinition: The cord, or rope, with which a camel's fore shank and his arm are bound together; (S, K;) and the like; consisting of a folded, or doubled, cord, or rope: each of the folds, or duplicatures, thereof would be thus termed if the word were used in the sing. form: (S:) Ibn-EsSeed [in the CK, erroneously, Ibn-Es-Seedeh] allows it; and therefore it is given as on his authority in the K: (TA:) and Lth allows it; but in this instance he allows what the Arabs do not allow: (T:) you say, Eaqalotu AlbaEiyra bivinaAyayoni , meaning I bound together the fore shanks and the arms of the camel with a rope, (S,) or with two ropes, (M, [but this is probably a mistake of a copyist,]) or with the two ends of a rope; (AZ, T, S, M;) without ' because the word has no sing.: (Kh, Sb, T, S:) Lth allows one's saying bivinaA='ayoni also; but the Basrees and Koofees [in general] agree that it is without ' : (T:) IB says that it has no sing. because it is a single rope, with one end of which one fore leg is bound, and with the other end the other leg; and IAth says the like: (TA:) this rope is also called ↓ vinaAyapN ; but a single rope for binding one fore shank and arm is not thus called. (T.) See also vinaAyapN . ― -b2- And see vaAnK . -A2- The finaA=' [or court, or open or wide space, in front, or extending from the sides, ] (M, K,) of a house: (M:) [in the CK, AlginA'u is erroneously put for AlfinA'u :] accord. to IJ, from vanaY , aor. yavoniY , because there one is turned back, by its limits, from expatiating; but A'Obeyd holds the v to be a substitute for f . (M.)

definition: I. q. EaqabapN : (AA, M, Mgh, K:) or the latter means a long mountain that lies across the road, and which the road traverses; and the former, any such mountain that is traversed: (T:) so called...
sourceDefinition: I. q. EaqabapN : (AA, M, Mgh, K:) or the latter means a long mountain that lies across the road, and which the road traverses; and the former, any such mountain that is traversed: (T:) so called because it lies before the road, and crosses it; or because it turns away him who traverses it: (Mgh:) or the road of what is termed Eaqabap : (S; and so in copies of the K:) or a high road of what is thus termed: (K accord. to the TA:) or a road in, or upon, a mountain, (M, K,) like that which is termed naqobN [q. v.]: (M:) or a road to a mountain: (M, K:) or a mountain (M, K) itself: (M:) or a part of a mountain that requires one, in traversing it, to ascend and descend; as though it turned the course of journeying: (Er-Rághib, TA:) pl. vanaAyaA : (T, S:) which signifies also [ such roads as are termed ] madaArij . (T.) Hence the phrase, fulaAnN Tal~aAEu Alv~anaAyaA Such a one rises to eminences, or to lofty things or circumstances, or to the means of attaining such things; like the phrase Tal~aAEu A^anojudK [q. v.]: (S:) or, like the latter phrase, is accustomed to embark in, or undertake, or to surmount, or master, lofty and difficult things: (Mgh:) or is hardy, strong, or sturdy; one who embarks in, or undertakes, great affairs. (TA. [See an ex. under the heading of Aibonu jalaA , in art. jlw : and see also art. TlE .]) ― -b2- Also, (T, S, M, &c.,) pl. vanaAyaA (T, S, Mgh, Msb) and vaniy~aAtN , (Msb,) One of certain teeth, (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) the foremost in the mouth, (M,) [namely, the central incisors, ] four in number, (T, M, Mgh, Msb,) to man, and to the camel, (T, M, &c.,) and to the wild beast, (M,) in the fore part of the mouth, (T, Mgh, K,) two above and two below: (T, M, Mgh, K:) so called as being likened to the vaniy~ap of a mountain, in form and hardness; (TA;) or because each of them is placed next to its fellow. (Mgh.) -A2- Also fem. of vaniY~N [q. v.]. (T, S, M, &c.) -A3- See also vunoyaA , in five places.

sourceDefinition: A cord, or rope, of goats' hair ( $aEar ), or of wool, (S, K,) or of other material; (K;) as also ↓ vinaA='N (K) and ↓ mivonaApN and ↓ mavonaApN ; (M, K;) which last is explained by IAar as signifying [simply] a cord, or rope: (M:) [or] the first has the meaning assigned to it above, voce vinaA='N ; syn. with vinaAyaAni : and signifies also a long rope; whence the saying of Zuheyr, describing the [she-camel termed] saAniyap , tamoTuw Alr~i$aA='a watujoriY fiY vinaAyatihaA mina AlmaHaAlapi qab~FA raAy^idFA qaliqaA (T,) meaning [ She draws the well-rope, and causes to run, ] with her vnAyp upon her, (ISk, T,) [ a wabbling, unsteady, sheave (?) of the large pulley; ] the vnAyp here being a rope of which the two ends are tied to the saddle ( qatab ) of the sAnyp ; the [ upper ] end of the well-rope being tied to its ↓ mivonaAp [which here means the folded middle part ]: (T:) but Aboo-Sa'eed says that it [here] means a piece of wood by which are connected the two extremities of the cheeks, or side-pieces, ( TrfA Almylyn , [the latter of which words I here render conjecturally, supposing it to be similar in meaning to AlqaEowi or AlqaEowayoni ,]) above the mHAlp , and a similar piece below; the mHAlp and [qu. or ] the sheave turning between the tow pieces thus called. (T, in a later portion of the art.)

definition: [act. part. n. of 1; Doubling, or folding; &c.]. Hence, huwa vaAnK rijolahu While he was bending his leg before rising, or standing up. (TA from a trad.) [And jaA='a vaAniYa EiTofihi : see art. ETf...
sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of 1; Doubling, or folding; &c.]. Hence, huwa vaAnK rijolahu While he was bending his leg before rising, or standing up. (TA from a trad.) [And jaA='a vaAniYa EiTofihi : see art. ETf .] One says of a horseman who has bent the neck of his beast on the occasion of his vehement running, jaA='a vaAniYa AlEinaAni [ He came bending the rein by pulling it with both hands a little apart]: (T:) or jaA='a vaAniyFA mino EinaAnihi [ he came bending a part of his rein]. (S.) And of the horse himself, one says, jaA='a saAbiqFA vaAniyFA , i. e. He came outstripping, with bent neck, by reason of briskness; because when he is fatigued, he stretches out his neck; and when he is not fatigued nor jaded by running, but comes in his first run, he bends his neck: and hence the saying of the poet, wamano yafoxaro bimivoli A^abiY wajad~iY yajiy^o qabola Als~awaAbiqi wahuwa vaAniY i. e. definition: a noun of number;
sourceDefinition: a noun of number; (S, Msb;) applied to the dual number; (Msb;) meaning [ Two; ] the double of waAHidN ; (M, K;) with a conjunctive A [when not immediately preceded by a quiescence, written A@vonaAni ]; (T, S, Msb;) but this is sometimes made disjunctive when connected with a preceding word by poetic license: (T, S:) of the masc. gender: (S:) fem. AivonataAni , (T, S, Msb,) in which, also, the A is conjunctive; (T, Msb;) and ↓ vinotaAni ; (T S, M, Msb, K;) the latter sometimes used, (T,) [much less frequently than the former, though the only fem. form mentioned in the M and K,] and of the dial. of Temeem; (Msb;) like as one says, hiYa A@bonapu fulaAnK and hiYa binotuhu : (T:) the t in the dual is a substitute for the final radical, Y , (M, TA,) as it is in A^asonatuwA , the only other instance of this substitution except in words of the measure AifotaEala : (Sb, M, TA:) in AivonaAni , the final radical, Y is suppressed: (Msb:) it has no sing.: (Lth, T:) if it were allowable to assign to it a sing., it would be AivonN [for the masc.] and AivonapN [for the fem.], like AibonN and AibonapN : (S:) accord. to some, (Msb,) it is originally vinoYN ; (T, Msb, CK;) and hence the dual vinotaAni : (Msb:) or it is originally vanaYN , (M, Msb, and so in a copy of the K,) the conjunctive A being then substituted for the Y whence the dual A@vonaAni , like A@bonaAni : (Msb:) this is shown by the form of its pl., which is A^avonaA='N , (M, K,) like A^abonaA='N [pl. of A@bonN , which is originally banaYN or banawN ,] and A=xaA='N [pl. of A^axN , which is originally A^axawN ]. (M.) In the saying in the Kur [xvi. 53], laA tat~axi*uwA A_i`lhayoni A@vonayoni [ Take not to yourselves two gods ], the last word is added as a corroborative. (M.) The phrase vinotaA HanoZalK occurs, by poetic license, for AivonataAni mino HanoZalK , meaning HanoZalataAni [ Two colo- cynths ]. (S.) You say also, AlqadaHi ↓ $aribotu A^avonaA='a , and $aribotu A@vonaYo h`*aA AlqadaHi , meaning [ I drank ] twice as much as the bowl, and as this bowl: and in like manner, $aribotu A@vonaYo mud~i AlbaSorapi and A@vonayoni bimud~i AlbaSorapi [ I drank twice the quantity of the mud~ of El-Basrah ]. (M.) And a poet says, ↓ famaA Hulibato A_il~aA Alv~alaAvapa waAlv~unaY walaA quy~ilato A_il~aA qariybFA maqaAluhaA meaning [ And she was not milked save ] three vessels and two, [ nor was she given her middaydrink save when her midday-resting was near. ] (IAar, M.) ― -b2- Hence, (Msb,) yawomu AlA@ivonayoni , (S, Msb,) or AlA@ivonaAni alone, (M, K,) One of the days of the week; [ the second; namely, Monday; ] because the first, with the Arabs, is AlA^aHadu ; (M;) as also ↓ Alv~inaY , like A_ilaY ; (K;) so in the copies of the K; [or,] accord. to some, ↓ Alv~uniY~u , [originally Alv~unuwYu ,] of the measure fuEuwl , like vudiY~N [pl. of vadoYN ], is used in this sense; (TA;) or ↓ Alyawomu Alv~unaY~u , [so in the M, accord. to the TT,] mentioned by Sb, on the authority of certain of the Arabs: (M:) the pl. is A^avonaA='N and A^avaAniynu , (M, K,) the latter mentioned on the authority of Th: but it has no dual: and those who say A^avonaA='N form this pl. from AlA@ivonu , although this has not been in use: (M:) or it has neither dual nor pl., (S, Msb,) being itself a dual; (S;) but if you would form a pl. from it, you would regard it as itself a sing., and make its pl. A^avaAniynu : (S, Msb:) IB says that A^avaAniynu has not been heard [from the Arabs], and is only mentioned by Fr, on the ground of analogy; that it is far-fetched in respect of analogy; and that the pl. heard is A^avonaA='N : Seer and others mention, as heard from the Arabs, A_in~ahu layaSuwmu AlA^avonaA='a [ Verily he fasts on the Mondays ]. (TA.) Alvnyn in ywm Alvnyn has no dim. (Sb, S in art. Ams .) IJ says that the article Al in Alvnyn is not redundant, though the word is not an epithet: Abu-l-'Abbás says that the prefixing of the article in this case is allowable because the virtual meaning is Alyawomu Alv~aAniY [ the second day ]. (M.) The saying Alyawomu AlA@ivonaAni means The name of to-day [ is AlAvnAn ]; and is like the saying Alyawomu yawomaAni [to-day is two days] and Alyawomu xamosapa Ea$ara mina Al$~ahori [to-day is fifteen of the month]. (Sb, M.) Sometimes, yawomu A@vonayoni , without the article Al , occurs in poetry. (M, K.) When a pronoun refers to AlAvnAn [as meaning Monday], this word may be treated in two ways, [as a sing. and as a dual,] but the more chaste way is to treat it as a sing., as meaning the day: (Msb:) [thus,] Aboo-Ziyád used to say, maDaY AlA@ivonaAni bimaA fiyhi [ Monday passed with what occurred in it ]; making it sing. and masc.; and thus he did in the case of every day of the week, except that he made AljumoEap fem.: Abu-I-Jarráh used to say, maDaY AlA@ivonaAni bimaA fiyhimaA , treating the word as a numeral; and thus he treated the third and fourth and fifth days, saying in each of these cases bimaA fiyhin~a . (M.) ― -b3- [ AivonaA Ea$ara , fem. AivonataA Ea$orapa ; respectively, in a case of nasb and khafd, AivonaYo Ea$ara and AivonataYo Ea$orapa ; and with A@ when not immediately preceded by a quiescence; mean Twelve: see Ea$arapN .]

definition: (S, Mgh) and ↓ vunaA='u (T, S) [ Two and two;
sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh) and ↓ vunaA='u (T, S) [ Two and two; two and two together; or two at a time and two at a time ]: they are imperfectly decl., in like manner as [ mavolavu and] vulaAvu , as explained in art. vlv ; (S, TA;) [because] changed from the original form of AivonaAni A@vonaAni ; (T, Mgh, TA;) or because of their having the quality of epithets and deviating from the original form of AivonaAni ; (Sb, S in art. vlv , q. v.;) or because they deviate from their original as to the letter and the meaning; the original word being changed as above stated, and the meaning being changed to AivonaAni A@vonaAni . (S ibid.) You say, jaAw^uwA mavonaY and ↓ vunaA='a (M, K) or mavonaY mavonaY , (S,) but this is a repetition of the word only, not of the meaning, (Mgh,) and in like manner one says of women, (M, K, *) i. e. They came two [ and ] two. (S, M, K.) And it is said in a trad., SalaApu All~ayoli mavonaY mavonaY , i. e. The prayer of night is two rek'ahs [ and ] two rek'ahs ( rakoEataAni rakoEataAni ). (TA.) [See also other exs. voce vulaAvu .] ― -b2- mavonaY AlA^ayaAdiY The repeating a benefit, or benefaction; or reiterating it; conferring it twice, or thrice; (As, T, K;) or twice, or more than twice: (K:) or the shares remaining of the slaughtered camel (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, K) in the game called Almayosir , (A'Obeyd, T, S, K,) which shares a bountiful man used to purchase, and give for food to the A^aboraAm , (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, K,) i. e., those who took no part in the game, not contributing: (M:) or the taking a portion time after time. (AA, T, S, M.) ― -b3- mavaAnK [is pl. of mavonFY as signifying A place of doubling, or folding &c.: and hence means ― -b4- ] The knees and elbows of a horse or similar beast. (T, K.) ― -b5- And The bends of a valley. (T, K. See vinoYN .) ― -b6- And, as pl. of mavonFY , The chords of the lute that are after the first: (M, K:) or mvnY signifies a chord [ of a lute ] composed of two twists: or, as some say, the second chord. (Har p. 244. See mavolavN .) ― -b7- mavonFY also signifies The zimaAm [or noserein ] of a she-camel: and Er-Rághib says that the mvnAp [i. e. ↓ mavonaAp or ↓ mivonaAp ] is the doubled, or folded, part of the extremity of the zimaAm . (TA.) ― -b8- AlmavaAniY as relating to the Kur-án is pl. of mavonFY , (Mgh,) or of ↓ mavonaApN : (AHeyth, T, Mgh:) it has three applications, accord. to A'Obeyd: (T, Mgh:) it signifies The Kur-án altogether; (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, Mgh, K;) so in the Kur xxxix 24; (A'Obeyd, T, Mgh;) meaning that the mention of reward and punishment is repeated, or reiterated, in it; (Fr, T;) or so called because the verse of mercy is conjoined with that of punishment; definition: , (K,) or Ajzr Alqawoma , (ISk, S,) He gave to him, or to the people, a sheep or a goat, for him, or for them, to slaughter;
sourceDefinition: , (K,) or Ajzr Alqawoma , (ISk, S,) He gave to him, or to the people, a sheep or a goat, for him, or for them, to slaughter; (ISk, S, K;) meaning a ewe or a ram or a she-goat; (ISk, S;) or a sheep, or goat, fit for slaughter: (TA:) and A^ajozarotuhu $aApF I gave to him a ewe or a ram or a she-goat, and he slaughtered it: (ISk, TA:) and A^ajozarotuka baEiyrFA , or $aApF , I gave to thee a camel, or a sheep or goat, that thou mightest slaughter it: (A:) [but] accord. to ISk, one does not say A^ajozarotuhumo naAqapF , because a she-camel is fit for other purposes than that of slaughter: (S:) and accord. to some, one should not say Ajzrhu jazuwrFA , but Ajzrhu jazarapF . (TA.) -A2- Ajzr He (a camel) attained to the fit time for his being slaughtered. (S, K.) ― -b2- Ajzr Aln~axolu The palm-trees attained to the fit time for the cutting off of the fruit. (S, K.) ― -b3- [And hence,] Ajzr Al$ayoxu (tropical:) The old man attained to the fit time for his dying; (K, TA;) being aged, and near to his perishing; like as the palm-tree attains to the fit time for having its fruit cut off. (TA.) Youths used to say to an old man A^ajozarota yaA $ayoxu , meaning, Thou hast attained to the fit time for thy dying, O old man: and he would say, A^aYo baniY~a watuHotaDaruwna , i. e., “ [O my sons, and] ye shall die youths: ” but accord. to one way of relation, it is A^ajozazota ; from A^ajaz~a Albur~u “ the wheat attained to the proper time for being out. ” (S.) ― -b4- Ajzr Alqawomu The people attained to the fit time for the cutting off of the fruit of the palm-trees. (Yz, TA.)

definition: , of a camel, The extremities;
sourceDefinition: , of a camel, The extremities; (S, A;) namely, (S,) the fore and kind legs, ( AlyadaAni waAlr~ijolaAni , S, K,) and the head, (S,) or neck: (A, K:) because the slaughterer receives them; (S;) they being his hire, (S, K,) or right, (A,) not being included among the shares in the game called Almayosir . (TA.) But when a horse is said to be Eabolu AljuzaArapi , (S,) or Daxomu AljuzaArapi , (M,) what is meant is thickness of the fore and hind legs, and abundance of sinews; and the head is not included, because largeness of the head, in a horse, is a fault. (S, M.)

definition: A man bald in the two sides of his head: (S:) or in the two sides of the fore part of his head: (Msb:) or in the fore part of his head: (Mgh, L:) or a little more bald than he who is termed A^anozaEu...
sourceDefinition: A man bald in the two sides of his head: (S:) or in the two sides of the fore part of his head: (Msb:) or in the fore part of his head: (Mgh, L:) or a little more bald than he who is termed A^anozaEu : (L:) it signifies more than AnzE , and less than A^ajolaY and A^ajolahu : (Mgh:) when a man is bald in the sides of his forehead, he is termed AnzE ; when the baldness is a little more, AjlH ; when it extends to the half, or the like, AjlY ; and then, Ajlh : (A 'Obeyd, TA:) the fem. is jaloHaA='u : and the pl. juloHN (L, Msb) and juloHaAnN . (L.) ― -b2- (tropical:) Having no horn; applied to a bull and a he-goat: (A:) and in this sense the fem. is applied to a ewe (T, M, Msb) or she-goat, (T, M, A, Msb,) and to a cow: (T, M, A:) and in like manner [the pl.] juloHN is applied to cows or bulls having no horns; (S, TA;) erroneously said in the K to be jul~aHN , like suk~arN . (TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) A [woman's camel-vehicle of the kind called] hawodaj that has not a high head or top: (Ibn-Kulthoom, IJ, S, K:) or without a top: (T:) or one that is of a square form: (As, IJ:) pl. ↓ A^ajolaAHN , (S, IJ,) like as A^aEozaAlN is pl. of A^aEozalu ; a very rare form of pl. of a sing. of the measure A^afoEalu . (IJ.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A flat roof not surrounded by a wall or anything else to prevent persons' falling from it. (IAth, K.) ― -b5- qaroyapN jaloHaA='u (tropical:) A town having no fortress: (A, TA:) pl. qurFY juloHN : the fortresses being likened to horns. (TA.) ― -b6- A^akamapN jaloHaA='u (assumed tropical:) [ A hill ] not having a pointed summit. (TA.) And haDobapN jaloHaA='u (assumed tropical:) [ A ] smooth [ hill ]. (A.) ― -b7- A^aroDN jaloHaA='u (assumed tropical:) A land in which are no trees. (TA.) ― -b8- yawomN A^ajolaHu (assumed tropical:) A hard, distressing, or calamitous, day; as also A^aSolaEu . (A, TA.)

(Mgh, Msb.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. rasanN [as meaning A rope, or cord ]; (S;) a certain thing well known; (Msb;) a thing with which one ties, binds, or makes fast, a beast &c.; syn. ribaATN : (M, K:) and i. q. rasanN [as meaning a halter ]; (M, Msb, K;) as in the Kur cxi. 5; (TA;) and so ↓ muHab~alN : (M, K:) in the former sense, the pl. [of pauc.] is A^aHobulN (S, M, K) and A^aHobaAlN (M, K) and [of mult.] HibaAlN (S, M, Msb, K) and HubuwlN (M, K) and HibaAlapN (L voce juroHN ) [and HubuwlapN , agreeably with a usage of the Arabs, which is, to add p to any pl. of the measure fiEaAlN or of that of fuEuwlN , (see HajarN ,)] and ↓ HabaAy^ilu , which is anomalous, as in the phrase HabaAy^ilu All~uw^oluw^i [ cords of pearls ], occurring in a trad.; or this is a mistranscription for janaAbi*u , (K, TA, [in the CK HanAy^idu ,]) with j [and n ] and * : (TA:) and in the latter sense, the pl. is HubuwlN . (M, Msb, K.) In a trad. in which it is said that a man's hand is to be cut off for his stealing a Habol , the Hbl of a ship may be mean. (Mgh in art. byD .) ― -b2- [Hence, (assumed tropical:) A bond; cause of union; or link of connexion: ] connexion with another by the bond of love or friendship or the like; (S, K, TA;) pl. HibaAlN : (TA:) mutual connexion by such a bond. (ISd, Msb, K.) You say, waSala fulaAnN fiY Haboli fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) Such a one married his daughter to such a one. (Har p. 223.) And huwa yaxoTubu fiY Haboli fulaAni (assumed tropical:) He aids such a one in seeking, or demanding, a woman in marriage. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., A_in~a bayonanaA wa bayona Alqawomi HibaAlFA wa naHonu qaATiEuwhaA (assumed tropical:) Verily there is between us and the party a connexion by the bond of love or friendship or the like, and we are severing it. (TA.) You say also, A_in~ahu lawaAsiEu AlHaboli (tropical:) Verily he is large, or liberal, in disposition; [or in the scope of his friendship; ] and Day~iqu AlHaboli (tropical:) narrow therein. (TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) A covenant, or compact: (S, Msb, K, TA:) (tropical:) a covenant, or an obligation, by which one becomes responsible for the safety, or safe-keeping, of a person or thing: (K, TA:) and (tropical:) a promise, or an assurance, of security, or safety; (A 'Obeyd, S, Msb, K, TA;) such as a man, desiring to make a journey, used [ and still uses ] to take from the chief of a tribe: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) pl. HibaAlN . (TA.) You say, kaAnato bayonahumo HibaAlN faqaTaEuwhaA (tropical:) There were between them covenants, and obligations whereby they were responsible for one another's safety, and they broke them. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur [iii. 108], A_il~aA biHabolK mina A@ll~`hi wa HabolK mina Aln~aAsi (tropical:) Unless [they have] a covenant from God and a covenant from men: (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA:) for the unbeliever requires a covenant from God, which consists in his being of those who have a revealed scripture without which he cannot retain his religion nor enjoy protection, and a covenant granted to him by men. (Er-Rághib, TA.) And it is also said in the Kur [iii. 98], waA@EotaSimuwA biHaboli A@ll~`hi i. e. (tropical:) [ And hold ye fast ] by the covenant of God: (TA:) or (tropical:) the means of approach, or access, unto God; i. e. the Kur-án, and the Prophet, and intelligence, &c., which are the means of obtaining the protection of God; for HabolN is metaphorically applied to (tropical:) any means of access to a thing: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or these words of the Kur mean (tropical:) and follow ye the Kur-án, and abstain from schism. (A'Obeyd, TA.) And in like manner, the saying of Ibn-Mes'ood, Ealayokumo biHaboli A@ll~`hi , means (tropical:) Keep ye to the Book of God; for it is a security for you, and a covenant, against the punishment of God. (A'Obeyd, TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) An elongated, or extended, tract of sand, (T, S, M, Mgh, K,) collected together, abundant, and high: (T, TA:) or HabolN mina Alr~amoli means a long, extended, tract of sand, collected together, and elevated: (Msb:) [or simply a long, or long and elevated, tract of sand; likened to a rope, as is indicated in the Mgh:] pl. HibaAlN . (TA.) ― -b5- [(assumed tropical:) A long, creeping, or twining, stalk or shoot or branch; likened to a rope or cord: pl. HibaAlN : often occurring in descriptions of plants by AHn and others.] ― -b6- See also HabalapN . ― -b7- AlHabolu (assumed tropical:) The wariyd ; [a name applied to each of the two carotid arteries, and sometimes to each of the two external jugular veins; ] also called Habolu Alwariydi ; a vein between the windpipe and the [ two sinews called the ] EilobaAwaAni ; (Fr, TA;) a certain vein in the neck, (S,) or in the Haloq . (Msb.) ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) The EaAtiq [or part between the shoulder-joint and the neck ]: (K:) or AlHabolu , (K,) or Habolu AlEaAtiqi , (TA,) signifies the Tariyqap [app. here meaning, as it does in some other instances, oblong muscle ] that is between the neck and the head of the shoulder-blade: or a sinew between the neck and the shoulderjoint: (K:) or Habolu AlEaAtiqi signifies a bond, or ligament, between the EAtq and the neck; (T, Msb, TA;) or between the neck and the shoulderjoint: (Lth, TA:) or certain sinews. (S.) ― -b9- (assumed tropical:) A certain vein, or nerve, ( Eiroq ,) in the fore arm, (K, TA,) extending from the wrist until it becomes concealed in the shoulder-joint: (TA:) or Habolu Al*~iraAEi is [ a vein, or nerve, ] in the arm: (S:) or HibaAlu Al*~iraAEayoni signifies the sinews that appear upon the two fore arms; and in like manner, those of a horse. (TA.) One says, huwa EalaY Haboli *iraAEika , (S, TA,) a prov., (S,) meaning (tropical:) He, or it, is near to thee: (T, S, Sgh:) or within thy power, or reach; or possible, or practicable, to thee; or easy to thee. (ISd, Z, TA.) ― -b10- Also, (K,) or Habolu AlfaqaAri , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) A certain vein, or nerve, ( Eiroq ,) in the back, (K, TA,) extending from the beginning thereof to its end. (TA.) ― -b11- AlHibaAlu fiY Als~aAqi , (K,) or HibaAlu Als~aAqayoni , (M,) (assumed tropical:) The sinews of the two shanks. (M, K.) ― -b12- AlHibaAlu fiY Al*~akari , (K,) or ↓ HabaAy^ilu Al*~akari , (M,) (assumed tropical:) The veins ( Euruwq ) of the penis. (M, K.) ― -b13- AlHabolu also signifies The station of the horses collected for a race, before they are let go. (K.) [Probably it was marked by an extended rope; and for that reason was thus called.] -A2- Also Heaviness; weight, or weightiness; ponderousness; syn. viqalN . (Az, K.)

definition: A calamity, or misfortune;
sourceDefinition: A calamity, or misfortune; (S, K;) as also ↓ HabuwlN : (K:) pl. HubuwlN . (S, K.) ISd cites as an ex. the saying of El-Akhtal, wa kunotu saliyma Alqalobi Hat~aY A^aSaAbaniY mina All~aAmiEaAti AlmuboriqaAti Hubuwlu [ And I was sound of heart until calamities befell me from the resplendent females, exhibiting their beauty ]. (TA.) ― -b2- rajulN HibolN (assumed tropical:) A learned, sagacious, intelligent man. (IAar, K. *) [And HibolN also signifies (assumed tropical:) Very intelligent, or very cunning. Pl. A^aHobaAlN .] You say, A_in~ahu laHibolN mino A^aHobaAlihaA , meaning (tropical:) Verily he is one who possesses much intelligence, or much cunning: and verily he is a gentle manager of cattle. (ISd, K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: : see HabalapN . -A2- It is also an inf. n.; i. e., of Habilato . (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) -A3- And it is also a simple subst.: (K, TA: [in the CK, wAsomu jamoEK is erroneously put for wA@somN :]) [i. e.] it also signifies The fœtus in the womb: (Mgh:) pl. A^aHobaAlN . (K.) It is said in a trad., nahaY Eano Habali ↓ AlHabalapi , (S, Mgh,) or nahaY Eano bayoEi Habali AlHabalapi , (Msb, K,) i. e. He forbade the selling of the offspring of the offspring (S, Msb, K) in the belly (Msb, TA) of the she-camel &c.; (Msb;) [i. e.,] the offspring of the fœtus (A'Obeyd, S, Msb) in the belly of the she-camel [&c.]; (A'Obeyd, Msb;) [i. e.,] what the fœtus will bring forth, if it be a female; (Mgh;) the p in AlHblp being the sign of the fem. gender; (A'Obeyd, Mgh, Msb;) or a sign of intensiveness of the signification: (IAmb, TA:) for the Arabs in the Time of Ignorance used to sell the offspring of the offspring in the bellies (T, M, Msb, TA) of pregnant beasts, (T, Msb,) or of sheep or goats: (M, TA:) or the meaning is, what is in the belly of the she-camel: (A'Obeyd, Esh-Sháfi'ee, K:) or the produce of the grape-vine before it has attained to maturity: (M, K:) but Suh disapproves of this last explanation, as a mistake occasioned by the p in AlHblp . (TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) Anything that is in another thing: thus, for instance, the pearl is the Habal of the oyster-shell; and the wine is the Habal of the glass bottle. (A, TA.) -A4- (tropical:) Fulness; (ISd, K, TA; [see Habila ;]) as also ↓ HubaAlN . (IAar, K.) ― -b2- (tropical:) Anger: (K, TA:) (tropical:) anger and grief; as in the saying bihi HabalN (tropical:) In him is anger and grief: (Az, ISd, K, TA:) from the same word as meaning the “ pregnancy ” of a woman. (Az, TA.) -A5- Habalo Habalo A cry by which sheep or goats are chidden. (Sgh, K.)

definition: One who binds, ties, or makes fast, a rope, or cord.
sourceDefinition: One who binds, ties, or makes fast, a rope, or cord. (TA.) Hence, (TA,) yaA HaAbilu A@*okuro Hal~FA , a prov., (K, TA,) meaning O binder, or tyer, of the rope, bear in mind the time of untying. (TA.) ― -b2- The setter of the snare ( HabaAlap ) for game; (S, TA;) as also ↓ muHotabilN . (TA.) It is said in a prov., AixotalaTa AlHaAbilu biAln~aAbili (S) (assumed tropical:) The setter of the snare became confounded with the shooter of the arrows: (TA in art. xlT :) or, in this instance, (S,) AlHAbl signifies the warp; and AlnAbl , the woof. (S, K.) And in another prov., vaAra HaAbiluhumo EalaY naAbilihimo (assumed tropical:) They kindled mischief among themselves: (K, TA:) AlHAbl [properly] signifying the owner of the HibaAlap ; and AlnAbl , the shooter with nabol , or the owner of nabol : i. e., their case became confused: and sometimes it is applied to a party whose case has become turned from its proper state, and who become roused, or stirred up, one against another. (Az, TA.) One says also, Haw~ala HaAbilahu EalaY naAbilihi (assumed tropical:) He turned it upside down. (K.) And AijoEalo HaAbilahu naAbilahu , and HaAbilahu EalaY naAbilihi , (assumed tropical:) Turn thou it upside down. (TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) An enchanter. (Sgh, K, TA.) -A2- A [lizard of the kind called] Dab~ that feeds upon the Hubolap [q. v.]; (S, M, K;) and so a gazelle. (TA.) -A3- HaAbilapN : see HubolaY .

definition: A certain insect, resembling the flea, (S, A, K,) to which, sometimes, there grow two wings, and then it flies;
sourceDefinition: A certain insect, resembling the flea, (S, A, K,) to which, sometimes, there grow two wings, and then it flies; (S;) or, as some say, larger than the flea; (TA;) or like the tick; (A;) accord. to Lth, a certain variegated insect ( duwayob~apN mujaz~aEapN ); (TA;) the Humap [i. e. venom, or sting, ] of which is like that of the hornet; (A, K;) which sticks to men, and bites, or stings; ( talodagu ;) and to which the extremities of whips are likened; (A;) or, accord. to Az, it has no Humap when it bites; but its bite occasions much pain, [ though ] it has no venom ( sum~ ) like that of hornets: (TA:) or (K) a certain small insect, (IDrd, TA,) resembling the tick, that sticks to men: (IDrd, K, TA:) or it is smaller than the [ black beetle called ] juEal ; (ISk, TA;) or, accord. to the M, a thing like a small pebble, speckled a little with red or yellow, but its prevailing colour is black; which collects, and enters beneath men, and in their groins, or armpits, or the like, and bites them; and rends the skins in which water or milk is kept; or, as in the T, a certain small insect, (TA,) which makes holes in the skins wherein water or milk is kept, and (as Az heard the Arabs of the desert to assert, TA) enters into the pudenda of girls; (K, TA;) and is of the same kind as jiEolaAn [pl. of juEalN ], but smaller; black, speckled with white: (TA:) because of its entering into the faroj of the virgin girl, it is called EaA$iqu AlA^abokaAri : (IB, TA:) pl. HaraAqiySu . (K.) ― -b2- Also The stone of a green unripe date. (AA, K.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taHoriymN , (S, Msb, K,) said of God, (K,) and of a man, (S, Msb,) He forbade it, prohibited it, or made it unlawful, (S, Msb, K, *) Ealayohi to him; (S;) as also ↓ AHrmhu , (S, * Msb, K,) inf. n. A_iHoraAmN . (S.) The saying Aall~`hu A^akobaru at the commencement of prayer is termed takobiyrapu Alt~aHoriymi [ The tkbyrp of prohibition ], because it prohibits the person praying from saying and doing anything extraneous to prayer: and it is also termed ↓ tkbyrpu AlA_iHoraAmi , meaning the tkbyrp of entering upon a state of prohibition by prayer. (TA.) It is said in a trad., of Ibn- 'Abbás, A_i*aA Har~ama Alr~ajulu A@moraA^atahu fahiYa yamiynN yukaf~iruhaA [ When the man declares his wife to be forbidden to him, it is an oath, which he must expiate ]: for the taHoriym of a wife and of a female slave may be without the intention of divorce. (TA.) And Har~amotu AlZ~uloma EalaY nafosiY , occurring in another trad., [lit. I have forbidden myself wrongdoing, said by Mohammad,] means I am far above wrongdoing. (TA.) taHoriymN [as the inf. n. of Hur~imN ] means The being refractory, or untractable; [as though forbidden to the rider;] whence muHar~amN [q. v.] applied to a camel. (TA.) ― -b2- [Also He made, or pronounced, it, or him, sacred, or inviolable, or entitled to reverence or respect or honour; whence AlmuHar~amu applied to the Haram of Mekkeh, &c:] he, or it, made him, or it, to be reverenced, respected, or honoured. (KL.) -A2- He bound it hard; namely, a whip. (KL.) ― -b2- He tanned it incompletely [ so that it became, or remained, hard ]; namely, a hide. (KL.) -A3- See also 4, in two places.

definition: , [inf. n. A_iHoraAmN ,] He entered upon a thing [or state or time ] that caused what was before allowable, or lawful, to him to be forbidden, or unlawful. (S, * Msb. [See also 5.]) And hence, (S,...
sourceDefinition: , [inf. n. A_iHoraAmN ,] He entered upon a thing [or state or time ] that caused what was before allowable, or lawful, to him to be forbidden, or unlawful. (S, * Msb. [See also 5.]) And hence, (S, Msb,) He purposed entering upon the performance of the Haj~ or the Eumorap : (Msb:) or he (the performer of the Haj~ or the Eumorap ) entered upon acts whereby what was allowable, or lawful, to him became forbidden, or unlawful; (K, TA;) as venereal intercourse, and the anointing of oneself, and wearing sewed garments, and hunting and the like: (TA:) you say, AHrAm biAlHaj~i and biAlEumorapi , because what was allowable to the person became forbidden; as the killing of objects of the chase, and [venereal intercourse with] women. (S.) And He entered into the Haram , i. e. Mekkeh or El-Medeeneh, (K, TA,) or the sacred territory of cither of those cities: (TA:) or he entered into a sacred, or an inviolable, state; or into a state of security or safety, (S, K, TA,) being assured by a compact, or bond, that he should not be attacked [&c.]: (TA:) or it signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (S,) he entered upon a sacred month; (S, Msb, K;) and so ↓ Hr~m , (K, TA, [in the CK Harama ,]) inf. n. taHoriymN . (TA.) And He entered [as a subject] into the covenanted state of security of the government of the Khaleefeh. (TA.) 'Omar said, AlS~iyaAmu A_iHoraAmN [ Fasting is a state of prohibition ], because the faster is prohibited from doing that which would break his fast. (Sh, TA.) And Alr~ajulu yuHorimu fiY AlgaDabi , a saying of El-Hasan, means The man swears in anger, because he becomes prohibited thereby ( bihi ↓ litaHar~umihi ) [from doing, or refraining from, a thing]. (TA.) See also 2, second sentence. ― -b2- AHrAm Eanohu He refrained from it [as though he were prohibited from doing it]. (ElMufaddal, TA.) -A2- AHrmhu : see 2, first sentence. ― -b2- See also 1. -A3- Also He overcame him in contending for stakes, or wagers, in a game of hazard; (AZ, Ks, S, K;) and so ↓ Hr~mhu , (K,) inf. n. taHoriymN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: The state of being forbidden, prohibited, or unlawful: (KL:) [and of being sacred, or inviolable; sacredness, or inviolability: (see Haruma , of which it is an inf. n.:)] and the state of being revered, respected, or honoured. (KL.) See also maHoramN . ― -b2- Also, (Az, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ HurumapN , (Mgh, K,) and ↓ HuramapN , (K,) Reverence, respect, or honour; (Az, K, TK;) a subst. from AiHotiraAmN , (Mgh, Msb,) like furoqapN from AifotiraAqN ; (Msb;) and ↓ maHoramN signifies the same; but properly, a place of Huromap : (Mgh:) pl. of the first HuramaAtN and HurumaAtN and HuromaAtN , like grfAt pl. of gurofapN . (Msb) When a man has relationship [to us], and we regard him with bashfulness, we say, lahu HuromapN [ Reverence, &c., is due to him; or is rendered to him ]. (Az, TA.) And we say, lilomusolimi EalaY Almusolimi HuromapN [ Reverence, &c., to the Muslim is incumbent on the Muslim ]. (Az, TA.) ― -b3- Also A thing that should be sacred, or inviolable; (S, Msb, K;) and so ↓ maHoramapN and ↓ maHorumapN (S, Msb) and ↓ maHoramN : (Msb:) as, for instance, a man's honour, or reputation: (TK:) a thing which one is under an obligation to reverence, respect, or honour [ and defend ]: (Jel in ii. 190:) a thing of which one is under an obligation to be mindful, observant, or regardful: (Bd ibid.:) [ everything that is entitled to reverence, respect, honour, or defence, in the character and appertenances of a person: a thing that one is bound to do, or from which one is bound to refrain, from a motive of reverence, respect, or honour: (see the next sentence:) and any attribute that renders the subject thereof entitled to reverence, respect, or honour: ] the pl. of HuromapN is HurumaAtN (Bd and Jel ubi suprà, and TA) [and HuramaAtN and HuromaAtN , as above,] and HuramN ; (Msb;) and that of ↓ maHoramN [and ↓ maHoramapN and ↓ maHorumapN ] is maHaArimu ; (Msb;) and maHoramaAtN and maHorumaAtN [also] are pls. of ↓ maHoramapN and ↓ maHorumapN . (As, S.) HurumaAtu A@ll~`hi means [ The inviolable ordinances and prohibitions of God: or] the ordinances of God, and other inviolable things: (Bd and Jel * in xxii. 31:) or what it is incumbent on one to perform, and unlawful to neglect: (Zj, K:) or all the requisitions of God relating to the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage and to other things: (Ksh in xxii. 31:) or the Haram [or sacred territory ] and the requisitions relating to the pilgrimage: (Bd ubi suprà:) or the requisitions relating to the pilgrimage in particular: (Ksh ubi suprà:) or the Kaabeh and the sacred mosque and the sacred territory and the sacred month and the person who is in the state of A_iHoraAm : (Ksh and Bd ibid.:) or the inviolability ( Huromap ) of the sacred territory and of the state of A_iHoraAm and of the sacred month: (TA:) or Mekkeh and the pilgrimage and the Eumorap , and all the acts of disobedience to God which He has forbidden: (Mujáhid, TA:) or [simply] the acts of disobedience to God. ('Atà, TA.) ― -b4- And [hence, because it should be regarded as sacred, or inviolable,] i. q. *im~apN [ A compact, a covenant, or an obligation; and particularly such as renders one responsible for the safety, or safe-keeping, of a person or thing, or for the restoration of a thing, or for the payment of a sum of money, &c.; or by which one becomes in a state of security or safety: and simply responsibility, or suretiship: and security, or safety; security of life and property; protection, or safeguard; a promise, or an assurance, of security, safety, protection, or safeguard; indemnity; or quarter: or an obligation, a duty, or a right, or due, that should be regarded as sacred, or inviolable, or the nonobservance of which is blameable ]. sourceDefinition: (K) and ↓ HaramapN (Lh, S, K) The desire of a female cloven-hoofed animal, (K,) or of a ewe, or she-goat, (S,) and of a she-wolf and of a bitch, (K,) for the male: (S, K:) HaramapN in ewes, or she-goats, is like DabaEapN in she-camels, and HinaA='N in ewes. (S.) It is also used, in a trad., in relation to male human beings. (K.) It is said in a trad., respecting those whom the hour [of the resurrection] shall overtake, tuboEavu Ealayohimu AlHiromapu wa yusolabuwna AlHayaA='a , i. e. Venereal desire [ shall be made to befall them, and they shall be bereft of shame ]. (S.)

definition: , applied to a man, Of, or belonging to, the Haram : fem.
sourceDefinition: , applied to a man, Of, or belonging to, the Haram : fem. Hiromiy~apN . (S, Msb, TA.) [In the TA it is said that Mbr mentions two forms of the epithet Hrmy~p as applied to a woman: it does not specify what these are; but one seems to be Huromiy~apN , for he says that it is from the phrase wa Huromapi Albayoti “ by the sacredness of the House ” of God.] Az says, on the authority of Lth, that when they applied the rel. n. from AlHaramu to anything not a human being, [as, for instance, to a garment, or piece of cloth,] they said ↓ vawobN HaramiY~N : (Msb:) [but] they also said Hiromiy~apN , (S,) or sihaAmN Hiromiy~apN , (Msb,) meaning Arrows of the Haram : (S, Msb:) and Hiromiy~apN [also, or qawosN Hiromiy~apN ,] meaning A bow made of a tree of the Haram . (Ham p. 284.) ― -b2- Also A man of the Haram whose food was eaten by a pilgrim, and in whose clothes this pilgrim performed his circuiting round the Kaábeh: and a pilgrim who ate the food of a man of the Haram , and performed his circuiting round the Kaábeh in this man's clothes: each of these was called the HiromiY~ of the other: every one of the chiefs of the Arabs who imposed upon himself hardship, or strictness, in his religious practices had a HrmY~ of the tribe of Kureysh; and when he performed the pilgrimage, would not eat any food but that of this man, nor perform his circuiting round the Kaabeh except in this man's clothes. (TA.)

[of HaraAmN , agreeably with analogy,] is HurumN ; (K;) and ↓ maHaArimu also is a pl. of HaraAmN , contr. to rule, (TA,) and signifies things forbidden by God. (K.) See also HiromN . ― -b2- HaraAma A@ll~`hi laA A^afoEalu , (as in some copies of the S,) or HaraAmu All~`h lA AfEl , (as in other copies of the S and in the K,) is a saying like yamiyna A@ll~`hi laA A^afoEalu , or yamiynu All~`h lA AfEl : (S, K:) it may mean a declaration that the wife or the female slave shall be forbidden [to him who utters it], without the intention of divorcing [thereby the former, or of emancipating the latter; so that it may be rendered, according to the two different readings, I imprecate upon myself, or that which I imprecate upon myself is, what is forbidden of God, if I do it: I will not do such a thing: in like manner, EalaY~a AlHaraAmu is often said in the present day]. (TA. [See 2.]) ― -b3- [ Aibonu HaraAmK An illegitimate son: and a disingenuous, or dishonest, person. ] ― -b4- $ahorN HaraAmN [ A sacred month ]: (Msb:) pl. HurumN . (S, Msb, K.) AlA^a$ohuru AlHurumu [ The sacred months ] (S, * Msb, K) were four; namely, *uw AlqaEodapi and *uw AlHij~api and AlmuHar~amu and rajabN ; (S, Msb, K;) three consecutive, and one separate: (S, Msb:) in these the Arabs held fight to be unlawful; except two tribes, Khath'am and Teiyi; unless with those who held these months as profane. (S, TA.) ― -b5- HaraAmN applied to a man signifies Entering into the Haram [or sacred territory of Mekkeh or of El-Medeeneh, or Mekkeh or El- Medeeneh itself]; and is applied also to a woman; and to a pl. number: (TA:) or i. q. ↓ muHorimN (S, Msb) as meaning [ in, or entering upon, the state of A_iHoraAm : i. e. entering upon the performance of those acts of the Haj~ , or of the Eumorap , whereby certain things before allowable, or lawful, to him became forbidden, or unlawful; (see 4;) or] purposing to enter upon the performance of the Haj~ or the Eumorap : (Msb:) as also ↓ HiromN : you say, A^anota Hil~N and Ant HiromN [ Thou art one who has quitted his state of A_iHoraAm and thou art in, or entering upon, the state of AHrAm ]: (TA:) the pl. of HaraAmN thus applied is HurumN : (S, Msb:) the fem. of ↓ muHorimN is with p ; and the pl. masc. muHorimuwna ; and the pl. fem. muHorimaAtN . (Msb.) ― -b6- See another meaning voce HiromN .
