definition: ― -b2- [Hence,] The appertenances, or conveniences, ( Huquwq and maraAfiq S, Msb, K,) that are in the immediate environs, (S, Msb,) of a thing, (Msb,) or of a well &c.
sourceDefinition: : see HaraAmN . ― -b2- [Hence,] The appertenances, or conveniences, ( Huquwq and maraAfiq S, Msb, K,) that are in the immediate environs, (S, Msb,) of a thing, (Msb,) or of a well &c., (S,) or that are adjuncts [or within the precincts ] of a house; (K;) because it is forbidden to any but the owner to appropriate to himself the use thereof: (Msb:) or, of a well, the place where is thrown the earth that has been dug out, (K, TA,) and the walking place on either side; in the case of a well dug in a waste land that has no owner, said in a trad. to be forty cubits: (TA: [but see badiYo'N :]) and of a river, or rivulet, or canal, the place where the mud is thrown out, and the walking-place on each side: (TA:) and of a house, the interior part upon which the door is closed: (Ibn-Wásil ElKilábee, TA:) or the interior part, or middle, ( qaSabap ,) thereof: (T, TA:) [and particularly the women's apartments, and the portion that is for bidden to men who are not related to the women within the prohibited degrees of marriage: ] and the court of a mosque: (T, TA:) [and in general,] a place which it is incumbent on one to defend [ from intrusion ]: (Ham p. 492:) a thing that one protects, and in defence of which one fights; [and particularly, like HuromapN as used by the vulgar, a man's wife; and also his female slave; or any woman under covert; and, like HuramN , pl. of HuromapN , as used in the classical language, his wives, or women under covert, and household; ] as also ↓ HaramN : pl. HurumN , (K,) the pl. of HariymN ; (TA;) and A^aHoraAmN , (K,) which is the pl. of ↓ HaramN . (TA.) ― -b3- A partner, copartner, or sharer. (K.) ― -b4- A friend: so in the saying, fulaAnN HariymN SariyHN Such a one is a genuine, or sincere, friend. (TA.) ― -b5- The garment of the muHorim (S, K,) [ which he wears during the performance of the Haj~ or the Eumorap ;] called by the vulgar ↓ A_iHoraAmN and ↓ HiraAmN (TA.) ― -b6- The clothes which the muHorimuwn used to cast off, (S, * K, TA,) when, in the time of paganism, they performed the pilgrimage to the House [ of God, at Mekkeh ], namely, those that were upon them when they entered the Haram [or sacred terri tory, ] (TA,) and which they did not wear (K, TA) as long as they remained in the Haram : (TA:) for the Arabs used to perform their circuiting round the House naked, with their clothes thrown down before them during the circuiting; (T, S, TA;) they saying, “ We will not perform the circuiting round the House in clothes in which we have committed sins, or crimes: ” and the woman, also, used to perform the circuiting naked, except that she wore a rahoT of thongs. (TA.) A poet says, kafaY HazanFA mar~iY Ealayohi kaA^an~ahu laqFY bayona A^ayodiY AlT~aAy^ifiyna Hariymu [ Sufficiently grievous is my passing by him as though he were a thing thrown away, a cast-off garment of a muHorim , before those performing the circuiting round the Kaabeh]. (S.

definition: of muHil~N : and as such signifying [also] one with whom it is unlawful to fight: (S:) or, as such, whom it is unlawful to slay: (TA in art.
sourceDefinition: : see HaraAmN , in two places: Contr. of muHil~N : and as such signifying [also] one with whom it is unlawful to fight: (S:) or, as such, whom it is unlawful to slay: (TA in art. Hl :) and, as such also, one who has a claim, or covenanted right, to protection, or safeguard. (S in art. Hl .) Er-Rá'ee says, qataluwA A@boni Eaf~aAna Alxaliyfapa muHorimFA (S,) meaning [ They slew ('Othmán) Ibn-' Affán, the Khaleefeh, ] while entitled to the respect due to the office of Imám and to the [ sacred ] city and to the [ sacred ] month: for he was slain [in ElMedeeneh and] in [the month of] Dhu-l-Hijjeh. (Ham p. 310.) And one says, A_in~ahu lamuHorimu Eanoka Verily he is one whom it is unlawful for thee to harm: (K:) or for whom it is unlawful to harm thee: (IAar, Th:) or whom it is unlawful for thee to harm and for whom it is unlawful to harm thee. (Az, TA.) And musolimN muHorimN A Muslim is secure, as to himself and his property, by the respect that is due to El-Islám: or a Muslim refrains from the property of a Muslim, and his honour, or reputation, and his blood. (TA.) ― -b2- One who is at peace with another. (IAar, K.) ― -b3- One who is in the Hariym of another. (K.) You say, huwa muHorimN binaA He is in our Hariym . (TA.) ― -b4- Fasting, or a faster: because the faster is prohibited from doing that which would break his fast. (TA.) ― -b5- And, for a like reason, Swear ing, or a swearer. (TA.)

definition: [ Forbidden, prohibited, or made un lawful: and made, or pronounced, sacred, or in violable, or entitled to reverence or respect or honour ].
sourceDefinition: [ Forbidden, prohibited, or made un lawful: and made, or pronounced, sacred, or in violable, or entitled to reverence or respect or honour ]. It is said in a trad., A^amaA Ealimota A^an~a AlS~uwrapa muHar~amapu , i. e. [ Knowest thou not that the face is ] forbidden to be beaten? or that it has a title to reverence or respect or honour? (TA.) ― -b2- AlmuHar~amu The first of the months (S, Msb, K, * TA) of the year (Msb) of the Arabs [ since the age of pagan ism ]; (TA;) the article Al being prefixed because it is originally an epithet; but accord. to some, it is not prefixed to the name of any other month; or, accord. to some, it may be prefixed to Sfr and $w~Al : (Msb:) and [ in the age of paganism, the seventh month, also called ] $ahoru A@ll~`hi AlA^aSab~u (K, TA.) [ AlASb~ being app. a dial. var. of AlA^aSam~u ,] i. e. rajabN ; [for] Az says, the Arabs used to call the month of rajab in the age of paganism, AlA^aSam~u and AlmuHar~amu ; and he cites the saying of a poet, A^aqamonaA bihaA $ahoraYo rabiyEK kilaAhumaA wa$ahoraYo jumaAdaY waA@sotaHal~uwA AlmuHar~amaA [ We stayed in it during the two months of Rabeea, both of them, and the two months of Jumádà; and they made El-Moharram to be profane; app. by postponing it, as the pagan Arabs often did]: the Arabs called it thus because they did not allow fighting in it [unless they had postponed it]: (TA:) the pl. is muHar~amaAtN (Msb, K) and maHaArimu and maHaAriymu . (K.) ― -b3- See also HaramN — muHar~amN applied to a camel means Refractory, or untractable: (TA:) [or,] thus applied, [like EaruwDN , q. v.,] submissive in the middle part, [but] difficult to be turned about, [i. e. stubborn in the head, ] when turned about: (K: [in the CK, Al*~aluwlu AlwasaTu is erroneously put for Al*~aluwlu AlwasaTi : in my MS. copy of the K, Al*~aluwlu AlwasT :]) and with p a she-camel not broken, or not trained: (TA:) or not yet completely broken or trained: (S, TA:) and muHar~amapu AlZ~ahori a she-camel that is refractory, or untractable; not broken, or not trained: in this sense heard by Az from the Arabs. (TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) A skin not tanned: (K:) or not completely tanned: (S:) or tanned, but not made soft, and not thoroughly done. (TA.) ― -b5- (tropical:) A new whip: (K:) or a whip not yet made soft. (S, A, TA.) ― -b6- (tropical:) An Arab of the desert rude in nature or disposition, chaste in speech, that has not mixed with people of the towns or villages. (TA.) ― -b7- (assumed tropical:) The part of the nose that is soft in the hand. (K.)

definition: Denied, or refused, a gift: (Msb, * TA:) or denied, or refused, good, or prosperity: (Az, K:) in the Kur lxx.
sourceDefinition: Denied, or refused, a gift: (Msb, * TA:) or denied, or refused, good, or prosperity: (Az, K:) in the Kur lxx. 25, (I' Ab, S,) [it has this latter, or a similar, meaning;] i. q. muHaArafN [q. v.]; (I' Ab, S, K;) who hardly, or never, earns, or gains, anything: (K:) or who does not beg, and is therefore thought to be in no need, and is denied: (Bd:) and who has no increase of his cattle or other property: (K:) opposed to mazoruwqN : (Az, TA:) accord. to some, who has not the faculty of speech, like the dog and the cat &c. (Har p. 378.) ― -b2- Held in reverence, respect, or honour; reverenced, respected, or honoured; and so ↓ muHotaramN . (KL. [But the latter only is commonly known in this sense.])

definition: He cast, or threw;
sourceDefinition: He cast, or threw; syn. ramaY [and, like this, trans. by means of bi ]. (K.) [Hence,] HaTaA^a bihi AlA^aroDa , (AZ, S, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. HaTo'N , (S,) He cast him, or threw him, down prostrate upon the ground: (AZ, S, K:) or, with violence: one says, AiHotamalahu faHaTaA^a bihi AlA^aroDa [ He raised him upon his back, and threw him down violently upon the ground ]. (Lth, TA.) And HaTaA^ato biwaladihaA She (a woman) cast forth her child from her womb. (TA in art. zkb .) And HaTaA^ati Alqidoru bizabadihaA The cooking-pot cast forth its froth, or scum, (S, TA,) in boiling. (TA.) And HaTaA^a bisaloHihi He cast forth his excrement, or ordure. (S.) And HaTaA^a [alone], aor. and , He cast forth his excrement, or ordure, at once, (K, TA,) quietly, or gently. (TA.) And HaTaA^a , (K,) or HaTaA^a bihaA , (S,) He broke wind, with a sound. (S, K.) ― -b2- HaTaA^a bihi Eano raA^oyihi He turned him back from the opinion, or judgment, that he had formed. (IAth, K.) ― -b3- HaTaA^ahu He struck him, or slapped him, on the back with his open hand: (S, K:) or struck him gently on the back with the palm of his hand: (S in art. lTH :) or slapped him on the back, or between the shoulders, or on the upper part of the side, or on the chest; (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, TA;) or on the back of the head: (AZ, TA:) and he struck him, or beat him, (Sh, K, *) with his hand; (Sh, TA;) but it is said that the meaning is, he struck him on the back of the neck: (TA:) it also occurs without ' . (TA.) ― -b4- HaTaA^ahaA He lay with her. (S, K. *)

sourceDefinition: (S, K) and HifovN and ↓ HafivapN (K) [ A certain portion or appertenance ] of the stomach of a ruminant animal, that which has TaraAy^iq [meaning either furrows or streaks, but more probably the former], as though it, or they, ( kaA^an~ahaA ,) were the coverings ( A^aTobaAq ) of the feces in the stomach: (Az, L:) or that [ part ] which has coverings ( A^aTobaAq [or probably this signifies here folds, one above another, ]) at the lower part of the stomach of a ruminant, towards the side of the latter, from which the feces of the stomach never pass forth: [app. meaning the third stomach, or omasum; commonly called the manyplies, because of its many plies, or folds, and strata super strata; and by some, the millet; from which the food, being already ruminated, does not pass out again to the mouth, as it does from the first and second stomachs:] it pertains to the camel, and to the sheep and goat, and oxen; or, accord. to IAar, [only] to the sheep and goat: (L:) the Hafv of the stomach of a ruminant; (S;) i. q. qibapN , (S, K,) or qibapN : (TA:) or that which is with the stomach of a ruminant, and which resembles it: (T, TA:) or that which has TaraAy^iq , by the side of which is the qbp , another thing, which has not TrAy^q : it is called HafivN and HavifN and HifovN and HivofN and faHivN and, as some say, fivoHN and viHofN : (AA, TA:) pl. A^aHofaAvN . (K.) ― -b2- Also the first, A certain great kind of serpent, resembling a jiraAb [or traveller's provision-bag ]. (K.)

definition: A certain kind of serpent, that blows, but does not hurt: (S:) a kind of serpent larger than that called HafivN , (K, TA,) speckled with black and white, party-coloured;
sourceDefinition: A certain kind of serpent, that blows, but does not hurt: (S:) a kind of serpent larger than that called HafivN , (K, TA,) speckled with black and white, party-coloured; that eats herbs, or dry pasture, and threatens, but does not hurt any one: (TA:) or, accord. to Sh, a bulky serpent, with a large head, red, speckled with white and black, resembling that called AlA^asowadu , but not the same as this latter; if one irritate it, its jugular vein becomes distended: accord. to ISh, it is larger than that called AlA^aroqamu , but is speckled with black and white in the same manner as this latter: pl. HafaAfiyvu . (Az, TA.) [Hence,] AiHoranofa$a Huf~aAvuhu (tropical:) His external jugular veins ( A^awodaAjuhu [likened to serpents]) became distended by rage, or anger. (TA.)

Hano*N (S, L, K, &c.) and taHonaA*N , [which latter is an intensive form,] He roasted a kid, &c.: (M, L:) or he roasted flesh-meat with heated stones, (T, A, L,) [ in a hole dug in the ground, (see Haniy*N ,)] in order to cook it thoroughly: (A:) or he roasted a sheep or goat, and put upon it heated stones to cook it thoroughly: (S, L, K:) or he roasted flesh-meat by covering it over in fire, or burying it therein: (AZ, L:) or he roasted it so that it dripped: (M:) or he roasted it without overdoing it [ so that the moisture dripped from it ]: or he scalded a kid &c., so as to remove its hair. (L.) [See also Haniy*N ; and see 4.] ― -b2- Hana*atohu Al$~amosa , (A, L, K,) aor. , inf. n. Hano*N , (L,) (tropical:) The sun burned him, (A, L, K,) namely, a traveller, and pained his brain. (T, L.) To a horse to which this is done you apply the epithets ↓ Haniy*N and ↓ maHonuw*N . (S, A, L, K.) If the horse do not sweat, you say of him, kabaA . (S, L.) ― -b4- Hana*a lahu : see 4.

definition: He turned aside from the place of the rain of the lightning, whichever way it turned.
sourceDefinition: He turned aside from the place of the rain of the lightning, whichever way it turned. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) HaAwa$ahu , (A,) inf. n. muHaAwa$apN , (TA,) He circumvented him: or he endeavoured to induce him to turn, or incline, or decline; or endeavoured to turn him by deceit, or guile: syn. daAwarahu : (A, TA: *) in war, and in litigation or contention [&c.]. (TA.) You say, Zalitu A^uHaAwi$uhu waA^uHaAwituhu Hat~aY faEala [ I continued during the day to circumvent him, or to endeavour to induce him to turn, &c., and to delude him, or act towards him with artifice, like a fish in the water, until he did what I desired: see also what next follows]. (A.) ― -b3- [And hence,] HaAwa$otuhu Ealayohi I excited, incited, urged, or instigated, him to do it. (Ibn-'Abbád, A, * Sgh, K.) (S, A.) ― -b3- Applied to a camel, or other [animal], Wild: (K:) [or] the epithet thus applied is tropical; (A, TA;) and what are thus called, (K,) or AlA_ibilu AlHuw$iy~apu [ the camels termed Hw$y~p ], (S, A, Msb,) are so named from ↓ AlHuw$u , the appellation of certain stallions of the camels of the jinn, or genii, which covered some of the she-camels of Arabs, (IKt, S, A, Msb, K,) as they assert, (S, K,) namely, of the she-camels of Mahrah, (K,) meaning the Benoo-Mahrah-Ibn-Heydán, (TA,) and the offspring were the camels called Aln~ajaAy^ibu Almahoriy~apu , (Msb, TA,) which scarcely ever become tired; and the like of this is said by AHeyth: (TA:) it is also said that ↓ AlHuw$u , (S, K,) from which the epithet above mentioned, thus applied, is a rel. n., (TA,) is the country of the jinn, (S, K,) beyond the sands of Yebreen, which no man inhabits: (S:) or an appellation of certain sons of the jinn, whose country is called bilaAdu AlHuw$i by Ru-beh: (TA:) or it is like AlwaHo$ : (Msb:) or A_ibilN Huw$iy~apN means camels of the jinn: or wild camels; (TA;) as also ↓ Huw$N : (S:) or camels not completely broken or trained, because of their unyielding spirit. (S, * A, K, * TA. *) ― -b5- You say also, kalaAmN Huw$iY~N (tropical:) Strange, uncouth, unusual, extraordinary, or unfamiliar, speech; such as is difficult to be understood; (Msb, K, TA;) i. q. waHo$iY~N ; (S, A;) [opposed to faSiyHN :] and in like manner, lafoZapN Huw$iy~apN a word, or phrase, that is strange, uncouth, unusual, &c.; as also lafoZapN waHo$iy~apN , and gariybapN , and $aAridapN ; all opposed to lafoZapN faSiyHapN . (Mz, 13th nwE .) ― -b6- And layolN Huw$iY~N (tropical:) A night that is dark (A, K) and terrible. (A, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (A, L, K,) sec. pers. xabibota , like Ealimota , aor. yaxab~u , inf. n. xib~N ; (S, L, K; *) or xab~a , [sec. pers. xababota ,] aor. yaxub~u , like yaqotulu , inf. n. xab~N ; (Msb; [in which xib~N is regarded as a simple subst.; but I doubt the correctness of this, and of the verb's being like qatala ;]) He (a man) was, or became, deceitful, (Msb, K, TA,) wicked, dishonest, or dissimulating, (K, TA,) and a mischief-maker: (TA:) [or] he was, or became, a great deceiver, or very deceitful, (S, A, L, K, TA,) wicked and deceitful, and a mischief-maker. (S, * A, * L, TA.) [In the K and TA, neither the aor. nor the inf. n. of xab~a as signifying “ he was, or became, a great deceiver, or very deceitful, ” is specified; nor the sec. pers. of the pret., which indicates the form of the aor.] ― -b2- [Hence, app.,] xab~a signifies also He alighted and abode in a depressed tract of ground, in order that his place might be unknown, from a motive of niggardliness [ to avoid claims upon his hospitality, thus deceiving passers by ]. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And He denied, or refused, what he possessed. (K.) -A2- xab~a , (S, A, K,) aor. yuxub~u , with damm, (S, A,) deviating from a general rule, accord. to which an intrans. v. of this class [of the measure faEala ] should be with kesr, (MF,) inf. n. xab~N (S, K) and xababN and xabiybN , (S, A, K,) He went the pace, or in the manner, denoted by xababN as explained below; said of a horse; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ Axtb~ : (Th, K:) and in like manner said of a man. (TA.) You say, jaAw^uwA taxub~u bihimu Ald~awaAb~u [ They came, the beasts going with them the pace, or in the manner, termed xababN ]. (A.) And xab~a fiY AlA^amori , aor. , inf. n. xababN , He hastened to begin the affair. (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xab~a , (aor. yaxub~u , TA, [inf. n. xab~N ,]) said of the sea, (tropical:) It was, or became, agitated, or in a state of commotion; (T, S, A, K, TA;) the waves dashing together, and the winds whirling; (T, A, TA;) such being the case at a certain period, when the ships make for the shore, for safety, or cast anchor. (T, TA.) definition: The nose, (AZ, JK, S, Msb, K,) [properly,] accord.
sourceDefinition: The nose, (AZ, JK, S, Msb, K,) [properly,] accord. to Th, of a beast of prey: (TA:) or the fore part thereof: (K:) or a large, or an elevated, nose: (MA:) or the part upon which a man contracts, or closes, the HanakaAni [or upper and lower portions of the mouth ]: as also ↓ xuroTumN ; (K;) sometimes, by poetic license, written ↓ xuroTum~N : (TA:) or it signifies also the part upon which contracts, or closes, the front of the HanakaAni : (JK:) [and a snout: often used in this sense; and so, in describing the fish termed kawosaj , in the S and K:] and the proboscis of an elephant; and, as being likened thereto, of a flea: (Th, TA:) pl. xaraATiymu . (Msb.) sanasimuhu EalaY AlxuroTuwmi , in the Kur [lxviii. 16], means (tropical:) [ We will brand him ] upon the nose; the nose of a man being thus termed metaphorically: (ISd, TA:) or it is like the phrase jadaEotu A^anofahu ; and means (assumed tropical:) we will stigmatize him with indelible disgrace; the term xrTwm , which signifies the “ proboscis ” of an elephant, being applied to his nose because it is regarded as unseemly: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or it means (assumed tropical:) [ we will brand him ] upon the face. (Fr, Th, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, (assumed tropical:) A spout. You say] AlAboriyqu AnaA='N lahu xuroTuwmN (assumed tropical:) [ The Abryq is a vessel having a spout ]. (Mgh in art. brq , and Bd and Jel in lvi. 18.) ― -b3- [Hence also, (assumed tropical:) The pointed toe of a boot and the like: pl. as above: see xifaAfN muxaroTayapN , below. ― -b4- And app. (assumed tropical:) The point of a sword: whence,] *uw AlxuroTuwmi the name of a certain sword. (K.)] ― -b5- [Hence, also,] xaraATiymu Alqawomi (tropical:) The chiefs of the people or party; (JK, S, K, TA;) those who are made the foremost of the people or party, in affairs, (JK, TA,) and in the military forces. (JK.) -A2- Also Wine: (JK, S:) or wine that quickly intoxicates: (K:) and the juice that first flows from the grapes, before they are trodden. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaxo$aY , inf. n. xa$oyapN (JK, S, M, Msb, K) and xa$oYN (JK, M, K) and xi$oYN (Sgh, K) [the second and third erroneously written in the CK xa$FA and (by indication) xi$FA ] and xa$aApN (M, K) and xa$oyaAnN , (JK, M, K,) though it has been said that the only instances of this kind are $anoA=nN and lay~aAnN , [see the former of these two,] but in one copy of the M found written xi$oyaAnN , (TA,) and maxo$aApN (JK, M, K) and maxo$iyapN , (M, K,) He feared; syn. xaAfa : (JK, S, M, Msb, K:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib and others, he dreaded; or feared with reverence, veneration, respect, honour, or awe. (TA.) You say, xa$iyahu He feared him, or it; [or he dreaded him, or it; i. e. feared him, or it, with reverence, &c.;] as also ↓ tx$~Ahu . (K.) [And xa$iYa minohu , meaning the same: or He feared, or dreaded, what might happen to him from him, or it. And xa$iYa Ealayohi $ayoy^FA He feared, or dreaded, for him a thing. ] And faEalotu *`lika xa$aApa A^ano yakuwna ka*aA [ I did that in fear, or dread, that such a thing might happen ]. (IAar, TA.) ― -b2- xa$ayotuhu also signifies Hope. (Er-Rághib, TA.) And the saying of Ibn-'Abbás to 'Omar, laqado A^akovarota mina Ald~uEaA='i biAlmawoti Hat~aY xa$iytu A^ano yakuwna *`lika A^asohala laka Einoda nuzuwlihi , is explained as meaning [ Verily thou hast prayed much for death, so that ] I hope [that it may be easier to thee when it happens]. (TA.) ― -b3- And sometimes xa$iytu means Ealimotu [ I knew, or know ]. (Msb.) So it is said to mean in the saying of the poet. walaqado xa$iytu biA^a mano tabiEa AlhudaY skana AljinaAna maEa Aln~abiY~i muHam~adi [ And I know assuredly that he who follows the right direction shall dwell in the gardens of Paradise with the Prophet Mohammad ]: (S, TA:) or the meaning may be, I hope. (TA.) ― -b4- In the saying in the Kur [xviii. 79], faxa$iynaA A^ano yurohiqahumaA TugoyaAnFA wakuforFA , the meaning is said, by Akh, to be And we disapproved [that he should make excessive disobedience, and ingratitude, to come upon them twain]; (S;) and so says Zj, explaining it as the saying of El-Khidr: or, accord. to Fr, the meaning is, and we knew. (TA. [See also A^azohaqa .]) -A2- xaA$aAniY faxa$ayotuhu : see 3.

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. xaT~N , He made [ a line, or lines, or] a mark, EalaY AlA^aroDi , upon the ground. (Msb.) You say, xaT~a Alz~aAjiru fiY AlA^aroDi , aor. and inf. n. as above, The diviner made a line, or a mark, or lines, or marks, upon the ground, and then divined. (TA.) And Alz~aAjiru yaxuT~u biA_iSobaEihi fiY Alr~amoli wayazojuru [ The diviner makes lines, or marks, with his finger upon the sand, and divines ]. (S.) Th says, on the authority of IAar, that Eilomu AlxaT~i is Eilomu Alr~amoli [or geomancy ]: I 'Ab says that it is an ancient science, which men have relinquished: but Lth says that it is practised to the present time; [to which I may add, that it has not even now ceased; being still practised on sand and the like, and also on paper;] and they have conventional terms which they employ in it, and they elicit thereby the secret thoughts &c., and often hit upon the right therein: the diviner comes to a piece of soft ground, and he has a boy, with whom is a style; and the master makes many lines, or marks, in haste, that they may not be counted; then he returns, and obliterates leisurely lines, or marks, two by two; and if there remain two lines, or marks, they are a sign of success, and of the attainment of the thing wanted: while he obliterates, his boy says, for the sake of auguring well, AibonaYo EiyaAno A^asoriEaA AlbayaAno [ O two sons of 'Iyán (meaning two lines or marks), hasten ye the manifestation ]: I 'Ab says that when he has obliterated the lines, or marks, and one remains, it is the sign of disappointment: and AZ and Lth relate the like of this. (TA.) It is said in a trad. of Mo'áwiyeh Ibn-El-Hakam Es-Sulamee, traced up by him to its author, kaAna nabiY~N mina AlA^anobiyaA='i yaxuT~u famano xaT~ahu Ealima mivola Eilomihi [ A prophet of the prophets used to practise geomancy; and he who matches his geomancy knows the like of his knowledge ]. (TA.) You say also, when a man is meditating upon his affair, and considering what may be its issue, or result, fulaAnN yaxuT~u fiY AlA^aroDi (tropical:) [ Such a one makes lines, or marks, upon the ground ]. (TA.) [See also nakata : and see St. John's Gospel, ch. viii. verses 6 and 8.] And xaT~a birijolihi AlA^aroDa means (tropical:) He walked, or went along. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, (S, Msb,) aor. as above, (Msb,) and so the inf. n., (Msb, K,) He wrote (S, Msb, K) a writing, or book, (Msb,) or a thing, (TA,) with the reed prepared for that purpose, (S, K,) or with some other thing; (K, TA;) [and so ↓ xT~T , for] taxoTiyTN is syn. with tasoTiyrN , or, as in the T, like tsTyr ; whence the saying, xuT~iTato Ealayohi *unuwbuhu His sins were written [or registered ] against him. (TA.) ― -b3- xaT~a AlxiT~apa , and xaT~ahaA linafosihi : see 8; for the latter, in two places. ― -b4- [Hence,] xaT~a Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) He prohibited it; or took it for himself; relating to anything. (K, TA.) ― -b5- xuT~u waHohuhu : or xaT~a : see 8. ― -b6- xaT~a AlgulaAmu : see 8. ― -b7- xaTaTotu biAls~ayofi wajohahu wawasaTahu (tropical:) [ I cut, or clave, with the sword his face and his waist ]. (TA.) And xaT~ahu biAls~ayofi niSofayoni (tropical:) [ He clave him, or it, in halves with the sword ]. (TA.) And jaAraAhu famaA xaT~a gubaArahu (tropical:) He contended with him in running, and did not cleave his dust. (JK, S, * A, L.) ― -b8- xaT~a A@ll~`hu nawo'ahaA [ God made its (a land's) rain-giving star or asterism (see nawo'N ) to pass it over: or may God make &c.]: from xaTiyTapN signifying “ a land not rained upon between two lands that have been rained upon: ” (S, TA: *) it was said by I' Ab [in a tropical sense, by way of imprecation, with reference to a woman], when he was asked respecting a man who had put the affair of his wife in her own hand and she had in consequence divorced him by a triple sentence: (S:) accord. to one relation, it is xaT~aA^a ; the meaning being “ may he make its rain to miss it: ” (S, TA:) and accord. to another, ↓ xaT~aY , originally xaT~aTa , like taqaD~aY AlbaAziY : the former, or first, is the weaker, or weakest, in authority, of these relations. (TA. [See also 2 in art. xTA^ .])

definition: A line, streak, or stripe;
sourceDefinition: A line, streak, or stripe; in, or upon, a thing: (K:) pl. xuTuwTN (S, K) and A^axoTaATN ; (K;) the latter, [a pl. of pauc.,] used by El-'Ajjáj: (TA:) and ↓ xuT~apN is [syn. with xaT~N as explained above, being] a subst. form [the inf. n.] AlxaT~u , like as nuqoTapN is from Aln~aqoTu : (S, K: *) you say, ↓ EalaY Zahori AlHimaAri xuT~ataAni Upon the back of the ass are two lines, or streaks, differing in colour from the rest of the body. (TA.) ― -b2- [In mathematics, A line. And hence, xaT~u AlAisotiwaA='i The equinoctial line. ] ― -b3- A slight track, or path, or road, in plain, or smooth, or soft, ground: pl. as above. (K.) And A road, or path: (Th, K:) as in the saying, Ailozamo *`lika AlxaT~a walaA taZolimo minohu $ayoy^FA [ Keep thou to that road, or path, and do not deviate from it at all ]: or in this sense the word is ↓ xuT~N . (TA.) Also A road, or way, or street, that is a common thoroughfare; and so ↓ xuT~N . (IDrd, K.) ― -b4- (tropical:) [ A streak, or stripe, of herbage. ] You say, AlkalaA^u xuTuwTN fiY AlA^aroDi (tropical:) The herbage consists of streaks, or stripes, upon the ground; the rain not having watered the country in common. (L, TA.) ― -b5- Writing, and the like. (TA.) [ Handwriting. Character; or particular form of letters. ― -b6- See also 1.]

definition: ― -b2- Also An affair: a matter: a case: an event: a state, or condition: syn.
sourceDefinition: : see xaT~N , in two places. ― -b2- Also An affair: a matter: a case: an event: a state, or condition: syn. A^amorN : (S, K:) and qiS~apN : (S:) or the like of qiS~apN : (JK, K:) and xaTobN : and HaAlN : (TA:) or HaAlapN : (Msb:) or, as some say, a dubious affair, of great magnitude or moment, to accomplish which, or to perform which, one finds not the way: (Har p. 436:) and a quality, or property. (Msb.) You say, sumotuhu xuT~apa xasofK [ I required, or constrained, him to do an affair of difficulty; or to become in a state of abasement, or ignominy ]: and xuT~apa suwo'K [ an evil affair ]. (L.) And huwayukal~ifuniY xuT~apF mina Alxasofi [ He requires, or constrains, me to do an affair of difficulty; &c.]. (JK. [See also xasofN .]) And it is said in a trad., of Keyleh, A^ayulaAmu A@bonu h`*ihi A^ano yafoSila AlxuT~apa wayanotaSira mino waraA='i AlHajazapi [ Is the son of this woman to be blamed for deciding the affair, or matter, or case, &c., and defending himself in the absence of the wrongdoers who would prevent his obtaining his right; or, of those who defend men, one from another, and decide between them justly? ]: i. e., when a dubious event, to the encountering of which he does not find the right way, befalls him, that he should not care for it, but decide it so as to settle it and extricate himself from it. (S, TA.) [See also HaAjizN .] Also, in a trad. respecting El-Hodeybiyeh, laAyasoA^luwniY xuT~apF yuEaZ~imuwna fiyhaA HurumaAti A@ll~`hi taEaAlaY A_il~aA A^aEoTiyotuhumo A_iy~aAhaA [ They shall not ask of me a matter wherein they honour the sacred things of God, ( exalted be He, ) but I will grant it to them ]. (TA.) And in the same, qado EaraDa Ealayokumo xuT~apa ru$odK faA@qobaluwhaA He hath proposed to you a case of evident rectitude; therefore do ye accept it. (TA.) And Taäbbatasharrà says, humaA xaT~ataA A_im~aA A_isaArN wamin~apN waA_im~aA damN waAlqatolu biAlHur~i A^ajodaru [ They are two case; either bondage and reproach, or else blood; and slaughter is more befitting to the free, or ingenuous ]: he means xuT~ataAni . (S. [See Ham p. 34.]) ― -b3- Also A course: as in the phrase xuT~apN naAy^iyapN A distant, or far-extending, course. (S, TA.) You say also, xu*o xuT~apF , i. e. xu*o xuT~apa AlAinotiSaAfi [ Take thou the course of exacting thy right, or due, with equity ]; meaning AinotaSifo [ exact thou thy right, or due, with equity ]. (S.) ― -b4- A proof; an evidence; a testimony; an argument; a plea; or an allegation; syn. Huj~apN . (O, TA.) So in the phrase, A^aqimo EalaY h`*aA AlA^amori bixuT~apK [app. Establish thou a proof, &c., against this thing, or case ]; as is said in the “ Nawádir. ” (TA.) ― -b5- An object of want which one has determined to accomplish: as in the saying, jaA='a wafiY raA^osihi xuT~apN He came having in his mind [lit. his head ] an object of want &c. : [but see the last sentence in this paragraph:] the vulgar say xuTobapN : (S, L:) the former is the word used by the Arabs: (L:) the latter, however, occurs in the “ Nawádir ” of AZ; therefore the attribution of it to the vulgar demands consideration. (TA.) ― -b6- Boldness to undertake affairs. (K.) ― -b7- Ignorance. (K.) You say, fiY raA^osihi xuT~apN In his head is ignorance: or, as some say, some affair: and it has another meaning explained above. (TA.)

definition: A piece of ground, or land, which a man takes to himself, and upon which he makes a mark, in order to its being known that he has chosen it to build there a house;
sourceDefinition: A piece of ground, or land, which a man takes to himself, and upon which he makes a mark, in order to its being known that he has chosen it to build there a house; whence the xiTaT of El-Koofeh and of El-Basrah: (S:) or a piece of ground, and a house, which a man takes to himself, and upon which he makes a mark, in land not possessed, that he may have it for himself exclusively, and build there; this being done when the Sultán gives permission to a number of the Muslims to found houses in a particular place, and to make their abodes there, as they did in El-Koofeh and El-Basrah: (L:) or a place which is taken and marked for building houses, or for habitation, or the like: (Mgh, Msb:) or, as is said in the Bári', a piece of ground, or land, which a man takes to himself, and upon which he makes a mark, it not having belonged to any one before him; as also ↓ xiT~N ; (Msb;) which latter is explained by IDrd as signifying a place which one takes to himself, and marks, from other places: (IB, L:) or both signify a piece of land in which one alights and takes up his abode, none having done so before him: (K:) the pl. of the former is HiTazN . (S, Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] fulaAnN bay~inN xiTaTi AlmakaArimi (tropical:) [ Such a one exhibits in himself the marks of generous, or honourable, qualities ]. (TA.)

definition: Spears of El-Khatt;
sourceDefinition: Spears of El-Khatt; so called from AlxaT~u , a place in El-Yemámeh, (S, Msb,) also called xaT~u hajarK , (S,) because they are brought thither (S, Msb) from India, (S,) and straightened in that place, (S, Msb, *) which is a coast for ships; not that the canes grow there: (Msb:) or they are so called from AlxaT~u which is the station for ships in El-Bahreyn, because they are sold there; not that it is the place of their growth: this place is also called AlxiT~u : (K:) but this demands consideration; for it is said [in the 'Eyn, i. e.] by Lth, (TA,) or by Kh, (Msb,) that when you convert the rel. n. into a subst., you say ↓ xiTiy~apN , (Msb, TA,) with kesr to the x , (Msb,) without rmAH , like as you say, viyaAbN qiboTiy~apN , (Msb, TA,) with kesr, (Msb,) but when you convert the rel. n. into a subst., you say, quboTiy~apN , (Msb, TA,) with damm, to distinguish the subst. from the rel. n., without vyAb : (Msb:) a single spear of this kind is called rumoHN xaT~iY~N : (TA:) AHn says that AlxaT~iY~u signifies the spears; and that it is a rel. n. used in the manner of a proper name; being a rel. n. from AlxaT~u , which is xaT~u AlbaHorayoni , where ships moor when they come from India. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. (JK, S, K) and , (K,) [the latter irreg.,] inf. n. xumuwmN (JK, K) and xam~N , (K,) It (flesh-meat) was, or became, stinking; (S, K;) said of what is roasted, or cooked; (S;) or mostly said of what is cooked, and what is roasted: (IDrd, K:) or became altered for the worse in odour; said of roasted meat, and of meat cut into strips and dried: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or became stinking after having been thoroughly cooked : (TA:) and said also of milk, (JK, K,) in like manner, (JK,) it became altered by the bad odour of the skin, (K, TA,) and corrupt: (TA:) and ↓ Axm~ signifies the same, (JK, S, K,) in both cases: (TA:) and xam~N also, said of a cake of bread not thoroughly baked, signifies the becoming altered in odour. (TA.) [Hence,] xam~a , inf. n. xumuwmN , is likewise said of a man. (TA. [See also 10.]) And one says, huwa laA yaxim~u , meaning (assumed tropical:) He will not become altered (JK, TA) from his state, or condition, (JK,) or from his liberality, and generosity. (TA.) And huwa Als~amonu laA yaxim~u , (S, TA,) [lit.] meaning [ It is the clarified butter ] that will not become altered [ for the worse ]: (TA:) a prov., relating to a man when one speaks well of him, and praises him. (S, TA.) And huwa Als~um~u laA yaxim~u , i. e. (assumed tropical:) It is unmixed poison. (TA.) ― -b2- xam~N signifies also The act of weeping violently. (K.) You say, huwa yaxim~u He weeps violently. (TK.) -A2- xam~a , (JK, S, K,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. xam~u , (TK,) He cleaned out a well: (S, K: *) and he swept a tent, or house, or chamber: (JK, S, K:) and ↓ Axtm~ signifies the same, (S, K,) in both cases. (TA, and so in some copies of the K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] huwa yaxum~u viyaAbahu (tropical:) He eulogizes him, commends him, or speaks well of him: (K, TA:) and xam~ahu bivanaA='K HasanK , aor. , inf. n. xam~N , (tropical:) He eulogized him: (TA:) [and so, app., xam~ahu alone; for] xam~N signifies The act of eulogizing. (K, TA.) ― -b3- xam~N also signifies The act of cutting; and so ↓ AixotimaAmN . (K.) ― -b4- And xam~a Aln~aAqapa , (K,) aor. , inf. n. xam~N , (TA,) He milked the she-camel: (K:) or xam~a , aor. , signifies he turned in his thumb upon his palm when milking. (JK.) -A3- xum~a , said of a domestic fowl, It was confined in a xum~ , i. e. cage, or coop. (K.)

definition: He knew the thing;
sourceDefinition: He knew the thing; syn. Ealimahu ; (M;) [and so daraY biAl$~aYo'i ; for] you say, darayotuhu (S, Msb, K) and darayotu bihi , (S, K,) aor. A^adoriY , (Msb, K,) inf. n. daroYN (S, M, Msb, K) and diroYN (Lh, M, K) and diroyapN (S, M, Msb, K) and daroyapN , (M, * K,) which last is said by Sb to be not used as an inf. n. of un., but as denoting a state, or condition, (M,) and, accord. to some copies of the S, duroyapN , (TA, [so in one of my copies of the S,]) and diraAyapN (S, M, Msb, K) and darayaAnN and diroyaAnN (M, K) and duriY~N , (TS, K,) I knew it; (S, Msb, K;) syn. Ealimotuhu (Msb, K) or Ealimotu bihi : (S:) or it has a more special meaning than Ealimotuhu : it is said to signify I knew it after doubting: so says Aboo-'Alee: (TA:) or I knew it by a sort of artifice, or cunning, or skill; (K, TA;) or with painstaking, and artifice or cunning or skill; (Har p. 24;) and therefore daraY is not said of God: (TA:) a rájiz says, (S, * TA,) but this is an instance of the rude speech of the Arabs of the desert, (TA,) ↓ laA hum~a laA A^adoriY waA^anota Ald~aAriY [ O God, I know not, but Thou art the knowing ]: (S, TA: [in Har, p. 24, it is cited as commencing with Aal~`hum~a , and therefore as a prose-saying, ascribed to Mohammad, and as adduced by some to show that Ald~aAriY is allowable as an epithet applied to God:]) or, as some relate it, laA A^adori , (S,) in which the Y is elided in consequence of the frequent usage of the phrase; (S, M;) like the phrases lamo A^ubalo and lamo yaku ; (S;) and like laA yaA^olu in the saying A^aqobala biDarobahK laA yaA^olu [q. v. in art. Alw ]. (M.) [The saying laA darayotu walaA A@y^otalyota or A^alayota &c. is explained in the latter part of the first paragraph of art. And IAar mentions the saying maA tadoriY maA diroyotuhaA , (M,) or durayotuhaA , (TA,) as meaning Thou knowest not ( maA taEolamu [which may also be rendered she knows not ]) what is her knowledge. (S.) A rájiz says, ↓ kayofa taraAniYA^a*~ariY waA^ad~ariY girariY ↓ gir~aAti jumolK watadar~aY (T, S, M) i. e. How seest thou me winnowing the dust of the mine and deceiving Juml by looking at her while she is inadvertent, (T, S,) she also deceiving me [by looking at me while I am inadvertent ]: tadar~aY being for tatadar~aY . (S.) See also 3. -A3- daraY raA^osahu , (K,) aor. yadoriY , inf. n. daroYN , (TA,) He scratched his head with the midoraY : (K:) or raA^osahu ↓ dr~Y he combed his head with the midoraY : (M: [see Ham p. 159, line 11: and see also *ar~aYa :]) and ↓ tadar~ato she (a woman, S) loosed and let down, or loosed and separated, or combed, her hair (S, K, TA) with the midoraAp . (TA.)

definition: , (M, K,) inf. n. A_idaAlapN , (T, TA,) [signifying He gave him a turn of good fortune, or a turn to prevail over another in war, &c.,] is from Ald~awolapu . (T, M, K, TA. [See what next precedes.])...
sourceDefinition: , (M, K,) inf. n. A_idaAlapN , (T, TA,) [signifying He gave him a turn of good fortune, or a turn to prevail over another in war, &c.,] is from Ald~awolapu . (T, M, K, TA. [See what next precedes.]) Hence, [in the CK from Ald~uwlap ,] the saying, A^adaAlanaA A@ll~`hu mino Eaduw~inaA [ God gave us, or may God give us, a turn to prevail over our enemy ]. (S, K.) And A^adaAlaka A@ll~`hu mino Eaduw~ika and EalaY Eaduw~ika , i. e. jaEala laka Ealayohi dawolapF [ May God appoint thee, or give thee, a turn to prevail over thine enemy ]. (Ham p. 547.) And AdAl A@ll~`hu zayodFA mino EamorKw [ God gave to Zeyd a turn to have the superiority over 'Amr; ] i. e. God took away the turn of good fortune, or the good fortune, ( Aldwlp ,) from 'Amr, and gave it to Zeyd. (Har p. 118.) Hence, also, (TA,) El-Hajjáj said, A_in~a AlA^aroDa satudaAlu min~aA kamaA A^udilonaA minohaA [ Verily the earth will be given (?) turn to prevail over us, like as we have been given a turn to prevail over it ]; (Lth, T, TA;) meaning that it will consume us, like as we have consumed [of] it. (T, TA.) And [hence] A_idaAlapN signifies galabapN [or Victory ]: (S, K:) or [rather], as some say, it signifies nuSorapN [i. e. aid against an enemy ]: (Har ubi suprà:) you say, Aall~`huma A^adiloniY EalaY fulaAnN O God, aid me against such a one. (S, and Har ubi suprà. [In the former, waA@noSuroniYEalayohi , as an explicative adjunct: in the latter, AY nS~irnY Elyh , for A@noSuroniY .])

definition: They took it, or had it, by turns.
sourceDefinition: They took it, or had it, by turns. (S, Msb, K. See 3.) You say, tadaAwalonaA AlA^amora We took [or did ] the affair by turns. (M.) And tadaAwalonaA AlEamala wa AlA^amorabayonanaA We did the work, and the thing, or affair, by turns, among us. (T.) And tadaAwaluwA AlbaATila They took it by turns to say, or to do, that which was false, wrong, vain, futile, or the like; syn. tabaT~aluwA bayonahumo . (Az and K in art. bTl .) And tadaAwalatohu AlA^ayodiY The hands took it by turns. (S.) And tadaAwalati Alr~iyaAHu rasoma Ald~aAra The winds blew by turns upon, or over, the remains that marked the site of the house [ so as to efface them ]; one time from the south, and another time from the north, and another time from the east, and another time from the west. (Az, TA in art. Ewr .) And, of a thing, you say, yutadaAwalu (T) or yutadaAwalu bihi (S) [meaning It is taken, or done, by turns ]. And tuduwowilati AlA^aroDu biAlr~aEoYi [ The land was pastured on by turns ]. (S and K in art. wZb .) [ tadaAwaluwhu also signifies They made frequent use of it; i. e., used it time after time, or turn after turn; namely, a word or phrase: but perhaps in this sense it is postclassical: see an ex. in De Sacy's “ Chrest. Arabe, ” sec. ed., p. 141 of the Arabic text.] And tadaAwalati AlA^a$oyaA='u The things alternated; or succeeded one another by turns, one taking the place of another: (L in art. nsx :) and [in like manner] AlA^azomanapu [ the times ]. (Msb and K in that art.) [See also 6 in art dfw .]

definition: A turn, mutation, change, or vicissitude, of time, or fortune, (K, TA,) from an unfortunate and evil, to a good and happy, state or condition;
sourceDefinition: A turn, mutation, change, or vicissitude, of time, or fortune, (K, TA,) from an unfortunate and evil, to a good and happy, state or condition; (TA;) [i. e.,] relating to good; as daborapN , on the contrary, relates to evil: (As, T and M in art. dbr :) [therefore meaning a turn of good fortune; a favourable turn of fortune: or] good fortune [absolutely]: (KL:) a happy state or condition, that betides a man: (MF:) [also] a turn which comes to one or which one takes [in an absolute sense]; syn. nawobapN : (K in art. nwb :) and [particularly] (K) a turn ( EuqobapN ) [ to share ] in wealth, and [ to prevail ] in war; as also ↓ duwlapN : ('Eesà Ibn-'Omar, * T, * S, * M, K: *) or each is a subst. [in an absolute sense, app. as meaning a turn of taking, or having, a thing,] from tadaAwaluwA Al$~aYo'a signifying “ they took, or had, the thing by turns: ” (Msb:) or ↓ duwlapN is in wealth; and dawolapN is in war; (Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà, T, S, M, Msb, K;) this latter being when one of two armies defeats the other and then is defeated; (Fr, T;) or when one party is given a turn to prevail ( tudaAl ) over the other: one says, kaAnato lanaA Ealayohimu Ald~awolapu fiY AlHarobi [ The turn to prevail over them in war was ours ]: (S:) and qado rajaEati Ald~awolapu EalaY h`w^ulaA='i [ The turn to prevail against these returned ]; as though meaning Almar~apu : so says Fr: but ↓ duwlapN , he says, is in religions and institutions that are altered and changed with time: (T:) accord. to Zj, (T,) or A'Obeyd, (so in two copies of the S,) ↓ duwlapN signifies a thing that is taken by turns; and dawolapN , the act [ of taking by turns ]; (T, S;) and a transition from one state, or condition, to another: (T: [in this last sense, app. an inf. n.: see 1, third sentence:]) you say, bayonahumo ↓ SaAra AlfaYo'u duwlapF , meaning [ The fY' (or spoil, &c.,) became ] a thing taken by turns among them: (S:) and the saying, in the Kur [lix. 7], bayona AlA^agoniyaA='i minokumo ↓ kaYo laA yakuwna duwlapF means That it may not be a thing taken by turns [ among the rich of you ]: (T:) or dawolapN relates to the present life or world; and ↓ duwlapN , to that which is to come: (M, K:) and it is said that the former of these two words signifies prevalence, predominance, mastery, or victory; and ↓ the latter, the transition of wealth, blessing, or good, from one people, or party, to another: (TA:) the pl. (of dawolapN , S, Msb) is dawilN , (S, M, Msb, K,) like as qiSaEN is pl. of qaSoEapN , (Msb,) and (of ↓ duwlapN , T, S, Msb), duwalN (T, S, M, Msb, K) and duwlaAtN , (S, TA,) and ↓ dawalN (M, K) is [a quasi-pl. n.] of both, because, as IJ says, dawolapN is regarded as though it were originally duwlapN . (M.) ― -b2- [In post-classical works, it signifies also A dynasty: and a state, an empire, or a monarchy. ] -A2- Also The HawoSalap [or stomach of a bird; its triple stomach: or only its first stomach; the crop, or craw ]: because of its AinodiyaAl [or flaccidity]. (Ibn-'Abbaád, K.) And The qaAniSap [which may here mean the same as the HwSlp , for this is one of the meanings assigned to it, and this explanation of dwlp is not given by Ibn- 'Abbád: or it may here mean the intestines, of a bird, into which the food passes from the stomach: or the gizzard ]. (K.) ― -b2- And The $iqo$iqap [or faucial bag of the he-camel]. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b3- And A thing like a mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag ] with a narrow mouth. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b4- And The side of the belly. (K.) [But] accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, maA A^aEoZama dawolapa baTonihi means How large is his navel! (TA.)

[in an absolute sense, app. as meaning a turn of taking, or having, a thing,] from tadaAwaluwA Al$~aYo'a signifying “ they took, or had, the thing by turns: ” (Msb:) or ↓ duwlapN is in wealth; and dawolapN is in war; (Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà, T, S, M, Msb, K;) this latter being when one of two armies defeats the other and then is defeated; (Fr, T;) or when one party is given a turn to prevail ( tudaAl ) over the other: one says, kaAnato lanaA Ealayohimu Ald~awolapu fiY AlHarobi [ The turn to prevail over them in war was ours ]: (S:) and qado rajaEati Ald~awolapu EalaY h`w^ulaA='i [ The turn to prevail against these returned ]; as though meaning Almar~apu : so says Fr: but ↓ duwlapN , he says, is in religions and institutions that are altered and changed with time: (T:) accord. to Zj, (T,) or A'Obeyd, (so in two copies of the S,) ↓ duwlapN signifies a thing that is taken by turns; and dawolapN , the act [ of taking by turns ]; (T, S;) and a transition from one state, or condition, to another: (T: [in this last sense, app. an inf. n.: see 1, third sentence:]) you say, bayonahumo ↓ SaAra AlfaYo'u duwlapF , meaning [ The fY' (or spoil, &c.,) became ] a thing taken by turns among them: (S:) and the saying, in the Kur [lix. 7], bayona AlA^agoniyaA='i minokumo ↓ kaYo laA yakuwna duwlapF means That it may not be a thing taken by turns [ among the rich of you ]: (T:) or dawolapN relates to the present life or world; and ↓ duwlapN , to that which is to come: (M, K:) and it is said that the former of these two words signifies prevalence, predominance, mastery, or victory; and ↓ the latter, the transition of wealth, blessing, or good, from one people, or party, to another: (TA:) the pl. (of dawolapN , S, Msb) is dawilN , (S, M, Msb, K,) like as qiSaEN is pl. of qaSoEapN , (Msb,) and (of ↓ duwlapN , T, S, Msb), duwalN (T, S, M, Msb, K) and duwlaAtN , (S, TA,) and ↓ dawalN (M, K) is [a quasi-pl. n.] of both, because, as IJ says, dawolapN is regarded as though it were originally duwlapN . (M.) ― -b2- [In post-classical works, it signifies also A dynasty: and a state, an empire, or a monarchy. ] -A2- Also The HawoSalap [or stomach of a bird; its triple stomach: or only its first stomach; the crop, or craw ]: because of its AinodiyaAl [or flaccidity]. (Ibn-'Abbaád, K.) And The qaAniSap [which may here mean the same as the HwSlp , for this is one of the meanings assigned to it, and this explanation of dwlp is not given by Ibn- 'Abbád: or it may here mean the intestines, of a bird, into which the food passes from the stomach: or the gizzard ]. (K.) ― -b2- And The $iqo$iqap [or faucial bag of the he-camel]. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b3- And A thing like a mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag ] with a narrow mouth. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b4- And The side of the belly. (K.) [But] accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, maA A^aEoZama dawolapa baTonihi means How large is his navel! (TA.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. mudaAwalapF , [in the CK, erroneously, mutadAwalapF ,] used in an imperative sense [with its verb and the objective complement thereof understood before it, and thus meaning daAwili AlfiEola mudaAwalapF Make thou the action to come round, or to be, by turns ]: (M, K:) or it may be rendered as meaning that the thing happened in this manner [i. e. the action being made to come round, or to be, by turns ]: (Sb, M:) or it means tadaAwulN baEoda tadaAwul [i. e. a taking, or doing, (a thing) by turn after (another's) doing so, and may be rendered virtually in the same manner as above, i. e. let the action be done by turns: or the action being done by turns ]: (S, O, K: [in the PS, tadaAwulFA baEoda tadaAwulK , which better explains the two manners in which it is said to be used:]) IAar says that it is an invariable expression, like HajaAzayoka and ha*aA*ayoka ; and is from the phrase tadaAwaluwA AlA^amora bayonahumo , said of persons when this takes a turn and this a turn. (T, TA.) 'Abd-Beni-l- Has-hás says, A_i*a $uq~a burodN $uq~a biAlburodi mivoluhu dawaAlayoka Hat~aY layosa liloburodi laAbisu [ When a burd (a kind of garment) is rent, the like thereof is rent with the burd, the action being done by turns, so that there is no wearer of the burd; it having been rent so as to fall off]: (S:) the poet is speaking of a man's rending the clothing of a woman to see her person, and her rending his also. (T, TA. [This verse is related with several variations: see another reading of it voce ha*aA*ayoka , in art. h* ; with another explanation of it.]) ― -b2- Ibn-Buzurj says, (T,) sometimes the article Al is prefixed to it, so that one says Ald~awaAlayoka , (T,) meaning One's walking with an elegant and a proud and self-conceited gait, with an affected inclining of the body from side to side, (T,) or one's urging, or pressing forward, and striving, ( A^ano yataHaf~aza , [in the CK, erroneously, An yataHaf~aza ,]) in his gait, or pace, (K,) when he moves about his shoulder-joints, and parts his legs widely, in walking. (T, K,* TA. In the copies of the K, jAl [or jA'k ] is erroneously put for HaAka , the reading in the T, TA. [The author of the TK follows the reading jAl ; and has fallen into several other evident mistakes in explaining this expression; which is itself, in my opinion, when with the article Al , a mistake for Ald~awaAliyoku , mentioned in art. dlk .]) A poet uses the phrase yamo$iY Ald~awaAlayoka as meaning Walking, or going, in the manner explained above: (Ibn-Buzurj, T and TA in the present art.:) or yamo$iY Ald~awaAliyka . (TA in art. dlk .)

Hence, (K,) muvoqalN A@sotaEaAna bi*aqanihi [ A heavily-burdened, or overburdened, camel sought to help himself to rise by means of his chin ]: (S, M, K:) a prov., applied to a low, base, or mean, and weak man, who seeks to help himself by means of another man like himself; (S;) or to him who seeks to help himself by means of one who has no power of defending, and by means of one more low, base, or mean, and weak, than he: (M:) or to him who seeks to help himself by means of one less than he: (K:) originating from the fact that a camel laden with a heavy load, and unable to rise, bears with his chin upon the ground. definition: A she-camel that relaxes her chin [ so as to make her lower lip hang down ] in going along: (S, K:) or that moves about her head in going along: (JK:) or that stretches her steps, and moves about her...
sourceDefinition: A she-camel that relaxes her chin [ so as to make her lower lip hang down ] in going along: (S, K:) or that moves about her head in going along: (JK:) or that stretches her steps, and moves about her head, by reason of strength, and briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, in going along: (A, TA:) pl. *uqunN : (TA:) and ↓ *aAqinapN , applied to a she-camel, signifies the same as *aquwnN . (IAar, TA.) ― -b2- dalowN *aquwnN (assumed tropical:) A bucket [ of leather ] which one has sewed in such a manner that its lip inclines on one side: (S, K:) or a large bucket inclining on one side: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and ↓ *alowN *aqanaY a bucket with an inclining lip: (IB, TA:) and ↓ dalowN *aqonaA='u a bucket that has had an addition made to one of its two sides, and consequently inclines on one side. (JK.)

definition: The part beneath the *aqan [or chin ]: (K:) or the part, of the breast, that is reached by the *aqan : or the *aqan [ itself ]: (TA:) or the head of the Huloquwm [or windpipe ]: (K:) or the prominent...
sourceDefinition: The part beneath the *aqan [or chin ]: (K:) or the part, of the breast, that is reached by the *aqan : or the *aqan [ itself ]: (TA:) or the head of the Huloquwm [or windpipe ]: (K:) or the prominent extremity of the Hlqwm : (S, K:) thus explained by A'Obeyd and AA in the saying of 'Áïsheh, “ [The Prophet died] between my HaAqinap and my *aAqinap : ” (TA: [see AlHaAqinapu :]) or the taroquw=p [ or collar-bone; or it may here mean the fore part of the throat, next the chest; or the uppermost part of the chest ]: (K:) but this, in the M, is an explanation of AlHaAqinapu : (TA:) or the lower part of the belly, next the navel: (K:) but this, also, is given as an explanation of AlHAqnp , by ISd and by Z: (TA:) or the pit of the uppermost part of the breast, or chest: or the upper part of the belly: (K:) and the stomach: (JK:) pl. *awaAqinu . (S, TA.) [See also AlHaAqinapu .] Hence the prov., laA^uloHiqan~a HawaAqinaka ba*awaAqinika [explained in art. Hqn ]: Al*~awaAqinu , accord. to Az, means the lower part of the belly. (S.) -A2- See also *aquwnN .

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, &c.,) aor. , (A, K,) inf. n. *ahaAbN (S, A, Msb, K) and *ihaAbN (TA) and *uhuwbN (S, A, K) and ma*ohabN , (A, K,) He (a man, S, [and a beast,]) went [ in any manner, or any pace ]; went, or passed, along; marched; journeyed; proceeded: went, or passed, away; departed: syn. ma$aY , (A,) or saAra , (K,) or mar~ : (S, A, K:) and said of a mark or trace or the like [as meaning it went away ]. (Msb.) [And hence, (assumed tropical:) It wasted away; became consumed, destroyed, exhausted, spent, or expended. ] ― -b2- *ahaba A_ilayohi He went, repaired, betook himself, or had recourse, to him, or it. (TA.) And they say also, *ahaba Al$~aA^oma [ He went to Syria ]; making the verb trans. without a particle; for although Al$A^m is here a special adv. n., they liken it to a vague locality. (TA.) ― -b3- *ahaba Eanohu He, or it, went from, quitted, relinquished, or left, him, or it. (TA.) ― -b4- *ahaba fiYAlA^aroDi , (A, Msb,) inf. n. *ahaAbN and *uhuwbN and ma*ohabN , He went away [ into the country, or in the land ]: (Msb:) [but it often means (assumed tropical:) he went into the open country, or out of doors, to satisfy a want of nature: or simply] (tropical:) he voided his excrement, or ordure. (A.) ― -b5- *ahaba bihi He went, or went away, with him, or it: (A:) and he made him, or it, to go, go away, pass away, or depart; (A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ A*hbhu , (S, A, Msb, K,) and bihi ↓ A*hb , (K,) but this is rare; (Zj, TA;) and ↓ *h~bhu , inf. n. ta*ohiybN : (MF:) [all may likewise be rendered he removed, dispelled, put away, or banished, it; properly and tropically: and (assumed tropical:) he made it to cease; made away with it, did away with it, made an end of it; wasted, consumed, destroyed, exhausted, spent, or expended, it; and these meanings may perhaps be intended by A^azaAlahu , whereby the first is explained in the A and K, as are also the second and third in the K:] or, accord. to some, when *ahaba is trans. by means of bi , accompaniment is necessarily signified; but not otherwise; so that if you say *ahaba bihi , the meaning is, he went away with him, or it; i. e., accompanying him, or it; [ he took away, or carried off or away, him, or it; ] but if you say ↓ A*hbhu or ↓ *h~bhu , the meaning is, he made him, or it, to go, go away, pass away, or depart, alone, without accompanying him, or it: this, however, is not agreeable with the phrase in the Kur [ii. 16], *ahaba A@ll~`hu binuwrihimo [though this may be well rendered God taketh away their light ]. (MF, TA.) [Hence,] one says, A^ayona yu*ohabu bika , which may mean (assumed tropical:) Where, or whither, wilt thou be taken away, and what will be done with thee and made to come to pass with thee, if this be thine intellect? or, accord. to Mtr, it is a saying of the people of Baghdád, addressed to him whom they charge with foolish judgment or opinion, as meaning A^ayona yu*ohabu biEaqolika (assumed tropical:) [ Where, or whither, is thine intellect taken away? ]. (Har p. 574.) [In like manner one says, *ahaba Eaqoluhu (assumed tropical:) His reason, or intellect, quitted him, or forsook him; he became bereft of his reason, or intellect. And *ahaba fuw^aAduhu (assumed tropical:) His heart forsook him, or failed him, by reason of fear or the like.] And *ahaba laHomuhu (assumed tropical:) [ His flesh wasted away ]. (K in art. bHr , &c.) And *ahaba Alr~ajulu fiY Alqawomi (tropical:) The man became lost [or he disappeared ] among the people, or party. (A.) And *ahaba AlmaA='a fiY All~abani (tropical:) The water became lost [or it disappeared ] in the milk. (A.) ― -b6- *ahaba Ealayohi (tropical:) It escaped his memory; he forgot it. (A, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, dubious, confused, or vague, to him. (MA.) ― -b7- *ahaba ma*ohabFA HasanFA (S, A, TA) (tropical:) He pursued a good way, course, mode, or manner, of acting or conduct or the like. (TA.) And *ahaba fiY Ald~iyni ma*ohabFA (assumed tropical:) He formed, or held, an opinion, or a persuasion, or a belief, respecting religion: or, accord. to Es-Sarakustee, he introduced an innovation in religion. (Msb.) And *ahaba ma*ohaba fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) He pursued the way, course, mode, or manner, of acting &c. of such a one. (Msb.) And *ahaba li*ahobihi and lima*ohabihi (tropical:) He pursued his way, course, mode, or manner, of acting &c. (JK, TA.) And *ahaba A_ilaY ma*ohabK (tropical:) He betook himself to [or took to or held ] a belief, a creed, a persuasion, a doctrine, an opinion, a tenet, or a body of tenets or articles of belief. (K, TA.) And fulaAnN ya*ohabu A_ilaY qawoli A^abiY Haniyfapa (tropical:) Such a one takes to, or holds, [ the saying, or] the belief, creed, persuasion, doctrine, &c., of Aboo-Haneefeh. (A.) [And *ahaba A_ilaY A^an~a AlA^amora ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He held, or was of opinion, that the thing, or affair, or case, was so. And *ahaba bilafoZK A_ilaYlafoZK A=xara (assumed tropical:) He regarded a word, or an expression, in his manner of using it, as equivalent to another word, or expression; as, for instance, when one makes a fem. noun masc. because it is syn. with a noun that is masc., or makes a verb trans. by means of a certain perticle because it is syn. with a verb that is trans. by means of that same particle: and also (assumed tropical:) he regarded a word, or an expression, as etymologically relating, or traceable, to another word, or expression. And *ahaba bihi A_ilaY maEonaY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He regarded it, or used it, (i. e. a word, or an expression,) as relating to such a meaning, or as meaning such a thing. ] ― -b8- *ahaba fiY Talabi Al$~aYo'i kul~a ma*ohabK (assumed tropical:) [ He tried every way, or did his utmost, in seeking the thing ]. (K in art. mwt .) And *ahaba fiYAll~iyni kul~a ma*ohabK (assumed tropical:) [ It attained the utmost degree of softness ]: said of the skin. (TA in that art.) ― -b9- Ai*ohabo A_ilayoka (assumed tropical:) Betake, or apply, thyself to thine own affairs; or occupy thyself therewith. (T and K * voce A_ilaY .) ― -b10- *ahaba A_ilaY A^abiyhi fiY Al$~abahi i. q. nazaEa (assumed tropical:) [ He inclined to his father in likeness; resembled him; or had a natural likeness to him ]. (S in art. nzE .) -A2- *ahiba , (S, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. *ahabN ; (TA;) and *ihiba , with two kesrehs, (IAar, K,) of the dial. of Temeem, held by AM to be a variation generally allowable in the case of a verb of which the medial radical letter is a faucial and with kesr; (TA;) He (a man) saw gold in the mine, (S,) or came suddenly, in the mine, upon much gold, and his reason departed in consequence thereof, (K,) and his eyes became dazzled, so as not to close, or move, the lids, or became confused, so as not to see, (S, K,) by reason of the greatness thereof in his eye: (S:) it is derived from *ahabN : and the epithet applied to a man in this case is ↓ *ahibN . (TA.)

definition: signifies, (K, TA,) in its primary acceptation, (TA,) Two [ hostile ] parties' tying of their horses, each at their frontier, and each in preparation for the other: (K, TA:) and ribaATu Alxayoli and muraAbaTatuhaA signify the same [as above].
sourceDefinition: signifies, (K, TA,) in its primary acceptation, (TA,) Two [ hostile ] parties' tying of their horses, each at their frontier, and each in preparation for the other: (K, TA:) and ribaATu Alxayoli and muraAbaTatuhaA signify the same [as above]. (S, TA.) [You say, raAbaTa AlfariyqaAni The two parties tied their horses at their respective frontiers, each in preparation for the other. ] And one says, with reference to horses, ↓ rabaTa , inf. n. raboTN and ribaATN , as well as rAbT , inf. n. muraAbaTapN and ribaATN . (Bd in viii. 62.) Hence, (Sgh, L, K,) rAbT , (Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. ribaATN (S, Mgh, Sgh, L, K) and muraAbaTapN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He, or it, (an army, Mgh) kept post, or remained, on, or at, the frontier (S, Mgh, Sgh, L, K) of the enemy, (S, Msb, K,) or over against the enemy. (Mgh.) And hence, i. e. from this latter application, (AAF, TA,) rAbT AlA^amora , (TK,) inf. n. ribaATN (AAF, K) and muraAbaTapN , (TK,) (assumed tropical:) He kept, or applied himself, constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously, to the thing, or affair. (AAF, K, TK.) It is said in the Kur [ch. iii., last verse], A@SobiruwA waSaAbiruwA waraAbiTuwA Be ye patient in endurance of what your religion requires, and vie ye in patience with your enemy, and persevere ye in fighting against your enemy, (Mgh, TA,) and in tying the horses [ at the frontier ]: (TA:) or the last of these verbs means keep ye post, or remain ye, on, or at, the frontier [ of the enemy ]: (Az, K:) or (assumed tropical:) be ye mindful of the times of prayer: or (assumed tropical:) apply yourselves constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously, to prayer: (TA:) or (assumed tropical:) wait ye for prayer after prayer; the doing this being termed by the Prophet ribaATN ; (Az, K, TA;) which word, thus used, is an inf. n. of raAbaTotu ; or, as some say, a simple subst., meaning, in this case, a thing whereby one is tied from acts of disobedience, and restrained from forbidden deeds. (TA.) [See also SaAbara .]

definition: A thing with which one ties, binds, or makes fast, (S, Msb, K,) a skin, (S, Msb,) and a beast, (S,) &c.
sourceDefinition: A thing with which one ties, binds, or makes fast, (S, Msb, K,) a skin, (S, Msb,) and a beast, (S,) &c.; (S, Msb;) a rope with which a beast is tied: (Mgh:) pl. rubuTN (S, Msb, K) and ruboTN ; (S, TA;) the latter a contraction of the former: (TA:) and ↓ mirobaTN and ↓ mirobaTapN also signify a thing with which a beast is tied. (K.) It is said in a prov., A_ino *ahaba EayorN faEayorN fiY Alr~ibaATi [ If an ass is gone away, an ass is tied to the cord ]: relating to contentment with what is present and relinquishment of what is absent. (Mgh.) [See also 3.] ― -b2- [Hence,] used by the vulgar in the sense of A^uxo*apN , meaning (assumed tropical:) A kind of fascination by which enchantresses withhold their husbands from other women. (TA in art. Ax* .) ― -b3- A snare for catching game. (S, Mgh.) You say, qaTaEa AlZ~aboYu ribaATahu [ The gazelle rent his snare ]. (S.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) The heart: (K:) as though the body were tied thereby. (TA.) Hence, (TA in art. qrD ,) qaraDa rbaATahu (assumed tropical:) He died: (M and K in that art.:) or he was at the point of death. (K in that art.) And jaA='a fulaAnN waqado qaraDa ribaATahu (tropical:) Such a one came having turned away, or back, harassed, distressed, or fatigued, (S, TA, and AZ and Az in art. qrD ,) and at the point of death: (AZ, Az:) or harassed, or distressed, by thirst, or by fatigue: (A in art. qrD :) or in a state of intense thirst and hunger. (M in that art.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) The spirit: as in the saying of El-'Ajjáj, describing a wild bull, fabaAta wahowa vaAbitu Alr~ibaATi [ And he passed the night firm in spirit ]. (TA.) -A2- See also rabiyTN , (of which it is a pl., or pl. pl.,) in three places. -A3- A single building of those which are called ribaATaAtN : (S, K:) [ a public building for the accommodation of travellers and their beasts; (see bariydN ;) an application well known, and mentioned in the TK:] a religious house, or house inhabited by devotees; a dwelling for Soofees; (El-Makreezee's “ Khitat ” ii. 427;) [ a hospice, or an asylum for poor Muslim students and others, like zaAwiyapN ;] a building for the poor: in this sense post-classical: pl., accord. to analogy, rubuTN and ribaATaAtN . (Msb.)

definition: Tied, bound, or made fast;
sourceDefinition: Tied, bound, or made fast; as also ↓ marobuwTN ; (K, TA;) applied to a horse, (Mgh,) or similar beast ( daAb~ap ); as also ↓ marobuwTapN ; (TA;) applied to the former, i. q. marobuwTN ; (Mgh;) or maAyurotabaTu [which may perhaps signify the same; but more probably, taken to be tied, or for keeping post, on the enemy's frontier ]; (S;) and [in like manner] rabiyTapN , applied to the latter, i. q. maAA@rotubiTa : (K:) and rabiyTN applied to a horse also signifies tied and fed in the court of a house: (TA:) pl. rubuTN (TA) and ↓ ribaATN , (Mgh,) or the latter is a pl. pl., being pl. of rubuTN . (TA.) Alxayoli ↓ mino ribaATi , in the Kur [viii. 62], means Of horses that are tied; (Bd, Mgh;) ribaATN being of the measure fiEaAlN in the sense of the measure mafoEwlN ; or an inf. n. used as a subst., being an inf. n. of rabaTa in the sense of raAbaTa ; (Bd;) or it is an inf. n. of raAbaTa ; and therefore [when used as an epithet, like any inf. n. so used,] is applied to one as well as to a pl. number; (Ham p. 222;) or pl. of rabiyTo : (Bd, Mgh:) or it means of mares: (Fr, TA:) and ribaATN signifies horses; five thereof, and upwards: (S, K:) or horses, themselves, that are taken to be tied, or for keeping post, on the enemy's frontier. (L.) And you say, lifulaAnK mina Alxayoli ↓ ribaATN Such a one has a stud constituting the source of his horses; like as you say tlaAdN . (S.) ↓ raAbTapN , also, applied to horses, signifies Tied in a town or country or the like: occuring in a trad., in which it is said that upon every horse shall be levied a deenár; but upon the rAbTp , nothing: properly meaning, in this case, *aAtu Alr~aboTi ; being like raADiyapN in the phrase Eiy$apN raADiyapN . (Mgh.) ― -b2- See also raAbiTN . ― -b3- Also, and ↓ raAbiTN , (assumed tropical:) A monk: one who abstains from worldly pleasures: a sage who restrains himself from worldly things. (K, TA.) [In the L and TA, Alr~abiyTu is also explained, as on the authority of Ez-Zejjájee, as signifying Al*~aAhibu ; but this I think a mistranscription, for Alr~aAhibu .] -A2- (assumed tropical:) Unripe dates soaked [ in water ]: (S, K:) or (assumed tropical:) fresh ripe dates soaked with water; also called manoquw$N : (Sgh, TA in art. nq$ :) or (tropical:) dried dates (A 'Obeyd, IF, A, K) put into jars ( jiraAr ), (A 'Obeyd, A,) and having water poured upon them, (A 'Obeyd, IF, K,) or moistened with water, in order that they may become like fresh ripe dates: (A:) but perhaps this is an adventitious term: (IF:) some say that it is rabiydN , and not original. (TA.)

definition: signifies The throwing, or casting, of stones: (S, K:) this is its primary meaning: (S, TA:) you say, rajamahu , aor.
sourceDefinition: signifies The throwing, or casting, of stones: (S, K:) this is its primary meaning: (S, TA:) you say, rajamahu , aor. , inf. n. rajomN , (S, Msb, TA,) He threw, or cast, stones at him; or pelted him with stones: (S, TA:) or he struck him, or smote him, with rajam , meaning stones: (Msb:) and rujuwmN is syn. with rajomN , as an inf. n.: thus some explain the saying, in the Kur [lxvii. 5], wajoEalonaAhaA rujuwmFA lil$~ayaATiyni [ And we have made them for casting at the devils; meaning shooting stars, which are believed to be hurled at the devils that listen by stealth, beneath the lowest heaven, to the words of the angels therein: but see other explanations below, voce rajomN ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (S, TA,) The act of slaying [ in any manner, but generally stoning, i. e. putting to death by stoning ]. (S, K.) So in rajomu Alv~ay~ibayoni A_i*aA zanayaA [ The slaying, or stoning, of the two married persons when they have committed adultery ]. sourceDefinition: , inf. n. tarojiymN , He placed upon the grave rujam [meaning large stones, to make a gibbous covering to it]. (TA.) It is related in a trad. of 'Abd-Allah Ibn-Mughaffal, that he said, laA turaj~imuwA qaboriY , i. e. Place not ye upon my grave rujam ; meaning thereby that they should make his grave even with the ground, not gibbous and elevated: the verb is thus correctly, with tesh-deed: but the relaters of trads. say, ↓ lA tarojumuwA qbrY : (S:) [and it is said that] Alqabora ↓ rajama , (K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. rajomN , (TA,) signifies Eal~amahu , (K,) i. e. He put a tombstone to the grave: (TK:) or he placed upon the grave rijaAm [a pl., like rujam , of rujomap ]: (K:) or, accord. to Aboo-Bekr, laA qaboriY ↓ tarojumuwA means Wail not ye at my grave; i. e. say not, at it, what is unseemly; from Alr~ajomu signifying “ the act of reviling. ” (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b3- Also a pl. of rujomapN . (S, Msb, K.)

sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K, &c.) and ruzotaAqN (Lh, L, TA) and rusodaAqN (ISk, K) and rusotaAqN , (Lh, S, Msb, K, &c.,) but this last disallowed by ISk, (TA,) [though allowed by many others, and of frequent occurrence,] and said by some to be post-classical, and to be correctly ruzodaAqN , (Msb,) arabicized, (S, Msb, K,) of Pers. origin, (S,) from ruwsotaA , (K,) [erroneously] said by IF to be from razodaqN signifying as explained above; (Msb;) A rural district; or district consisting of cultivated land with towns or villages; syn. sawaAdN , (S,) or sawaAdN and qurFy : (K:) Yákoot explains rusotaAq as applied, in his time, in the country of the Persians, to any place [or district ] in which are sown fields, and towns or villages; not to cities, like El-Basrah and Baghdád; so that it is, with the Persians, like sawaAdN with the people of Baghdád, and is a more special term than kuwrapN [in Arabic] and A_isotaAn [in Persian]: (TA:) or it is used as meaning an outlying district, or a border-district, of a country: (Msb:) [but the correctness of this last explanation is questionable:] the pl. is razaAdiyqu (Msb) [and razaAtiyqu and rasaAdiyqu ] and rasaAtiyqu (S, Msb) and ruzodaAqaAtN (Har p. 249) [&c.].

definition: He remained, stayed, or dwelt, long in the house, or abode.
sourceDefinition: He remained, stayed, or dwelt, long in the house, or abode. (K, TA.) ― -b2- rAzm bayonahumaA He conjoined them two; (K;) [as, for instance, two kinds of food, by taking them in immediate succession: ] he mixed them. (TA.) You say, rAzmt AlA_ibilu The camels mixed two pastures. (S, TA.) And rAzmt AlA_ibilu AlEaAma The camels pastured upon the HamoD [or salt, or sour, plants ] one time, and xul~ap [or sweet plants ] another time, this year. (TA.) [In the case of a man,] muraAzamapN in eating signifies the making a consecutive, or successive, connexion [between two things]; kamaA yuraAzimu Alr~ajulu bayona AljaraAdi waAlt~amori [ like as when the man makes a consecutive, or successive, connexion between the eating of locusts and that of dates; or makes locusts and dates consecutive, or successive ]: (S, TA:) or muraAzamapN in relation to food signifies the making an interchange, by eating one day flesh-meat, and one day honey, (K, TA,) and one day dates, (TA,) and one day [ drinking ] milk, (K, TA,) and one day [ eating ] bread without any seasoning or condiment, (TA,) and the like; not keeping continually, or constantly, to one thing: (K, TA:) or the intermixing the [ acts of ] eating with thanks, and the mouthfuls with praise; (IAar, K, TA;) by saying, between the mouthfuls, Praise be to God: (IAar, TA:) or the mentioning God between every two mouthfuls: (Th, TA:) or the eating the soft and the dry or tough [ alternately ], and the sweet and the sour, and the unseasoned, or disagreeable in taste, and the seasoned: agreeably with all of these interpretations is explained the saying of 'Omar, A_i*aA A^akalotumo faraAzmuwA : (K, TA:) as though he said, [ When ye eat, ] eat what is easy and agreeable to swallow with what is unseasoned, or disagreeable in taste: (TA:) or mix ye, in your eating, what is soft with what is rough, or harsh, or coarse: (IAth, TA:) or make ye praise to follow [ your eating ]. (S.) ― -b3- muraAzamapu Als~uwqi means The purchasing in the market less than what will make up the full quantity of the loads. (K.)

definition: She (a camel) uttered a cry such as is termed razamap [q.
sourceDefinition: She (a camel) uttered a cry such as is termed razamap [q. v.] when loving, or affecting, her young one: (S:) or she (a camel) uttered a cry of yearning towards her young one: (K:) and in like manner, Arzmt EalaY waladihaA is said of a ewe, or she-goat: but sometimes A_irozaAmN means the uttering of a cry, or sound, absolutely: and Arzmt said of a she-camel occurs in a trad. as meaning she uttered a cry. (TA.) One says, laA A^afoEalu *aAka maA A^arozamato A^um~u HaAy^ilK [ I will not do that as long as a mother of a female young camel utters her gentle yearning cry ]: (S, K: *) a prov. (K.) And hence, i. e. from Arzmt said of a she-camel, (TA,) Arzm is also said of thunder, (S, K,) meaning (tropical:) It made a vehement sound, or noise: (K, TA:) or it made a sound, or noise, (S, K,) not vehement. (K.) [And it seems that ↓ razimato and razima signify the same as Arzmt and Arzm said of a she-camel and of thunder: for] the inf. n. razamN , used in relation to a camel and to thunder, signify The making a sound or noise. (KL.) Arzmt is also said of a cooking-pot, meaning (assumed tropical:) It made a noise by its boiling. (Ham p. 663.) And you say, Arzmt Alr~iyHu fiY Aljawofi (assumed tropical:) The wind made a sound [ in the belly ]. (K.)

definition: Firm, or steadfast, standing upon the ground: (S, K:) and ↓ murozimN and ↓ raAzimN signify [the same;
sourceDefinition: Firm, or steadfast, standing upon the ground: (S, K:) and ↓ murozimN and ↓ raAzimN signify [the same; or] firm, or steadfast, upon the ground: and the pl. of the last is ruz~aAmN , occurring in a verse cited voce rizaAmN , q. v. (TA.) ― -b2- Also The lion; and so ↓ murozimN ; (K, TA;) because he lies upon his breast on his prey, not quitting it: (TA:) or ruzamN (Ham p. 362) and ↓ razaAmN (TA, and Ham ibid., [but in the latter without any syll. signs,]) like saHaAbN , and ↓ razaAmapN like saHaAbapN , [which is of a form denoting intensiveness of signification,] (TA,) are epithets applied to a lion, meaning that lies upon his breast on his prey, (Ham, TA,) and growls. (Ham.) Accord. to J, it is applied in a verse of Sáïdeh Ibn-Ju-eiyeh to an elephant: but accord. to IB, and the Expos. of Skr, it is there applied to a lion, as meaning That has remained firm, or steadfast, in his place. (TA.)

definition: A quantity remaining in a [ receptacle of the kind called ] jul~ap , [a meaning said in the TA, in art.
sourceDefinition: A quantity remaining in a [ receptacle of the kind called ] jul~ap , [a meaning said in the TA, in art. rdm , to be erroneously assigned in the K, in that art, to ridomapN ,] of dates, amounting to half thereof, or a third, or thereabout: (TA:) or, accord. to Sh, the third part, or fourth part, of a [ sack such as is called ] giraArap , (Mgh, TA,) or thereabout, (Mgh,) of dates or flour: or, accord. to Zeyd Ibn-Kuthweh, like qawosN , signifying the quantity of the fourth part of the jul~ap , of dates: (TA:) or, accord. to the Tekmileh, [the pl.] rizamN signifies the [ sacks called ] garaAy^ir , in which is wheat: and hence the rizam of clothes [explained in what here follows. (Mgh.) ― -b2- A kaArap [or bundle, put in one piece of cloth and tied up, ] of clothes; (S, Msb, TA;) what are tied up in one piece of cloth, (K, TA,) of clothes: (TA:) or clothes, and other things, put together [ in a bundle ]; as also ↓ razomapN : (Mgh:) IAmb explains it as meaning the thing in which are sorts ( Durawb ) and mixtures of clothes: and hence the author of the K has taken a meaning assigned by him to rizomapN , which, he says, is also written ↓ razomapN , namely, DarobN $adiydN [ a vehement beating ], altering and substituting: (TA:) the pl. of rizomapN is rizamN . (S, Msb.)

definition: A man strong and stubborn.
sourceDefinition: A man strong and stubborn. (K.) ruzaAmN , [a mistranscription, app. for ↓ raz~aAmN , for it must be with teshdeed to the z , as is shown by an ex. in a copy of the S, consisting of two verses, of which the former here follows,] as an epithet applied to a man, means Stubborn, behaving with forced hardness or hardiness: it occurs, accord. as some relate it, in the saying of a rájiz, [so in the S and TA, but correctly, a poet using the sixth species of the metre termed Als~ariyE ,] which others relate thus: ↓ A^ayaA baniY Eabodi manaAfi Alr~uz~aAmo A^anotumo HumaApN waA^abuwkumu HaAmN [ O sons of 'Abd-Menáf, the firm, or steadfast, upon the ground, (accord. to this reading; but accord. to the reading that seems to be raz~aAmo , the stubborn, &c., as a sing., referring to 'AbdMenáf himself;) ye are defenders, and your father was a defender, HaAmo being for HaAmK ]: ruz~aAm being pl. of raAzimN . (So in one of my two copies of the S: in the other copy omitted.)

sourceDefinition: A sect who said that the office of Imám, after 'Alee, belonged to Mohammad Ibn-El-Hanafeeyeh, and then to his son 'Abd-Allah, and who accounted lawful those things that are [ esteemed by the orthodox ] forbidden: (KT:) or a sect of the extravagant zealots of the class of innovators, of the schismatics, or followers of 'Alee, who say that the office of Imám belonged to Aboo-Muslim El-Khurásánee, after El-Man- soor, and some of whom arrogated to themselves divinity, one of them being El-Mukanna', who made the moon to appear to them in Nakhshab, and of whose persuasion there is in this day a party in Má-wará-en-Nahr. (TA.)
