sourceDefinition: is a name of The right star [app. γ , i. e. Bellatrix, ] in the left arm of Aljab~aAr [or Orion ]. (Kzw. [Golius says, as on the authority of Kzw, that it is “ a star in the right shoulder of Orion: ” but Kzw says that this star (which is a of Orion) is called manokibu AljawozaA='i and yadu AljawozaA='i ; and then he mentions that in the left arm, as being called Almrzm : whence it seems that Golius was misled by the omission of some words in a copy of the work of Kzw.]) And AlmirozamaAni , (S, K,) also called mirozamaA Al$~iEorayayoni , (S,) is the name of Two stars [ of which one is commonly known as B of Canis Major, and the other is app. B of Canis Minor, though Golius says, on the authority of Ulugh Beg, that the former is in the right hind leg of Canis Major, ] with the $iEorayaAni [by which latter appellation are meant Sirius and Procyon ], (K,) or one of which is in [or by ] Al$~iEoraY [commonly so called, i. e. Sirius, ] and the other is in Al*~iraAE [by which is meant Al*~iraAE AlmaqobuwDap , i. e. the asterism consisting of a and B of Canis Minor ]; (S;) or one of them is Al*rAE AlmqbwDp [mentioned above and the other is Al$~iEoraY (q. v.) commonly so called]: thus says Ibn-Kunáseh: both are of the stars of rain: and sometimes the sing. appellation ( Almirozamu ) is used [app. as applied to Sirius, or to Bellatrix, or perhaps to B of Canis Minor]. (TA.) nawo'u Almirozami [means The auroral setting of some one of the stars above mentioned; for it] is so termed because of its intense cold. (TA. See 1.) Als~amaAku Almirozamu is another name for Als~imaAku Alr~aAmiHu [ The star Arcturus ]. (Az and TA in art. rmH . [This star neither sets nor rises aurorally in the cold season, nor is it one of the Mansions of the Moon; but it rises aurorally during “ the first of the rains, ” the autumnal rain, called AlwasomiY~ .]) ― -b2- A^um~u mirozamK (tropical:) The north wind: (S, K, TA:) or the cold north wind: (Skr, on a verse of Sakhr-el-Gheí:) from razaAmapu Aln~aAqapi meaning “ the [gentle] yearning cry of the she-camel: ” (TA:) or it signifies, (ISd, TA,) or signifies also, (K,) the wind: (ISd, K, TA:) thus expl. by ISd without any restriction. (TA.)

(IDrd, O.)

And raqada Alv~awobu , inf. n. raqodN and ruqaAdN , (TA,) (tropical:) The garment became old and worn out, and no longer of use; (A, * TA;) like naAma . (A.) And raqadati Als~uwqu (tropical:) The market became stagnant, or dull, with respect to traffic; like naAmat . (Th, TA.) And raqada AlHar~u (tropical:) The heat remitted, or subsided. (TA. [See also rakada .])

definition: [The hare; and now applied to the rabbit also;] a certain animal, (TA,) well known, (M, A, K, TA,) like the EnAq [?], having short fore legs and long hind legs, that treads the ground with the hinder...
sourceDefinition: [The hare; and now applied to the rabbit also;] a certain animal, (TA,) well known, (M, A, K, TA,) like the EnAq [?], having short fore legs and long hind legs, that treads the ground with the hinder parts of its [ hind ] legs: (TA:) a certain very prolific animal, called in Pers. xrkw$ [or xaroGuw$o ]: it is said that it is one year a male and another year a female, and menstruates like women; and its fore legs are shorter than its hind legs: when it sleeps, it keeps its eyes open; and when it is sick, it eats green canes ( qaSab ), and its sickness ceases: (Kzw:) the word is a gen. n., (TA,) of the fem. gender, (Msb, TA,) accord. to El-Jáhidh; (TA;) but (Msb) applied to the male and the female; (M, A, K, TA;) as is also ↓ A^aronabapN , (Msb,) which is a dial. var.: (Mgh, Msb:) or to the female [only]; the male being called xuzazN ; (T, M, K, TA;) accord. to Lth; but others allow its application to the male: (T:) the female is also called Eikori$apN : and the young, xironiqN : (TA:) the pl. is A^araAnibu (T, S, M, Msb, K) and A^araAnK , (Lh, S, M, K,) the latter, like vaEaAlK for vaEaAlibu , occurring in poetry, (S, M, *) and not allowed by Sb except in poetry. (M.) The A in A^aronabN is augmentative, accord. to Lth: accord. to most of the grammarians it is disjunctive, (so in a copy of the T and in the TA,) or radical: (so in another copy of the T:) Lth says that no word commences with a radical A but such as is triliteral; as A^aroDN and A^aro$N . (T, TA.) [Hence,] one says of the low, abject, or ignominious, and weak, A_in~amaA huwa A^aronabN [ He is only a hare ]; because that animal cannot defend itself, and even the lark will endeavour to make it its prey. (A, TA.) See another ex. below, voce A^aronabapN . [Hence, also,] AlA^aronabu is the name of (assumed tropical:) A certain constellation, [ Lepus, ] comprising twelve stars in its figure, having no observed stars around it, situate beneath the feet of Aljab~aAr [i. e. Orion ], and facing the west. (Kzw.) ― -b2- Also, (K,) or ↓ maronabN accord. to the L, (TA,) or both, (M,) and ↓ yaronabN , A jura* [or large field-rat ], (M, L, K,) like the jerboa, (M, L,) having a short tail. (M, L, K.) ― -b3- AlA^aronabu AlbaHoriY~u , accord. to Kzw, A certain marine animal, the head of which is like that of the A^aronab [or hare ], and the body like that of a fish: or, accord. to Ibn-Seenà, a small testaceous animal, which is of a poisonous quality when drunk [app. meaning in water ]: so that, accord. to this explanation, the resemblance [to the Arnb commonly so called] is in the name, not the form. (TA.) -A2- Also A sort of ornament worn by women. (M, K.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. rahonN , (S, TA,) or ruhuwnN , (Msb,) It (a thing, S, Msb, TA) continued, subsisted, lasted, endured, remained, or remained fixed or stationary; it was, or became, permanent, constant, firm, steady, stead fast, stable, fixed, fast, settled, or established. (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA.) This is the primary signification. (Mgh, TA. *) ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh,) rahana biAlmakaAni (tropical:) He remained, stayed, dwelt, or abode, in the place. (A, Mgh, TA.) ― -b3- And rahana , (JK, S, K,) aor. , (K, TA,) or , (JK, [but this I think to be a mis take,]) inf. n. ruhuwnN , (K,) said of a man, and of a camel, (JK, S, * TA,) and of any beast (TA,) He was, or became, lean, or emaciated; (JK, S, K, TA;) and fatigued, tired, weary, or jaded. (JK, TA.) You say, rakiba Hat~aY rahana He rode until he became lean, or emaciated. (ISh, TA. [See raAhinN .]) -A2- As trans., see 4, first signification. ― -b2- [Hence,] as a law term, rahonN signifies The putting, or placing, an article of real property [ to remain ] as a pledge, or security, or making it to be such, for a debt that is obligatory or that will become obligatory. (TA.) You say, rahanahu Al$~aYo'a , and rahanahu Einodahu , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. rahonN (Msb, TA) [and rahiynapN , q. v. voce rahonN ]; and ↓ Arhnhu Al$~aYo'a ; (S, K;) all signify the same; (S;) i. e. He deposited the thing with him (Msb, K) [ as a pledge ] to be in lieu of that which he had taken, or received, from him: (K:) [i. e. he pledged the thing to him, or with him: ] and rahanotu AlmataAEa biAld~ayoni , inf. n. rahonN , I restricted the commodity or placed it in custody, for, or by reason of, the debt; and bAldyn ↓ Arhnthu is a dial. var. thereof, but of rare occurrence, and disallowed by those who are held in esteem: (Msb:) for, properly, they say, (Msb,) zayodFA Alv~awoba ↓ A^arohanotu signifies I gave to Zeyd the garment, or piece of cloth, in order that he should deposit it as a pledge (Msb, K *) with some one. (Msb.) 'Abd-Allah Ibn Hemmám Es-Saloolee says, (S,) or Hemmám Ibn-Murrah, (TA,) maAlikaA ↓ najawotu wa A^arohanotuhumo falam~aA xa$iytu A^aZaAfiyrahumo [ And when I dreaded their nails, I escaped, and gave them, or left with them, as a pledge, Málik ]: thus, says Th, all relate the verse, except As, who says wa A^arohanuhumo mAlkA [i. e. leaving with them, as a pledge, Málik ]: he likens this phrase to the say ing qumotu wa A^aSuk~u wajohahu ; and this is a good way of explaining it; for the w is that which is a deno tative of state; the meaning being SaAk~FA wajohahu : [accord. to the former reading, in the opinion of Th,] the poet means I left Málik remaining with them; not as a pledge; because [when the leaving a thing as a pledge is meant, in his opinion,] one does not say, Al$~aYo'a ↓ A^arohanotu , but only rahanotuhu . (S, TA.) [See, however, 4.] You say also, rahanahu Eanohu , inf. n. rahonN , meaning He made him, or it, to be a pledge in lieu of him, or it: a poet, asserted by IJ to be a pagan, says, Airohano baniyka Eanohumu A^arohano baniYo [ Make thou thy sons to be pledges in lieu of them: in that case I will make my sons to be pledges: baniY being for baniY~a ]. (TA.) And rahanotuhu lisaAniY (assumed tropical:) [ I made my tongue to be as though it were a pledge to him, to be restrained, or to be used, for his sake or benefit ]: in this case one should not say ↓ A^arohanotuhu ; (IAar, K;) though one says thus of a garment, or piece of cloth, [&c.,] as well as rahanotuhu . (TA.)

definition: He made (a thing, Msb,) to continue, subsist, last, endure, remain, or remain fixed or stationary;
sourceDefinition: He made (a thing, Msb,) to continue, subsist, last, endure, remain, or remain fixed or stationary; to be, or become, permanent, can stant, firm, steady, steadfast, stable, fixed, fast, settled, or established; (S, * Mgh, * Msb, K; *) and so ↓ rahana ; (K;) but the former is the more ap proved: (TA:) and also he found it to be so. (Msb.) You say, Arhn lahumu AlT~aEaAma , (T, S, K, TA,) and Al$~araAba , (T, S, TA,) and AlmaAla , (TA,) (tropical:) He continued, or made permanent, to them the food, (T, S, K, TA,) and the beverage, (T, S, TA,) and the property. (TA.) [And accord. to an expla nation of A^urohinato (referring to dates), by 'Alee Ibn Hamzeh, cited in a marginal note in a copy of the S, in art. A^arohana, whb signifies He prepared food, and continued it, or made it permanent. ] ― -b2- [Hence Arhnhu as used by some in another sense of rahanahu :] see 1, in six places. [That it is allowable to use it thus may be inferred from phrases here following.] ― -b3- You say, A^arohanotu maAliY I staked my property. (JK.) And A^arohanuwA bayonahumo xaTarFA They gave, of their own free will, what the party approved, whatever were its amount, to be to them a stake at a race. (TA.) And A^arohanotu bihi waladiY (S, K, *) inf. n. A_irohaAnN , (S,) (assumed tropical:) I made my children to be as a stake for him, or it. (S, K. *) And Arhnhu lilomawoti (assumed tropical:) He resigned him to death. (IAar, TA.) definition: , originally an inf.
sourceDefinition: , originally an inf. n., (Msb,) is syn. with ↓ marohuwnN ; (Mgh, Msb;) i. e. (Msb) it signifies [ A pledge; ] a thing deposited with a person (Msb, * K) to be in lieu of a thing that has been taken, or received, from him; (K;) or a thing that is deposited as a security for a debt: and ↓ rihaAnN has a similar meaning, but is specially applied to a thing that is deposited as a bet, or wager, or stake; and is likewise originally an inf. n.: (Er-Rághib, TA:) ↓ rahiynapN , also, is syn. with rahonN [as meaning the act of giving as a pledge ], like as $atiymapN is syn. with $atomN ; the p being added to give intensiveness to the significa tion: then, like rahonN , it is used as syn. with marohuwnN [in the sense explained above, as will be seen in what follows in this paragraph]; (IAth, TA;) [i. e.] rahiynapN is an inf. n. like $atiymapN , applied to denote the pass. part. n. [used as a subst. pro perly so termed] like rahonN , not as an epithet; (Bd in lxxiv. 41;) [or, in other words,] rahiynapN signifies anything by reason of which a thing [ such as a debt or the like ] is restricted, or appro priated, to oneself; as also ↓ murotahanapN : (K: [I here follow two copies of the K, in which it is said, kul~u maA A@Hotubisa bihi $aYo'N farahiynapN wa murotahanapN : in the CK, and in the copy of the K followed in the TA, farahiynuhu wa murotahanuhu , which perverts the meaning, though ↓ rahiynN and ↓ murotahanN may be used in the same sense as rahiynapN and muzotahanapN , as will be seen in the course of this paragraph: and in the TA, in the place of A@Hotubisa , is put yHbs , meaning yuHobasu : there is, however, this difference between ↓ rahiynapN and ↓ murotahanapN ; that the former properly signifies a thing deposited as a pledge; and the latter, a thing taken, or received, as a pledge: ]) the pl. of rahonN is rihaAnN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and ruhuwnN (Mgh, Msb, K) and ruhunN , (Mgh, K,) this last said to be a pl. of rahonN by Aboo-' Amr Ibn-El-' Alà, but disap proved by Akh, because a word of the measure faEolN has not a pl. of the measure fuEulN except in rare and anomalous instances, though he says that it may be [as it is said to be in the Msb] pl. of rihaAnN , which is pl. of rahonN , (S,) and Fr says that ruhunN is pl. of rihaAnN , but this is denied in the M, because any pl. may not be pluralized except when there is express authority for it and when the case does not admit of any other decision; (TA;) and ruhonN , also, is another pl. of rahonN , (TA,) [or rather it is a contraction of ruhunN ;] and another pl. of rahonN [or rather a quasi-pl. n.] is ↓ rahiynN , (IJ, K,) like as EabiydN is of EabodN : (TA:) the pl. of ↓ rahiynapN is rahaAy^inu . (S, K.) galiqa Alr~ahonu bimaA fiyhi . [ The pledge became, or has become, per manent as a possession, with what was, or is, comprised in it, ] is a prov., applied to him who has fallen into a case from which he cannot hope to escape: it is said in a trad., laA yagolaqui Alr~ahonu , (Meyd,) [i. e. The pledge shall not remain, or let not the pledge remain, in the hand of its receiver when its depositer is able to release it; for] lA is here either negative or prohibitive: you say, galiqa Alr~ahonu , aor. yagolaqu , inf. n. guluwqN [or galaqN ], meaning The pledge remained in the hand of the receiver when the depositor was able to release it: (Nh, cited in a copy of the “ Jámi' es-Sagheer: ”) the trad. means that the receiver of the pledge shall not have a right to it when the depositer has not released it within a certain time: for it was a custom in the Time of Ignorance for the receiver to keep possession of the pledge in this case; but El-Islám abolished it. (Meyd, * Nh.) You say also, huwa rahonN bika*aA and bk*A ↓ rahiynapN He, or it, is [ a person, or thing, ] pledged for such a thing: (IAth, TA:) or taken [ as a pledge ] for such a thing; as also ↓ rahiynN and ↓ murotahanN . (TA.) And A^anaA rahonN bika*aA and ↓ rahiynN and ↓ rahiynapN I am taken [ as a pledge ] for such a thing. (Mgh.) And [hence,] A^anaA laka rahonN bika*aA (JK, TA) and ↓ rahiynapN (TA) I am responsible, or a surety, to thee for such a thing. (JK, TA.) And biqayodihi ↓ rijoluhu rahiynapN [ His leg, or foot, is a pledge for the safe-keeping of his shackle: for if the meaning were marohuwnapN it would be rahiynN , without p ]. (TA.) And Alxaloqu Almawoti ↓ rahaAy^inu [ Mankind, or all created beings, are the pledges of death ]. (TA.) And huwa rahonu yadi Almaniy~api [ He is the pledge of the hand of death, or of fate, or destiny ]; said of one when he has sought, or courted, death. (TA.) And yadiY laka rahonN [ My hand is a pledge to thee ]; by which is meant responsibility, or suretiship. (TA.) And qaborK ↓ A_in~ahu larahiynu [ Verily he is the pledge of a grave, which will render him up on the day of resurrection]. (TA.) It is said in the Kur lxxiv. 41, ↓ kul~u nafosK bimaA kasabato rahiynapN , meaning [ Every soul is a thing ] pledged with God [ for what it shall have wrought; its works being regarded as a debt, for which it will be either released or held in custody to be punished everlastingly]: rhynp being an inf. n. like $atiymapN applied to denote the pass. part. n. [in a manner before mentioned] like rahonN ; for if it were an epithet [i. e. used in the proper sense of a pass. part. n.] the word would be rahiynN . (Bd.) And in lii. 21 of the same, kul~u ↓ A@moriy^K bimaA kasaba rahiynN , i. e. [ Every man is ] pledged ( marohuwnN , Bd, Jel) with God ( Einoda A@ll~`hi ) for what he shall have wrought; so that if he have done good, He will release him; but other wise, He will destroy [or hold in confinement and punish] him; (Bd;) or to be punished for evil, and recompensed for good. (Jel.) And it is said in a trad., biEaqiyqatihi ↓ kul~u gulaAmK rahiynapN [ Every boy that is born is a pledge for his Eqyqp , i. e. for the victim that is to be sacrificed for him when his head is shaven the first time; which is com monly regarded as his ransom from the fire of Hell]: i. e., the Eqyqp is absolutely necessary for him; wherefore he is likened, when not released from it, to a pledge in the hand of the receiver: El-Khattábee says that the best explanation of it is that of Ahmad Ibn-Hambal; that if the Eqyqp be not sacrificed for the boy and he die an infant, he will not intercede for his parents. (TA.) ― -b2- See also what next follows.

definition: Continuing, subsisting, lasting, enduring, remaining, or remaining fixed or stationary, permanent, constant, firm, steady, steadfast, stable, fixed, fast, settled, or established.
sourceDefinition: Continuing, subsisting, lasting, enduring, remaining, or remaining fixed or stationary, permanent, constant, firm, steady, steadfast, stable, fixed, fast, settled, or established. (S, * Mgh, Msb.) You say TaEaAmN raAhinN (S, Mgh) Food that continues, or is permanent, &c. (Mgh.) sourceDefinition: , [aor. yariynu ,] inf. n. rayonN , [in its primary acceptation, app. signifies It was, or became, rusty, or covered with rust. And hence,] It (a garment, or piece of cloth,) was, or became, dirty, or filthy; syn. taTab~aEa . (M, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence also,] rAnt nafosahu , (S, M, K, *) aor. tariynu , inf. n. as above, (S,) His soul [or stomach ] became heavy; or heaved, or became agitated by a tendency to vomit; syn. gavato , (S, M, K,) and xabuvato . (S, K.) ― -b3- And rAn Ealayohi , (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (Msb,) It (anything) covered it; namely, a thing: (M:) or it (anything) overcame him; (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, * Mgh, Msb, K;) as also rAn bihi ; (A'Obeyd, T, S, Mgh, K;) and raAnahu . (A'Obeyd, S, Mgh, K.) [And raAna with yaruwnu for its aor. signifies the same; as will be seen from a verse cited below.] You say of a sin, misdeed, or transgression, ( *anob ,) rAn EalaY qalobihi , (Zj, T, S, Mgh, K,) aor. as above, (Zj, T, S,) inf. n. rayonN (Zj, T, S, M, K) and ruyuwnN , (S, M, K,) It covered his heart: (Zj, T, M:) or it overcame his heart. (S, Mgh, K.) raAna EalaY quluwbihimo maA kaAnuwA yakosibwuna , in the Kur [lxxxiii. 14], means [ What they used to do ] hath become like rust upon the clearness of their hearts, so as to make the knowledge of good from evil to be obscured to them: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or hath covered their hearts: (Zj, T:) or hath overcome their hearts: [or hath spread a blackness upon their hearts; for,] accord. to El-Hasan, it means that sin has followed upon sin so that the heart has become black: (S:) and accord. to Aboo-Mo'adh the Grammarian, and a saying of the Prophet, Alr~ayonu means the heart's becoming black in consequence of sins. (T.) You say also, riyna EalY qalobihi His heart became covered [&c.]. (M.) And riyna bihi He was overcome: (T, Mgh:) or his property was beset by debt: (T:) or he fell into grief, by reason of debt: (M:) or he fell into that from which he could not escape, (AZ, T, S, Mgh, K,) and with which he had not power to cope: (AZ, T, S:) or i. q. AunoquTiEa bihi [i. e. he became disabled from prosecuting his journey, his means having failed him, or his beast breaking down with him or perishing ]; (T, S, M;) so says El-Kanánee El-Aarábee: (T, S:) and he died. (M.) And raAnato bihi Alxamoru , (T,) or rAnt Ealayohi Alxamoru , (S, M, [in one copy of the S AlHum~aY ,]) The wine overcame him; (S, M;) and overwhelmed him: (M:) or overcame his heart and his reason: (T:) and in like manner one says of drowsiness, and of anxiety; by way of comparison. (M.) And rAn Aln~uEaAsu fiY AlEayoni Drowsiness overcame the eye: (S, TA: *) or infected, or pervaded, the eye. (Msb.) Et-Tirimmáh says, maxaAfapa A^ano yaruwna Aln~awomu fiyhimo bisukori sinaAtihimo kul~a Alr~uyuwni [ In fear that sleep might overcome them, by reason of the intoxication of their sensations of drowsiness, with every degree of overcoming ]. (TA. [This, together with a signification assigned to maruwna in art. rwn in the K, shows that raAna signifying “ he, or it, overcame, ” &c., has yaruwna as well as yariynu for its aor.]) And you say also, rAn Ealayohi Almawotu , and rAn bihi , Death took him away. (M.)

sourceDefinition: is of the measure A^afoEalu , (S,) like A^aHomaru : (K:) or, as some say, of the measure faEoyal ; but this is a weak assertion, for it is said that there is no Arabic word of this measure; maroyamu being a foreign proper name, and DahoyaA^ being disputed. (MF, TA.) [In some of its senses it is an epithet, and used as such: in some, app. an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant: and in some, a simple subst.: but in all its senses it is imperfectly decl.; and therefore seems to be originally an epithet.] ― -b2- Brisk, lively, sprightly, agile, or quick. (K.) ― -b3- A man who walks with short steps: (TA:) and short in stature and in step; (K, TA;) likewise applied to a man. (TA.) ― -b4- Ignoble, base, or base-born. (K.) The offspring of fornication or adultery; or the offspring of fornication, begotten on a slave. (Abu-l-Mekárim, TA.) One whose origin, or lineage, is suspected; or an adopted son; or one who claims as his father a person who is not his father; or who is claimed as a son by a person who is not his father; syn. daEiY~N . (S, K.) ― -b5- A devil: (K:) accord. to some, a dial. var. of A^azab~u . (TA.) ― -b6- The hedge-hog. (IAar, K.) ― -b7- A disagreeable, a disapproved, or an abominable, thing or affair. (K.) ― -b8- A calamity, or misfortune. (K.) ― -b9- Much water: (AA, S:) and so A^a*oyabu . (K in art. *yb .) ― -b10- [ A south-easterly wind; i. e.] the [ wind termed ] nakobaA=' [q. v.] that blows between the SabaA and the januwb : (S, M, K:) or the south wind, or a southerly wind; syn. januwbN ; (M, K;) of the dial. of Hudheyl; so affirm Mbr in his “ Kámil ” and IF and Et-Tarábulusee: IAth says that the people of Mekkeh use this appellation much; and it is related to be God's name for what men call the jnwb : Sh says that the people of El-Yemen, and those who voyage upon the sea between Juddah and 'Adan, cali the jnwb by the name of AlA^azoyabu , and know not any other name for it; and that is because it is boisterous, and stirs up the sea, turning it upsidedown: [whence it seems to mean the boisterous, or violent: ] ISh says that *aAtu A^azoyaba signifies any violent wind. (L,TA.) ― -b11- [Hence it appears that it signifies also Violence. ] ― -b12- Also Enmity. (S, K.) ― -b13- And Briskness, liveliness, sprightliness, agility, or quickness: (ISk, S, K, TA:) [see also A^a*oyabu :] it is fem.: one says, mar~a fulaAnN walahu A^azoyabu munokarapN [ Such a one passed having a disapproved briskness, &c.]: this is said when one passes quickly by reason of briskness, &c. (ISk, S.) ― -b14- And Fear, or fright: (AZ, S, K:) and so A^a*oyabu . (K in art. *yb .) One says, A^axa*aniY mino fulaAnK AlA^azoyabu [ Fear, or fright, arising from such a one, seized me ]. (AZ, S.)

definition: A lion stretching himself when about to spring or leap.
sourceDefinition: A lion stretching himself when about to spring or leap. (S, K.) ― -b2- A quick camel: pl. sibaToraAtN : it has no broken pl. (Sb, M.) ― -b3- Also, the pl. above mentioned, Camels long, upon the surface of the ground [or horizontally ]. (S, K.) The t [says J] is not the denotative of the fem. gender: (S:) it is like that in rijaAlaAtN (S, K) and Ham~aAmaAtN , as masc. pls.: (S:) but IB says, the t in this word is the denotative of the fem. gender; for it is an epithet applied to jimaAlN , which is fem. as a [broken] pl.; as is shown by the saying AljimaAlu saArato , and raEato , &c.: and he adds, J's saying that it is like rjAlAt and Hm~AmAt is a mistake, inasmuch as he confounds rjAlAt with Hm~AmAt ; for rijaAlN is a fem. pl., as is shown by one's saying Alr~ijaAlu xarajato , and saArato ; but Ham~aAmN is masc., and should not regularly have a pl. with A and t , but, as Sb says, it has this pl. form, like some other masc. words, in lieu of a broken pl., and would not have it if it had a broken pl. (TA.) ― -b4- Also the sing., Penetrating; effective; (Lth, M, K;) [as though stretching far; ] sharp in intellect; clever; acute: (K: [in the CK, AlmADiY Als~ahomi is put by mistake for AlmADY Al$~ahomu :]) or sharp in intellect, and very bold or daring or courageous. (TA.) ― -b5- Lank hair. (M.) ― -b6- A man (Sh) lank and tall. (Sh, K.) ― -b7- And with p , A corpulent woman. (M.)

definition: (Lth, T, S, M) and ↓ sit~a , (Lth, T, S, M, K,) the former masc.
sourceDefinition: (Lth, T, S, M) and ↓ sit~a , (Lth, T, S, M, K,) the former masc. and the latter fem., (S,) [signifying Six, ] are originally sidosapN (Lth, T, M) and sidosN ; (Lth, T, S, M, K;) the latter s is changed into t , and the d is incorporated into it; (Lth, T, S, M, K;) for the dim, of sit~apN is sudayosapN [and that of sit~N is sudayosN ], and the pl. is A^asodaAsN . (Lth, T, S.) You say, EinodiY sit~apu rijaAlK wa nisowapK [ I have with me, or at my abode, six men and women ], i. e., three men and three women: and you may say, EinodiY sit~apu rijaAlK wa nisowapN , meaning, six men, and also women: and in like manner you do in the ease of any number that can be divided so as to apply to two plurals, as six and seven and the higher numbers: but in the case of a number that cannot be divided so as to apply to two plurals, as five and four and three, you put the latter noun in the nom. case only, saying, for ex., EinodiY xamosapu rijaAlK wa nisowapN . (ISk, S.) [Respecting a peculiar pronunciation of the people of El-Hijáz, and a case in which sit~ap is imperfectly decl., see valaAvapN and tisoEapF .] ― -b2- sit~apa Ea$ara [indecl. in every case, meaning Sixteen, ] is pronounced by some of the Arabs sit~apa Eo$ara : and [the fem.] sit~a Ea$orapa , thus in the dial. of El-Hijáz [and of most of the Arabs], is pronounced sit~a Ea$irapa in the dial of Nejd. (S in art. E$r .) ― -b3- sit~umiAy^apK [meaning Six hundred ] should be written thus, without separating the two words; because sit~N is originally sidosN and the union of the two words is to compensate for the incorporation of the d into the t . (El-Hareeree, in De Sacy's Anthol. Gramm. Ar., p. 72 of the Arabic text.)

definition: and ↓ sayosabaY , (K,) or the former and ↓ sayosabaA='u , which is mentioned by Th, (M,) A kind of tree;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ sayosabaY , (K,) or the former and ↓ sayosabaA='u , which is mentioned by Th, (M,) A kind of tree; (M, K;) accord. to AHn, it grows from its seeds, and becomes tall, but does not endure the winter; it has leaves like those of the difolaY [q. v.], beautiful; people sow it in the gardens, desiring its beauty; and it has a produce like the oblong pericarps ( xaraAy^iT ) of sesame, but thinner: (M, TA:) AHn adds that, when its pericarps dry, it makes a rustling sound ( a sound such as is termed xa$oxa$ap ) [ in the wind ], like the [ species of cassia called ] Ei$oriq : (TA:) [the sesbania Aegytiaca of Persoon; æschynomene sesban of Linn.; (Delile, Flor. Aegypt. Illustr., no. 682;) dolichos sesban of Forskål (in his Flora Aegypt. Arab, p. lxx., no. 362):] AHn further says, waHakaY Alfar~aA='u fiyhi sayosabFA : (M, TA:) [this may perhaps mean that Fr has mentioned, as a var. of this word, ↓ sayosabN , as it is in the accus. case: but I think that the right reading is ↓ sayosabFY , and also sayosabaY , (which last has been mentioned above on the authority of the K,) for it is immediately added in the TA, “ it is masc. and fem., ” app. indicating that it is with, and without, tenween: then it is there further and strangely added, “ it is brought from India: ”] a rájiz uses the form ↓ Als~ayosabaA , at the end of a verse, for Als~ayosabaAna , necessarily eliding [the n for the sake of the rhyme]. (M, TA.)

definition: (S, M, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (S, M, Msb, K, &c.) and Ealayohi (M, Msb, K,) aor. yasoTuw , (Msb,) inf. n. saTowN (S, M, Msb, K) and saTowapN , (M, Msb, K,) or the latter is an inf. n. un., (S,) He sprang, or rushed, upon him; made an assault, or attack, upon him; syn. SaAla : (M, K:) he sprang upon him and seized him violently or laid violent hands upon him: (Bd in xxii. 71:) he seized him violently with uplifted hand: (Er-Rághib, TA:) he overbore him, overpowered him, or subdued him, ( qaharahu , Lth, S, Msb, K, or taTaAwala Ealayohi , T, TA,) by seizing him violently, or laying violent hands upon him, (Lth, S, K,) and abased him; or he seized him with great violence: (Msb:) or he stretched forth his hand to him [ to seize him ]. (Th, M, TA.) And in like manner, (M,) one says of a stallion [camel], yasoTuw EalaY Taruwqatihi [ He springs, or rushes, upon, or he overbears, the she-camel that he covers ]. (S, M. *) ― -b2- saTaA EalaY Aln~aAqapi , (S, M, K,) and Alfarasi , inf. n. saTowN and suTuw~N , (M,) He (the pastor) put his hand into the raHim [or vulva ] of the she-camel, (S, M, K,) and of the mare, (M,) to extract, (S, K,) or and extracted, (M,) the sperma of the stallion: (S, M, K:) when this is not extracted, the she-camel does not conceive: (S:) or this is done when she has been leaped by a stallion of low race; or when the sperma is bad, and she has not conceived in consequence of it. (M.) And He extracted from her (i. e. a she-camel, TA) the fœtus, dead: (M, TA:) and masaTa signifies “ he extracted the sperma of the stallion: ” thus Az distinguishes between the two verbs. (TA.) Accord. to IAar, one says, saTaA EalaY AlHaAmili , and saATa , which is formed by transposition, meaning He extracted the fœtus, or young one, of the pregnant female. (TA.) And A'Obeyd mentions Als~aTowu as used in relation to a woman: it is said in a trad. of El-Hasan, laA baA^osa A^ano yasoTuwa Alr~ajulu EalaY AlmaroA^api [ There is, or will be, no harm in the man's extracting the fœtus of the woman ]; (M, TA;) which Lth explains by saying, when her child sticks fast in her belly, dead, it may be extracted [by him] when fear is entertained for her and a woman is not found to do this. (TA.) ― -b3- saTaA said of a horse, (M, K,) inf. n. saTowN , (M,) He went at random, heedlessly, or in a headlong manner, not obeying guidance. (M, K.) ― -b4- Also, said of a horse, He went with wide step: (S, M, K:) or raised his tail in running; the doing of which is approved. (M.) ― -b5- Also (tropical:) It was, or became, abundant, or copious; said of water. (S, M, Msb, K, TA.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) He tasted food; (K, TA;) and took it with the hand, or with the extended hand. (TA.) ― -b7- And i. q. EaAqaba [app. as meaning He punished: see saTowapN , below]. (M, TA.) ― -b8- And saTaAhaA He compressed her; [and so saTaA^ahaA and $aTaA^ahaA ;] on the authority of Aboo-Sa'eed. (TA.)

(S, M. *) ― -b2- saTaA EalaY Aln~aAqapi , (S, M, K,) and Alfarasi , inf. n. saTowN and suTuw~N , (M,) He (the pastor) put his hand into the raHim [or vulva ] of the she-camel, (S, M, K,) and of the mare, (M,) to extract, (S, K,) or and extracted, (M,) the sperma of the stallion: (S, M, K:) when this is not extracted, the she-camel does not conceive: (S:) or this is done when she has been leaped by a stallion of low race; or when the sperma is bad, and she has not conceived in consequence of it. definition: [originally inf.
sourceDefinition: [originally inf. n. of saliEa , q. v.,] Marks left by fire upon the skin. (TA.) -A2- A certain kind of bitter tree; (S, K;) which, in the Time of Ignorance, was used in one or the other of the manners described above in the explanations of tasoliyEN ; (K, TA;) or they used, in the case of drought, or barrenness of the earth, to hang somewhat of this tree and of the Eu$ar to the tails *unaAbaY [a sing. used as a pl.]) of [wild] bulls or cows, then to kindle fire therein, and make them to ascend upon the mountain; and thus, they assert, they used to obtain rain: (S, TA:) the author of the K says that J has made a mistake in saying *nAbY , in the above-cited passage; that he should have said A^a*onaAb ; but others had made this remark before the author of the K; and 'Abd-El-Kádir Ibn-'Omar El-Baghdádee says that the mistake is to be imputed to these, and not to J, who has only used a sing. in the sense of a pl., like as Ald~ubura is used in the Kur [liv. 45], for AlA^adobaAra : (MF, TA:) AHn cites an Arab of the desert, of the saraAp , as saying that the slE grows near to a tree, and then clings to it, and climbs it, with long, green, leafless shoots, twining upon the branches and interweaving themselves, and having a fruit like bunches of grapes, which is small, and, when ripe, becomes black, and is eaten only by the monkeys, or apes, not by men, nor by the beasts that are left to pasture at their pleasure; and adding, I have not tasted it, but I think that it is bitter; and when it is broken, there flows from it a viscous fluid, clear, and having strings: such is the description of the man of the srAp : (TA:) or it is a certain poisonous plant, (K, TA,) not to be tasted, like zaroE [here meaning wheat or barley ] when it first comes forth, scantily scattered in the ground, and having a small, yellow, prickly leaf, its prickles being downy; it is a herb, or leguminous plant, which spreads itself upon the surface of the ground, like [ the plant called ] raAHapu Alkalobi , having no root, and it is not improbable that the ostrich may feed upon it, notwithstanding its bitterness, for it sometimes feeds upon the colocynth: (Aboo-Ziyád, TA:) or it is a species of aloes: (K:) or a herb, or leguminous plant, (K, TA,) of those termed *ukuwr [ that are hard and thick, or thick, and inclining to bitterness, or thick and rough ], (TA,) of bad, or nauseous, or disgusting, taste: (K, TA:) so says Aboo-Nasr: (TA:) [Forskål found this name applied in El-Yemen to the sælanthus quadragonus: (Flora Ægypt. Arab., pp. cv. and 33:) and the cacalia sonchifolia: (Ibid., p. cxix.:) and the name of saE A^aboyaD , or salaE Albaqar , to the senecio hadiensis. (Ibid., pp. cxix. and 149.)]

sourceDefinition: [ A ganglion; ] a thing like the gud~ap , that comes forth upon the body, or person; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ saloEapN , (K,) which is the form of the word now commonly known, (TA,) and ↓ salaEapN , (K,) and ↓ silaEapN : (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) or an excrescence (S, Mgh, K) of flesh, (Mgh,) that arises in the body, (S, Mgh, K,) or a [ kind of spontaneous swelling that comes forth upon the body, such as is termed ] xuraAj , (Msb,) like the gud~ap , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) that moves about when moved, (S, Msb, K,) or moves to and fro between the skin and the flesh, (Mgh,) and varies from [ the size of ] a chick-pea to [ that of ] a melon; (S, K;) also termed DawaApN : (S:) the physicians say that it is a thick tumour, not adhering to the flesh, moving about when moved, having a cyst, or case which encloses it, and capable of increase, because it is extrinsic to the flesh, wherefore the doctors of practical law allow its being cut off, when it is safe to do so: (Msb:) or a xuraAj [vide suprà] in the neck: (K:) or a gud~ap in the neck: (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) pl. silaEN . definition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) first pers.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) first pers. samawotu , like Ealawotu , (S,) aor. yasomuw , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. sumuw~N ; (S, M, K;) and samiYa , first pers. samiytu , (Th, S, TA,) like Ealiytu ; (S;) He, (a man, Th, S,) or it, (a thing, M,) was, or became, high, lofty, raised, upraised, uplifted, upreared, exalted, or elevated; it rose, or rose high: (S, M, Msb, K:) and ↓ tsAmY signifies the same. (MA. [See also 5.]) ― -b2- samaAliYa Al$~aYo'u The thing became raised from afar so that I plainly distinguished it: (K:) or, as in the S, samaA liYa Al$~axoSu the form, or figure, seen from a distance, rose, or became raised, to me [i. e. to my view ] so that I plainly distinguished it. (TA.) ― -b3- samaA AlhilaAlu The moon near the change rose murotafiEFA [app. meaning upreared, not decumbent: see A^adofaqu ]. (TA.) ― -b4- [ samaA lahu or naHowahu He rose, and betook himself, to, or towards, him, or it. Hence,] maAsamawotu lakumo I will not [or (unless the phrase be an apodosis) I did not ] rise and hasten to fight you. (TA.) ― -b5- samaA baSarahu His sight, or eye, rose, or became raised. (S, TA.) [And samaATarofuhu lit. signifies the same; but means (assumed tropical:) His look was lofty; or he was proud: see saAmK , below.] ― -b6- samaA is also said of him who is termed HasiybN and $ariyfN [i. e. it signifies He was, or became, noble; or high, or exalted, in rank ]. (TA.) ― -b7- samatp him~atuhu A_ilaY maEaAliY AlA^umowri [ His ambition soared, or aspired, to high things, or the means of attaining eminence; ] he sought glory, or might, and eminence. (Msb, TA.) ― -b8- samaAbiY $awoqa baEoda A^ano kaAna A^aqoSara [ A yearning, or longing, of the soul arose in me after it had ceased ]. (TA.) ― -b9- humo yasomuwna EalaY AlmiAy^api They exceed [or are above ] the number of a hundred. (TA.) ― -b10- samawoA , (S, K, TA,) and ↓ AstmwA , (S,) They went forth to pursue the animals of the chase (S, K, TA) in their deserts: (TA:) [or] one says of the hunter, or sportsman, yasomuw AlwaHo$a , and ↓ yasotamiyhaA , meaning he sees, or looks to see, ( yataEay~anu ,) the coming forth of the wild animals, and pursues them. (M. [See also 8 below.]) ― -b11- samaA AlfaHolu , inf. n. samaAwapN , The stallion sprang, or rushed, upon, (S,) or he overbore, (S, * M, K,) his she-camels that had passed seven or eight months since the period of their bringing forth. (S, M, K.) -A2- samaAbihi : see 4. -A3- See also 2.

definition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) accord.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) accord. to Sb originally with b , but Lh says that the former is that which is usual, (M,) [inf. n. tasomiyapN ,] and in like manner ↓ AsmAhu , (S,) i. e. AsmAhu fulaAnFA and bifulaAnK , (M, K,) and accord. to Th, fulaAnFA ↓ samaAhu and bifulaAnK , (K, [in the correct copies of which the form of the verb first mentioned is without teshdeed, while in the CK the first and last are both alike with teshdeed, or, as is said in the M, Th has mentioned samawotuhu , but none other has mentioned it,]) He named him, or called him, Such a one; (S, M, Msb, K;) as Zeyd; i. e., he made Zeyd to be his name, his proper name. (Msb.) ― -b2- [One says also, sm~Y A@ll~`ha EalaY $aYo'K , or simply sm~Y Ealayohi , which is the more common, meaning He pronounced the name of God, saying bisomi A@ll~`hi ( In the name of God ), upon, or over, a thing; such as food, and an animal about to be slaughtered.] The Prophet said, sam~uwA wasam~ituwA wadan~uwA , [cited, with some variations, and expl., in arts. dnw and smt ,] meaning sam~uwA A@ll~`ha [ Pronounce ye the name of God, &c.]; i. e. whenever ye eat, [before ye begin to do so, accord. to the general custom, or] between two mouthfuls. (M.)

definition: , (S, M, K, TA,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, K, TA,) inf. n. musaAmaApN , (TA,) He vied, competed, or contended for superiority, in highness, loftiness, or eminence, or in glory, or excellence, [or in an absolute sense,] with him; syn. EaAlaAhu , (M,) or faAxarahu , and baAraAhu . (K.) It is said in the trad. respecting the lie [against 'Áïsheh], lamo takuni A@moraA^apN tusaAmiyhaA gayoru zayonaba , meaning There was not any woman that vied with her in eminence ( tufaAxiruhaA and tuEaAliyhaA ) except Zeyneb; AlmusaAmaApu meaning AlmuTaAwalapu fiY AlHuiZowapi . (TA.) And one says, fulaAnN laA yusaAmaY waqado EalaA mano saAmaAhu [ Such a one will not be vied with in highness, &c.: and he has overcome him who vied with him, &c.]. (S.) And A_in~a A^amaAmiY maA laA A^usaAmiY , said when one fears an affair, or event, before him; on the authority of IAar; meaning [ Verily before me is an affair, or event, ] with which I cannot vie. (M.) A poet cited by Th says, baAta A@bonu A^adomaA='a yusaAmiY AlA^anodaraA saAmaY TaEaAma AlHaY~i Hat~aY naw~araA and he says that saAmaY means AirotafaEa , and SaEida ; but [it seems that the verse should be rendered, Ibn-Admà passed the night aspiring to reach the heap of reaped wheat: he aspired to attain the wheat of the tribe until it attained to maturity: for ISd says,] in my opinion he means, as the seed-produce rose by growth, he rose to it, until it attained to maturity, when he reaped it and stole it: and he cites also the saying, faA@rofaEo yadayoka vum~a saAmi AlHanojaraA [ And raise thy hands, then endeavour to reach the windpipe ]; explaining saAmi AlHanojara as meaning raise thy hands to his Haloq [or throat, properly, fauces ]. (M.)

definition: He raised, upraised, uplifted, upreared, exalted, or elevated, him, or it;
sourceDefinition: He raised, upraised, uplifted, upreared, exalted, or elevated, him, or it; as also bihi ↓ samaA [lit. he rose, &c., with him, or it ]. (M, K.) ― -b2- A^asomayotuhu mino baladK I made him to go up, or away, from a town, or country. (TA.) ― -b3- AsmAnA , (TA,) or ↓ AisotamaAnaA , (M,) He, or it, incited us to hunt, or chase: so says Th. (M, TA.) -A2- Also He looked at, or towards, his, or its samaAwap [expl. immediately before the mention of this phrase in the M as meaning the form, or figure, seen from a distance, and the aspect, of anything]. (M, TA.) -A3- And AsmY He (a man) took the direction of, (S,) or came to, (M,) Es-Semáweh ( Als~amaAwap , S, M) a certain water in the desert ( AlbaAdiyap , M) or a place between El-Koofeh and Syria, (K,) a well-known desert. (TA.) -A4- See also 2.

sourceDefinition: He (a hunter, or sportsman, [ AlS~AEidu in the CK being a mistranscription for AlS~aAy^idu ,]) attired himself with the socks, or stockings, called misomaAp , (M, K, TA,) to protect himself from the heat of the burning ground, (TA,) for the hunting of gazelles, in the time of heat. (M.) And (M, in the K “ or ”) AstmAhu He asked of him the loan of the socks, or stockings, above named, for that purpose, (M, K, *) i. e. for the hunting of gazelles at midday. (TA.) And AstmY , (M, CK,) or AstmY AlZ~ibaA='a , (so in some copies of the K and in the TA,) He sought, or pursued, the gazelles in their caves, or hiding-places, ( faY giyraAnihaA , M, and so in copies of the K, by the giyraAn being meant the kunus , M,) or in what was not their time, or season, ( fiY gayori A@nihaA , thus in some copies of the K,) at the auroral rising of Canopus ( suhayol [which rose aurorally, in Central Arabia, about the commencement of the era of the Flight, on the 4th of August, O. S.]): (M, K:) so says IAar. (M.) [Freytag says, on the authority of scholia to the Deewán of Jereer, as follows: In the time of the greatest heat, they drive out a wild animal repeatedly from its hiding-place, permitting it to return thither at night, when, thus disturbed, it does not issue from its place; in order that they may be able to strike it.] ― -b2- And He hunted, or chased, wild animals. (M.) ― -b3- See also 1, latter part, in two places. ― -b4- And see 4. -A2- Aisotamayotuhu also signifies I made him the object of a visit: or I perceived in him good, or goodness, by a right opinion formed from its outward signs. sourceDefinition: The higher, or upper, or highest, or uppermost, part of anything: [in this sense] masc. (M.) ― -b2- [In its predominant acceptation,] a word of well-known meaning; (K, TA;) i. e. (TA) [The sky, or heaven; ] the canopy of the earth: (M, Msb, TA:) in this sense (M, Msb) masc. and fem.; (IAmb, S, M, Msb, K; *) sometimes fem.; (M;) rarely so, and thus as having the next but one of the significations here following: (Fr, Msb:) Az says that it is fem. because it is pl. [or coll. gen. n.] of samaA='apN : (TA:) or it is as though it were pl. of ↓ samaAwapN , [or rather its coll. gen. n.,] like as saHaAbN is of saHaAbapN : (Msb, TA:) Er-Rághib says that the samaA=' as opposed to the A^aroD is fem., and sometimes masc.; and is used as a sing. and as a pl.; as the latter in the Kur ii. 27 [where it is shown to apply to seven heavens]; and that it is like naxolN and $ajarN and other [coll.] gen. ns.: (TA:) in this sense (M) the pl. is A^asomiyapN [a pl. of pauc.] (S, M, K) and sumiY~N , (M, K,) the latter [originally sumuwYN ] of the measure fuEuwlN , and both [also] pls. of samaA='N in another sense, mentioned in what follows, (TA,) and samaAwaAtN or sam`waAtN , (S, M, Msb, K,) and accord. to the K, [in which all of these are mentioned as though pls. of samaA='N in all its senses,] ↓ samFA , [in the CK sumFA ,] but in the M samaA='N [like the sing., as mentioned above], where it is said that it must be a pl. in the Kur ii. 27 for the reason already stated, as though pl. of samaA='apN or samaAwapN ; (TA;) and a poet assigns to samaA='N the anomalous pl. samaA='K , by his saying, samaA='u A@loA_il`hi fawoqa saboEi samaA=y^iyaA [ The heaven of God, above seven heavens ]: (S, M:) the dim. is ↓ sum~y~apN . (Ham p. 452.) ― -b3- And Any canopy, or covering over-head, of a person. (S, Msb, * TA.) ― -b4- And hence, (S, TA,) The ceiling, or roof, (S, Msb, K, TA,) of a house, or chamber, or tent, (S, K, TA,) and of anything; (K, TA;) in this sense masc.; (Msb, TA;) and ↓ samaAwapN also has this meaning. (S.) ― -b5- And The riwaAq , (M, K,) i. e. the $uq~ap [or oblong piece of cloth ] that is beneath the upper, or uppermost, $uq~apN , (M,) of a bayot [or tent]; (M, K;) in which sense it is fem., and sometimes masc.; (M;) as also ↓ samaAwapN ; (M, K;) [and so, app., ↓ simaAyapN ; for] one says, A^aSolaHa simaAyatahu , with kesr, [ He repaired his smAyp ,] meaning, his samaAwap . (TA.) ― -b6- And The clouds; (Zj, K;) because of their height: (Zj, TA:) or a cloud. (Msb.) ― -b7- And Rain; (S, M, Msb, K;) because it comes forth from the samaA=' [i. e. sky or clouds]: (TA:) or a good rain ( maTorapN jay~idapN ): (K, TA:) or a new rain ( maTorapN jadiydapN ): (T, TA:) or, as some say, rain that has not fallen upon the earth; so called in consideration of what has been said above [of its meaning the “ clouds ” &c.]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [but] one says, maA zilonaA naTaA^u Als~amaA='a Hat~aY A^atayonaAkumo [ We ceased not to tread upon the rain until we came to you ]: (S, TA:) applied to rain, it is masc., and fem. also because of its connexion with the samaA=' that canopies the earth; (M;) or it is fem., as meaning saHaAbapN : (Msb:) the pl. [of mult.] is sumiY~N (S, M, Msb, TA) and [of pauc.] A^asomiyapN . (S, TA.) banuw maA='i Als~amaA='i is an appellation of The Arabs; [signifying the sons of the water of the heaven; ] because of their keeping much to the deserts which are the places of the falling of rain [by means of which they subsist]: or by maA=' AlsmA=' is meant Zemzem, which God made to well forth for the Arabs, who are therefore like the sons thereof. (TA.) ― -b8- [Hence, app., as being likened to rain by reason of the swiftness of his running,] a certain horse, (M, K,) belonging to Sakhr the brother of El-Khansà, (M,) was named Als~amaA='u . (M, K.) ― -b9- [Hence, likewise, as being likened to rain, (assumed tropical:) Bounty. ] One says, A^aSaAbaniY bira$oHapK mino samaAy^ihi (assumed tropical:) [ He gave me a gift from his store of bounty ]. (A in art. r$H .) ― -b10- Also (assumed tropical:) Herbage; because produced by the rain, which is thus called. (TA.) ― -b11- And The back of a horse; (S, Msb, K;) because of its height: coupled with [its opposite] A^aroDN [q. v.]. (S, TA.) ― -b12- And of a sandal, [in like manner opposed to A^aroDN ,] The upper part [ of the sole, i. e. the upper surface thereof ], upon which the foot is placed. (M.) -A2- See also samaAwapN .

sourceDefinition: is an inf. n. of $ajara , and signifies The being, or becoming, intricate, complicated, perplexed, confused, or intricately intermixed; as also ↓ Ai$otijaArN . (TA.) You say, $ajara AlA^amoru bayonahumo , (Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. $ajorN (Msb, TA) and $ujuwrN , (K, TA,) The affair, or case, was, or became, complicated, intricate, or confused, so as to be a subject of disagreement, or difference, between them; syn. AiDoTaraba ; (Msb;) and so $ajara bayonahumo [in which AlA^amoru is understood]; syn. Aixotalafa : (S:) it was, or became, an occasion of contention, or dispute, or of disagreement, or difference, between them. (K, TA.) fiymaA $ajara bayonahumo , in the Kur iv. 68, means Respecting that which hath become complicated, or intricate, or confused, [ so as to be a subject of disagreement, or difference, ] between them: and hence the word $ajarN , [“ trees, ” and “ shrubs, ”] because of the intermixing, or confusion, of the branches: (Bd:) or respecting the disagreement, or difference, that has happened between them. (Zj, Mgh.) And it is said in a trad., A_iy~aAkumo wamaA $ajara bayona A^aSoHaAbiY Avoid ye the disagreement, or difference, that hath occurred among my companions. (TA.) -A2- $ajarahu , (K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. $ajorN , He tied it; namely, a thing. (TA.) ― -b3- $ajarahu Eanohu , (S, A, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. $ajorN , (S,) He, or it, averted, or diverted, him, from it; (S, A, K;) namely, an affair: (K:) he removed, or put away, (TS, K,) him, (K,) or it, (TS,) from it: (TS, K:) he withheld, or debarred, and repelled, him from it. (S, A.) ― -b4- $ajara Albayota , (S, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) He propped up the byt [or tent ] with a pole. (S, K, TA. definition: It was, or became, knit, or connected, together, one part with another;
sourceDefinition: It was, or became, knit, or connected, together, one part with another; as also Ai$otabaka : it was, or became, commingled, one part amid, or within, another; (TA;) and so ↓ t$Ajr : (Ham p. 161:) it was, or became, intricate, complicated, perplexed, confused, or intricately intermixed. (TA: see 1, first sentence.) It is said in a trad., relating to conflict and faction ( fitonap ), ya$otajiruwna fiyhaA A@$otijaAra A^aTobaAqi Alr~aA^osi They become knit together therein, like the knitting together of the bones of the head that interjoin, one with another, one entering into another: or the meaning is, they disagree, or differ, one with another. (TA.) You say, A$tjrwA birimaAHihimo (TA) and bihaA ↓ t$AjrwA (S, A, Msb, TA) They became knit together, or commingled, one with another, [ in conflict, ] with their spears: (TA:) or they thrust, or pierced, one another with their spears. (S, A, Mgh, Msb, TA.) And A$tjrwA (Zj, S, A, Msb, K) and ↓ t$AjrwA (Zj, S, A, Mgh, K) They became commingled, or confused, or embroiled, disagreeing, or differing: (Zj, TA:) they contended, or disputed, together; (S, A, Mgh, Msb;) or disagreed, or differed. (S, * A, * Mgh, Msb, * K.) ― -b2- Also He preceded, outwent, or outstripped; (K, * TA;) and so ↓ An$jr . (K.) ― -b3- And, said of sleep, It withdrew, or kept aloof, from one; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ An$jr . (K.) -A2- Also (S, K) said of a man, (S,) He put his hand beneath his $ajor , against the part beneath his chin: (S:) or he put his hand beneath his chin and leaned upon his elbow, (K, TA,) not laying his side upon the bed. (TA.) ― -b2- [And, said of a horse, He was bridled, reined, or curbed: (Freytag, from the Deewán of the Hudhalees:) or perhaps the verb in this sense is in the passive form:] -A3- see 1, last sentence but two.

sourceDefinition: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ $ijarN and $iyarN , (K,) in which last the j is changed into Y , like as the Y is changed into j , as in ganij~N , originally ganiY~N , or, accord. to IJ, the Y in $iyarN is not changed from j because it remains Y in the dim., in which, where it so changed, it should be changed back into j , whereas the dim. of $iyarapN is said to be $uyayorapN and $iyayorapN , and because it has kesr instead of fet-h to the $ , [whence it appears that IJ knew not $ijarN ,] (TA,) [as coll. gen. ns., Trees; and shrubs, or bushes; which latter are also called, for distinction, diq~u Al$~ajari ; and sometimes applied to plants in general; and, as a gen. n., sometimes meaning the tree, &c.;] the kind of plant that has a trunk, or stem: (S, A, K:) or the kind that has a hard trunk, or stem, (Mgh, Msb,) like the naxol &c.: (Msb:) or such as produces seed, and does not come to an end in its year: (Mgh:) or such as rises, or rises high, of itself, whether slender or large, and whether it withstand the winter or lack strength to do so: (K:) called $ajarN from $ajara , because of the intermixing, or confusion, of the branches: (Bd in iv. 68, and TA: *) n. un. with p , (Msb, K,) i. e. $ajarapN (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) and ↓ $ijarapN and $iyarapN : (TA:) the pl. [of $ajarN ] is A^a$ojaArN (S, Msb) and [of $ajarapN ] $ajaraAtN (Msb, TA) and [of $iyarapN ] $iyaraAtN : (TA:) ↓ $ajoraA='u also signifies the same as $ajarN : (K:) or it is a pl. [or rather a quasi-pl. n.] of $ajarapN ; a pl. [or quasi-pl. n.] of which there are few other instances; qaSobaA='u of qaSabapN , and TarofaA='u of TarafapN , and HalofaA='u of HalafapN ; or, accord. to As, the sing. [or n. un.] of HlfA='u is HalifapN : and accord. to Sb, $ajoraA='u is sing. and pl., and so are qaSobaA='u and TarofaA='u and HalofaA='u : (S:) or $ajoraA='u signifies tangled, or luxuriant, or abundant and dense, $ajar : (A:) or a collection of $ajar . (TA.) ― -b2- $ajarapu Albaq~i &c.: see in arts. bq &c. ― -b3- In the saying in a trad., that the $ajarap and the Saxorap are of, or from, Paradise, by the former is said to be meant The grape-vine: or the tree beneath which allegiance was sworn to the Prophet; and which, it is said, was a $amurap [or gum-acacia-tree]: (TA:) and by the latter, the Sxrp [or rock] of Jerusalem. (TA in art. Sxr , q. v.) ― -b4- By Al$~ajarapu AlT~ay~ibapu , mentioned in the Kur in xiv. 29, is said to be meant The palm-tree: or a certain tree in Paradise: and by Al$~ajarapu Alxabiyvapu , in the next verse but one, the colocynth, and the ka$uwv : [see art. xbv :] or each may have a more general application. (Bd in xiv. 31.) And Al$~ajarapu AlmaloEuwnapu , mentioned in the Kur xvii. 62, means The tree called Alz~aq~uwm : and some explain it as meaning the Devil: and Aboo-Jahl: and El-Hakam Ibn-Abi-l-'As. (A.) [And (assumed tropical:) A genealogical tree; a pedigree. ] ― -b6- Also, (CK,) or ↓ $ajorapN , (O, and K accord. to the TA, [but probably thus in the TA only because found to be so in the O,]) (assumed tropical:) A small speck, or speckle, on the chin of a boy: (O, K:) on the authority of IAar. (TA.) ― -b7- And one says, maA A^aHosana $ajarapa DaroEihaA , (so in my copy of the A, and accord. to the CK,) or DrEhA ↓ $ajorapa , (O, and so accord. to the text of the K as given in the TA, [but Z has, in the A, distinguished the phrase as tropical, and hence it seems that he held the former reading to be the right,]) (tropical:) How goodly are the shape, (A,) or the size, (O, K,) and the appearance, of her udder! Sxr , q. v.) ― -b4- By Al$~ajarapu AlT~ay~ibapu , mentioned in the Kur in xiv. 29, is said to be meant The palm-tree: or a certain tree in Paradise: and by Al$~ajarapu Alxabiyvapu , in the next verse but one, the colocynth, and the ka$uwv : [see art. xbv :] or each may have a more general application. (Bd in xiv. 31.) And Al$~ajarapu AlmaloEuwnapu , mentioned in the Kur xvii. 62, means The tree called Alz~aq~uwm : and some explain it as meaning the Devil: and Aboo-Jahl: and El-Hakam Ibn-Abi-l-'As. definition: He made him to know.
sourceDefinition: He made him to know. (S.) You say, A$Erhu biAlA^amori and AlA^amora , (K,) the latter of which is less usual than the former, because one says $aEara bihi but not $aEarahu , (MF,) He aquainted him with the affair; made him to know it. (K.) And A^a$oEarotu A^amora falaAnK I made known the affair of such a one. (A.) And A^a$oEarotu fulaAnFA I made such a one notorious for an evil deed or quality. (A.) ― -b2- Also, (inf. n. A_i$oEaArN , Msb,) He marked it, namely a beast destined for sacrifice at Mekkeh, (S, * Mgh, Msb, * K, TA,) by stabbing it in the right side of its hump so that blood flowed from it, (S,) or by making a slit in its skin, (K,) or by stabbing it (K, TA) in one side of its hump with a miboDaE or the like, (TA,) so that the blood appeared, (K, TA,) or by making an incision in its hump so that the blood flowed, (Msb,) in order that it might be known to be destined for sacrifice. (S, Msb.) ― -b3- [Hence, app.,] (assumed tropical:) He wounded him so as to cause blood to come. (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting the assassination of 'Othmán, A^a$oEarahu mi$oqaSFA (assumed tropical:) He wounded him so as to cause blood to come with a m$qS [q. v.]: (TA:) and in another trad., A^a$oEira A^amiyru Almuw^ominiyna (assumed tropical:) [ The Prince of the Faithful was wounded so that blood came from him ]. (S.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) He pierced him with a spear so as to make the spearhead enter his inside: and A$Erhu sinaAnFA (tropical:) he made the spear-head to enter into the midst of him: [but this is said to be] from A$Erhu bihi “ he made it to cleave to it. ” (TA.) A^a$oEira is said specially of a king, meaning He was slain. (A, TA.) ― -b5- Also He made it to be a distinguishing sign: as when the performance of a religious service is made, or appointed, by God to be a sign [whereby his religion is distinguished]. (TA.) ― -b6- And A$ErwA They called, uttering their $iEaAr [whereby they might know one another]: or they appointed for themselves a $iEaAr in their journey. (Lh, K, TA. [See also 10.]) -A2- maA A^a$oEarahu [ How good, or excellent, a poet is he ! ]. (TA in art. xzY : see muxozK in that art.) -A3- A$Er [from $aEorN or $aEarN signifying “ hair ”] It (a fœtus, S, A, K, in the belly of its mother, TA) had hair growing upon it; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ t$E~r ; (S, K;) and ↓ $E~r , inf. n. ta$oEiyrN ; and ↓ Ast$Er . (K.) ― -b2- And A$Ert She (a camel) cast forth her fœtus with hair upon it. (Ktr, K.) ― -b3- And A$Er He lined a boot, (A, K,) and a jub~ap , (A,) and the miyvarap of a horse's saddle, and a qalanosuwap , and the like, (TA,) with hair; (A, K;) as also ↓ $aEara ; (Lh, A, K;) and ↓ $E~r , (K,) inf. n. ta$oEiyrN : (TA:) or, said of a myvrp , he covered it with hair. (A.) ― -b4- And A$Erhu He clad him with a $iEaAr [i. e. an innermost garment ]. (S, A, K.) And He put on him a garment as a $iEaAr , i. e., next his body. (TA.) sourceDefinition: [an inf. n., (see 1, first sentence,) and used as a simple subst. signifying] Knowledge; cognizance: (K, TA:) or knowledge of the minute particulars of things: or perception by means of [ any of ] the senses. (TA.) One says, layota $iEoriY fulaAnFA maA SanaEa , (Ks, Lh, S, * Msb, * K, *) and layota $iEoriY lahu maA SanaEa , and layota $iEoriY Eanohu maA SanaEa , (Ks, Lh, K, *) i. e. Would that I knew what such a one did, or has done; (S, * K, * Msb, * TA;) for would that my knowledge were present at, or comprehending, what such a one did, or has done; the phrase being elliptical: (TA:) accord. to Sb, layota $iEoriY is for lyt $iEoratiY , the p being elided as in huwa A^abuw Eu*orihaA [for hw Abw Eu*oratihaA ], (S, TA,) the elision of the p in this latter instance, as Sb says, being peculiar to the case of the words being preceded by Abw ; [but see Eu*orapN ;] and as in A_iqaAmap when used as a prefixed noun; though layota $iEoratiY is not now known to have been heard. A^a$oEaArN . (S, K.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) Falsehood; because of the many lies in poetry. (B, TA.)

definition: [ The star Sirius;
sourceDefinition: [ The star Sirius; ] a certain bright star, also called Almirozamu ; (TA; [but see this latter appellation;]) the star that rises [ aurorally ] after AljawozaA=' [by which is here meant Gemini ], in the time of intense heat, (S, TA,) and after AlhaqoEap [app. a mistranscription for AlhanoEap ]: (TA:) [about the epoch of the Flight, it rose aurorally, in Central Arabia, on the 13th of July, O. S.: (see Aln~avorapu ; and see also manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl :) on the periods of its rising at sunset, and setting aurorally, see dabarN and dabuwrN :] the Arabs say, A_i*aA TalaEati Al$~iEoraY jaEala SaAHibu Aln~axoli yaraY [ When Sirius rises aurorally, the owner of the palm-trees begins to see what their fruit will be]: (TA:) there are two stars of this name; Al$~iEoraY AlEabuwru and Al$~iEoraY AlgumayoSaA='u , (S, K,) together called Al$~iEorayaAni : the former is that [above mentioned] which is in [a mistake for “ after ”] AljawozaA=' , and the latter is [ Procyon, ] in the *iraAE [by which is meant Al*~iraAEu AlmaqobuwDapu , not Al*~iraAEu AlmabosuwTapu ]; (S;) and both together are called the two Sisters of Suheyl ( suhayol [i. e. Canopus ]): (S, K:) the former was worshipped by a portion of the Arabs; and hence God is said in the Kur-án to be Lord of Al$~iEoraY : (TA:) it is called AlEabuwr because of its having crossed the Milky Way; and the other is called AlgumayoSaA=' because said by the Arabs to have wept after the former until it had foul thick matter in the corner of the eye: (K in art. gmS :) the former is also called Al$~iEoraY AlyamaAniy~apu [ the Yemenian, or Southern, $ErY ]; and the latter, Al$~iEoraY Al$~aAmiy~apu [ the Syrian, or Northern, $ErY ]. (Kzw.)

definition: A sign of people in war, (S, Msb, K,) and in a journey (K) &c.
sourceDefinition: A sign of people in war, (S, Msb, K,) and in a journey (K) &c., (TA,) i. e. (Msb) a call or cry, (A, Mgh, Msb,) by means of which to know one another: (S, A, Mgh, Msb:) and the $iEaAr of soldiers is a sign that is set up in order that a man may thereby know his companions: (TA:) and $iEaAr signifies also the banners, or standards, of tribes. (TA in art. brm .) It is said in a trad. that the $iEaAr of the Prophet in war was yaA manoSuwru A^amito A^amito [ O Mansoor, (a proper name of a man, meaning “ aided ” &c.,) kill thou, kill thou ]. (TA.) And it is said that he appointed the $iEaAr of the refugees on the day of Bedr to be yAbaniY Eabodi Alr~aHom`ni : and the $EAr of El-Khazraj, yA baniY Eabodi A@ll~`hi : and that of El-Ows, yaA baniY Eubayodi A@ll~`hi : and their $EAr on the day of El-Ahzáb, H`m= laA yunoSaruwna . (Mgh.) ― -b2- And Thunder; (Tekmileh, K;) as being a sign of rain. (TK.) ― -b3- $iEaAru AlHaj~i means The religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage; and the signs thereof; (K;) and, (TA,) as also ↓ Al$aEaAy^iru , (S,) the practices of the pilgrimage, and whatever is appointed as a sign of obedience to God; (S, Msb, * TA;) as the halting [ at Mount 'Arafát ], and the circuiting [ around the Kaabeh ], and the saEoY [or tripping to and fro between Es-Safà and El-Marweh ], and the throwing [ of the pebbles at Minè ], and the sacrifice, &c.; (TA;) and ↓ $aEiyrapN and ↓ $iEaArapN and ↓ ma$oErN signify the same as $iEaArN : (L:) ↓ $aEiyrapN is the sing. of $aEaAy^iru meaning as expl. above; (As, S, Msb;) or, as some say, the sing. is ↓ $iEaArapN : (As, S:) or ↓ $aEiyrapN and ↓ $iEaArapN , by some written ↓ $aEaArapN , and ↓ ma$oEarN , signify a place [ of the performance ] of religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage; expl. in the K by muEoZamuhaA , which is a mistake for mawoDiEuhaA ; (TA;) and ↓ ma$aAEiru , places thereof: (S:) or AlHaj~i ↓ $aEaAy^iru signifies the maEaAlim [or characteristic practices ] of the pilgrimage, to which God has invited, and the performance of which He has commanded; (K;) as also ↓ Alma$aAEiru : (TA:) and A@ll~`hi ↓ $aEaAy^iru , all those religious services which God has appointed to us as signs; as the halting [ at Mount 'Arafát ], and the saEoY [or tripping to and fro between Es-Safà and El-Marweh ], and the sacrificing of victims: (Zj, TA:) or the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage, and the places where those rites and ceremonies are performed; (Bd in v. 2 and xxii. 33;) among which places are Es-Safà and El-Marweh, they being thus expressly termed; (Kur ii. 153;) and so accord. to Fr in the Kur v. 2: (TA:) or the obligatory statutes or ordinances of God: (Bd in v. 2:) or the religion of God: (Bd in v. 2 and xxii. 33:) the camels or cows or bulls destined to be sacrificed at Mekkeh are also said in the Kur xxii. 37, to be mino $aEaAy^iri A@ll~`hi , i. e. of the signs of the religion of God: (Bd and Jel:) and [hence the sing.] ↓ $aEiyrapN signifies [sometimes] a camel or cow or bull that is brought to Mekkeh for sacrifice; (S, K;) such as is marked in the manner expl. voce A^a$oEara ; (Msb;) and $aEaAy^iru is its pl.; (K;) and is also pl. of $iEaArN : and the [festival called the] Eiyd is said to be a $iEaAr of the $aEaAy^ir [i. e. a sign of the signs of the religion ] of El-Islám. (Msb.) ― -b4- $iEaAru Ald~ami is said to mean (tropical:) The piece of rag: or (tropical:) the vulva: because each is a thing that indicates the existence of blood. (Mgh.) -A2- Also The [ innermost garment; or] garment that is next the body; (S, Msb;) the garment that is next the hair of the body, under the divaAr ; as also ↓ $aEaArN ; (K;) but this is strange: (TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^a$oEirapN and [of mult.] $uEurN . (K.) [Hence,] one says, labisa $iEaAra Alham~i (tropical:) [ He involved himself in anxiety ]. (A.) And jaEala Alxawofa $iEaArahu (assumed tropical:) [ He made fear to be as though it were his innermost garment ], by closely cleaving to it. (TA in art. drE .) [Hence, also,] it is said in a prov., humu Al$~iEaAru duwna Ald~ivaAri , meaning (assumed tropical:) They are near in respect of love: and in a trad., relating to the Ansár, A^anotumu Al$~iEaAru waAln~aAsu Ald~ivaAru (assumed tropical:) Ye are the special and close friends [ and the people in general are the less near in friendship ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A horse-cloth; a covering for a horse to protect him from the cold. (K.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) A thing with which wine [app. while in the vat] is protected, or preserved from injury: (L, K: [for Alxamoru , the reading in the CK, the author of the TK has read Alxumuru (and thus I find the word written in my MS. copy of the K) or Alxumoru , pls. of AlximaAru ; and Freytag has followed his example: but Alxamoru is the right reading, as is shown by what here follows:]) so in the saying of El-Akhtal, fakaf~a Alr~iyHa waAlA^anodaA='a EanohaA mina Alz~arajuwni duwnahumaA Al$~iEaAru [evidently describing wine, and app. meaning (assumed tropical:) And the $EAr of the wine, ( Al$~iEaAru mina Alz~arajuwna , i. e. $iEaAru Alz~arajuwni ,) while yet in the vat, intervening as an obstacle to them, kept off the wind and the rains, or dews, or day-dews, from it, namely, the wine]. (L.) ― -b4- See also $aEaArN , in two places. -A3- Also Death. (O, K.)

rawSourceText: A sign of people in war, (S, Msb, K,) and in a journey (K) &c., (TA,) i. e. (Msb) a call or cry, (A, Mgh, Msb,) by means of which to know one another: (S, A, Mgh, Msb:) and the $iEaAr of soldiers is a sign that is set up in order that a man may thereby know his companions: (TA:) and $iEaAr signifies also the banners, or standards, of tribes. (TA in art. brm .) It is said in a trad. that the $iEaAr of the Prophet in war was yaA manoSuwru A^amito A^amito [ O Mansoor, (a proper name of a man, meaning “ aided ” &c.,) kill thou, kill thou ]. (TA.) And it is said that he appointed the $iEaAr of the refugees on the day of Bedr to be yAbaniY Eabodi Alr~aHom`ni : and the $EAr of El-Khazraj, yA baniY Eabodi A@ll~`hi : and that of El-Ows, yaA baniY Eubayodi A@ll~`hi : and their $EAr on the day of El-Ahzáb, H`m= laA yunoSaruwna . (Mgh.) ― -b2- And Thunder; (Tekmileh, K;) as being a sign of rain. (TK.) ― -b3- $iEaAru AlHaj~i means The religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage; and the signs thereof; (K;) and, (TA,) as also ↓ Al$aEaAy^iru , (S,) the practices of the pilgrimage, and whatever is appointed as a sign of obedience to God; (S, Msb, * TA;) as the halting [ at Mount 'Arafát ], and the circuiting [ around the Kaabeh ], and the saEoY [or tripping to and fro between Es-Safà and El-Marweh ], and the throwing [ of the pebbles at Minè ], and the sacrifice, &c.; (TA;) and ↓ $aEiyrapN and ↓ $iEaArapN and ↓ ma$oErN signify the same as $iEaArN : (L:) ↓ $aEiyrapN is the sing. of $aEaAy^iru meaning as expl. above; (As, S, Msb;) or, as some say, the sing. is ↓ $iEaArapN : (As, S:) or ↓ $aEiyrapN and ↓ $iEaArapN , by some written ↓ $aEaArapN , and ↓ ma$oEarN , signify a place [ of the performance ] of religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage; expl. in the K by muEoZamuhaA , which is a mistake for mawoDiEuhaA ; (TA;) and ↓ ma$aAEiru , places thereof: (S:) or AlHaj~i ↓ $aEaAy^iru signifies the maEaAlim [or characteristic practices ] of the pilgrimage, to which God has invited, and the performance of which He has commanded; (K;) as also ↓ Alma$aAEiru : (TA:) and A@ll~`hi ↓ $aEaAy^iru , all those religious services which God has appointed to us as signs; as the halting [ at Mount 'Arafát ], and the saEoY [or tripping to and fro between Es-Safà and El-Marweh ], and the sacrificing of victims: (Zj, TA:) or the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage, and the places where those rites and ceremonies are performed; (Bd in v. 2 and xxii. 33;) among which places are Es-Safà and El-Marweh, they being thus expressly termed; (Kur ii. 153;) and so accord. to Fr in the Kur v. 2: (TA:) or the obligatory statutes or ordinances of God: (Bd in v. 2:) or the religion of God: (Bd in v. 2 and xxii. 33:) the camels or cows or bulls destined to be sacrificed at Mekkeh are also said in the Kur xxii. 37, to be mino $aEaAy^iri A@ll~`hi , i. e. of the signs of the religion of God: (Bd and Jel:) and [hence the sing.] ↓ $aEiyrapN signifies [sometimes] a camel or cow or bull that is brought to Mekkeh for sacrifice; (S, K;) such as is marked in the manner expl. voce A^a$oEara ; (Msb;) and $aEaAy^iru is its pl.; (K;) and is also pl. of $iEaArN : and the [festival called the] Eiyd is said to be a $iEaAr of the $aEaAy^ir [i. e. a sign of the signs of the religion ] of El-Islám. (Msb.) ― -b4- $iEaAru Ald~ami is said to mean (tropical:) The piece of rag: or (tropical:) the vulva: because each is a thing that indicates the existence of blood. (Mgh.) -A2- Also The [ innermost garment; or] garment that is next the body; (S, Msb;) the garment that is next the hair of the body, under the divaAr ; as also ↓ $aEaArN ; (K;) but this is strange: (TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^a$oEirapN and [of mult.] $uEurN . (K.) [Hence,] one says, labisa $iEaAra Alham~i (tropical:) [ He involved himself in anxiety ]. (A.) And jaEala Alxawofa $iEaArahu (assumed tropical:) [ He made fear to be as though it were his innermost garment ], by closely cleaving to it. (TA in art. drE .) [Hence, also,] it is said in a prov., humu Al$~iEaAru duwna Ald~ivaAri , meaning (assumed tropical:) They are near in respect of love: and in a trad., relating to the Ansár, A^anotumu Al$~iEaAru waAln~aAsu Ald~ivaAru (assumed tropical:) Ye are the special and close friends [ and the people in general are the less near in friendship ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A horse-cloth; a covering for a horse to protect him from the cold. (K.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) A thing with which wine [app. while in the vat] is protected, or preserved from injury: (L, K: [for Alxamoru , the reading in the CK, the author of the TK has read Alxumuru (and thus I find the word written in my MS. copy of the K) or Alxumoru , pls. of AlximaAru ; and Freytag has followed his example: but Alxamoru is the right reading, as is shown by what here follows:]) so in the saying of El-Akhtal, fakaf~a Alr~iyHa waAlA^anodaA='a EanohaA mina Alz~arajuwni duwnahumaA Al$~iEaAru [evidently describing wine, and app. meaning (assumed tropical:) And the $EAr of the wine, ( Al$~iEaAru mina Alz~arajuwna , i. e. $iEaAru Alz~arajuwni ,) while yet in the vat, intervening as an obstacle to them, kept off the wind and the rains, or dews, or day-dews, from it, namely, the wine]. (L.) ― -b4- See also $aEaArN , in two places. -A3- Also Death. (O, K.)

definition: A poet: (T, S, Msb, K:) so called because of his intelligence;
sourceDefinition: A poet: (T, S, Msb, K:) so called because of his intelligence; (S, Msb;) or because he knows what others know not: (T, TA:) accord. to Akh, it is a possessive epithet, like laAbinN and taAmirN : (S:) pl. $uEaraA='u , (S, Msb, K,) deviating from analogy: (S, Msb:) Sb says that the measure faAEilN is likened in this case to faEiylN ; and hence this pl.: (TA:) or, accord. to IKh, the pl. is of this form because the sing. is from $aEura , and therefore should by rule be of the measure faEiylN , like $ariyfN [from $arufa ]; but were it so, it might be confounded with $aEiyr meaning the grain thus called, therefore they said $aAEirN , and regarded in the pl. the original form of the sing. (Msb.) A wonderful poet is called xino*iy*N : one next below him, $aAEirN : then, ↓ $awayoEirN [the dim.]: (Yoo, K:) then, ↓ $uEoruwrN : and then, ↓ mata$aAEirN . (K.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A liar: because of the many lies in poetry: and so, accord. to some, in the Kur xxi. 5. (B, TA.) ― -b3- $iEorN $aAEirN Excellent poetry: (Sb, T, K:) or known poetry: but the former explanation is the more correct. (TA.) One also says, sometimes, kalimapN $aAEirapN , [by klmp ] meaning qaSiydapN : but generally in a phrase of this kind the two words are cognate, as in wayolN waAy^ilN and layolN laAy^ilN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ More, and most, knowing or cognizant or understanding: see 1, first sentence. ― -b2- And,] applied to a verse, (T,) or to a poem, (S,) More [and most ] poetical. (T, S. *) -A2- Also, (S, A, K,) and ↓ $aEirN , (A, K,) and ↓ $aEoraAniY~N , (K,) which last (SM says) I have seen written $aEaraAniY~N , (TA,) A man having much hair upon his body: (S, A:) or having hair upon the whole of the body: (IAth, L voce A^ajoradu [q. v.], in explanation of the first:) or having much and long hair (K, TA) upon the head and body: (TA:) and the first and second, a goat having much hair: fem. of the first $aEoraA='u : (TA:) and pl. of the first $aEorN . (S, K.) One says A^$oEavu A^a$oEaru , meaning Having his head unshaven and not combed nor anointed. (TA.) And fulaAnN A^a$oEaru Alr~aqabapi [lit. Such a one is hairy in the neck ] is said of a man though he have not hair upon his neck, as meaning (tropical:) such a one is strong, like a lion. (A, * TA.) ― -b2- [The fem.] $aEoraA='u also signifies A testicle, or scrotum, ( xuSoyapN ,) having much hair: (TA:) and the sawo'ap [or pudendum ]: thus used as a subst. (IAar, TA in art. mET .) See also $iEorapN . ― -b3- And A furred garment. (Th, K.) ― -b4- And as an epithet, (tropical:) Evil, foul, or abominable: [as being likened to that which is shaggy, and therefore unseemly:] (K, * TA:) in the K, Alxa$inapu is erroneously put for Alxabiyvapu . (TA.) One says, daAhiyapN $aEoraA='u , (S, A, K,) and waboraA='u , (S, A,) and zab~aA='u , (TA in art. zb ,) (tropical:) An evil, a foul, or an abominable, (TA,) or a severe, or great, (K,) calamity or misfortune: pl. $uEorN . (K, TA.) And one says to a man when he has said a thing that one blames or with which one finds fault, jiy^ota bihaA $aEoraA='a *aAta wabarK (tropical:) [ Thou hast said it as a foul, or an abominable, thing ]. (S, A. *) ― -b5- And A^a$oEaru signifies also The hair that surrounds the solid hoof: (S:) or [the extremity, or border, of the pastern, next the solid hoof; i. e.] the extremity of the skin surrounding the solid hoof, (K, TA,) where the small hairs grow around it: (TA:) or the part between the hoof of a horse and the place where the hair of the pastern terminates: and the part of a camel's foot where the hair terminates: (TA:) pl. A^a$aAEiru , (S, TA,) because it is [in this sense] a subst. (TA.) ― -b6- Also The side of the vulva, or external portion of the female organs of generation: (K:) it is said that the A^a$oEaraAni are the A_isokataAni , which are the two sides [or labia majora ] of the vulva of a woman: or the two parts next to the $uforaAni , which are the two borders of the A_isokataAni : or the two parts between the A_isokataAni and the $uforaAni : (L, TA:) or the two parts next to the $uforaAni , in the hair, particularly: (Zj, in his “ Khalk el-Insán: ”) the A^a$aAEir of the HayaA=' [or vulva of a camel &c.] are the parts where the hair terminates: (TA:) and the A^a$aAEir of a she-camel are the sides of the vulva. (S, L, TA.) ― -b7- And A thing that comes forth from [ between ] the two halves of the hoof of a sheep or goat, resembling a vuw^oluwl [or wart ]; (Lh, K;) for which it is cauterized. (Lh, TA.) ― -b8- And Flesh coming forth beneath the nail: pl. $uEurN , (K, TA,) with two dammehs, (TA,) or $uEorN . (So in the CK.) ― -b9- And [the fem.] $aEoraA='u also signifies (tropical:) Land ( A^aroD ) containing, or having, trees: or abounding in trees: (A, K:) [and so, app., ↓ $aEoraAnu ; for] there is a mountain in [the province of] El-Mowsil called $aEoraAnu , said by AA to be thus called because of the abundance of its trees: (S:) or $aEoraA='u signifies many trees: (A 'Obeyd, S:) or i. q. A^ajamapN [i. e. a thicket, wood, or forest; &c.]: (TA:) and a meadow ( rawoDapN , AHn, A, K, TA) having its upper part covered with trees, (AHn, K * TA,) or abounding in trees, (TA,) or abounding in herbage: (A:) and a tract of sand ( ramolapN ) producing [ the plant called ] naSiY~ (Sgh, L, K) and the like. (Sgh, K.) ― -b10- And (assumed tropical:) A certain tree of the kind called HamoD , (K, TA,) not having leaves, but having [ what are termed ] hadab [q. v.], very eagerly desired by the camels, and that puts forth strong twigs or branches; mentioned in the L on the authority of AHn, and by Sgh on the authority of Aboo-Ziyád; and the latter adds that it has firewood. (TA.) ― -b11- And (assumed tropical:) A certain fruit: (AHn, TA:) a species of peach: (S, K:) sing. and pl. the same: (AHn, S, K:) or a single peach: (IKtt, MF:) or AlA^a$oEaru is a name of the peach, and the pl. is $uEorN . (Mtr, TA.) ― -b12- Also (assumed tropical:) A kind of fly, (S, K,) said to be that which has a sting, (S,) blue, or red, that alights upon camels and asses and dogs; (K;) as also ↓ $uEayoraA='u : (TA:) a kind of fly that stings the ass, so that he goes round: AHn says that it is of two species, that of the dog and that of the camel: that of the dog is well known, inclines to slenderness and redness, and touches nothing but the dog: that of the camel inclines to yellowness, is larger than that of the dog, has wings, and is downy under the wings: sometimes it is in such numbers that the owners of the camels cannot milk in the day-time nor ride any of them; so that they leave doing this until night: it stings the camel in the soft parts of the udder and around them, and beneath the tail and the belly and the armpits; and they do not protect the animal from it save by tar: it flies over the camels so that one hears it to make a humming, or buzzing, sound. (TA. [See also $uEoruwrN , under which its pl. $uEorN is mentioned.]) ― -b13- And [hence, perhaps, as this kind of fly is seen in swarms,] (assumed tropical:) A multitude of men. (K.)
