See also $iEorapN . ― -b3- And A furred garment. (Th, K.) ― -b4- And as an epithet, (tropical:) Evil, foul, or abominable: [as being likened to that which is shaggy, and therefore unseemly:] (K, * TA:) in the K, Alxa$inapu is erroneously put for Alxabiyvapu . (TA.) One says, daAhiyapN $aEoraA='u , (S, A, K,) and waboraA='u , (S, A,) and zab~aA='u , (TA in art. zb ,) (tropical:) An evil, a foul, or an abominable, (TA,) or a severe, or great, (K,) calamity or misfortune: pl. $uEorN . (K, TA.) And one says to a man when he has said a thing that one blames or with which one finds fault, jiy^ota bihaA $aEoraA='a *aAta wabarK (tropical:) [ Thou hast said it as a foul, or an abominable, thing ]. (S, A. *) ― -b5- And A^a$oEaru signifies also The hair that surrounds the solid hoof: (S:) or [the extremity, or border, of the pastern, next the solid hoof; i. e.] the extremity of the skin surrounding the solid hoof, (K, TA,) where the small hairs grow around it: (TA:) or the part between the hoof of a horse and the place where the hair of the pastern terminates: and the part of a camel's foot where the hair terminates: (TA:) pl. A^a$aAEiru , (S, TA,) because it is [in this sense] a subst. (TA.) ― -b6- Also The side of the vulva, or external portion of the female organs of generation: (K:) it is said that the A^a$oEaraAni are the A_isokataAni , which are the two sides [or labia majora ] of the vulva of a woman: or the two parts next to the $uforaAni , which are the two borders of the A_isokataAni : or the two parts between the A_isokataAni and the $uforaAni : (L, TA:) or the two parts next to the $uforaAni , in the hair, particularly: (Zj, in his “ Khalk el-Insán: ”) the A^a$aAEir of the HayaA=' [or vulva of a camel &c.] are the parts where the hair terminates: (TA:) and the A^a$aAEir of a she-camel are the sides of the vulva. (S, L, TA.) ― -b7- And A thing that comes forth from [ between ] the two halves of the hoof of a sheep or goat, resembling a vuw^oluwl [or wart ]; (Lh, K;) for which it is cauterized. (Lh, TA.) ― -b8- And Flesh coming forth beneath the nail: pl. $uEurN , (K, TA,) with two dammehs, (TA,) or $uEorN . (So in the CK.) ― -b9- And [the fem.] $aEoraA='u also signifies (tropical:) Land ( A^aroD ) containing, or having, trees: or abounding in trees: (A, K:) [and so, app., ↓ $aEoraAnu ; for] there is a mountain in [the province of] El-Mowsil called $aEoraAnu , said by AA to be thus called because of the abundance of its trees: (S:) or $aEoraA='u signifies many trees: (A 'Obeyd, S:) or i. q. A^ajamapN [i. e. a thicket, wood, or forest; &c.]: (TA:) and a meadow ( rawoDapN , AHn, A, K, TA) having its upper part covered with trees, (AHn, K * TA,) or abounding in trees, (TA,) or abounding in herbage: (A:) and a tract of sand ( ramolapN ) producing [ the plant called ] naSiY~ (Sgh, L, K) and the like. (Sgh, K.) ― -b10- And (assumed tropical:) A certain tree of the kind called HamoD , (K, TA,) not having leaves, but having [ what are termed ] hadab [q. v.], very eagerly desired by the camels, and that puts forth strong twigs or branches; mentioned in the L on the authority of AHn, and by Sgh on the authority of Aboo-Ziyád; and the latter adds that it has firewood. (TA.) ― -b11- And (assumed tropical:) A certain fruit: (AHn, TA:) a species of peach: (S, K:) sing. and pl. the same: (AHn, S, K:) or a single peach: (IKtt, MF:) or AlA^a$oEaru is a name of the peach, and the pl. is $uEorN . (Mtr, TA.) ― -b12- Also (assumed tropical:) A kind of fly, (S, K,) said to be that which has a sting, (S,) blue, or red, that alights upon camels and asses and dogs; (K;) as also ↓ $uEayoraA='u : (TA:) a kind of fly that stings the ass, so that he goes round: AHn says that it is of two species, that of the dog and that of the camel: that of the dog is well known, inclines to slenderness and redness, and touches nothing but the dog: that of the camel inclines to yellowness, is larger than that of the dog, has wings, and is downy under the wings: sometimes it is in such numbers that the owners of the camels cannot milk in the day-time nor ride any of them; so that they leave doing this until night: it stings the camel in the soft parts of the udder and around them, and beneath the tail and the belly and the armpits; and they do not protect the animal from it save by tar: it flies over the camels so that one hears it to make a humming, or buzzing, sound. (TA. [See also $uEoruwrN , under which its pl. $uEorN is mentioned.]) ― -b13- And [hence, perhaps, as this kind of fly is seen in swarms,] (assumed tropical:) A multitude of men. (K.)

definition: signifies takoviyru Al$~anaAEapi [app.
sourceDefinition: signifies takoviyru Al$~anaAEapi [app. meaning The uttering, or saying, much, or often, what is bad, evil, abominable, foul, or unseemly: and the doing what is bad &c. much or often ]: (K:) or the uttering, or saying, what is bad, evil, abominable, foul, or unseemly, (KL, PS,) against any one: (PS:) and the representing, or regarding, as bad, &c.: (KL, PS: *) and the committing [ an action that is bad, &c., or] a fault, or vitious action. (KL.) You say, $an~aEotu Ealayohi , inf. n. ta$oniyEN , (S, O,) I uttered, or said, what was bad, evil, abominable, foul, or unseemly, against him: (PS:) from Al$~anaAEapu . (O.) And $n~E Ealayohi AlA^amora , inf. n. as above, He showed, or declared, to him that the affair was bad, evil, &c.: (TA: [see also 5:]) or characterized the affair to him as bad, evil, &c. (Msb.) -A2- And The striving, labouring, or exerting oneself, and being quick, and vigorous, or energetic, syn. Alt~a$omiyru , (S, O, K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, Alt~a$ohiyru ,]) and AlAinokimaA$u , and Aljid~u , (O, K,) in pace, or going; (O, * K;) as also ↓ Alt~a$an~uEu (K) [and ↓ AlA_i$onaAEu ]: thus $n~E is said of a man, meaning He strove, laboured, or exerted himself, and was quick: (TA:) and in like manner $an~aEato is said of a she-camel, (As, A'Obeyd, S, O,) and of camels, (O,) as also ↓ t$n~Et , (S, * O, expl. in the former by jad~ato only,) and ↓ A$nEt ; (O;) in pace, or going: (S, O:) or ↓ A$nEt said of a she-camel means she was quick, or swift. (K.)

definition: He showed, or declared, the case of the people, or party, to be bad, evil, abominable, foul, or unseemly, by reason of their disagreement, and the unsound, or unsettled, state of their opinion.
sourceDefinition: He showed, or declared, the case of the people, or party, to be bad, evil, abominable, foul, or unseemly, by reason of their disagreement, and the unsound, or unsettled, state of their opinion. (TA.) -A2- And t$n~E He (a man) purposed to do a bad, an evil, an abominable, a foul, or an unseemly, thing or affair. (TA.) ― -b2- See also 2, last sentence, in two places. ― -b3- Hence, (IAar, TA,) He prepared himself for fight: (IAar, K, TA:) or, said of a party of men, they prepared themselves for fight: (O:) and accord. to AA, t$n~E lil$~ar~i He prepared himself for evil, or mischief. (O, TA.) ― -b4- And It ( a garment, or piece of cloth,) became rent, or slit. (O, K.) -A3- t$n~E AlgaArapa He spread, or dispersed, the horsemen making a raid, or sudden attack, upon an enemy. sourceDefinition: and miloHaAnu , (S, A,) thus in a verse of El-Kumeyt, as related by Ibn-Selemeh, with kesr to the $ and m , (S,) or the former word is written ↓ $ayobaAnu , and sometimes $iybaAnu , and the latter is as above, (K,) and sometimes maloHaAnu , (TA,) (tropical:) The two months of winter; (A, TA;) [as though meaning the second of the Six Seasons, commencing two months after the autumnal equinox; (see the former of the two tables in p. 1254;)] i. q. $ahoraA qimaAHK , (S, A, K, TA,) which are the two coldest months; (S, K, TA;) so called because of the earth's being then white with snow and hoar frost; (S, TA;) falling at the period of the [ auroral ] rising of the Scorpion and the Vulture, ( AlEaqorab and Aln~asor , [by which latter is meant Aln~asoru AlwaAqiEu , i. e. the star a of Lyra,]) said by him who knows not to be the two Kánoons [i. e. kaAnuwnu AlA^aw~alu and kaAnuwnu Alv~aAniY , corresponding to December and January O.S.]: (TA:) [it appears that they nearly agree with the two Kánoons; for El-Kazweenee and others say that Alqalobu (i. e. the heart of the Scorpion, which is the 18th of the Mansions of the Moon,) and Aln~asoru AlwaAqiEu rise together, and their auroral rising in Central Arabia, about the commencement of the era of the Flight, accord. to my calculation, (see manaAzilu Alqamari in art. nzl ,) was on the 25th of November O. S.: see also miloHaAnu , and qimaAHN : it is also said that] $iybaAnu [used alone] is a name of [ the month ] kAnwn AlAw~l , because of the whiteness of the earth by reason of the hoar-frost and snow. definition: White-haired, white-headed, or horary: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) [it is said to be] anomalous in form;
sourceDefinition: White-haired, white-headed, or horary: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) [it is said to be] anomalous in form; (S, Mgh, Msb;) for an epithet of this measure is only formed [by rule] from a verb of the measure faEila , aor. yafoEalu ; (S, TA;) and it is a condition of the formation of such an epithet that it must denote a defect or the like, or a colour: but A^a$oyabu signifies white-headed, or hoaryheaded; [so that it does denote a colour;] and ElKhafájee says that it is reckoned among epithets denoting defects, or blemishes, like A^aEomaY and A^aEoraju : (MF, TA:) it is said in the K that it has no faEolaA=' , i. e., (TA,) the epithet $ayobaA='u is not applied to a woman; (Msb, TA;) $amoTaA='u being used in its stead; (TA;) though one says $aAba raA^osuhaA : (Msb, TA:) [but see Har p. 418, where $ayobaA='u is mentioned, applied to a woman, as meaning aged, and white, or hoary, in the head: and see $ayobaA='u in art. $wb :] the pl. is $iybN ; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) with which is syn. $uy~abN ; (TA, as from the K; [but not found by me in the copies of the K to which I have had access;]) and ↓ $uyubN : (K, TA:) this last is said by IM to be allowable in poetry, EalaY Alt~amaAmi [here meaning as though it were a word composed of sound letters]; and this is the assertion of the lexicologists [in general]: ISd thinks it to be pl. of ↓ $aAy^ibN [q. v.], like as buzulN is of baAzilN ; or pl. of ↓ $ayuwbN [which app. means very white or hoary in the head ], accord. to the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz, who say dajaAjapN bayuwDN and dajaAjN buyuDN . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, raA^ayotu AljibaAla $iybFA (tropical:) I saw the mountains white with snow and hoar frost. (A, TA.) And $iybN [used alone] signifies (assumed tropical:) Mountains upon which snow falls, and which are white, or hoary, therewith: (S, L:) or mountains white with snow or with dust: and, some say, white clouds: sing. A^a$oyabu . (L, TA.) And, applied to truffles ( kamoA^ap ), (assumed tropical:) White and large: (TA:) or simply white. (Id. voce taEaA$iybu .) ― -b3- yawomN A^a$oyabu (assumed tropical:) A day in which are cold and clouds and SuraAd [correctly Sur~aAd , meaning thin clouds, or cold and humid clouds, in which is no water ]; as also ↓ yawomN $ayobaAnu . (K.) ― -b4- layolapu Al$~ayobaA='i , (K,) or layolapu $ayobaA='a , (TA,) and layolapN $ayobaA='u , (TA voce Hur~N ,) (assumed tropical:) The last night of the [ lunar ] month: (K, TA:) its first night is called layolapu Hur~apK and layolapN Hur~apN . (K voce Hur~N .) baAtato bilayolapi $ayobaA='a , and bilayolapi Al$~ayobaA='i : see in art. $wb .

definition: , aor. , (AZ, S, K,) inf. n. SaboEN , (AZ, S,) He pointed at him, or towards him, with his finger, ( biA_iSobaEihi ,) disparagingly: (AZ, S, K:) or, as some say, he meant some evil thing to him when...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , (AZ, S, K,) inf. n. SaboEN , (AZ, S,) He pointed at him, or towards him, with his finger, ( biA_iSobaEihi ,) disparagingly: (AZ, S, K:) or, as some say, he meant some evil thing to him when he (the latter) was inadvertent, not knowing. (TA.) ― -b2- And SabaEa fulaAnFA EalaY fulaAnK He directed such a one to such a one by pointing, or indication: (S, K:) because, when one directs a man to a way, or road, or to a thing that is latent, or obscure, he points towards it with the finger. (TA.) One says, maA SabaEaka EalayonaA What directed thee to us? (TA.) And SabaEa bayona Alqawomi He directed others to the people, or party. (TA.) Of one who magnifies himself, or acts proudly, in his government, or administration, one says, SabaEahu Al$~ayoTaAnu (assumed tropical:) [app. meaning The Devil has directed him ]: and A^adorakatohu A^aSaAbiEu Al$~ayoTaAni [ The fingers of the Devil have reached him ]. (TA. [See the pass. part. n. below.]) ― -b3- And one says, qur~iba A_ilayohi TaEaAmN famaA SabaEa fiyhi i. e. [ Food was presented, or offered, to him, or was placed, or put, before him, and ] he did not put his finger into it. (TA.) [See also SabaA^a , near the end.] ― -b4- And SabaEa Ald~ajaAjapa , (O, K,) inf. n. as above. (TA,) He inserted his finger into the hen in order that he might know if she were [ near ] laying an egg or not: (O, K:) mentioned by Z. (TA.) ― -b5- And SabaEa AlA_inaA='a He put his finger upon the vessel so that what was in another vessel flowed upon it [ into the former vessel ]: (A'Obeyd, S, O, K:) or, as some say, he put together his two fingers, [or two of his fingers, ] then discharged, or let flow, what was in the vessel, of wine, or beverage, into a thing with a narrow head [or mouth ]: or, accord. to Az, he discharged, or let flow, what was in the vessel, of wine, or beverage, between the extremities of [ either of ] his two thumbs and fore fingers, in order that it might not become scattered, and pour forth copiously. (TA.) ― -b6- And SabaEahu , inf. n. as above, He hit, or hurt, his finger. (TA.) -A2- SabaEa EalaY Alqawomi , inf. n. as above, meaning He came forth upon the people, or party, is said to be originally SabaA^a , with ' . (TA.)

(of ASbE , MA) A^aSaAbiEu and (of ASbwE , MA) A^aSaAbiyEu . (MA, K.) ― -b2- One says, bihimo tuvonaY AlA^aSaAbiEu [ With the mention of them the fingers are bent ]; meaning that they are reckoned as the best, [or among the best,] for the best are not many. Hnw and HnY .] ― -b3- And lilr~aAEiY EalaY maA$iyatihi A_iSobaEN (tropical:) [ The pastor has a finger pointing at his cattle, or camels or sheep or goats ]; meaning, [ has upon his cattle ] an impress of a good state or condition; (S, K, * TA;) i. e. they are pointed at with the fingers because of their goodliness and fatness and good tending. (TA.) [See also a verse cited voce SulobN .] And similar to this saying is the prov., Ealayohi mina A@ll~`hi taEaAlaY A_iSobaEN HasanN , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Upon him is, from God, ( acknowledged be his absolute supremacy, )] an impress of a good state or condition. (Meyd.) And one says also, A_in~ahu laHasanu AlA_iSobaEi fiY maAlihi , meaning (assumed tropical:) Verily he is good in respect of the impress upon his cattle [ indicative of their state or condition ]. (IAar, TA.) ― -b4- And fulaAnN mugil~u AlA_iSobaEi (tropical:) Such a one is unfaithful, treacherous, or perfidious. (O, K, * TA. *) ― -b5- And lahu A_iSobaEN fiY h`*aA AlA^amori (tropical:) [ He has a finger in this affair ]. (TA.) ― -b6- The Prophet said qalobu Almuw^omini bayona A_iSobaEayoni mino A^aSaAbiEi A@ll~`hi yuqal~ibuhu kayofa $aA='a (tropical:) [ The heart of the believer is between two of the fingers of God: He turneth it about as He pleaseth ]. (O.) ― -b7- And a man says, in respect of a difficult affair, when he has been made to have recourse to a strong man, able to bear his burden, A_in~ahu yaA^otiY Ealayohi biA_iSobiEK waAHidapK (assumed tropical:) [ Verily he will make an end of it with one finger ]: and A_in~ahu yakofiyhi biSugoraY A^aSaAbiEihi (assumed tropical:) [ Verily the smallest of his fingers will suffice him for its accomplishment; the b thus prefixed to the agent being redundant, as in kafaY biA@ll~`hi $ahiydFA and many other instances]. (O.) ― -b8- A^abuw AlA_iSobaEi is one of the surnames of The Devil. (TA. [See SabaEahu Al$~iyoTaAnu , above.]) ― -b9- [ A_iSobaEN signifies also (assumed tropical:) A prong, as resembling a finger: so in the S and K in art. Hfr , and in other instances.] ― -b10- A^aSaAbiEu AlfatayaAti , (O, TS, K,) in the “ Minháj ” of Ibn-Jezleh ASAbE AlftyAn , [app. a mistranscription,] and in the I, ASAbE Albunay~aAti , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) [ Common clinopodium, or wild basil, ] the sweet-smelling plant called in Pers. (S, K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, O, K,) aor. , (O, Mgh, K,) inf. n. SaqoEN , (O,) He struck him, or beat him: (K:) or he struck [or slapped ] him with his expanded hand: (TA:) [like SafaEahu :] or, (S, Mgh, O, K,) as also ↓ SawoqaEahu , (O, K,) he struck him (S, Mgh, O, K) upon his head, (O, K,) or upon his SawoqaEap , (S, O,) [i. e.] upon the top of his head: (Mgh:) this last is the primary signification: and hence, metaphorically, he struck him, or beat him, in an unrestricted sense: (Mgh, * O, TA:) and he struck it, namely, a dry, or tough, and solid thing, with a similar thing; as, for instance, a stone with a stone, and the like: or, as some say, he struck it, namely, anything dry, or tough. (TA.) It is said in a trad., respecting Munkidh, SuqiEa A=m~apF i. e. He was struck on the top of his head: (O:) or he had his head broken so that the wound reached the membrane over his brain. (TA.) ― -b2- One says also, SaqaEa bihi AlA^aroDa (O, K) He threw him down, or prostrated him, on the ground; (K;) [lit.] he smote the ground with him. (Ibn-'Abbád, O.) ― -b3- And SaqaEatohu AlS~aAqiEapu i. q. SaEaqatohu AlS~aAEiqapu , (S, O, K,) The thunderbolt smote him. (TA.) And SuqiEa He was smitten by a thunderbolt; i. q. SuEiqa ; of the dial. of Temeem: (O:) and so SaqiEa ; (K, TA;) like SaEiqa . (TA.) ― -b4- And SaqaEahu bikaY~K He branded him, or marked him by cauterizing, upon his head, [or his SawoqaEap ,] or his face. (O, K.) ― -b5- And SaqaEa Alv~ariydapa , aor. and inf. n. as above, He ate the vrydp [or mess of crumbled bread with broth ] from its SawoqaEap [or top, or upper part, or hollow made therein ]. (TA. [See also Q. Q. 1.]) -A2- SaqoEN also signifies The raising of the voice: (O, TA:) and the uttering it by consecutive emissions. (TA.) You say, SaqaEa biSawotihi He raised his voice. (TA.) And hence, (TA,) SaqaEa said of a cock, (S, O, K,) aor. , (O,) inf. n. SaqoEN and SuqaAEN (IDrd, O, K) and SaqiyEN , (K,) He [ crowed, or] uttered a cry: (IDrd, S, O, K:) and so saqaEa . (S.) ― -b2- And, accord. to IAar, The being eloquent in speech, and lighting upon the [ proper ] meanings. (TA.) ― -b3- SaqaEa biDaroTapK , said of an ass, He emitted a sounding wind from the anus, in a moist and dispersed state. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ― -b4- SaqaEa Albayota He attached to the tent the rope called SiqaAE [q. v.]. (Az, O, TA.) ― -b5- And SaqaEa , (S, O, K,) said of a man, (K,) He went away, (S, O, K, TA,) fiY kul~i Aln~awaAHiY [ in all directions ]: (TA:) one says, maA A^adoriY A^ayona SaqaEa , (S, O, TA, [but in the second, laA is put in the place of maA ,]) and baqaEa , (TA,) meaning I know not whither he went away: (O, TA:) and the verb is seldom used in this sense without the particle of negation. (TA.) Or it signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (O,) or so SaqiEa , (S, TA,) like fariHa , not SaqaEa , (TA,) He deviated from the way, (S, O, K, TA,) and alighted, or descended and abode, alone, by himself: (TA:) or he deviated from the way of goodness and generosity. (IF, O, K, TA.) And SaqoEN signifies The going astray; losing one's way; or becoming lost; and perishing; or dying. (TA. [But I think that this is probably a mistranscription for SaqaEN , inf. n. of SaqiEa .]) You say also, SaqiEa fulaAnN naHowa ka*aA Such a one repaired towards such a thing. (TA.) ― -b6- And SaqiEati Albiy^oru , aor. , (A'Obeyd, S,) inf. n. SaqaEN , The well collapsed; or broke down. (A'Obeyd, S, K. *) -A3- SaqiEato , (TA,) inf. n. SaqaEN , (O, K, TA,) said of horses, and of birds, &c., They became white (O, K, TA) in the [ SawoqaEap , or] uppermost part of the head, (TA,) or in the middle of the head. (O, K.) ― -b2- And [the inf. n.] SaqaEN , in relation to the head, signifies The being bald: or, as some say, the going away of the hair. (TA.) -A4- SuqiEati AlA^aroDu The earth, or ground, became overspread with the SaqiyE [i. e. hoarfrost, or rime ]; (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ A^uSoqiEat ; each with damm. (IDrd, K.)

definition: A district, quarter, or tract, syn.
sourceDefinition: A district, quarter, or tract, syn. naAHiyapN , (S, O, Msb, K,) of a country: (Msb:) and a place, region, quarter, tract, or point, towards which a person, or thing, goes, tends, or is directed; syn. jihapN : and a place of alighting, or of descending and stopping or sojourning or abiding or lodging or settling; or a place of abode or settlement; syn. maHal~apN : (Msb:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aSoqaAEN , (O, TA,) and pl. pl. A^aSaAqiEu : (TA:) and SuqogN is a dial. var. thereof. (IJ, TA; and K in art. Sqg .) One says, fulaAnN mino A^aholi h`*aA AlS~uqoEi i. e. mino h`*ihi Aln~aAHiyapi [ Such a one is of the people of this district, &c.]. (S, O.) And huwa fiY SuqoEi baniY fulaAnK He is in the naAHiyap [or district, &c.], and the maHal~ap [or place of alighting, &c.], of the sons of such a one. (Msb.) See also miSoqaEN . ― -b2- Also A part, or portion, of the surrounding and inferior sides of a well: pl. A^aSoqaAEN : but the more approved word is with s . (TA.)

definition: [ Smitten by a thunderbolt: (see its verb, SaqiEa :) or] smitten as by a thunderbolt from the enemy: so accord.
sourceDefinition: [ Smitten by a thunderbolt: (see its verb, SaqiEa :) or] smitten as by a thunderbolt from the enemy: so accord. to some: (O, TA:) 'Ows Ibn-Hajar says, A^abaA dulayojapa mano liHaY~K muforadK SaqiEK mina AlA^aEodaA='i fiY $aw~aAli (S, * O, TA, but in the TA A^aAabaA ) [which may be rendered O Aboo-Duleyjeh, who is for a solitary tribe, smitten as though by a thunderbolt from the enemies, in Showwál (which was, in the time of the poet, a cold month) ?]: or, accord. to IAar, the meaning here is, in a state of retirement, remote from the enemies; (S, * O;) for when the winter pressed severely upon the man, he used to retire to a distance, lest a guest should alight at his abode; the enemies being the strange guests; and by saying fY $w~Al , he means that the cold was in Showwál: (O, TA:) or SaqiEN means absent and remote, so that one knows not where he is: or that has gone away, and alighted alone, or by himself: (TA:) [pl. SaqoEaY :] see an ex. voce daqiEN . -A2- A^aroDN SaqiEapN , (TA,) and ↓ maSoquwEapN , Earth, or ground, overspread with the SaqiyE [i. e. hoarfrost, or rime ]: (S, Msb, TA:) and in like manner, $ajarN SaqiEN , and ↓ muSoqaEN , trees overspread with the SaqiyE . (TA.)

definition: A Christian's cell, or chamber, (K, KL,) for retirement, or seclusion, having a high and slender head;

definition: The small in the ear;
sourceDefinition: The small in the ear; (S, Mgh, O, K, TA;) of men and of others: (TA:) [see also 1:] fem. SamoEaA='u ; (S, Mgh, O, K, TA;) applied in this sense to a woman, and to other than woman; (TA;) thus to a she-goat; and such I'Ab held to be allowable as a victim for sacrifice; (O, TA;) or, applied to a she-goat, whose ear is like that of the gazelle, between such as is termed sak~aA=' and such as is termed A^a*onaA=' ; or, accord. to Az, applied to a ewe or she-goat, whose ear is little, and cleaving to the head: (TA:) [pl. SumoEN .] ― -b2- Hence, The ostrich; because of the smallness of his ear, and its cleaving to his head. (TA.) ― -b3- And the fem., applied to an ear, Small, or little, and contracted towards the head. (O, K.) ― -b4- Also, the masc., applied to a kaEob [as meaning a joint of the bones, and particularly an anklejoint, and an ankle-bone, and also a joint, or knot, of a cane or reed], Small, or slender, and even. (O, K.) A woman is said to be SamoEaA='u AlkaEobayoni Small, or slender, in the kaboEaAn [i. e. ankle-joints or ankle-bones ]. (TA.) And dogs are said to be SumoEu AlkuEuwbi i. e. Small in the kEwb [app. meaning joints of the legs, i. e. tarsal and other joints ]: (S, K:) so too the legs of a wild bull, meaning slender, not swollen, in the kuEuwb ; even and smooth therein; thus in the saying of En-Nábighah Edh-Dhubyánee, describing dogs and a [wild] bull: fabav~ahun~a Ealayohi waA@sotamar~a bihi SumoEu AlkuEuwbi bariyoA=tN mina AlHaradi [ And he (the owner of the dogs) has dispersed them (the dogs) against him; and legs ( qawaAy^imu being understood) slender and even and smooth in the joints, free from the disease that would render them unsteady, (such being here meant by AlHarad , which is properly in camels,) have been strong to bear him. ] (L, TA. [See also De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, sec. ed., ii. 438-9.]) You say also qanaApN SamoEaA='u AlkuEuwbi i. e. [ A spear-shaft ] even and smooth [ in the knots, or joints ]: or, as some say, compact in the interior, hard, and slender in the knots. (TA.) And rumoHN A^aSomaEu AlkaEobi i. e. A spear pointed in the kEb [app. meaning the knot that forms its lower extremity ]. (TA.) ― -b5- A^aSomaEu applied to a feather means Slender in the Easiyb [or shaft ]: (O, TA:) AlEasiybu All~aTiyfu in the K is a mistake for All~aTiyfu AlEasiybi : (TA:) or the best of feathers; (K, TA;) such as is used for feathering an arrow, of the kind called ZuhaAr [q. v.]: (TA:) pl. SumoEaAnN , (O, K,) which is said to mean the best of the feathers of a bird. (O.) ― -b6- Applied to a plant, it means Having fruit come forth that has not yet broken open: (O, K:) or, as some say, saturated with moisture, and compact: and SamoEaA='u is said to have this latter meaning applied to a plant such as is termed baqolap : (TA:) and the same, (i. e. the fem.,) applied to the plant called buhomaY , that has risen high, (Az, S, O, K,) and attained its complete growth, (Az, O, TA,) before the bursting open of its pericarps: (S, O, K:) [and so as applied to any plant: (see busorN :)] or, applied to a plant, smooth and round and slender: (O, K:) or any calyx ( buroEuwmap ) that has not yet opened: (AHn, O, K:) and, applied to the plant called bhmY , of which the calyxes have not opened, and the awn has not yet appeared: (O:) or, thus applied, fresh, or juicy, and not yet burst open: or having its fruit, or produce, coming forth upon its upper part: accord. to IAar, thus applied, it is an intensive epithet, [app. meaning full-grown and flourishing, ] like jaEodN applied to the Sil~iyaAn , and A^asoHamu applied to the naSiY~ : (TA:) the pl. is SumoEN . (O, K.) ― -b7- A^aSomaEu Alqalobi means Vigilant, and sharp, or acute, in mind: (S, O, K:) and qalobN A^aSomaEu an intelligent and acute mind: (TA:) and AlA^aSomaEaAni the sharp, or acute, (S, O, K,) and vigilant (K) mind, (S, O, K,) and the resolute, ( EaAzim , S, and so in the L,) or prudent, or discreet, or intelligent, or firm and sound, ( HaAzim , O, K,) judgment, or opinion: (S, O, K:) accord. to As, A^aSomaEu applied to the mind ( fuw^aAd ), and to judgment, or opinion, means EaAzimN [expl. above]: and rajulN A^aSomaEu Alqalobi means a man of acute intelligence. (TA.) [See also SamiEN .] And one says also EazomapN SamoEaA='u i. e. An effective resolution, or determination. (TA.) ― -b8- [It is said that] A^aSomaEu signifies also A sharp sword: (O, K:) this and the next two significations are related as on the authority of El-Muärrij; but Az says that all that has been related as from him is of the things that are not to be regarded unless the transmission from him prove to be correct. (TA.) ― -b9- And One that ascends, or rises by degrees, to the most elevated of places. (O, K.) ― -b10- And i. q. saAdirN [which means In a state of confusion or perplexity, and unable to see his right course: &c.: see this latter word]. (O, K.) ― -b11- And AlS~amoEaA='u also signifies The saAlifap [meaning the side of the upper part of the neck ], (O, K,) and the place of the ear: (O:) this is said to be its meaning as used in a verse of Abu-n-Nejm, (O, TA,) describing a male ostrich. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K,) aor. , inf. n. SahorN , (K,) He melted, or liquefied, a thing, (S, A, K,) such as fat, (A, TA,) and the like; (TA;) as also ↓ ASThr . (K.) The saying laA^aSoharan~aka biyamiynK mur~apK app. means (assumed tropical:) I will assuredly melt thee [in the fire of Hell by making thee to swear a bitter oath ]: (S:) or (tropical:) I will assuredly make thee to swear a hard oath. (A.) One says also, Saharotu fulaAnFA biyamiynK kaA*ibapK tuwojibu lahu Aln~aAra (assumed tropical:) [ I caused such a one to melt, by making him to swear a false oath that would procure for him, as a consequence thereof, the fire of Hell]. (AO.) ― -b2- Also, inf. n. as above, He, or it, burned: he thoroughly cooked with fire. (TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) It (heat) affected him severely. (A.) And Saharatohu Al$~amosu (tropical:) The sun affected him severely by its heat, (S, * A, K, * TA,) so that it pained his brain. (TA.) Ibn-Ahmar says, describing the young one of a qaTaAp , (S, O,) which was bearing water to it, (O,) tarowiY laqFY A^uloqiYa fiY SafoSafK ↓ taSoharuhu Al$~amosu famaA yanoSahiro i. e. [ She bearing water to a castaway, cast upon a plain, ] which the sun was melting, [or severely affecting, ] and [ which did not melt, meaning] which endured the sun's melting it. (S, * O. [In both of my copies of the S, and in the O and TA, the first word is tarowiY , as above; not turowiY .]) And you say, Sahara AlHar~u AlHirobaA='a (tropical:) The heat made the chameleon's back to glisten. (TA.) ― -b4- And Sahara xubozahu He seasoned his bread with SuhaArap , (AZ, A, TA,) i. e. melted fat. (A, TA.) And Sahara raA^osahu He anointed his head with SuhaArap . (A, K.) And Sahara badanahu He anointed his body with Sahiyr [which is like SuhaArap ]. (L, TA.) -A2- Saharahu also signifies (assumed tropical:) He brought, or drew, it (i. e. a thing, O) near, A_ilayohi [ to him or it ]; and so ↓ AShrhu . (O, TA.)

sourceDefinition: Relationship; nearness with respect to kindred; syn. qaraAbapN : (A, K:) and [ affinity; or] the sacred, or inviolable, tie ( Huromap ) of relationship consisting in being a father or brother or other kinsman of a man's wife: (Mgh, K:) and ↓ SuhuwrapN the sacred, or inviolable, tie ( Huromap ) of relationship by marriage: (A:) Fr makes the former word of the fem. gender. (Sgh, TA.) ― -b2- And A relation, or kinsman, or kinswoman, of a man's wife: (Kh, S, A, Msb:) and of a woman's husband: (A:) or the father or brother or other kinsman of a woman's husband; syn. Hamo'N [and HamN &c. (see art. Hmw )]: (Kh, As, ISk, Msb:) and the father or brother or other kinsman of a man's wife: (Kh, As, ISk, S, Msb, K:) so accord. to some of the Arabs: (Kh, As, S, Msb:) or none says otherwise, accord. to As, and IAar says the like: (Mgh:) or any relation of a man's wife or of a woman's husband whom it is unlawful to marry; as the father, and brother, and son, and paternal uncle, and maternal uncle: (Az, Msb:) or a man's relation by marriage: and a kinsman of a man's relation by marriage: (A:) or a man who has married among a people: (Lth, Mgh:) and the husband of a man's daughter: and the husband of a man's sister: (IAar, K:) Fr says that, in the Kur xxv. 56, it signifies, a relation whom it is lawful to marry; as the daughter of a paternal uncle, and of a maternal uncle, and the like: and nasab in the same, a relation whom it is unlawful to marry: Zj, that the former signifies a relation whom it is unlawful to marry: and the latter, such as is not a Sihor , of those mentioned in the Kur [iv. 27], from the words “ your mothers are forbidden unto you ” to the words “ and your combining [as your wives] two sisters: ” I'Ab explains nsb and Shr in the former passage of the Kur differently from Fr [altogether], and differently in part from Zj; saying that the former applies to the seven relations first mentioned in iv. 27 in the Kur, and Shr to the remaining six there mentioned and that mentioned in the next preceding verse; [so that it includes a man's foster-mother, who has suckled him; his fostersister, who has been suckled with him; his wife's mother; his step-daughter under his guardianship, born of his wife unto whom he has gone in; his son's wife; his wife's sister combined with that wife; and his father's wife; ] and this, says Az, is correct: (Mgh:) in the Kur xxv. 56, it means *uw SihorK , whether male or female: (Jel:) or *awaAtu SihorK : (Bd:) pl. A^aSohaArN (S, A, Msb, K, &c.) and SuhoraA='u ; (K;) which latter is extr. (TA.) [ SihorapN , applied to a female, pl. DiharaAtN , is app. postclassical.] ― -b3- And (tropical:) A grave, or sepulchre: (ISd, K:) for they used to bury their daughters alive, and say, “ We have married them to the grave: ” then, in the time of El-Islám, this expression was used, and it was said, niEoma AlS~ihoru Alqaboru [ An excel-lent son-in-law is the grave ]: or it means, correctly, that which supplies the place of the Shr . (ISd.)

definition: [The species of glasswort, or kali, called ] gaAsuwl , for [ washing ] clothes: n.
sourceDefinition: [The species of glasswort, or kali, called ] gaAsuwl , for [ washing ] clothes: n. un. with p : (K:) accord. to IDrd, the gum of a certain plant, or a certain plant [ itself ], with which clothes are washed: (O:) of the dial. of El-Yemen: (TA:) and, (O, K,) accord. to Ed-Deenawaree, (O,) i. e. AHn, (TA,) a certain plant, (K,) resembling small cucumbers, (O, K, TA,) [or] in shape like asparagus, (TA,) but thicker (O, K, TA) in a great degree, (O, TA,) four-sided in the stalks, (O, K, TA,) and having in it an acidity (O, TA,) and a bitterness ( maraArap O) or a taste between sweet and sour ( mazaAzap TA): it is crushed ( yu$odaxu O) or cut into slices ( y$rH TA) and its juice is expressed into milk such as is termed raAy^ib [q. v.], which in consequence becomes pleasant, (O, K, TA,) and somewhat biting to the tongue; and its leaves are put into sour milk, like as is done with the leaves of the mustard: (O, TA:) it is good as an aphrodisiac. (O, K, TA.)

definition: [ A bedfellow ].
sourceDefinition: [ A bedfellow ]. DajiyEuka means He who lies, or sleeps, with thee; (S, O, Msb;) i. q. ↓ muDaAjiEuka ; (K;) which latter is likewise applied to a female; as also DajiyEapN : and you say, huwa DajiyEuhaA meaning He is he who lies, or sleeps, with her in one innermost garment; and hiYa DajiyEatuhu She is she who so lies, or sleeps, with him. (TA.) And [hence] one says, biy^osa AlD~ajiyEu AljuwEu (tropical:) [ Very evil is the bedfellow, hunger ]. (TA.)

definition: A place in which, or on which, one lies upon his side [or in any manner, or sleeps ];
sourceDefinition: A place in which, or on which, one lies upon his side [or in any manner, or sleeps ]; (O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ muDoTajaEN : (O, K:) [ a bed; and the like: ] pl. maDaAjiEu : (Msb, TA:) which means sometimes places of sleep, or of passing the night: (Bd in iv. 38:) and beds; or other things spread upon the ground to lie upon. (Jel ibid., and Bd in xxxii. 16.) ― -b2- [Hence] the pl. is used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Wives, or women: so in the saying, huwa Tay~ibu AlmaDaAjiEi i. e. (assumed tropical:) He has well-born wives or women; like kariymu AlmafaAri$i . (TA.) ― -b3- And maDaAjiEu Algayovi means (tropical:) The places of falling of rain. (O, K, TA.) One says, baAtati Alr~iyaADu maDaAjiEa lilogayovi (tropical:) [ The meadows were during the night places of the falling of rain ]. (A, TA.)

(TA.)

definition: Flesh-meat roasted, but not thoroughly cooked: (S, A, O:) accord.
sourceDefinition: Flesh-meat roasted, but not thoroughly cooked: (S, A, O:) accord. to El-Mufaddal, flesh-meat cut in pieces; (O;) and thus in the K; (TA;) but IF says that this is nought, unless it be cut in pieces roasted: (O:) it is at variance with what is said by the leading authorities, for they say that it means flesh-meat roasted upon heated stones: or roasted upon the fire, but not thoroughly cooked: (TA:) or cooked in a fryingpan. (TA in art. ErS .) (S, O.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, A, Mgh, &c.,) inf. n. TarodN (S, A, L, Mgh, Msb, K) and TaradN , (S, A, L, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) He drove away him, or it; as also ↓ Tr~dhu and ↓ AiT~aradahu : (L:) he drove him away, expelled him, or banished him, (ISk, S, L, K,) and said to him, Depart thou, or go thou away, from us: (ISk, S, L:) he removed him, or it; put, or placed, him, or it, at a distance, away, or far away; (S, A, Mgh, L, K; *) with his hand, or arm, or with an instrument in his hand; as when one says Taradotu Al*~ubaAba Eani Al$~araAbi [ I drove away the flies from the wine, or beverage ]. (Durrat el-Ghowwás, in De Sacy's Anthol. Gramm. Ar., p. 60 of the Ar. text.) You say, Taradotuhu fa*ahaba [ I drove him away, &c., and he went away ], (Sb, S, Msb,) using *hb in the place of the quasi-pass., (Msb,) not using [in this case] the measure AinofaEala (S, A) nor AifotaEala , (S,) [i. e.] you do not say ↓ AnTrd nor ↓ AT~rd , (Sb, Msb,) except in a bad dialect. (S, A, Msb.) And you say, mar~a fulaAnN yaToruduhumo Such a one went along driving them away and pursuing them. (S, L.) ― -b2- And Tarada AlA_ibila , [aor. ,] (S, L,) inf. n. TarodN and TaradN , He drove, or brought, or gathered, the camels together, from their several quarters. (S, L, K. *) ― -b3- [And Tarada , aor. and inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He coursed, pursued, hunted, or strove to gain possession of or to catch, wild animals or the like]: the inf. n. TaradN is expl. as signifying muzaAwalapu AlS~ayodi [and TarodN is very frequently used in this sense]. (S, K.) You say, xaraja yaTorudu Humura AlwaHo$i (tropical:) He went forth to course, pursue, hunt, snare, entrap, or catch, the wild asses. (A.) And Taradati AlkilaAbu AlS~ayoda (assumed tropical:) The dogs drove away, and pursued closely, the wild animals, or the like. (L.) And AlS~ayoda ↓ TArd , inf. n. TiraAdN , (assumed tropical:) He circumvented, in order to snare, entrap, or catch, the wild animal, or wild animals, or the like; and in like manner, a serpent. (L.) ― -b4- And Taradotu Alqawoma I came to the people, or party, or came upon them, or destroyed them, ( A^atayotuhumo , K, or A^atayEtu Ealayohimo , T, S, L,) and passed through them. (T, S, L, K.) ― -b5- And Alr~iyHu taTorudu AlHaSaY waAlS~afaY (tropical:) The wind blows away with violence the pebbles and the dust. (A.) ― -b6- And AlqiyEaAnu taTorudu Als~araAba (tropical:) The plains have the mirage running along them like water. (A.) ― -b7- And Taradotu baSariY fiY A^amori Alqawomi (tropical:) [ I directed my observation to the affair, or case, of the people, or party ]. (A.) ― -b8- And Taradotu AlxilaAfa fiY AlmasoA^alapi (assumed tropical:) I put forward an opposition, or a contradiction, in the question: app. from AlmuTaAradapu meaning “ the making to run in a race. ” (Msb.)

(Mz, 12th nwE . [See also the contr. $a*~a : and see muT~aridN , below.])

sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) A rivulet, or streamlet, [ regular, or uninterrupted, and ] swift in course. (L.) ― -b2- [In a copy of the A, among tropical phrases, I find jadowalN muT~aridu AlA^anaAbiybi waAlkuEuwbi ; but it seems that there is an omission here, and that after jadowalN we should read muT~aridN ; and then, warumoHN Alx , i. e. (tropical:) A spear even and regular in the internodal portions and the knots. ] See muTar~idN . ― -b3- [Hoseyn Ibn-Homám El-Murree applies muT~arid , as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates, to A coat of mail, app. meaning even and regular in texture: see Ham p. 189.] ― -b4- baEiyrN muT~aridN (assumed tropical:) A camel that continues his pace, or course, uninterruptedly, and does not become out of breath from running. (L.) ― -b5- muT~aridu Aln~asiymi is used by a poet as a name for (assumed tropical:) The nose of a running horse [app. meaning uninterrupted in breathing ]. (S, L.) ― -b6- muT~aridN applied to a word, form or measure, construction, or government, means (tropical:) Agreeable with the common, or constant, course of speech in respect of analogy, or rule; agreeable with common, or constant, analogy, or rule: and, applied to the same, or to a rule, agreeable with the common, or constant, course of speech in respect of usage; agreeable with common, or constant, usage; commonly, or constantly, obtaining: (Mz, 12th nwE :) [but what is thus termed is not strictly speaking and in every case without exception; for, taking 24 to represent universality, 23 in comparison therewith is muT~arid ;] 20 in comparison with 23 is gaAlib ; 15 is kaviyr ; 3 is qaliyl ; and I is naAdir . (Mz, 13th nwE . [See also the contr. $aA*~N : and see 8 in this art.])

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaTiybu , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. TiybN (S [but there mentioned app. as a subst.], O, Mgh, Msb, K) and TiybapN (S, O, K) and TaAbN (K) and TuwbaY [q. v. infrà] (Ksh and Bd in xiii. 28) and taToyaAbN , (S, K,) [the last of which is of a measure denoting intensiveness, and is said in the TA to be with fet-h because it is unsound, whereas the inf. n. of a sound verb, if of the measure tfEAl , is with kesr, but this is a strange mistake, (see 2 in art. byn ,)] It was, or became, the contr. of xabiyv , (S, Mgh,) in two senses: (Mgh:) [i. e.] it was, or became, [ good, ] pleasant, delightful, delicious, sweet, or savoury; syn. la*~a ; (A, K;) or kaAna la*iy*FA ; (Msb;) or it was esteemed [ good, ] pleasant, delightful, delicious, sweet, or savoury, in taste, and in odour: (Mgh:) and it was, or became, pure, (Mgh, K,) or clean. (Mgh.) [See also Tay~ibN .] ― -b2- [Hence,] TaAbato nafosuhu (assumed tropical:) His mind [or he himself] was, or became, [ cheerful, happy, pleased, ] dilated, or free from straitness. (Msb.) And Tibotu bihi nafosFA i. q. TaAbato bihi nafosiY (assumed tropical:) [i. e. I, or my mind, was, or became, cheerful, happy, pleased, or dilated, by means of it; agreeably with what next precedes: or pleased, content, or willing, to grant, concede, give, or do, it ]: (S, O, K:) [for] TaAbato nafosuhu biAl$~aYo'i [often] signifies (tropical:) He granted, conceded, or gave, the thing, liberally, [ willingly, or of his own good pleasure, ] without constraint, and without anger. (TA.) And faEalotu *`lika biTiybapinafosK (assumed tropical:) I did that [ of my own free will; willingly; ] not being constrained by any one. (S, O.) And TaAbato nafosiY Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) [ My mind was agreeable to it ]; said when a thing is agreeable, or suitable, to one's mind; and [in like manner] Tibotu nafosFA Ealayohi . (TA.) And TaAbato nafosuhu liloEamali wagayorihi [ He was cheerful, happy, pleased, or willing, to do work &c. ]. (K in art. n$T .) And TaAbato nafosiY Eano *`lika tarokFA (assumed tropical:) [ I was pleased, willing, or content, to leave, give up, relinquish, or be without, that ]; and [in like manner] Tibotu nafosFA Eanohu : whence, in the Kur [iv. 3], faA_ino Tibona lakumo Eano $aYo'K minohu nafosFA (assumed tropical:) [ But if they be pleased, or willing, or content, to give up, or relinquish, or remit, unto you somewhat thereof ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And TAb , (A, O, Msb, TA,) inf. n. TiybN (Msb, K) and TiybapN , (K,) (tropical:) It was, or became, lawful, allowable, or free. (A, O, Msb, K, * TA.) [In the K, AlT~iybu and AlT~iybapu are expl. as meaning AlHil~u , which Golius has supposed to mean in this case “ quod licitum, legitimum; ” and which Freytag has in like manner expl. as meaning “ res licita, ” and “ licitum: ” but it is here an inf. n., of Hal~a ; not syn. with the epithet AlHalaAlu , which is given as an explanation of AlT~ay~ibu .] You say, TaAba liY ka*aA (tropical:) Such a thing became, or has become, lawful, &c., to me. (A.) Hence the saying of Aboo-Hureyreh, AaloA=na TaAba AlD~iraAbu , (TA,) or TaAba A@moDarobu , (O, TA,) as some relate it, accord. to the dial. of Himyer, (TA,) meaning TaAb A@lD~arobu , i. e. (assumed tropical:) Now fighting has become lawful. (O, TA.) faA@nokiHuwA maA TaAba lakumo mina A@ln~isaA='i , in the Kur [iv. 3], means (assumed tropical:) [ Then take ye in marriage ] such as are lawful to you [ of women ]. (Mgh.) ― -b4- And TaAbati AlA^aroDu , (K, TA,) inf. n. TiybN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) The land became abundant in herbage. (K, TA.) -A2- See also 2, in two places: ― -b2- and see 10.

(Mgh.) [See also Tay~ibN .] ― -b2- [Hence,] TaAbato nafosuhu (assumed tropical:) His mind [or he himself] was, or became, [ cheerful, happy, pleased, ] dilated, or free from straitness. (Msb.) I, or my mind, was, or became, cheerful, happy, pleased, or dilated, by means of it; agreeably with what next precedes: or pleased, content, or willing, to grant, concede, give, or do, it ]: (S, O, K:) [for] TaAbato nafosuhu biAl$~aYo'i [often] signifies (tropical:) He granted, conceded, or gave, the thing, liberally, [ willingly, or of his own good pleasure, ] without constraint, and without anger. (assumed tropical:) Now fighting has become lawful. sourceDefinition: is an inf. n. of TaAba , (K,) and syn. with TiybN and also with Tay~ibN , q. v.: a poet says, praising 'Omar Ibn-'Abd-El-'Azeez, muqaAbalu AlA_iEoraAqi fiY AlT~aAbi AlT~aAbo bayona A^abiY AlEaASiY waA=li AlxaT~aAbo [i. e. Rooted by the father's and the mother's side in unsullied goodness, or the like, between Abu-l- 'Ásee on the one side and the family of ElKhattáb on the other: for it is evidently cited as an ex. of AlTAb used as a subst. and as an epithet; so that by fY AlTAb AlTAb is meant fY AlT~iybi AlT~ay~ibi : otherwise it might be supposed that the literal repetition is meant to denote simply corroboration, as appears to be the case in an instance which will be mentioned in what follows:] the object of praise being the son of 'Abd-El-'Azeez the son of Marwán the son of El-Hakam the son of Abu-l-'Ás [or 'Ásee], and his mother being Umm-'Ásim the daughter of 'Ásim the son of 'Omar the son of El-Khattáb. (S, O.) ― -b2- Ea*oqu A@boni TaAbK is the name of A sort of palm-trees in El-Medeeneh [app. so called because of the sweetness of their fruit, or TAb may in this instance be for TaAbap , a name of ElMedeeneh]: (K:) or, as also ruTabu A@boni TaAbK , a sort of dates of El-Medeeneh: (S, O:) or Aibonu TaAbK is a name of a sort of fresh ripe dates: (K:) and Ea*oqu A@boni TaAbK and Ea*oqu A@boni zayodK are two sorts of dates: (S:) accord. to IAth, ruTabu A@boni TaAbK is the name of a sort of dates of El-Medeeneh so called in relation to Ibn-Táb, a man of its inhabitants. (TA.) ― -b3- TAb TAb is [asserted to be] One of the names of the Prophet in the Gospel; [but where said to occur, I know not;] the interpretation of mA^* mA^* ; [app. a mistranscription for maA* maA* , meaning “ very good in disposition, ” &c.;] the second word corroborating, and denoting intensiveness of signification. (TA.)

definition: , of the measure fuEolaY from AlT~iybu , originally TuyobaY , (Zj, S, O, Msb,) an inf.
sourceDefinition: , of the measure fuEolaY from AlT~iybu , originally TuyobaY , (Zj, S, O, Msb,) an inf. n. of TaAbN , (Ksh and Bd in xiii. 28,) syn. with TiybN : (Seer, K: [in my MS copy of the K Tay~ib , a manifest mistake:]) and fem. of A^aToyabu : (ISd, K:) and pl. of Tay~ibapN , (K,) accord. to Kr, who says that there is no word like it except kuwsaY pl. of kay~isapN , and DuwqaY pl. of Day~iqapN ; but ISd says that, in his opinion, TuwbaY and kuwsaY and DuwqaY are fems. of A^aToyabu and A^akoyasu and A^aDoyaqu , because fuEolaY is not a pl. measure: Kr also adds that they did not say ↓ TiybaY , like as they said kiysaY and DiyqaY ; (TA; [see DuwqaY , in art. Dyq ;]) [but Sgh says that] ↓ TiybaY is a dial. var. of TuwbaY : (O:) Aboo-Hátim Sahl Ibn-Mohammad Es-Sijistánee relates that an Arab of the desert, reciting as a pupil to him, persisted in pronouncing TuyobaY for TuwbaY : (TA:) it signifies HusonaY [as meaning A good final, or ultimate, state or condition ]: and (some say, O, Msb) xayorN [meaning good, good fortune, and the like ]: (O, Msb, K:) and xiyrapN [meaning God's blessing or favour, &c.]; (K;) as some say: (TA:) or eternal life: (Zj, TA:) or a pleasant life: (Msb:) and (O, K) a certain tree in Paradise; (S, O, K;) thus the Prophet is related to have said; and MF says that it is a proper name thereof, not admitting the article Al , and the like is said in the M: (TA:) or it signifies Paradise in the Indian language; (O, K;) or, accord. to Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr, in the Abyssinian language: (O:) as also ↓ TiybaY . (K.) These different significations are assigned by different persons to this word in the phrase in the Kur [xiii. 28] TuwbaY lahumo [which seems to be best rendered as an announcement, meaning A good final state, &c., shall be to them, or be their lot ]: (Msb, TA:) Sb holds that it is an invocation of good, or a prayer, [as though qulo i. e. “ say thou ” were understood before it,] and that TwbY is virtually in the nom. case, i. e. marofuwE , as is shown by the words immediately following waHusonu maA=bK : but Th, who makes TwbY to be an inf. n. like rujoEaY , says that one reading is TuwbaY lahumo waHusona maA=bK , like the phrase saqoyFA lahu : MF, however, [supposing Th to have said TuwbFY , though I think it indubitable that he said TuwbaY , and only meant that it was used as virtually, not literally, with tenween,] observes that rujoEFY , with tenween, is not known to have been transmitted from any one of the leading authorities on the Arabic language. (TA.) Katádeh says that TuwbaY lahumo is a phrase of the Arabs; who say, TuwbaY laka A_ino faEalota ka*aA waka*aA [ A good final state &c., be to thee, or be thy lot, or shall be to thee, if thou do such and such things ]: and it is said in a trad., TuwbaY lil$~aA^omi [ May good, &c., betide Syria ]; in which case, TwbY is of the measure fuEolaY from AlT~iybu , and does not mean “ Paradise, ” nor “ the tree. ” (L, TA.) One says, TuwbaY laka and TuwbaAka ; (S, K;) but not Tuwabyoka : (Yaakoob, S, O: [in one of my copies of the S Tuwbiyka :]) or TuwbaAka is a barbarism: (O, K:) it is disallowed by the T, and by most of the grammarians: but Akh says that it is used by some of the Arabs; and Ibn-El-Moatezz uses it in the following verse: mar~ato binaA saHarFA TayorN faqulotu lahaA TuwbaAki yaA layotanaA A_iy~aAki TuwbaAki [ A flock of birds passed by us a little before daybreak, and I said to them, Good betide you: would that we were you: good betide you ]: Esh- Shiháb El-Khafájee says that l is understood [before the k ] in TwbAk ; but MF has argued well against this assertion. (TA.)

definition: A sort of palm-trees of El-Basrah, (L, K, TA,) the dates of which, when the gathering has been delayed beyond the usual time, fall, one after another, from their stones, so that the raceme remains...
sourceDefinition: A sort of palm-trees of El-Basrah, (L, K, TA,) the dates of which, when the gathering has been delayed beyond the usual time, fall, one after another, from their stones, so that the raceme remains with nothing upon it but the stones hanging to the bases of the dates; though they are large; and if the fruit is gathered when fully ripe, the stone does not come off with it. (L, TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and ↓ TaAbN , (S, M, O, K,) the latter originally TaAy^ibN and deprived of its medial radical letter, or of the measure faEalN , (M, TA,) Contr. of xabiyvN , (S, Mgh, O,) in two senses: (Mgh:) [i. e. good, ] pleasant, delightful, delicious, sweet, or savoury; syn. la*iy*N ; (Msb, K; *) or esteemed [ good, ] pleasant, delightful, delicious, sweet, or savoury, ( musotala*~N ,) in taste, and in odour: (Mgh:) and pure, (Mgh, K,) or clean. (Mgh.) You say TaEaAmN Tay~ibN Food [ pleasant in taste; or] that descends easily [ and agreeably ] down the throat. (TA.) And maA='N Tay~ibN Sweet water; (O, TA;) or pure water. (TA.) [And raAy^iHapN Tay~ibapN A pleasant, sweet, or fragrant, odour. ] And baladN Tay~ibN A country that has no salsuginous places in it: (O, TA:) or a land of good and fertile soil. (Mgh.) And SaEiydN Tay~ibN Pure ground. (Zj, Mgh, O.) And Alkalimu AlT~ay~ibu (assumed tropical:) [ The good saying ] i. e. laA A_il`ha A_il~aA A@ll~`hu [ There is no deity but God ]. (TA.) And fulaAnN fiY bayotK Tay~ibK i. e. (tropical:) [ Such a one is of a good house, or family; meaning,] of high, or noble, birth. (TA.) And fulaAnN Tay~ibu AlA_izaAri (assumed tropical:) Such a one is continent, or chaste. (O.) And fulaAnN Tay~ibu AlA^axolaAqi (assumed tropical:) Such a one is [ of good, or pleasant, dispositions; ] easy in converse, conversable, or affable. (O, TA.) [And Tay~ibu Aln~afosi (assumed tropical:) Cheerful, happy, pleased, or dilated, in mind. (See TaAbato nafosuhu .) And nafosN Tay~ibapN bi$aYo'K (assumed tropical:) A mind cheerful, happy, pleased, or dilated, by means of a thing: or pleased, content, or willing, to grant, concede, give, or do, a thing: and Tay~ibapN Eano $aYo'K (assumed tropical:) pleased, willing, or content, to leave, give up, relinquish, or be without, a thing. (See, again, 1.)] ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Lawful; allowable; allowable by, or agreeable to, law; legitimate; legal; or free. (Mgh, Msb, K.) laA yasotawiY A@loxabiyvu waA@lT~ay~ibu , in the Kur [v. 100], means (assumed tropical:) The unlawful and the lawful of property and the unrighteous and the righteous of deeds and the sound and the unsound of tenets or the like and the good and the bad of mankind [ shall not be equal in your estimation]. (Mgh.) [See also the next paragraph.]

(O.) ― -b2- See also Tayobapu .

sourceDefinition: pass. part. n. of 2. (TA.) Hence, (TA,) Hilofu AlmuTay~abiyna [ The covenant of the perfumed men ]: (K, TA:) these were five tribes; Benoo-'Abd-Menáf and Benoo-Asad-Ibn-'AbdEl-'Ozzà and Benoo-Teym and Benoo-Zuhrah and Benu-l-Hárith and Benoo-Fihr: (TA:) and they were so called for the following reason: when Benoo-'Abd-Menáf desired to assume [the offices of] the HijaAbap and the rifaAdap and the liwaA=' and the siqaAyap , [see arts. Hjb &c.,] which belonged to Benoo-'Abd-ed-Dár, and these refused their consent, all of the above-mentioned, (K, TA,) having assembled in the house of Ibn-Jud'án, in the Time of Ignorance, (TA,) concluded a ratified covenant for the accomplishment of their affair, engaging not to fail in aiding one another: then they mixed some perfumes, and dipped their hands therein; after which they wiped their hands upon the Kaabeh in token of confirmation of the covenant: and Benoo-'Abded-Dár, also, and their confederates, (K, TA,) composing six tribes, Benoo-'Abd-ed-Dár and Jumah and Makhzoom and 'Adee and Kaab and Sahm, (TA,) concluded together another covenant, and were thence called AlA^aHolaAf : (K, TA:) this is the account commonly known and received: another account is the following: there came a man of the Benoo-Zeyd to Mekkeh for the purpose of [the religious visit termed] the Eumorap , having with him merchandise, and a man of Sahm bought this of him, and refused to pay him for it; whereupon he called to them from the summit of Aboo-Kubeys, and they arose, and entered into a covenant together to do him justice: thus relates Eth-Tha'álibee: (TA:) Mohammad was one of the muTay~abuwn , (K, TA,) being then twenty-five years old; and so was Aboo-Bekr: and 'Omar was an A^aHolafiY~ . (TA.) ― -b2- AlmuTay~abapu : see Tayobapu .

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n., EitoqN ; (S, O;) or Eataqa Alfarasu , aor. ; and Eatuqa ; The mare, (S, O,) or horse, (K,) preceded, and became safe, or secure: (S, O, K:) [or,] accord. to IDrd, Eatuqa Alfarasu , with damm, signifies the horse became such as is termed Eatiyq [q. v.]. (O.) The meaning of The state, or act, of preceding, or having precedence, [assigned to the inf. n. EitoqN ,] is said to be the turning-point of the art.: and hence, Eataqa Alxayola , said of a horse, means He preceded the other horses, and became safe, or secure, from them. (Mgh.) And Eataqotu Al$~aYo'a , aor. , I preceded the thing. (Msb.) ― -b2- Eataqa AlEabodu , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. EitoqN (S, Mgh, O, K) and EatoqN , (K,) or the former is a simple subst. and the latter is an inf. n., (Msb, K,) as also EataAqN (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and EataAqapN , (S, O, Msb, K,) The slave became free; (S, O;) the slave passed forth from the state of slavery. (Mgh, K.) And sometimes EitoqN is used in the place of A_iEotaAqN ; (Mgh;) and so is EataAqN , in the saying Halafa biAlEataAqi [ He swore by emancipation ]: (TA:) but see 4. [Hence,] one says, fulaAnN mawolaY EataAqapK [ Such a one is a freed slave ]. (S, O, K. [See also EatiyqN .]) ― -b3- Eataqato mina AlS~ibaA is said of a girl when she has attained to the marriageable state [meaning She has passed forth from the state of childhood ]. (O, TA.) And Eataqato , aor. , She (a girl) attained to the commencement of the state of puberty: and as some say, had not married: (K, * TA:) [or] she (a woman) passed forth from the state, or condition, of serving her father and mother, and from being possessed by a husband. (Msb.) ― -b4- Eataqa baEoda A@sotiEolaAjK , aor. , He (a man, S, O) became thin, or fine, or delicate, in his external skin, after having been coarse and rough; (S, O, K;) as also Eatuqa . (K.) ― -b5- Eataqa , said of anything, It attained its utmost point, reach, or degree. (TA.) ― -b6- Eataqati Albakorapu The young she-camel became free from AlquroHap [or purulent pustules in the mouth ] and AlEur~ap [i. e. mange, or scab ]: until this is the case, she is not reckoned a bakorap : so said an Arab of the desert. (TA.) ― -b7- Eataqa , (Msb,) or Eataqa AlmaAlu , (S, O, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. EitoqN ; (Fr, S, O;) and Eatuqa ; (K;) It, (Msb,) or the property, or cattle, (Fr, S, O, K,) became in a good, right, or proper, state. (Fr, S, O, Msb, K.) ― -b8- See also 4. ― -b9- Eatuqa Al$~aYo'u , (S, Mgh, O, K,) inf. n. EataAqapN ; (S, Mgh, O;) and Eataqa , aor. (S, O, K) and ; (K;) The thing became old. (S, Mgh, O, K.) Both of these verbs, in this sense, are said of clarified butter. (TA.) And you say, Eatuqati Alxamoru ; (S, Msb, K;) and Eataqat , (Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. EatoqN and EitoqN ; (Msb;) The wine became old (Msb, K) and good. (K.) ― -b10- Eataqato Ealayohi yamiynN , (S, O, K,) aor. ; (S, K; in one of my copies of the S ;) and Eatuqato ; (S, O, K;) The oath was binding on him: (K:) or was old, and binding on him; as though he kept it [long], not violating it. (S, O.) -A2- Eataqahu bifiyhi , inf. n. definition: A horse that precedes, outstrips, or outgoes;
sourceDefinition: A horse that precedes, outstrips, or outgoes; as also ↓ EaAtiqN ; or this signifies a horse that precedes, and becomes safe, or secure; (TA; [see 1, first and second sentences;]) or that precedes, outstrips, or outgoes, the [ other ] horses: (Msb:) and the former, a generous, or an excellent, horse: (Msb, TA:) or a horse swift and excellent; or that excites admiration by his generousness or excellence; syn. raAy^iEN : (S, Mgh, O, TA:) pl. EitaAqN : (S, O, Msb:) EatiyqapN applied to a young she-camel means generous, excellent, or swift: (TA:) and EitaAqN has this meaning applied to camels, (TA,) or to such as are termed A^aroHabiy~aAt , (S, O, TA,) and to horses; (K, TA;) or the EitaAq of horses are the generous, or excellent, thereof; and so of birds; (Mgh;) [the noble thereof, in a sense wider that that in which this epithet is applied in English falconry;] or of birds, such as prey; (S, O, K, TA;) EatiyqN being applied to one of them: (TA:) EitaAqu AlT~ayori is also applied [particularly] to eagles: (IAar, TA voce EuqaAbN :) and Eatiyqu AlT~ayori , to the hawk, or falcon: (O, TA:) and EatiyqN signifies anything generous, or excellent; (S;) and anything choice, or best; (S, O, K;) thus applied to a hawk, and dates, and water, and fat: (S:) or AlEatiyqu means dates [themselves], (AHn, O, K,) as in a verse of 'Antarah (or of Khuzaz-Ibn-Lowdhán, S, TA) cited voce ka*aba , (O,) as a proper name thereof; (K;) or, as some say, the dates termed $ihoriyz ; and its pl. is EutuqN : (TA:) and water [itself]: (K:) and fat [itself]: and accord. to IAar, anything that has attained the utmost degree in goodness or badness or beauty or ugliness is termed EatiyqN ; pl. EutuqN . (TA.) ― -b2- Also Beautiful, or comely: so in the saying, fulaAnN Eatiyqu Alwajohi [ Such a one is beautiful, or comely, in respect of the face ]. (O, TA.) And AimoraA^apN EatiyqapN means A woman beautiful, or comely; generous, or noble. (TA.) ― -b3- And (applied to a man, S, O) Thin, or fine, or delicate, in his external skin, after having been coarse and rough. (S, O, K.) ― -b4- And, applied to a slave, signifying Freed from slavery, or emancipated; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, * K;) as also ↓ EaAtiqN , and ↓ muEotaqN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) and some of the relaters of traditions say ↓ maEotuwqN , (TA,) but this is not allowable: (Msb, TA:) EatiyqapN is applied to a female, (S, O, Msb, K,) and EatiyqN also: Msb:) the pl. of EatiyqN is EutaqaA='u , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) and EitaAqN also sometimes occurs, like kiraAmN as a pl. of kariymN ; (Msb;) and the pl. of EatiyqapN is EataAy^iqu . (S, O, Msb.) AlEatiyqu is an appellation applied to Es-Siddeek, (S, K,) i. e. (S) to Aboo-Bekr, (S, O, K,) as a surname, (K,) because he was said by the Prophet to be freed ( Eatiyq ) from the fire [of Hell]: or because of his beauty, or comeliness: (S, O, K:) or he was so named by his mother. (O, K.) ― -b5- And Old; (S, Mgh, O, L, Msb, K;) as also ↓ EaAtiqN : (S, O:) the former is applied in this sense to anything, even to a man: (S, L:) and the pl. is EitaAqN , which occurs in a trad. applied to the earlier verses of the Kur-án that were revealed at Mekkeh, (L, TA,) and EutoqN , (S, K, *) or EutuqN , with two dammehs, (Mgh, Msb,) like burudN pl. of bariydN , (Msb,) applied to daraAhim , (Mgh, Msb,) EutoqN being [probably] a contraction of EutuqN (like as burodN is of burudN ) and in like manner applied to danaAniyr , (S,) [and Eut~aqN occurs in the TA in art. sm , agreeably with general analogy if pl. of EaAtiqN ,] but Eut~uqN , with two dammehs and teshdeed, is a mistake. (Mgh.) Albayotu AlEatiyqu is an appellation of The Kaabeh, (S, O, K,) given to it in the Kur-án [xxii. 30 and 34, as meaning the Old House ], (O,) because it was the first house founded upon the earth, (O, K,) as is said in the Kur [iii. 90]: (O:) or [as meaning (assumed tropical:) the Freed House, ] because it was freed from submersion (O, K) in the days of the Deluge, (O,) being taken up; (TA;) or from the imperious, overbearing, or tyrannical, of mankind; or from the Abyssinians; or because not possessed by any one; (O, K;) and [thus expl.] it is tropical. (TA.) You say qanoTarapN EatiyqapN [ An old bridge ], (S, O, K,) with p , (S, O,) and qanoTarapN jadiydN [meaning the contr.], (S, O, K,) without p , (S, O,) because EatiyqapN has the meaning of the measure faAEilapN , (S, O, K,) but jadiydN has the meaning of the measure mafoEuwlapN . (S, O.) And raAHN EatiyqN , (O, K,) without p , (O,) and EatiyqapN and ↓ EaAtiqN [app. meaning Old wine ]: (K:) and ↓ xamorN EaAtiqN and EatiyqN and ↓ EutaAqN good and old wine: (K, in a later portion of the art.:) or ↓ EaAtiqN means old wine: (S, O, TA:) or long kept in its receptacle: (L, TA:) or of which no one has broken the seal [ upon the mouth of its jar ]: (S, O, TA:) or that has just attained to maturity: (Z, TA:) Hassán says, [using it as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates,] kaA@lomisoka taxoliTuhu bimaA='i saHaAbapK A^awo EaAtiqK kadami Al*~abiyHi mudaAmi [ Like musk which thou mixest with the water of a cloud, or old wine (&c.) like the blood of the slaughtered animal, made to continue long in its unopened jar]. (S, O, TA: but the last, for taxoliTuhu , has muxotaliTN .) ― -b6- And AlEatiyqu signifies Wine [itself]. (K.) And [ What is termed ] AlT~ilaA='u [app. as meaning expressed juice of grapes boiled until the quantity thereof is reduced to one third or half ]. (K.) ― -b7- And Milk. (K.) ― -b8- And A [ sort of ] male palm-tree, (K, TA,) well known, (TA,) of which the female palm-tree will not shake off, or drop, its fruit ( laA tanofuDu naxolatuhu ). (K, TA.) ― -b9- And vawobN EatiyqN means jay~idu AlHbkpi [app. a mistranscription, for jay~idu AlHaboki , i. e. A garment, or piece of cloth, well woven ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: : see the next preceding paragraph, in six places. ― -b2- Also A young bird (S, O, K, TA) above the stage of that which is termed naAhiD , (S, O, TA,) i. e. of that of which the first feathers have fallen off and strong feathers have grown; (TA;) when it has flown and become independent; (K, TA;) thought by A'Obeyd to be from the meaning of “ outgoing, ” or “ outstripping, ” kaA^an~ahu yaEotiqu A^aYo yasobiqu [as though it outwent, or outstripped]: (S, O, TA:) or of the young of the sandgrouse ( AlqaTaA ), or of the pigeon, while not yet firm, or strong, (K, TA,) not advanced in age: (TA:) pl., in this and the following senses, EawaAtiqu . (K.) ― -b3- And A girl that has attained to the commencement of the state of puberty, (S, O, K,) and become kept behind the curtain in the tent, or house, of her family, (S, O,) and not been separated to a husband: (S, O, K:) said by IAar to be so called because she has passed forth from the state of childhood, and attained to being marriageable; (O;) or because she has passed forth from the state, or condition, of serving her father and mother, and has not yet been possessed by a husband; but AAF says that this is not valid: or that has attained to the wearing of the garment called diroE , and has passed forth from the state of childhood and of being required to help in the service of her family: (TA:) or such as is between the stages of puberty and middle age: (K:) or a woman who has passed forth from the state, or condition, of serving her father and mother, and from being possessed by a husband: (Msb:) pl. as above, and Eut~aqN also; the latter occurring in a trad. (TA.) ― -b4- And A ziq~ [or wine-skin], (T, S, &c.,) of which the wine is good: (T, TA:) or of which the odour is pleasant, because of its oldness: (S:) or wide, (Ibn-'Abbád, O, L, K,) and good: or wide as applied to a [leathern water-bag such as is called] mazaAdap . (TA.) ― -b5- And A bow ( qawosN ) that has become altered in colour; as also EaAtikN : (IF, O:) or EaAtiqapN (S, O, K) and EaAtiqN (K) a bow that has become old and red; (S, O, K;) as also EaAtikapN . (S, O.) -A2- AlEaAtiqu also signifies The part, of the manokib [or shoulder ], which is the place of the [ garment called ] ridaA=' : (S, O, K:) or the part between the manokib and the neck; (Mgh, Msb, K:) which is the place of the ridaA=' : (Msb:) or the part, of the katif [properly the shoulder-blade, but app. here meaning, as in some other instances, the shoulder itself], which is the place of the suspensory-cord of the sword: (Ham p. 556:) it is [said to be] masc. and fem.; (S, O, Msb;) sometimes fem.; (K;) but this is not of established authority: a verse which is cited by IB [and in the O] as an instance of its being fem. is asserted by some to be forged: (TA:) the pl. is EawaAtiqu (Msb, K, and Ham ubi suprà,) and EutoqN . (K.) One says rajulN A^amoyalu AlEaAtiqi A man bent, or bending, [or sloping, ] in [ the part which is ] the place of the ridaA=' . (S, O.) Habolu AlEaAtiqi see in art. Hbl . ― -b2- And [the pl.] AlEawaAtiqu signifies also Aln~awaAHiY [ The sides; or lateral, or outward, or adjacent, parts or portions; &c.: see the sing., naAHiyapN ]. (Ibn- 'Abbád, O.)

[a beast, or] a horse, (Msb,) or they, i. e. cattle, ( maAl , Fr, S, O,) became lean, meagre, or emaciated; (S;) lost his, or their, fatness or plumpness: (O, K:) or became weak. (Msb.) [See also EajafN , below.] -A2- Eajafahu , or Eajafa Ald~aAb~apa , see 4. ― -b2- Eajafa nafosahu Eani AlT~aEaAmi , aor. , inf. n. EajofN and EujuwfN , He withheld himself from the food, though desiring it, preferring that one who was hungry should have it; (O, K;) or (K) he left the food, though desiring it, (O,) in order that he who was eating with him might become satisfied in stomach; (O, K;) as also ↓ Ej~f , inf. n. taEojiyfN . (K.) And Eajafa nafosahu EalaY fulaAnK [ He restrained himself for such a one ] means he chose that such a one should have the food in preference to himself. (S.) EujuwfN also signifies The leaving, or relinquishing, food, (IAar, O, K, TA,) with desire for it. (TA.) And [hence, app.,] The withholding oneself from evil acts or dispositions. (TA.) ― -b3- And Eajafa nafosahu , (L, K,) aor. , inf. n. EajofN , (L, TA,) He constrained himself to be forbearing. (L, K, TA.) You say, Eajafa nafosahu EalaY fulaAnK , (O, K,) aor. , inf. n. EajofN [and app. EujuwfN also], (O,) He bore, or endured, what proceeded from such a one, and did not punish him. (O, K.) And Eajafa nafosahu EalaY AlmariyDi , (O, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (O,) He constrained himself to exercise patience toward the sick man in tending him in his sickness; as also binafosihi Ealayohi ↓ A^aEojafa . (O, K.) ― -b4- And Eajafa Eano fulaAnK [ nafosahu being app. understood] He withdrew himself, or became aloof, from such a one. (K.)

sourceDefinition: Lean, meagre, or emaciated; (S;) having lost his fatness or plumpness: (O, K:) or weak: (Msb:) and ↓ EajifN signifies the same, applied to a man and to a woman: and ↓ EajiyfN also signifies lean, meagre, or emaciated: (TA:) and ↓ maEojuwfN [likewise] is syn. with A^aEojafu , applied to a camel; (O, K;) as also ↓ munoEajifN , (K, TA,) in some copies of the K erroneously written mutaEaj~ifN : (TA:) the fem. of A^aEojafu is EajofaA='u : and the pl. is EijaAfN , which is irreg., having this form to assimilate it to simaAnN , (S, O, Msb, K,) or to its like DiEaAfN , (Msb,) and which is applied to males and to females: (O, TA:) the pl. of ↓ EajifN , also, is EijaAfN : (TA:) and the pl. of ↓ EajiyfN , if this be of established authority, may be EajofaY , agreeably with analogy. (MF, TA.) [Hence,] wajohN A^aEojafu and ↓ EajifN A face having little flesh. (TA.) And livapN EajofaA='u A gum having little flesh. (TA.) And $afataAni EajofaAwaAni Two thin lips. (Ks, O, K.) ― -b2- And naSolN A^aEojafu A thin, or slender, arrow-head: (S, O, K:) pl. niSaAlN EijaAfN . (O, K.) ― -b3- And A^aroDN EajofaA='u Land in which is no good. (O, K.) And A^araDuwna EijaAf Lands not rained upon. (O.) And EijaAfN is sometimes used [alone] as signifying Lands affected by drought: a poet says, describing clouds ( saHaAb ), laqiHa AlEijaAfu lahu lisaAbiEi saboEapK meaning The lands affected by drought produced herbage by reason thereof at a period of seven days after the rain. (L, TA.)

definition: A certain plant, (S,) or a sort of trees [or shrubs ], (K,) growing in plain, or soft, land: n.
sourceDefinition: A certain plant, (S,) or a sort of trees [or shrubs ], (K,) growing in plain, or soft, land: n. un. with p : (S, K:) it is said to be of the trees [or shrubs ] of the Sayof [meaning either spring or summer ], soft, or pliable, dust-coloured, and having a rough produce like the Hasak [or prickly heads of thistles and similar plants ]: (TA:) Aboo-Ziyád says, (O, TA,) as related by AHn, (O,) that it is of sweet, or pleasant, odour, dustcoloured, inclining to greenness, having a yellow blossom; (O, TA;) and when it becomes aggregated and abundant in a place, that place is called HawomaAnN : (O:) it has no grains nor thorns: (O, TA:) it and the vumaAm and the DaEap grow in plain, or soft, land, and on the mountain; and none of these has thorns: its firewood is the best of firewood in odour, and the quickest in taking fire and in blazing: (O:) AHn [also] says, certain of the Arabs of the desert informed me that its root is wide, occupying a [ considerable ] piece of ground; and it sends forth many shoots, proportionate to the root, without leaves, [but see xuwSN ,] being only slender shoots, at the extremities whereof are [ buds, or the like, such as are termed ] zamaE , at the heads of which appears a yellow substance like hair: and he says that, accord. to the ancient Arabs of the desert, it occupies a space like that of a man sitting, becomes white when it dries up, has a yellow produce, is eaten in the fresh and dry state by the camels and sheep or goats, and its flame is intensely red, whence one says, kaA^an~a liHoyatahu DiraAmu EarofajapK or EarofajK [ As though his beard were the blazing, or flaming, of an 'arfajeh or of 'arfaj ]. (TA.) The fire of the Erfj is called naAru Alz~aHofatayoni [The fire of the two walks]; because he who kindles it walks to it, and when it burns up he walks from it: (T, TA:) or because it quickly blazes and quickly subsides; so when it blazes they walk from it, and when it subsides they walk to it. (O. [See also art. zHf .]) When the greenness of plants appears in it, it is termed EarofajapN xaADibapN . (Aboo- 'Obeyd El-Bekree, TA.) When it has been rained upon, and its stalk has become soft, one says vaq~aba Euwdu AlEarofaji : when it has become somewhat black, qamila : when a little more so, AiroqaAT~a : when more so, A^adobaY : and when its xuwS are perfect, A^axowaSa . (AA, TA.) ― -b2- kaman~i Algayovi EalaY AlEarofajapi [ Like the benefit conferred by the rain upon the 'arfajeh ], meaning its falling upon it when dry, and causing it to become green, is a prov., said, accord. to AZ, to him upon whom thou hast conferred a benefit and who says to thee, Dost thou confer a benefit upon me? (TA.) ― -b3- laY~u AlEarofajapi signifies A certain mode of coïtus. (O, K.)

(TA.) ― -b2- Earaqotu maA EalaY AlEuraAqi mina All~aHomi I pared off what was on the bone, of flesh, with a miEoraq , i. e. a large, or broad, knife or blade. (TA.) ― -b3- And [hence,] Earaqatohu Als~inuwna , aor. as above, i. e. [ The years, or droughts, or years of drought, ] took from him [ his flesh, or rendered him lean ]; namely, a man. (TA.) AlxuTuwbu ↓ taEar~aqatohu , also, signifies the like, i. e. [ Afflictions, or calamities, ] took from him [ his flesh, &c.]. (TA.) biY EaAmu AlmaEaASiymi ↓ A^ay~aAma A^aEoraqa cited by Th, he expl. as meaning In the days when the year of the maEaASim took away my flesh: i. e., when the dirt, consequent upon drought, reached my maEaASim [or wrists]; AlmaEaASiymi being here used by poetic license for AlmaEaASimi : but ISd says, “ I know not what this explanation is. ” (L.) And Euriqa , inf. n. EaroqN , signifies He (a man) was, or became, emaciated, or lean. (K.) ↓ Alt~aEar~uqu is also used in relation to other than material objects; as the strength and patience of camels, which are meant by xilaAlahun~a [“ their properties ” or “ qualities, ” xilaAl in this case being pl. of xal~apN ,] in the phrase yataEar~aquwna xilaAlahun~ [ They exhaust, or wear out, their properties, or qualities, of strength and patience], in a verse cited by IAar, describing camels and a company of riders. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence, app.,] TariyqN yaEoruquhu Aln~aAsu (K, TA) A road which men travel [as though they pared it]. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, A^aEoraqa fiyhi A^aEomaAmuhu waA^axowaAluhu [ His paternal uncles and his maternal uncles implanted, or engendered, in him, by natural transmission, a quality, or qualities, possessed by them, or what is termed a strain ]; (S, O, TA; [in which the meaning is indicated by the context;]) and so ↓ Er~q . (L, TA.) [See also the saying Darabato fiyhi fulaAnapu biEiroqK *iY A^a$abK in the second quarter of the first paragraph of art. (S, * O, * K.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce TaAbN , in art. Tyb . And see also the last form of 1 ( Earuqa ) in the present art.] -A5- A^aEoraqa also signifies He (a man, S, O) went, or came, ( SaAra , S, or A^ataY , K,) or journeyed, ( saAra , O,) to El-'Irák: (S, O, K:) and ↓ AEtrqwA They entered upon, or took their way in or into, the country of El-'Irák. (Th, TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ EuraAqN (K) [the latter also a pl.] A bone of which the flesh has been taken: (S, O:) or a bone of which the flesh has been eaten: (Msb, K:) or a bone of which most of the flesh has been taken, some thin and savoury portions of flesh remaining upon it: (TA:) or the former signifies a bone upon which is flesh: and one upon which is no flesh: or, as some say, whereof most of that which was upon it has been taken, some little remaining upon it: (Mgh:) or, as some say, a piece of flesh-meat; as also ↓ EaroqapN : (TA:) or EaroqN signifies a bone with its flesh: and ↓ EuraAqN , a bone of which the flesh has been eaten: (K:) thus they are correctly expl. accord. to Ez-Zejjájee; and the like is said by AZ respecting ↓ EuraAqN : (TA:) but accord. to A'Obeyd, this signifies a piece of flesh-meat; and IAmb says that this is the right explanation, because the Arabs say A^akalotu AlEuraAqa , and they do not say A^akalotu AlEaZoma : (Har p.26:) [or, app., the flesh-meat of a bone: and likewise the portions, of trees, that are cropped by camels: (see EuraAmN :)] the pl. (of EaroqN , S, Mgh, O) is ↓ EuraAqN , (S, Mgh, O, K,) which is extr, (IAth, K,) a pl. of a measure of which, as that of a pl., there are few instances, (ISk, S, O,) [see an ex. voce janaAHN ,] and EiraAqN , also, (IAar, K,) which is more agreeable with analogy. (IAar, TA.) ― -b2- Also A road which men travel [as though they pared it] so that it becomes plainly apparent: (K, * TA:) an inf. n. used as a subst. [properly so termed]. (TA.) ― -b3- See also EaraqN , near the end.
