definition: A certain appertenance of a tree;
sourceDefinition: A certain appertenance of a tree; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) the root thereof; or the part thereof that is beneath the ground; (MA;) or its branching roots [ collectively ]: (TA:) pl. [of mult.] EuruwqN (S, O, Msb, K) and EiraAqN and [of pauc.] A^aEoraAqN . (K.) ― -b2- It is said in a trad., layosa liEiroqK ZaAlimK Haq~N , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) i. e. li*iY EiroqK ZaAlimK , (Mgh, O, Msb,) meaning (tropical:) [ There is no right pertaining ] to him who plants, (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) or sows, (S,) in land, (Mgh, Msb,) or in land which another has brought into cultivation (S, O, Msb) after it has been waste, (S, O, Msb, *) wrongfully, in order that he may have a claim to that land: (S, Mgh, O, Msb:) the epithet being tropically applied to the Eiroq , (Mgh, Msb,) as it properly applies to the owner thereof: (Mgh:) but some, in relating this trad., say liEiroqi ZaAlimK , making the former noun to be a prefix to the latter, governing it in the gen. case. (O.) ― -b3- The roots of the A^aroTaY ( Euruwqu AlA^aroTaY ) are long, red, penetrating into the moist earth, succulent, compact, and dripping with water: and to them, in a trad., certain camels are likened in respect of their redness and plumpness and the compactness of their flesh and fat. (TA.) ― -b4- AlEuruwqu also signifies A certain plant with which one dyes: (S, O:) or AlEuruwqu AlS~uforu , a certain plant used by the dyers, called in Pers. zarodaJuwbap [or zarodN Juwbo ], (K, TA,) i. e. yellow wood: (TA:) or i. q. Alhurodu : or AlmaAmiyraAnu , (K,) or AlmaAmiyraAnu AlS~iyniY~u : (TA:) or Alkurokumu AlS~agiyru : (K:) all which are nearly alike. (TA. [See also baqolapu AlxaTaATiyfi , voce bql .]) ― -b5- And AlEuruwqu AlHumoru Madder, ( Alfuw~apu , K, TA,) with which one dyes. (TA.) ― -b6- And AlEuruwqu AlbiyDu A certain plant that fattens women; also called AlmusotaEojilapu . (K.) ― -b7- [ EuruwqN seems sometimes to signify Straggling plants or stalks, spreading like roots: see janobapN . ― -b8- And it signifies also Sprouts from the roots of trees: see EusoluwjN .] ― -b9- And EiroqN signifies also The root, origin, or source, of anything: (K, TA:) and the basis thereof. (TA.) [And particularly The origin of a man, considered as the root from which he springs: hence Eiroqu Alv~araY is said to be applied by Imra-el-Keys to Adam, as the root, or source, of mankind; or to Ishmael, as, accord. to some, the root, or source, of all the Arabs: (see “ Le Diwan d'Amro'lkais, ” p. 33 of the Ar. text, and p. 103 of the Notes:) and the pl.] A^aEoraAqN signifies the ancestors of a man. (Har p. 634.) [And A quality, or disposition, possessed by a parent or by an ancestor or by a collateral of such person, considered as the source of that quality of a disposition in a descendant or in a collateral of a descendant: and such a quality, or disposition, when transmitted; a strain; i. e. a radical, a hereditary, an inborn, or a natural, disposition: and a radical, or hereditary, share in some quality or the like: pl. A^aEoraAqN .] One says, tadaArakahu A^aEoraAqu xayorK [ Good qualities or dispositions possessed by a parent or by an ancestor or by a collateral of such a person, or strains of a good kind, extended to him ]; and A^aEoraAqu $ar~K or sawo'K [ evil qualities or dispositions &c., or strains of an evil kind ]. (TA.) And AlEiroqu das~aAsN [ The natural disposition is wont to enter; i. e., to be transmitted to succeeding generations]. (TA in art. ds , q. v.) And Erqt fiyhimo Eiroqa sawo'K [i. e. Ear~aqato , or, accord. to more common usage, A^aEoraqato , meaning She implanted, or engendered, in them, or among them, an evil strain, or radical or hereditary disposition ]. (TA in art. Drb .) And lahu EiroqN fiY Alkarami [ He has a radical, or hereditary, share in generousness or nobleness of origin ]: (S, O:) and in like manner one says of a person between whom and Adam is no living ancestor, lahu EiroqN fiY Almawoti [ He has a radical, or heriditary, share in death ]; meaning that he will inevitably die. (O. [See also EariyqN .]) ― -b10- [Hence, app., A little, or modicum, or small quantity or admixture, of something]. One says, fiyhi EiroqN mino HumuwDapK , and muluwHapK , i. e. In it is a little, or a modicum, of acidity, and of saltness. (TA.) And fiY Al$~araAbi EiroqN mina AlmaA='i In the wine is a small quantity [or admixture ] of water. (S, O, K.) ― -b11- Also A certain appertenance of the body; (O, Msb, K, TA;) i. e. the hollow [ canal ] in which is the blood; (TA;) [ a blood-vessel; a vein, and an artery: also any duct, or canal, in an animal body: and sometimes, though improperly, a nerve: or any one of the appertenances of the body that resemble roots: ] pl. [of mult.] EuruwqN (O, Msb, K) and EiraAqN (K) and [of pauc.] A^aEoraAqN . (Msb, K.) [Hence it may be applied to A spermatic duct: and hence, app.,] it is said in a trad., Ealayokumo biAlS~awomi faA_in~ahu maHosamapN liloEiroqi , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Keep ye to fasting, for it is ] a cause, or means, of stopping venereal intercourse: or an impediment to venery, and a cause of diminishing the seminal fluid, and of stopping venereal intercourse or passion. (T * and TA in art. Hsm .) ― -b12- Euruwqu AlA^aroDi means The pores through which exudes the moisture of the earth. (TA.) ― -b13- And (i. e. Erwq AlArD ) i. q. $aHomapu AlA^aroDi [the significations of which see in art. $Hm ]. (TA.) -A2- EiroqN also signifies The body. (K, TA.) Thus in the saying, A_in~ahu laxabiyvu AlEiroqi [ Verily he is corrupt, or impure, in respect of the body ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And Milk. (K.) One says, naAqatuka daAy^imapu AlEiroqi , meaning Thy she-camel has a constant flow, or abundance, of milk: or has constant milk. (TA.) [See also EaraqN , first quarter.] ― -b3- And Numerous offspring: (IAar, K:) or milk and offspring; as in the saying, maA A^akovara Eiroqa A_ibilika waganamika [ How abundant are the milk and offspring of thy camels and thy sheep or goats! ]. (TA.) [See, again, EaraqN , first quarter.] -A3- Also Salt land that gives growth to nothing. (K.) ― -b2- And (K) A piece, or tract, of land exuding water and producing salt, (AHn, K,) that gives growth to trees, (AHn, TA,) or that gives growth to the [ species of tamarisk called ] TarofaA=' : (K:) a signification the contr. of that in the next preceding sentence. (TA.) ― -b3- And A mountain that is travelled, or traversed: (TA:) or a mountain that is rugged, and extending upon the earth, (K, * TA,) debarring one by reason of its height, (TA,) and not to be ascended, because of its difficult nature, (K, TA,) but not long. (TA.) And A small mountain (K, TA) apart from others. (TA.) Thus it has two contr. significations. (K.) ― -b4- And A thin Habol [or elongated and elevated tract (not jabal as in the CK)] of sand extending along the ground: (K, TA:) or an elevated place: pl. EuruwqN . (K.) ― -b5- See also EiraAqN , latter half, in two places. -A4- Eiroqu maDan~apK and Eiloqu maDan~apK (the latter of which is that commonly known, TA) signify A thing of which one is tenacious; (O;) a thing held in high estimation, of which one is tenacious, (S and K and TA in art. Dn ,) and for which people vie in desire: (TA in that art.:) but [said to be] used only in a case of negation: one says, maA huwa EinodiY biEiroqi maDan~apK , meaning It is not, in my estimation, a thing of any value, or worth. (TA.)

definition: Sweat; i. e. the moisture, or fluid, that exudes (S, * O, * K, TA) from the skin of an animal; (K, TA;) or the water of the skin, that runs from the roots of the hair: a gen. n.; having no pl.; (TA;)...
sourceDefinition: Sweat; i. e. the moisture, or fluid, that exudes (S, * O, * K, TA) from the skin of an animal; (K, TA;) or the water of the skin, that runs from the roots of the hair: a gen. n.; having no pl.; (TA;) or no pl. of it has been heard: (Msb:) Lth says, I have not heard a pl. of AlEaraqu ; but if it be pluralized, it should be, accord. to analogy, A^aEoraAqN . (O, TA.) ― -b2- It is metaphorically used [in a similar sense] in relation to other things than animals. (K.) [Thus] it signifies The [ exuded ] moisture of a well: (K:) and in like manner of earth, or land, when the dew, or rain, has percolated in it ( nataHa fiyhaA ) so that it has met the moisture thereof. (TA.) ― -b3- And The dibos [or honey ] of dates; (K;) because it flows, or exudes, from them. (TA.) ― -b4- And Milk; because it flows in the ducts ( Euruwq ) [thereof] until it comes at the last to the udder: (K:) or milk at the time of bringing forth; as in the saying, maA A^akovara Earaqa ganamiki How abundant is the milk of thy sheep, or goats, at the time of their bringing forth! (AZ, O.) [See also EiroqN , latter half.] ― -b5- And (K) The offspring of camels: (S, O, K:) so in the saying, maA A^akovara Earaqa A_ibilihi [ How numerous are the offspring of his camels! ]. (S, O.) [See, again, EiroqN , latter half.] ― -b6- And Advantage, profit, utility, or benefit: (O, K, TA; in [several of] the copies of the second of which, Aln~aqoEu is erroneously put for Aln~afoEu : TA:) and a recompense, or reward: (K, TA; in some copies of the former of which, Alt~uraAbu is erroneously put for Alv~awaAbu : TA:) or a little thereof; (K, TA;) likened to Earaq [as meaning “ sweat ”]. (TA.) Earaqu AlxilaAli means A thing that one gives, or yields, for friendship: (S, O, TA:) or a reward for friendship. (TA.) A poet says, namely El-Hárith Ibn-Zuheyr, describing a sword named Aln~uwn , (O, TA,) belonging to Málik Ibn-Zuheyr, which Hamal Ibn-Bedr took from him on the day when he slew him, and which El-Hárith took from Hamal when he slew him, (TA,) wayuxobiruhumo makaAna Aln~uwni min~iY wamaA A^uEoTiytuhu Earaqa AlxilaAli [ And he shall tell them the place of En-Noon, from me, and that I was not given it as a reward for friendship ]; meaning, that I took this sword by force. (O, TA. [In the S, the former hemistich of this verse is given differently, and, as is said in the TA, erroneously.]) ― -b7- laqiytu mino fulaAnK Earaqa Alqirobapi (which is a prov., TA) means [ I experienced from such a one ] hardship, as expl. by As, who says that he knew not the origin thereof, (S, O,) or difficulty, or distress, as expl. by IDrd: (O:) and it is said that the Earaq [or sweat] is of the man, not of the qirobap [or water-skin]; and the origin of the saying is, that water-skins ( qirab ) are [generally] carried only by female slaves that bear burdens, and by him who has no assistant; but sometimes a man of generous origin becomes poor, and in need of carrying them himself, and he sweats by reason of the trouble that comes upon him, and of shame; (S, O;) wherefore one says, taja$~amotu laka Earaqa Alqirobapi [expl. in art. j$m ], (S,) or ja$imotu A_ilayoka Earaqa Alqirobapi [likewise expl. in art. j$m ]: accord. to Ks, the meaning is, I have suffered fatigue, and imposed upon myself difficulty, for thee, [or in coming to thee, ] so that I have sweated like the sweating of the water-skin: or, accord. to A'Obeyd, I have imposed upon myself, in coming to thee, what no one has attained, and what will not be; (O, TA.)

It is metaphorically used [in a similar sense] in relation to other things than animals. (K.) [Thus] it signifies The [ exuded ] moisture of a well: (K:) and in like manner of earth, or land, when the dew, or rain, has percolated in it ( nataHa fiyhaA ) so that it has met the moisture thereof. (TA.)
And The dibos [or honey ] of dates; (K;) because it flows, or exudes, from them. (TA.)

And Milk; because it flows in the ducts ( Euruwq ) [thereof] until it comes at the last to the udder: (K:) or milk at the time of bringing forth; as in the saying, maA A^akovara Earaqa ganamiki How abundant is the milk of thy sheep, or goats, at the time of their bringing forth! (AZ, O.) [See also EiroqN , latter half.]
And (K) The offspring of camels: (S, O, K:) so in the saying, maA A^akovara Earaqa A_ibilihi [ How numerous are the offspring of his camels! ]. (S, O.) [See, again, EiroqN , latter half.]

A^aSolN : (O, K:) or a source of wealth or property: or the main portion of the root of a tree. from which the Euruwq [or minor roots ] branch off: (K:) or, as some say, EiroqaApN has this last meaning; or, as others say, ↓ EiroqapN . (Ltl., O.) They said, AisotaA^oSala A@ll~`hu ↓ EaroqaAtahumo and EiroqaAtihimo ; if they pronounced the first letter with fet-h, they so pronounced the last letter [before the pronoun]; and if they pronounced the former with kesr, they thus pronounced the latter, regarding the word as pl. of ↓ EiroqapN : (K:) or, accord. to Lth, the Arabs are related to have said, AisotaA^oSala A@ll~`hu EiroqaAtahumo , meaning $aA^ofatahumo [i. e. (O.) definition: The double suture that is in the lower part of the [leathern water-bag called] mazaAdap and raAwiyap ;
sourceDefinition: The double suture that is in the lower part of the [leathern water-bag called] mazaAdap and raAwiyap ; (Lth, O, K;) and this is of the firmest kinds of suture therein: (Lth, O:) or the suture that is in the middle of the qirobap [or water-skin]: (TA:) or the piece [or strip ] of skin that is put upon the place where the two extremities, or edges, of the [ main ] skin meet when it is sewed in, or upon, the lower part of the mzAdp : (K:) or the appertenance of the qrbp , and of the mzAdp , &c., which is [ a strip of skin ] doubled and then sewed [ thereon thus ] doubled: (Msb:) or, accord. to AZ, the [ piece of ] skin that is doubled, and then sewed upon the lower part of the [water-skin or milk-skin called] siqaA=' : (S:) and, (K,) accord. to As, (S, O,) i. q. TibaAbapN ; (S, O, K;) i. e. the piece of skin with which the punctures of the seams are covered: (S, O: see also EaraqN , latter half: [and see TibaAbapN :]) pl. EuruqN (Lth, AZ, S, O, K, TA) and EuroqN (TA) and A^aEoriqapN ; (Lth, O, TA;) the last a pl. of pauc. (Lth, O.) And EiraAqu Als~uforapi signifies The suture surrounding the [ round piece of skin called ] suforap [q. v.]. (K.) ― -b2- Also Nearness, together, of the stitch-holes in a skin or hide: [so I render taqaArubu Alxrzi ; reading Alxurazi : and it seems to mean also uniformity thereof: for it is added,] hence the prov., liA^amorihi EiraAqN , meaning (assumed tropical:) His affair is uniform, right, or rightly disposed. (TA.) ― -b3- Also The side, or shore, (Lth, O, K,) of water, (K,) or of a sea, or great river, along the whole length thereof. (Lth, O, K. * [It is said in the K that EuruqN is pl. of EiraAqN in this sense: but afterwards, that the pl. of the latter in all its senses is A^aEoriqapN also; to which the TA adds EuroqN .]) And accord. to AZ, Any pasturage adjacent to a great river or a sea. (TA.) And EiraAqu Aln~ahori , (K,) or Alr~akiybi , (TA,) The border of the rivulet [ for irrigation ] (K, TA) by which the water enters a HaAy^iT [i. e. garden, or garden of palm-trees surrounded by a wall ], (TA,) from its nearest to its furthest extremity. (K, TA.) ― -b4- Also The quTor [app. meaning side (but see this word)] of a mountain, by itself; [or so, perhaps, EiraAqu jabalK ;] and so ↓ EiroqN [or Eiroqu jabalK ]. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ― -b5- And, as also ↓ EiroqN , Remains of the [ plants, or trees, called ] HamoD . (K.) ― -b6- EiraAqu Ald~aAri The court, or yard, in front, or extending from the sides, of the house. (IB, K.) ― -b7- EiraAqu AlA^u*uni The circuit, or surrounding edge, of the ear. (K.) ― -b8- EiraAqu AlZ~ufuri The flesh surrounding the nail. (K, * TA.) ― -b9- EiraAqu AlHa$aA The intestines that are above the navel, lying breadthwise, or across, in the belly. (K.) ― -b10- And EiraAqN signifies also The inside of feathers. (AA, K.) ― -b11- The EiraAqaAni of the horse's saddle are The two edges of the daf~ataAni , at the fore part of the saddle and its hinder part. (IDrd, TA voce qarabuwsN , q. v.) -A2- [Also A pace, or rate of going. ] One says in relation to a horse, on the occasion of drawing forth the sweat, and of careful tending, and fattening, AiHomilohu EalaY AlEiraAqi AlA^aEolaY waAlEiraAqi AlA^asofali , meaning [ Urge, or make, thou him to go ] the vehement pace and the inferior pace. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, TA.) -A3- AlEiraAqu is the name of A certain country, (S, O, Msb, K,) well known, (Msb, K,) extending from 'Abbádán to El-Mow- sil in length and from El-Kádiseeyeh to Hulwán in breadth; (K;) masc. and fem.: (S, O, Msb, K:) said to be so named because upon the EiraAq , i. e. “ side, ” or “ shore, ” of the Tigris and Euphrates: (O, * K: [in which, and in other works, several other supposed derivations are mentioned, but such as I think too fanciful to deserve notice:]) accord. to some, it is arabicized, (S, O, Msb, K,) from a Pers. appellation, (S, O,) i. e. from A_iyraAn $ahor , (As, O, * K, TA,) of which the meaning is [said to be] “ having many palmtrees and [other] trees; ” (K;) but [SM justly says,] in my opinion the meaning requires consideration. (TA.) ― -b2- AlEiraAqaAni is an appellation of El-Basrah and El-Koofeh. (S, O, K.)

definition: , (S, O, K,) applied to a man and to a horse, means [ Rooted, i.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, K,) applied to a man and to a horse, means [ Rooted, i. e.] having a radical, or hereditary, share, ( lahu Eiroq , S, O,) in generousness or nobleness [of origin, which, accord. to the S and O, and common usage, seems to be implied by the epithet when used absolutely], (S, O, K,) and also in meanness or ignobleness [thereof; or having a strain of, i. e. an inborn disposition to, generousness or nobleness, and also meanness or ignobleness]. (S, * O, * K.) And you say also fiY Alkarami ↓ fulaAnN muEoraqN and fiY All~uw^omi [ Such a one is rooted, &c., in generousness or nobleness and in meanness or ignobleness ]; and lahu fiY ↓ A_in~ahu lamuEoraqN Alkarami ; (S, O;) and lahu fiY Alkarami ↓ A_in~ahu lamaEoruwqN , [the part. n. being formed] on the supposition of the suppression of the augmentative letter [in its verb, which is A^uEoriqa ]: (TA:) and in like manner, (S, O, TA,) in a trad., (O, TA,) a man of whom there is no living ancestor between him and Adam is said to be lahu fiY Almawoti ↓ muEoraqN (S, O, TA) i. e. Made to have a radical, or hereditary, share ( EiroqN ) in death; (O, TA;) meaning that he will inevitably die. (S, O, TA.) [In the Ham p. 438, ↓ muEoriqN is expl. as syn. with EariyqN : but in the verse to which this explanation relates it is evidently employed in the sense of the act. part. n. of A^aEoraqa as used in the phrase A^aEoraqa fiyhi A^aEomaAmuhu waA^axowaAluhu , q. v.] ― -b2- gulaAmN EariyqN means [ A boy, or young man, ] slender, or spare, and light of spirit. (TA.)

(TA.)

definition: Any great trees having thorns;
sourceDefinition: Any great trees having thorns; these being of two sorts, genuine ( xaAliS ) and not genuine ( gayoru xaAliSK ): the former sort are the Earof , the EurofuT , the TaloH , the salam , the sidor , the sayaAl , the samor , the yanobuwt , the greater qataAd , the kanahobal , the garob , and the Eawosaj : the other sort are the $awoHaT . the naboE , the $iroyaAn , the saraA=' , the na$am , the Eujorum , and the tA^olab ; and these are called the EiDaAh of bows ( EiDaAhu AlqiyaAsi [i. e. AlqisiY~i ] pl. of qawosN ): the small thorny trees are called EiD~N [q. v.]: and such as are neither EiD~ nor EiDaAh , of thorny trees, are the $ukaAEaY , the HulaAwaY , the HaA* , the kub~ , and the sul~aj : (S:) or, as AZ says in the beginning of his book of herbage and trees, EiDaAhN is the general name of certain thorny trees which have different particular names: the genuine EiDaAh ( AlEiDaAhu AlxaAliSu ) are those which are large and have strong thorns: such as are small, of thorny trees, are called EiD~N and $irosN [q. v.]: of the EiDaAh are the samur , the EurofaT , the sayaAl , the qaraZ , the greater qataAd , the kanahobal , the Eawosaj , the sidor , the gaAf , and the garob : these are the genuine EiDaAh : and of the EiDaAh of bows ( EiDaAhu AlqiyaAsi i. e. AlqisiY~i ) are the $awoHaT , the naboE , the $iroyaAn , and the saraA=' : (TA voce EiD~N :) or EiDaAhN signifies any trees having thorns; as the TaloH and the Eawosaj : or, accord. to some, except the qataAd and the sidor : (Msb:) or the greatest of trees: or the xamoT [q. v., for it is variously explained]: or any having thorns: or such as are great and tall, of these: (K:) [ HubolapN and sinofapN are terms applied to the fruit, or produce, of trees of the kind called EiDaAh : see the former of those words:] a single tree thereof is called EiDaAhapN (S, K) and ↓ EiDahapN and ↓ EiDapN , (S, Msb, K, [but in the copies of the K the last of these is erroneously written EiDah ,]) the radical h being rejected in the last, as it is in $afapN ; or, accord. to some, the rejected radical letter is w ; (AAF, S, Msb; *) opinions differing on this point because of the different forms of the pl.; (AAF, S, TA;) the pl. being EiDaAhN and (of pauc., TA) EiDawaAtN (AAF, S, K, TA, in the CK EiDowAtN ,) and EiDuwna ; (K;) [the second and third of which are pls. of ↓ EiDapN ;] or, accord. to ISd, EiDaAhN may be an instance of the kind of pl. that differs from its sing, [only] in respect of the p , like qataAdN , of which the sing. is qataAdapN , [i. e., what is more properly termed a coll. gen. n.,] or it may be a broken pl., as though its sing. were EiDahapN : (TA:) the dim. [of EiDahapN ] is ↓ EuDayohapN . (S, TA.) [Hence,] one says, fulaAnN yanotajibu gayora EiDaAhihi [lit. Such a one takes the back of other than his own EDAh , to tan therewith]; meaning (assumed tropical:) such a one arrogates to himself the poetry of another. (S. See a verse cited in art. njb .) [See also 1, first sentence.]

EaforN , (S, O, Msb,) He rubbed it (namely a vessel) with dust: and ↓ Ef~rhu he rubbed it much with dust: (Msb:) or the latter, he defiled, or soiled, it with dust: (Mgh:) and the former, and ↓ latter, (S, O, K,) of which the inf. n. is taEofiyrN , (S, O,) he rolled, or turned over, him, or it, fiY Alt~uraAbi in the dust: (S, O, K:) or he hid ( das~a ) him, or it, therein. (K.) It is is said in a trad. of Aboo-Jahl, muHam~adN wajohahu bayona A^aZohurikumo ↓ halo yuEaf~iru [ Doth, or shall, Mohammad defile his face with dust, or rub his face in the dust, in the midst of you? ], meaning his prostrating himself in the dust: and at the end he says, ↓ laA^aTaA^an~a EalaY raqabatihi A^awo laA^uEaf~iran~a wajohahu fiY Alt~uraAbi [ I will assuredly trample upon his neck, or I will defile, or roll, his face in the dust ]; meaning that he would abase him, or render him abject. (TA.) ― -b2- He dragged him, being about to roll him in the dust: and you say vawobahu fiY AAlt~uraAbi ↓ AiEotafara [ He dragged his garment in the dust ]. (Aboo-Nasr, L, TA.) ― -b3- And Eafarahu , (K,) inf. n. EaforN , (TA,) He cast him upon the ground; as also ↓ AEtfrhu . (K.) You say, ↓ AEtfrhu AlA^asadu The lion cast him upon the ground: (A:) or the lion seized him, and broke his neck, (S, O, TA,) and cast him upon the ground, and shook him about. (TA.) And ↓ AEtfrhu He leaped, or sprang, upon him, or at him, ( saAwarahu , O, K, for which $aAwrh is erroneously put in some copies of the K, TA,) and dragged him, and cast him upon the ground. (TA.) [See also 2.] -A2- Eafira , aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. EafarN , (Msb,) He, or it, was of the colour termed Euforap : (Msb, K:) or of a colour resembling that. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: A boar; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ EuforN : or a swine, as a common term: or the young one of a sow. (K.) -A2- EiforN (S, A, O, K) and ↓ EafirN (Sgh in TA in art. nfr ) and ↓ EiforiyapN , (A, O, K,) in which the Y is to render the word quasi-coordinate to $iro*imapN , [I substitute this word for $iro*iwapN , in the L, and $iro*i*apN in the TA,] and the p to give intensiveness, (L, TA,) and ↓ EiforiytN , (A, O, K,) in which the t is to render the word quasicoordinate to qinodiylN , (TA,) [or to render it a contraction of EiforiyapN ,] and ↓ EaforiytN , which occurs in one reading of the Kur, [xxvii. 39, and is agreeable with modern vulgar pronunciation,] (O, CK,) and ↓ EiforaAtN , (CK,) and ↓ EufaAriyapN , (A, O, L, K,) in which the Y is to render the word quasi-coordinate to Eu*aAfirapN , and the p is to give intensiveness, (TA,) and ↓ Eifir~N , (O, K,) and ↓ EiforiY~N , (Sgh, K,) and ↓ EufaroniyapN , (Sgh, K,) and ↓ EiforiynN , and ↓ Eifir~iynN , (Lh, TA,) and ↓ EafaronFY , (Lth, TA,) [respecting which last, see the latter portion of this paragraph,] applied to a man, (S, O, K,) and to a jinnee, or genie, (Kur, ubi suprá,) Wicked, or malignant; (S, O, K;) crafty, or cunning; (S, O;) abominable, foul, or evil; (K;) abounding in evil; (TA;) strong, or powerful; (A;) insolent and audacious in pride and in acts of rebellion or disobedience; (A, TA;) who roils his adversary in the dust: (A:) and the epithet applied to a woman is EiforapN , (S, O,) and ↓ EiforiytapN , (Lh, K,) and ↓ Eifir~apN : (Sh, O:) or ↓ EiforiytN signifies anything that exceeds the ordinary bounds; and ↓ EufaAriyapN is syn. with it: (AO, S, O:) and ↓ EiforiytN and ↓ EiforiynN and ↓ Eifir~iynN (Zj, K) applied to a man, and as applied in the Kur, ubi suprá, [to a jinnee,] (Zj,) sharp, vigorous, and effective, in an affair, exceeding the ordinary bounds therein, with craftiness, or cunning, (Zj, O, K,) and wickedness, or malignity: (Zj:) or ↓ EiforiytN is properly applied to a jinnee, and signifies evil in disposition, and wicked or malignant; and is metaphorically applied to a man, like as is $ayoTaAnN : (B:) it is applied to an evil jinnee that is powerful, but inferior to such as is termed maAridN : (Mir-át ez-Zemán:) ↓ EiforiyapN also signifies i. q. daAhiyapN [app. meaning very crafty or cunning, rather than a calamity ]: (S, O:) ↓ EiforiyapN and ↓ EiforiytN are also applied as epithets to a $ayoTaAn [or devil]: (Kh, S:) the pl. of the former of these two epithets is EafaAriyapN , (Kh, S, O,) or EafaAriY~u ; (Fr;) and that of ↓ Efryt is EafaAriytu ; (Kh, Fr, S, O;) and that of ↓ Eifir~N is Eifir~uwna ; (Sh;) and that of EiforN is A^aEofaArN . (TA in art. j$m .) You say, fulaAnN niforiytN ↓ EiforiytN , and niforiyapN ↓ EiforiyapN ; [ Such a one is wicked, or malignant; &c.;] the latter of these two words being an imitative sequent. (AO, S, O.) And in a trad. it is said, A_in~a A@ll~`ha yaboguDu Aln~iforiyapa A@l~a*iY laA yurozaA^u fiY A^aholK walaAmaAlK ↓ AlEiforiyapa (AO, S) [ Verily God hates ] the crafty or cunning, the wicked or malignant, the abounding in evil; or him who collects much and refuses to give; or him who acts very wrongfully or unjustly or tyrannically; [ who will not suffer loss in his family nor in his property. ] (TA.) ― -b2- A^asadN EiforN , and ↓ EiforiyapN , and ↓ EiforiytN , and ↓ EufaAriyapN , (K,) and ↓ Eifir~N , (TA,) and ↓ EafaronFY , (K, [respecting which see what follows: in the CK Eafarot`Y , which is wrong in two respects:]) A strong, (K,) powerful, great, (TA,) lion: (K, TA:) or AlEafaronaY the lion; so called because of his strength: (S, O:) and labuw^apN EafaronFY , (S, O, TA,) like the masc., (TA. (S.)

sourceDefinition: (IDrd, S, A, O, Msb, K) and ↓ EaforN (IDrd, A, O, K) Dust: (IDrd, S, O, Msb:) [like EafaArN the dust of the earth: (Freytag, from Meyd:)] or the exterior of the dust or earth: (A, K:) and the surface of the earth; (Msb;) as also AlA^aroDi ↓ Eaforu : (TA:) pl. A^aEofaArN . (K.) You say AlA^aroDi mivoluhu ↓ maA EalaY Eafori There is not upon the face of the earth the like of him, or it. (O, TA.) And kalaAmN laA Eafara fiyhi , (K,) or lahu ↓ laA Eafora , (TS, TA,) [lit., Language in which is no dust; or which has no dust; like the saying kalaAmN laA gubaAra Ealayohi “ language on which is no dust; ” meaning] (assumed tropical:) language in which is nothing difficult to be understood. definition: Dust-coloured inclining to white;
sourceDefinition: Dust-coloured inclining to white; of a whitish dust-colour: (TA:) or white, but not of a clear hue: (Msb:) or, applied to a buckantelope, white, but not of a very clear white, (AZ, As, S, O, K,) being like the colour of the surface of the earth: (AZ, As, Mgh:) or a buck-antelope having a tinge of red over his whiteness, (AA, S, A, K,) with a short neck; and such is the weakest of antelopes in running: (AA, S, O:) or having a redness in his back, with white flanks: (K:) [in the CK, after the words thus rendered, is an omission, of the words A^awi AlA^aboyaDu wa :] or such as inhabits elevated, rugged, stony tracts, and hard grounds; and such is red: (AZ:) or having white horns: (A:) fem. EaforaA='u : (S, K, &c.:) also applied to a she-goat, meaning of a clear white colour: (TA:) pl. EuforN . (S, A, O.) ― -b2- El-Kumeyt says, wakun~aA A_i*aA jab~aAru qawomK A^araAdanaA bikayodK HamalonaAhu EalaY qaroni A^aEofaraA [ And we used, when an insolent tyrant of a people desired to execute against us a plot, to carry him upon the horn of an antelope of a whitish dustcolour, or white but not of a clear hue, &c.]; meaning, we used to slay him, and to carry his head upon the spear-head; for the spear-heads, in time past, were of horns. (S, O.) ― -b3- Hence the saying ramaAniY Eano qaroni A^aEofara i. q. rmAnY bidaAhiyapK (tropical:) [ He sent upon me a calamity; or he made a very crafty man to be my assailant ]: for the same reason, also, qaronu A^aEofara is proverbially used to signify (tropical:) A difficulty, or distress, that befalls one: and one says to a man who has passed the night in disquieting distress, kunota EalaY qaroni A^aEofara (tropical:) [ Thou wast pierced by grief ]. (TA.) One says also, of him who is frightened and disquieted, kaA^an~ahu EalaY qaroni A^aEofara [ He is as though he were upon the horn of an antelope of a whitish dustcolour, &c.: meaning, upon the head of a spear ]: the like of this phrase is used by Imra-el-Keys. (A.) ― -b4- Also EaforaA='u , A ewe of a colour inclining to whiteness. (O.) ― -b5- And A^aEofaru , Red sand. (S, O.) ― -b6- [Food of the kind called] variyd made white: (K, TA:) from EuforapN signifying the “ colour of the earth. ” (TA.) ― -b7- EaforaA='u White. (K.) ― -b8- A^aroDN EaforaA='u Untrodden land. (K, TA.) ― -b9- AlEaforaA='u The thirteenth night [ of the lunar month ]: (S, O:) or the night of blackness: (A:) but accord. to IAar, All~ayaAliY AlEuforu signifies the white nights; (A;) and so says Th, without particularizing: (TA:) or the nights thus called are the seventh and eighth and ninth nights of the lunar month; (K;) because of the whiteness of the moon [therein]. (TA.) It is said in a trad. layosa Euforu All~ayaAliY kaA@ld~aA=diy^i The moon-lit nights are not like the black nights: some say that this is a proverb. (TA.)

EaforaA='u : (S, K, &c.:) also applied to a she-goat, meaning of a clear white colour: (TA:) pl. EuforN . (S, A, O.) ― -b2- El-Kumeyt says, wakun~aA A_i*aA jab~aAru qawomK A^araAdanaA bikayodK HamalonaAhu EalaY qaroni A^aEofaraA [ And we used, when an insolent tyrant of a people desired to execute against us a plot, to carry him upon the horn of an antelope of a whitish dustcolour, or white but not of a clear hue, &c.]; meaning, we used to slay him, and to carry his head upon the spear-head; for the spear-heads, in time past, were of horns. (S, O.) ― -b3- Hence the saying ramaAniY Eano qaroni A^aEofara i. q. rmAnY bidaAhiyapK (tropical:) [ He sent upon me a calamity; or he made a very crafty man to be my assailant ]: for the same reason, also, qaronu A^aEofara is proverbially used to signify (tropical:) A difficulty, or distress, that befalls one: and one says to a man who has passed the night in disquieting distress, kunota EalaY qaroni A^aEofara (tropical:) [ Thou wast pierced by grief ]. (TA.) One says also, of him who is frightened and disquieted, kaA^an~ahu EalaY qaroni A^aEofara [ He is as though he were upon the horn of an antelope of a whitish dustcolour, &c.: meaning, upon the head of a spear ]: the like of this phrase is used by Imra-el-Keys. (A.) ― -b4- Also EaforaA='u , A ewe of a colour inclining to whiteness. (O.) ― -b5- And A^aEofaru , Red sand. (S, O.) ― -b6- [Food of the kind called] variyd made white: (K, TA:) from EuforapN signifying the “ colour of the earth. ” (TA.) ― -b7- EaforaA='u White. (K.) ― -b8- A^aroDN EaforaA='u Untrodden land. (K, TA.) ― -b9- AlEaforaA='u The thirteenth night [ of the lunar month ]: (S, O:) or the night of blackness: (A:) but accord. to IAar, All~ayaAliY AlEuforu signifies the white nights; (A;) and so says Th, without particularizing: (TA:) or the nights thus called are the seventh and eighth and ninth nights of the lunar month; (K;) because of the whiteness of the moon [therein]. (TA.) It is said in a trad. layosa Euforu All~ayaAliY kaA@ld~aA=diy^i The moon-lit nights are not like the black nights: some say that this is a proverb. (TA.)

definition: Remaining, staying, dwelling, or abiding.
sourceDefinition: Remaining, staying, dwelling, or abiding. (S, K, TA.) ― -b2- And Going forth; thus having two contr. significations, (TA.) ― -b3- And Continuing, lasting, or enduring. (S, K, TA.) ― -b4- And Present, or ready: (S, K, TA:) applied in this sense to food, and to beverage; and to property, or camels, or cattle; as also A=hinN : one says, xu*o mino EaAhini maAlihi and A=hinihi [ Take thou of what is present, or ready, of his property, &c.]. (TA.) ― -b5- Also, applied to property, or camels, or cattle, Long-possessed, or long-possessed and homeborn, or inherited from parents. (S, K.) So in the saying, A^aEoTaAhu mino EaAhini maAlihi [ He gave him of what had been long-possessed, &c., of his property, &c.]. (S.) -A2- Applied to a branch, rod, or twig, of a tree, Broken without becoming separated, so that it remains suspended and lax: this is said by Abu-l-'Abbás to be the primary signification [app. in relation to what here follows]. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence,] (assumed tropical:) Lax, and sluggish, or lazy. (IAar, K, TA.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Poor; syn. faqiyrN : (K, TA:) because of his broken state. sourceDefinition: A difficult thing, or affair: (Msb:) and the same, (K,) or ↓ EawoSaA='u , (O, TA,) applied to a calamity ( daAhiyap ) difficult, severe, grievous, or distressing: (O, K, TA:) IJ holds it to be used [only] as a subst. (M, voce SawiybN .) ― -b2- Also Language Difficult to be understood: (Msb:) obscure; or not comprehended or understood; as also ↓ A^aEowaSu and ↓ EaAy^iSN , which last is [originally] an inf. n., like faAlijN &c.: (TA:) poetry of which the meaning is difficult to be elicited; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ A^aEowaSu : (O, K:) also EawiySN , (K, TA,) and EawiySapN , (TA,) and ↓ EawoSaA='u , (S, Msb, K, TA,) applied to a word, or an expression, or a sentence, or the like, ( kalimap ,) strange: (S, K:) or difficult to be understood. (Msb.) ― -b3- Also, applied to earth [ turaAb ), Hard: (K:) and ↓ EawoSaA='u , applied to a piece of sand ( ramolap ), difficult to traverse: (MF:) or, accord. to ISh, the latter is applied as an epithet to what is termed mayovaA='u , [of which one signification is an even, or a soft, tract of sand,] in the sense of muxaAlifapN [app. meaning opposing one's progress ]: and the state, or quality, thereof, is termed ↓ EawaSN . (O, TA.) ― -b4- And, applied to a place, Rugged, high, and difficult. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ― -b5- Also, (K,) or ↓ EawoSaA='u , (S, O, TA,) [as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates,] A difficult affair: (K, TA:) or the most difficult of affairs. EiyaAfN , (S, Mgh, O,) or EiyaAfapN , (Msb, [but probably a mistranscription for the former,]) or both, or the latter is a simple subst., and the former is an inf. n., also EayofN and EayafaAnN , (ISd, K,) He (a man, S, O, Msb, [and any animal,]) disliked it, or loathed it, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) namely, food, (S, O, Msb, K,) or water, (Mgh,) or beverage, (S, O, Msb, K,) and would not drink it, (S, O, K,) and sometimes it is said in relation to other things, (K,) but mostly in relation to food: (ISd, TA:) and ↓ AiEotaAfahu signifies the same as EaAfahu . (TA.) A poet says, (namely, Anas Ibn-Mudrik, O, TA, and so in a copy of the S,) A_in~iY waqatoliY sulayokFA vum~a A^aEoqiluhu kaAlv~awori yuDorabu lam~aA EaAfati Albaqaru [ Verily I, in the case of my slaying Suleyk and then giving the bloodwit for slaying him, am like the bull that is beaten when the cows loathe the water]: for when the cows hold back from entering into the water and drinking, they are not beaten, because they have milk, but only the bull is beaten, in order that they may be frightened, and therefore drink. (S, O, TA. [See also the Ham, p. 416; where the former hemistich is somewhat differently related.]) And hence the saying, h`*aA mim~aA yaEaAfuhuAlT~aboEu [ This is of the things that the natural disposition dislikes, or loathes ]. (Mgh.) -A2- Eifotu AlT~ayora , aor. A^aEiyfuhaA , inf. n. EiyaAfapN , I augured from the birds, (S, O, K, TA,) good or evil, (O, K, TA,) taking warning, or the like, by considering their names, and their places of alighting (S, O, K, TA) and of passage, (TA,) and their cries: thus, correctly, as in the T and S and M and L, i. e. waA^aSowaAtihaA ; for which the authors of the O and K have substituted waA^anowaAy^ihaA , deceived by the word masaAqiT in what goes before: and the verb is used in like manner in relation to gazelles or other animals passing with the right side, or the left side, turned towards the spectator: (TA:) AlEiyaAfapu primarily signifies the man's throwing a pebble at a bird, or crying out at it; and, if it turn its right side towards him in flying, the auguring good from it; and if its left side, evil: (Har p. 308:) or, accord. to Az, it signifies the seeing a bird, (TA,) or a raven, or crow, (Msb, TA,) or the like, (Msb,) and auguring evil [or good ] therefrom: (Msb, TA:) and also the saying [a thing] conjecturally, or surmising; without seeing anything: and it is said in a trad. to be mina Aljiboti [expl. in art. jbt ]: the verb in Eifotu AlT~ayora , as ISd says, is originally Eayifotu . (TA.) -A3- EaAfati AlT~ayoru , aor. taEiyfu , inf. n. EayofN , (S, O, K,) is like EAft having for its aor, taEuwfu and inf. n. EawofN , (K, TA,) i. e. (TA) The birds circled over the water, or over carcasses or corpses, and went to and fro, not going away, desiring to alight. (S, O, TA. [See also art. Ewf .])

definition: is a term employed in the case when a woman brings forth and her milk is suppressed in her breast, wherefore her fellow-wife, or female neighbour, draws it, by the single sucking and the two...
sourceDefinition: is a term employed in the case when a woman brings forth and her milk is suppressed in her breast, wherefore her fellow-wife, or female neighbour, draws it, by the single sucking and the two suckings: (Nh, O, L, K, * TA: but in the K, fataroDiEuhaA is erroneously put for fataroDiEuhu ; and Almar~apa and Almar~atayoni are put for Almar~apa and Almar~atayoni : TA:) thus in the saying of ElMugheereh, (O, K, TA,) as expl. by himself, (O, TA,) laA tuHar~imu AlEayofapu [i. e. The woman's sucking once and twice in drawing the breast of another woman whose milk is suppressed after child-birth will not render unlawful the marriage of either of them to a relation of the other, nor the marriage of a relation of either to a relation of the other; as the case of regular or continued suckling of a child does]: (O, K, TA: [but in the O and CK, tuHar~amu is erroneously put for tuHar~imu : see a similar saying voce maz~apN :]) the action is performed in order that the obstructed channels by which the milk issues may become opened: and it is thus termed because the woman loathes it: (Az, O, K:) A'Obeyd says, We know not AlEayofap in sucking the breast, but think it to be AlEuf~ap : his saying thus, however, is disapproved by Az. (O, K, * TA.) -A2- EayofapN is also the subst. from EaAfati AlT~ayoru [q. v., app. signifying A circling of birds over the water, &c.]. (S, O, K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) aor. , inf. n. gav~N , (TK,) He fatigued, or wearied, him, ( kad~ahu ,) biAlA^amori [ by, or with, the affair ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- And He forced him to do a thing against his will, so that he afflicted, distressed, or oppressed, him. (TA.) And you say, gat~a Ald~aAb~apa $awoTFA A^awo $awoTiyoni or wearied, the beast by urging it to run a heat, or two heats. (K, TA.) ― -b3- Also He grieved him; (K, TA;) and afflicted, distressed, or oppressed, him. (TA.) And gut~a He was grieved [&c.]. (Sh, TA.) ― -b4- And He overcame him, or silenced him, biAlkalaAmi [ by speech, i. e. by what he said ]. (K, TA.) [Hence] it is said in a trad. respecting prayer, yaA mano laA yaguv~uhu duEaA='u Ald~aAEiyna O Thou whom the praying of those who pray does not overcome. (TA.) And [hence, perhaps,] one says, gav~a AlD~aHika (aor. and inf. n. as above, TA,) He concealed laughter, (S, K, TA,) by putting his hand, or his garment, over his mouth. (TA.) ― -b5- Also He squeezed his throat, or throttled him: (K:) and he squeezed his throat for the period of an breath, or of two breaths, or, as some say, more than that. (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting the mission [of Mohammad], faA^axa*aniY jiboriylu fagat~aniY And Gabriel took me, and squeezed me vehemently, so that I experienced distress as when one is forcibly plunged into water: inf. n. gat~N : and gaT~N signifies the same. (TA.) ― -b6- gat~ahu fiY AlmaA='i , (S, K, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) is syn. with gaT~ahu ; (S, K, TA:) meaning He immersed, or plunged, him, or it, into the water. (TA.) ― -b7- And one says, gat~ahumu A@ll~`hu biAlEa*aAbi , inf. n. as above, God plunged them. or may God plunge them, with consecutive plungings, into punishment. (TA.) ― -b8- And gat~a , aor. and inf. n. as above, He took successive draughts, keeping the vessel to his mouth. (AZ, TA.) And gat~a AlmaA='a , (K, TA,) and gat~a fiY AlA_inaA='i , (TA.) He drank, taking draught after draught, or gulp after gulp, without removing the vessel from his mouth. (K, TA.) ― -b9- And gat~a Al$~ay^oa Al$~ay^oa He made the part of the thing to follow another part thereof, (K, TA,) whether in drinking or in speaking [&c.] (TA.) ― -b10- ― -b11- It is said in a trad. respecting Mohammad's pool, yagut~u fiyhi miyzaAbaAni i. e. Two spouts were pouring forth into it with an uninter rupted pouring: or it is said to mean, two spouts were running into it with a murmuring sound; accord. to which latter explanation we must read yagit~u : and some say that it is ygT~ . (Az., L, TA.) [See also another reading voce Eab~a .] ― -b12- And one says, gat~ahu biju$amihi He threw his breast upon him. (TA in art. j$m .) -A2- gat~a , aor. , It was, or became, bad, or corrupt; said of food; and likewise of speech. (Aboo-Bekr, TA.) [See also gav~a .]

definition: and ↓ musotagozirN One who gives a thing in order that he may obtain in return more than he gives.

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (K,) inf. n. gaforN , (S, Mgh, Msb,) He covered, veiled, concealed, or hid, it; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) i. e., anything. (TA.) This is the primary signification. (Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence] gafar Al$~ayoba biAlxiDaAbi He covered, or concealed, the white, or hoary, hair with dye; (K;) as also ↓ A^agofarahu . (TA.) ― -b3- And gafara AlmataAEa , (S, K,) fiY AlwiEaA='i , (K,) He put the goods, or utensils, into the bag, or receptacle, and concealed them; (K;) as also ↓ Agfrhu . (K.) ― -b4- [Hence also] gafara lahu *anobahu , (S, Msb, * K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. magofaripN , (S, K,) or this is a simple subst., (Msb,) and guforaAnN and gaforN (S, Msb, K) and gufuwrN (Lh, K) and gafiyrN and gafiyrpN , (K,) He (God) covered, his sin, crime, or offence; (K;) forgave it; pardoned it; (Msb, K;) as also *anobahu ↓ Agtfr , (S,) or Agtfr lahu maA SanaEa he forgave him what he had done: (Msb:) or guforaAnN and magofirapN , on the part of God, signify the preserving a man from being touched by punishment: and sometimes gafara lahu signifies [ he forgave him, or pardoned him: and also] he forgave him, or pardoned him, apparently, but not really; and thus it is used in the Kur xlv. 13, accord. to the B. (TA.) As an ex. of the last of the inf. ns. mentioned above on the authority of the K, the following saying, of a certain Arab, is cited: A^asoA^aluka Algafiyraho waAln~aAqapa Algazyiraho waAlEiz~a fiY AlEa$iyraho faA_in~ahaA Ealayoka yasiyraho [ I beg of Thee (O God) forgiveness, and a she-camel abounding in milk, and might among the kinsfolk, or in the tribe, for they are to Thee things easy ]. (TA.) [See also the paragraph commencing with gafiyrapN .] ― -b5- In the following saying of Zuheyr, the verb is used tropically: A^aDaAEato falamo tugofaro lahaA gafalaAtuhaA meaning [ She lost her young one, and ] her acts of negligence with respect to her young one were not forgiven her, by the wild beasts, so they ate it. (TA.) ― -b6- ↓ gafara AlA^amora biguforatihi , (S, * K,) and ↓ bigafiyratihi , (K,) aor. , (S,) [lit. He covered the affair with its cover, ] means (assumed tropical:) he rectified the affair with that wherewith it was requisite that it should be rectified. (S, K.) [And ↓ Agtfrhu perhaps signifies the same: see murotaA^abN , in art. rA^b .] -A2- gafira , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. gafarN , (S,) It (a garment, or piece of cloth,) became villous; as also ↓ AgfAr~ , (S, K,) inf. n. AigofiyraArN . (S.) -A3- gafara , (S, K,) aor. , inf. n. gaforN , (S,) It (a wound) became recrudescent; or reverted to a bad, or corrupt, state; (S, K;) as also gafira , [of which see another meaning in what follows,] aor. , inf. n. gafarN . (S.) And in like manner the former is said of a sick person: (S:) [i. e.] gafara signifies likewise He (a sick person) relapsed into disease, after convalescence; as also gufira : (K, TA:) and in like manner one says of a wounded person. (TA.) And [hence, app.,] it is also said of an excessive lover, meaning He experienced a return of his desire, (K, TA,) after consolation. (TA.) ― -b2- gafira said of a wound signifies also It healed: thus having two contr. meanings. (IKtt, TA.) -A4- gafara Aljalabu Als~uwqa , (K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. gaforN , (TA,) means rax~aSahaA [more correctly A^aroxaSahaA i. e. The beasts, or other things, brought thither for sale, made the market cheap ]. (K, TA.)

definition: A helmet that encloses and embraces the whole head.
sourceDefinition: A helmet that encloses and embraces the whole head. (K.) AO says, in his “ Book on the Coat of Mail and the Helmet, ” that bayoDapN is a general name for a helmet, which has plates like the bones of the skull, fastened together, edge to edge, by nails. (TA.) ― -b2- jaAw^uwA jam~aA='a gafiyrFA , and Aljam~aA='a Algafiyra , (S, K,) and jam~aA='a Algafiyri , and jam~FA gafiyrFA , and Aljam~a Algafiyra , and jam~a Algafiyri , and ↓ jam~aA='a AlgafiyraY , and ↓ jam~aA='a gafiyrapF , and Aljam~aA='a ↓ Algafiyrapa , and ↓ jam~aA='a Algafiyrapi , and ↓ jam~a Algafiyrapi , and bijam~aA='i Algafiyri , and ↓ bijam~aA='i Algafiyrapi , (K,) are phrases meaning They came all together, high and low, none of them remaining behind, and they being many: (S, K:) accord. to Sb, (K,) it ( Aljm~A=' Algfyr , S, which is the only form that he mentions, TA, [or rather the former of these two words,]) is a subst., (S, K,) put in the place of an inf. n., (K,) i. e. put in the accus. case like an inf. n. of the same meaning, (TA,) i. e., [as when you say] mararotu bihimo jumuwmFA kaviyrFA [I passed by them they being very many]: (K:) it is not a verb, [by which is here meant, as in many other instances, an inf. n.,] but is put in the accus. case like an inf. n. of the same meaning, as when you say jaAw^uwniY jamiyEFA , and qaATibapF , and Tur~FA , and kaAf~apF , [They came to me all together,] and the article Al is prefixed like as it is prefixed in the saying A^aworadahaA AlEiraAka , meaning A^aworadahaA EiraAkFA [He brought them (the camels) to the water all together]: (S:) Sb says that it is one of those denotatives of state which have the art. Al prefixed, and is extr.; and that Algfyr is an epithet inseparable from Aljm~A=' ; meaning that you do not say Aljm~A=' and then be silent: (TA:) others hold it to be an inf. n.: IAmb allows it to be in the nom. case, on the condition that hum is understood [before it; i. e., the complete phrase being jaAw^uwA humu Aljam~aA='u Algafiyru ]: and Ks says that the Arabs put Aljm~A' Algfyr in the accus. case fiY Alt~amaAmi [i. e. in the case of its occurring after a proposition rendered complete by the mention of the agent. as when you say jaA='a Alqawomu Aljam~aA='a Algafiyra ], and in the nom. case fiY Aln~uqoSaAni [i. e. in the case of its occurring when what precedes it is not a complete proposition, and is only rendered complete by it as the agent, as when you say jaA='a Aljam~aA='u Algafyiru ]. (K.) ― -b3- It is said in a trad., that Mohammad, being asked by Aboo-Dharr, what was the number of the apostles, answered val`vumiAy^apK waxamosapa Ea$ara jam~a Algafiyri , meaning, Three hundred and fifteen: a great number. (Nh, TA.) -A2- See also gafarN , first sentence.

definition: ― -b2- maA fiyhimo gafiyrapN [ There is not in them any disposition to forgive;
sourceDefinition: : see guforapN , and 1. ― -b2- maA fiyhimo gafiyrapN [ There is not in them any disposition to forgive; ] means they do not forgive any one a sin, a crime, or an offence. (S, K.) And maAEinodahumo Ea*iyrapN walaA gafiyrapN [ They have not a disposition to excuse nor a disposition to forgive; ] means they do not excuse nor do they forgive a sin, a crime, or an offence, of any one. (TA.) The rájiz (Sakhr-el-Ghei, L) said, (on seeing his companions, with whom he was journeying, fly from the Benu-l-Mustalik, whom they chanced to meet, L,) yaA qawomi layosato fiyhimu gafiyraho faA@mo$uwA kamaA tamo$iY jimaAlu AlHiyraho [ O my people, there is not in them any disposition to forgive: therefore march ye as march the camels of El-Heereh ]: (S, L:) he mentioned particularly the camels of El-Heereh because they carry burdens; and meant, march ye heavily, and defend yourselves, and do not fly. (L.) -A2- Also Abundance, and increase, in family and cattle or other property. (TA, from a trad.) -A3- See also gafiyrN , in five places.

definition: What is worn beneath the helmet: (Mgh, Msb:) or a piece of mail, ( zaradN , S K,) woven (S) from the diroE [or coat of mail ], (S, K,) according to the size of the head, (S,) worn beneath the [ kind of cap called ] qalanosuwap ;
sourceDefinition: What is worn beneath the helmet: (Mgh, Msb:) or a piece of mail, ( zaradN , S K,) woven (S) from the diroE [or coat of mail ], (S, K,) according to the size of the head, (S,) worn beneath the [ kind of cap called ] qalanosuwap ; (S, K;) as also ↓ migofarapN and ↓ gifaArapN : (K:) or the raforaf [or pendent appertenance ] of the helmet: (TA:) or a piece of mail, ( HalaqN , or HilaqN , as in different copies of the K,) which an armed man, (K,) or a man, accord. to some lexicons, (TA,) wears in the manner of a qinaAE ( yataqan~aEu bihaA ); as also ↓ migofarapN and ↓ gifaArapN : (K:) accord. to ISh, the migofar is a piece of mail ( HalaqN ) which a man puts beneath the helmet, hanging down upon the neck: and sometimes, he says, it is like the qalanosuwap , except that it is more ample; a man throws it upon his head, and it reaches to the coat of mail; then the helmet is put on over it; and this mgfr hangs down upon the shoulders: sometimes, also, the mgfr is [ a covering for the head ] made of diybaAj [i. e. silk brocade ], and of [ the cloth called ] xaz~ [q. v.], beneath the helmet: accord. to “ the Book of the Coat of Mail and the Helmet, ” by AO, migofarN and ↓ gifaArapN are names applied to a portion of mail [ forming a headcovering ], which is also called tasobigapN [q. v.]; and sometimes the rings are exposed to view; and sometimes they line them within, and cover them externally, with diybaAj or xaz~ or [ the kind of silk stuff called ] bizoyawon ; and they stuff it with something ( H$~whA bmA kAn ); and sometimes they make above it a qawonas [or tapering top ] of silver &c.: (TA:) the term migofar is also applied to the helmet itself. (Mgh.) -A2- See also mugofuwrN , in three places.

sourceDefinition: , [aor. yagiynu , inf. n. gayonN ,] Such a thing covered, veiled, or concealed, him, or it: (Ham p. 574:) [and so ↓ A^agaAnahu ; whence] one says, Algayonu Als~amaA='a ↓ AgAn The clouds covered, or overspread, or wholly covered, the sky. (S, K.) And giyna EalaY ka*aA Such a thing was covered over. (S.) [Hence,] giyna EalaY qalobihi , inf. n. gayonN ; as also ↓ A^ugiyna [in the CK (erroneously) Aagoyana ]; (assumed tropical:) His heart was invaded by desire, or appetite, as by a thing that covered it: or was covered [ so as to be rendered unsusceptible ]: or was enveloped by the like of rust [or clouded or rendered dull ]. (K, TA. [For Alr~ayon , meaning “ the like of rust ” covering the heart, the CK has Ald~ayon .]) The saying, in a trad., A_in~ahu layugaAnu EalaY qalobiY (S, Msb, TA) Hat~aY A^asotagofira A@ll~`ha fiY Alyawomi saboEiyna mar~apF (TA) is from the phrase giyna EalaY ka*aA signifying as expl. above, (S,) and means (assumed tropical:) Verily my heart is invaded as though it were covered, by unmindfulness from which mankind will not be free so that I beg forgiveness of God in the day seventy times: (TA:) or it means, being used metonymically, verily I become diverted from AlmuraAqabap [meaning the fear of God, or, as a conventional term, the constant knowledge of God's cognition of me in all my states or circumstances, ] by the affairs that are for good relating to the present world; for these, though matters of importance, are, in comparison with the affairs relating to the other world, as idle sport, in the estimation of the people who follow the rule of AlmuraAqabap . (Msb.) ― -b2- One says also, giynati Als~amaA='u , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. gayonN ; as also gaAnat , inf. n. gayonN ; [like gaAmat ;] (TA;) The sky became covered (Msb, TA) with gayon (Msb) or gayom (TA) [i. e. clouds, or an expanse of clouds ]. -A2- ginotu , aor. A^agiynu , [inf. n. gayonN ,] I was, or became, thirsty. (S, K.) And gaAnati AlA_ibilu i. q. gaAmat (S, K, TA) i. e. The camels were, or became, thirsty. (TA.) ― -b2- And gaAnato nafosuhu , (S,) or nafosiY , (K,) aor. tagiynu , (S, K,) inf. n. gayonN , (TA,) His, or my, soul [or stomach ] heaved, or became agitated by a tendency to vomit; syn. gavato . (S, K.)

sourceDefinition: Green: (S, TA:) or green inclining to blackness: (so in one of my copies of the S:) and [its fem.] gayonaA='u is applied to a tree ( $ajarapN ) as meaning green, (AO, S, K, TA,) abounding with leaves, having tangled, or dense, branches, (AO, S, TA,) and soft, or tender: and sometimes it is thus applied to herbs: (TA:) or [applied to a tree] it signifies great, having wide shade: from the phrase gaAna Ealayohi ka*aA , expl. in the beginning of this art.: (Ham p. 574:) and A^agoyanu signifies [also] such as is tall, (K, TA,) of trees, or, by way of comparison [thereto], of men: (TA:) the pl. is giynN : (S, TA:) which is expl. by Kr as meaning the abundance, and collected state, and beauty, of [the trees called] A^araAk and sidor ; but what is well known is that it is pl. of gayonaA=' applied to a tree; of which ↓ giynapN , with kesr, has also been mentioned as a pl., though, as ISd says, this is not known in the [genuine] language, nor is it agreeable with the analogy of Arabic. (TA.)

definition: The bariyd , i. e., (IDrd, S, O,) the warner before the lion; (S, O, K;) a certain beast of prey, [sometimes called by us the lion's provider, ] that cries out before the lion, as though warning men...
sourceDefinition: The bariyd , i. e., (IDrd, S, O,) the warner before the lion; (S, O, K;) a certain beast of prey, [sometimes called by us the lion's provider, ] that cries out before the lion, as though warning men of his presence; said to resemble the jackal ( Aibonu A=waY ); (IDrd, TA;) and said to be the jackal [itself]; but some say otherwise: (TA voce bariydN :) a Pers. word, (IDrd, S, O,) arabicized, (IDrd, S, O, K,) originally farowaAnahu [or ParowaAnah ], (IDrd, TA,) or originally ParowaAnak : (S, O, K:) said by AHát to be [also] called the waEowaE . (TA.) ― -b2- And (hence, TA) The guide of the messenger on a beast of the post. (O, K, TA.) And sometimes The guide of an army was thus called. (S, TA.) ― -b3- And, (O, K,) accord. to some, (O,) it signifies The lion [himself]. (O, K.)

(TA.)

definition: A flock of sheep, or herd of goats: (S, O:) or a flock of sheep from ten to forty: (AZ, A'Obeyd, S, O, K:) or from three to ten;
sourceDefinition: A flock of sheep, or herd of goats: (S, O:) or a flock of sheep from ten to forty: (AZ, A'Obeyd, S, O, K:) or from three to ten; thus in the copies of the K; but in the L, to twenty: (TA:) and two, and more: (S, O, K:) and hence, (S, O,) Alfizoru was a surname of Saad Ibn-ZeydMenáh: he came to the mawosim [or fair, and place of meeting, app. of the pilgrims,] with some goats, and allowed them to be taken as spoil, saying, “ Whoso takes of them one, it shall be his, but a fizor [i. e. a pair or more ] of them shall not be taken; ” fizorN here meaning two and more: whence the prov., laA A=tiyka miEozaY Alfizori , meaning [ I will not come to thee ] until the goats of El-Fizr shall become gathered together; and [that means never, for] those goats will never become gathered together: (S, O, K:) or, accord. to ISd, this surname was given to him because he said to his sons, one after another, “ Pasture ye these goats, ” and they were incompliant to him; so he called to the people, “ Collect yourselves together; ” and they did so; and he said, “ Take ye them as spoil; but I do not allow to any one more than one; ” therefore they separated them at once, and they became scattered in the country: this was the origin of the prov.: and one of their provs. relating to leaving a thing undone is the saying, laA A^afoEalu *alika miEozaYAlfizori [ I will not do that until the goats of El-Fizr shall become gathered together. (TA.) Accord. to AO, (S, O, TA,) fizorN means The kid (S, O, K, TA) itself: (S, O, TA:) and one says, laAA^afoEaluhu maA nazaA fizorN [ I will not do it as long as a kid leaps ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And The male young one of the namir [or leopard]: (TA:) or the male young one of the [ beast of prey called ] babor [q. v.], (O, K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, bayor ,]) as is said in the T, and likewise in the Tekmileh: (TA:) and fizorapN signifies the female young one thereof; (O, K, TA;) or, as some say, the sister thereof: (TA:) and ↓ fazaArapN signifies the female of the babor ; (O, Msb, TA;) thus says IAar, (O,) [and] thus is said in the T: (TA:) or the mother of the babor is called fzArp ; and also the female of the namir ; (K, TA;) thus says IAar. (TA.) -A2- Also The A^Sol [or origin, &c.,] (O, K) of a thing. (O.) -A3- And A small thing, (O, K,) like a naboxap [or blister ], in the root of the thigh, (O,) below the extremity of the pubes, resembling a gud~ap [or ganglion ], from an ulcer that comes forth in a man, (O, K,) or from a wound. (O.)

definition: A wide road; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ fuzorapN : (O, K:) or a wide and conspicuous road: or, accord. to ISh, a road that passes over the [ eminences termed ] nijaAf [pl. of najafN ] and the [ hills, or...
sourceDefinition: A wide road; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ fuzorapN : (O, K:) or a wide and conspicuous road: or, accord. to ISh, a road that passes over the [ eminences termed ] nijaAf [pl. of najafN ] and the [ hills, or small mountains termed ] quwr [pl. of qaArapN ], and cleaves them as though it made furrows upon their heads: you say, A^axa*onaAAlfaAzira and A^axa*onaATariyqa AlfaAziri , meaning [ We took ] the road that made a track upon the heads and the base of the mountains. (TA.) And ↓ faAzirapN [or TariyqN faAzirapN ] signifies A road taking its course in a tract of sand amid sands that are compact and cleaving to the ground, (K, TA,) and soft; appearing like an extended, long, natural cleft in the ground: (TA:) the same meaning is also assigned to faArizapN . (K * and TA in art. frz .) -A2- Also A species of ants, (O,) black ants, (K,) in which is a redness: (O, K:) mentioned also among words of which the final radical is z [as being called faArizN ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And The round black thing [app. a species of animalcule ] found in [ dried ] dates. (O.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (Lth, O, K,) inf. n. faSoEN , (Lth, S, O,) He squeezed, or pressed, a fresh ripe date, (Lth, S, O, K,) with his two fingers [or his thumb and a finger ], (Lth, O,) so that it should become divested of its skin; (Lth, S, O;) and in like manner, a fig: (Lth, O:) or he made it (i. e. a fresh ripe date) to come forth from its skin, (A'Obeyd, O,) [to which SM adds, as from A' Obeyd,] in order that it might ripen quickly. (TA.) The act thus explained is forbidden in a trad.; [but I have not found for what reason.] (S, O.) ― -b2- And He rubbed a thing with his two fingers, (in the K, erroneously, with his finger, TA,) in order that it might become soft, and open so as to disclose what was in it. (IDrd, O, K, TA.) ― -b3- And He pulled or stripped, or put off, [a garment or the like]. (O, TA.) You say, faSaEa EimaAmatahu (O, K,) Eano raA^osihi (K) He removed, or took off, his turban from his head. (O, K.) ― -b4- Said of a boy [not yet circumcised], He withdrew his prepuce from his glans; and so ↓ AftSE . (S, O, K.) ― -b5- faSaEato said of a mare; She disclosed and concealed alternately her vulva on the occasion of staling. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yafiYo'u , inf. n. faYo'N (S, O, Msb) and fuyuwo'N , (O,) He (a man, Msb) returned; (S, O, Msb;) and so ↓ AfA=' , and ↓ AstfA=' : (M, TA:) faYo'N , as also ↓ fayoy^apN and ↓ fiyy^apN , [or the former of these, accord. to analogy, is an inf. n. of unity, and the latter an inf. n. of modality,] and A_ifaA='apN and AistifaA='apN al' signify rujuwEN : (K:) or, accord. to some, faA='a signifies particularly he returned to a good state or condition. (MF, TA.) One says, faA='a mino gaDabihi He returned [ to a good state, or recovered, from his anger ]: (M, TA:) and fulaAnN sariyEu AlfaYo'i mino gaDabihi [ Such a one is quick in respect of the returning &c. from his anger ]: (S, M, * O:) and ↓ A_in~ahu lasariyEu Alfiyoy^api , (M,) or ↓ laHasanu Alfiyoy^api , (S, O,) i. e. [ Verily he is quick, or good, in respect of ] the returning [to a good state, or from his anger, or in respect of the manner of returning &c.]: (S, M, O:) and ↓ huwa sariyEu AlgaDabi sariyEu Alfiyoy^api [ He is quick in respect of anger, quick in respect of returning, or recovering, therefrom]. (A, TA.) And faA='a A_ilaY AlA^amori , and faA='ahu [i. e. faA='a AlA^amora ], inf. n. faYo'N and fuyuwo'N , He returned [ to the affair, or to the command, i. e. to that which was commanded ]. (M, TA.) Hat~aY tafiYo'a A_ilaY A^amori A@ll~`hi , in the Kur xlix. 9, means Until it [referring to a party ( TaAy^ifap ) before mentioned] return to the ordinance of God, or to that which God has commanded: (Bd:) or until it return (T, Msb) to obedience, (T,) or to that which is right. (Msb.) And faA='a A_ilaY AlA^amori , inf. n. faYo'N , signifies also He reconsidered the affair, or case. (TA.) ― -b2- faA='a Almuw^oliY (M, Msb, K) mini A@moraA^atihi , (M, K,) inf. n. faYo'N , (TA,) or ↓ fayoy^apN , (Msb,) means The man who had sworn to abstain from conjugal intercourse with his wife expiated his oath and returned to her. (M, Msb, * K. [See Kur ii. 226.]) But MF observes that this usage of faA='a to signify He expiated an oath belongs to the conventional language of the law. (TA.) In the case of a man who has sworn that he will abstain from conjugal intercourse with his wife, a period of four months is appointed to him in the Kur-án; and if he have such intercourse with her in the four months, it is said of him, qado faA='a , meaning He has returned [or reverted ] from his oath, to the doing that which he swore that he would not do, and is bound to expiate his oath: if he have not had such intercourse with her until the end of the four months from the day of his swearing, then, Ibn-'Abbás and a number of the Companions pass upon her a single sentence of divorce, making the [said sentence of] divorce to have effect at the end of the months; but many of the Companions and others say that in this case he must return, and expiate his oath, or he must divorce. (T, TA.) And [hence] one says ↓ lahu EalaY A@moraA^atihi fayoy^apN He has the right of returning to his wife: (Msb, TA:) and huwa yamoliku ↓ fayoy^atahaA He possesses the right of returning to her; namely, a wife whom he has divorced. (A, TA.) ― -b3- AlfaYo'u EalaY *iY Alr~aHimi occurs in a trad. as meaning The being favourably inclined, or affectionate, to the relation; and returning to kind treatment of him. (TA.) ― -b4- faA='a said of the shade, (M, Msb,) aor. yafiYo'u , (Msb,) inf. n. faYo'N , (M, Msb, K, *) It shifted, or removed; (M, K; *) or [rather] it returned from the side of the west to the side of the east: (Msb:) and AlZ~ilaAlu ↓ tafay~aA^ati The shades became changed in their manner of being; (S, O;) or [rather] they returned [ towards the east ] after midday. (T, TA. [See the Kur-án xvi. 50.]) ― -b5- And faA='ati Al$~ajarapu ; and ↓ tfy~A^t ; (M;) and ↓ fy~A^t , inf. n. tafiyoy^apN ; (S, O, TA;) The tree had much shade. (M, TA.) faA='ati AlHadiydapu The iron implement became blunt after its being sharp. (T, TA.) -A2- fiy^otu Alganiymapa , (mentioned, but not expl., in the K,) inf. n. faYo'N , (TA,) means I took the spoil. (TK.) [See also 10.]

definition: : ― -b2- and tfy~A^t Al$~ajarapu : see 1, near the end.
sourceDefinition: : ― -b2- and tfy~A^t Al$~ajarapu : see 1, near the end. ― -b3- tfy~A^ fiyhi means He shaded himself in it; i. e., in the shade termed faYo' . (M.) One says, tafay~aA^otu fiY faYo'i Al$~ajarapi [ I shaded myself in the afternoon-shade of the tree ]. (S, O.) And tfy~A^ biAl$~ajarapi [ He shaded himself by means of the tree; or] he entered into the A^afoyaA=' [or afternoon-shades ] of the tree: (MA:) and [it is said that] tafay~aA^otu Al$~ajarapa signifies I entered into the A^afoyaA=' of the tree, and shaded myself thereby: (Har p. 500:) and Aboo-Temmám has made it trans. by itself [i. e. without a prep.] in his saying, fatafay~aA^otu Zil~ahu mamoduwdFA [as though meaning And I protected myself from the sun by its shade, when it was extended ]: but [perhaps he has thus used the verb in the last of the senses here following, for] it is said that this is irregular. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence] one says, tafay~aA^otu bifayoy^ika meaning (tropical:) I have had recourse to thee for protection. (A, TA.) ― -b5- tfy~A^ is said of a branch or twig [as meaning It bent, in a languid manner ]. (T, M, L, K, voce taraA^~ada ; &c.) And one says, tfy~A^t lizawojihaA , meaning She bent herself over her husband, and affected languor, or languidness, to him, feigning coyness, or opposition, and threw herself upon him: (T, * TA:) from AlfaYo'u signifying “ the act of returning: ” and some say tqy~A^t , with q ; but Az says that this is a mistake, and that it is correctly with f (TA.) -A2- tfy~A^ signifies also tatab~aEa [ He sought a thing time after time, or repeatedly, &c.]. (Har p. 500.) And one says, fulaAnN yatafay~aA^u AlA^axobaAra and ↓ yasotafiyw^uhaA [app. meaning Such a one seeks after news, or tidings, time after time, or repeatedly, &c.]. (A, TA.)

definition: Afternoon-shade;
sourceDefinition: Afternoon-shade; shade after the declining of the sun from the meridian; (T, * S, O;) [i. e.] the faYo' is what was sun, and has been annulled, or superseded, by shade; (M, K;) or that from which the sun has departed: so called because of its “ returning ” from side to side: (S, O: [see 1, first sentence:]) ISk says, (S, O,) the Zil~ is what sun has annulled, or superseded; [correctly, what sun annuls, or supersedes; (see Zal~N ;)] and the faYo' is what has annulled, or superseded, sun: (S, Mgh, O:) but AO says, on the authority of Ru-beh, that on which the sun has been and from which it has departed is faYo' and Zil~ ; and that on which the sun has not been is Zil~ : (S, O:) [see more under this latter word:] pl. [of pauc.] A^afoyaA='N and [of mult,] fuyuwo'N . (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K.) ― -b2- And Spoil, booty, or plunder; syn. ganiymapN [q. v.]; (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) thus called, by the inf. n., because it returns from one party to another; (Msb;) and fay~N in this sense is not allowable; (Mgh, Msb;) nor is it in the preceding sense: (Mgh:) or such as is obtained without difficulty: and therefore likened to shade. (MF.) And The [ tax, or tribute, termed ] xaraAj [q. v.]: (S, O, K:) frequently occurring in trads. as meaning such, of the possessions of the unbelievers, as accrues to the Muslims without war: (TA:) or such as is obtained from the believers in a plurality of gods after the laying-down of arms: (A 'Obeyd, Mgh and Msb voce ganiymapN :) or such as God has restored [as though it were theirs of right] to the people of his religion, of the possessions of those who have opposed them, without fighting, either by the latter's quitting their homes and leaving them vacant to the Muslims, or by their making peace on the condition of paying a poll-tax or other money or property to save themselves from slaughter: such is termed faYo' in the Kur-án. (T. [See more under ganiymapN .]) -A2- Also A flock of birds: (O, K:) [or a number of birds disposed in a row: ] also termed EaraqapN and Saf~N . (O, TA.) -A3- yaA faYo'a , (M, O, K, in the CK [erroneously] yA faYo'u ,) or, accord. to Ks, correctly yA faY~a [q. v.]. (M,) [ Oh! or O my wonder? ] an expression of regret, (M, O, K,) accord. to most, (TA,) or of wonder, (Ks, M, K, TA,) meaning yaA EajabiY . (Ks, M.) [See $aYo'N , last three sentences.]

definition: A [ party, portion, division, or distinct body, of men, such as is termed ] TaAy^ifap : (S, O, K, TA:) or a company (Msb, TA) of soldiers who fight in the rear of an army, and to whom the latter has...
sourceDefinition: A [ party, portion, division, or distinct body, of men, such as is termed ] TaAy^ifap : (S, O, K, TA:) or a company (Msb, TA) of soldiers who fight in the rear of an army, and to whom the latter has recourse in the case of fear or defeat: (TA:) or a company of men who [ in war ] have recourse, for aid, one to another: (Er-Rághib, TA:) a word having no proper sing.: (Msb, TA:) originally fiYo'N ; (S, O, K;) the p being substituted for the medial Y , which is dropped: (S, O:) or its original form is fiy^owN [or fiy^oYN or fiy^owapN or fiy^oyipN (see art. fA^w and fA^Y )]; the final [radical] letter being that which is elided; for it is from faA^awotu [or faA^ayotu ] “ I divided; ” and fiy^apN is syn. with firoqapN : (IB, L, TA:) pl. fiy^aAtN and fiy^uwna , (S, O, Msb, K,) in which latter the w and n are for the making good what is deficient [in the sing.]. (Msb.)

(L and TA * in arts. tfA^ and fyA^ .)

definition: A thing that has been made a faYo' [or spoil, &c.
sourceDefinition: A thing that has been made a faYo' [or spoil, &c.]. (TA.) And A person whose country, or province, or town, has been conquered, and become a faYo' to the Muslims. (IKt, O, TA.) It is in a trad. of some of those who have gone before, ↓ laA yuw^am~aru mufaA='N EalaY mufiYo'K , meaning An emancipated slave shall not be made governor over an Arabian; (K, TA;) or, as in the Nh [and O] and L, lA yaliyan~a [ shall by no means rule ]; (TA;) as though it were said, none of the people of the Sawád (which was conquered by force and became a faYo' to the Muslims) shall rule over the Companions (O, TA) and their next successors. (TA.)

definition: a dial. var. of kusoTN , or, accord. to Yaakoob, the q is a substitute [for k ]; (M;) said by IF to be Arabic; (Msb;) [ Costus; so in the present day;] a certain substance, (AA, Msb,) or perfume,...
sourceDefinition: a dial. var. of kusoTN , or, accord. to Yaakoob, the q is a substitute [for k ]; (M;) said by IF to be Arabic; (Msb;) [ Costus; so in the present day;] a certain substance, (AA, Msb,) or perfume, (Mgh,) or wood, (M,) or a certain Indian wood, and also Arabian, (K,) with which one fumigates; (AA, M, Mgh, Msb;) well known; (Msb;) also called kusoTN and ku$oTN (AA) and qu$oTN : (TA in art. q$T :) or a wood which is brought from India, and which is put into the substances used for fumigating, and into medicine: (Lth:) or a certain drug of the sea: (S:) [it is said in the S and TA, voce HinozaAbN , that the carrot of the ( jazaru AlbaHori ) is called qusoTN :] in a trad., AlqusoTu AlbaHoriY~u [or qusoT of the sea ] is mentioned as one of the best of remedies: and in another trad., qusoT is coupled by the conjunction w with A^aZofaAr , or, accord. to one relation thereof, is prefixed to the latter word, governing it in the gen. case: and IAth says, that it is a sort of perfume: but some say that it is aloes-wood ( Euwd , q. v.): [see also ZafaAriY~N :] and others, a well-known drug, of sweet odour, with which women and infants are fumigated: (TA:) it is diuretic, beneficial to the liver in a high degree, and for the colic, and for worms, and the quartan fever, as a beverage; and for rheum, and defluxions, and pestilence, when the patient is fumigated therewith; and for the [ leprous-like disorder called ] bahaq , and the [ discolouration of the face termed ] kalaf , when applied as a liniment; (K;) and it confines the bowels, expels wind, strengthens the stomach and heart, occasions pleasurable sensation, is an ingredient in many sorts of perfume, and is the best of perfumes in odour when one fumigates therewith. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: Equity; justice: (S, * M, Mgh, Msb, K: *) [an inf. n. having no proper verb, or] a subst. from A^aqosaTa . (Mgh, Msb.) -A2- Equitable; just: (S, * M, K:) an inf. n. used as an epithet, like its syn. EadolN ; (M, K;) and [therefore] applied alike to a sing. n. [and to a dual] and to a pl.: (K:) you say miyzaAnN qisoTN an equitable, or a just, balance; and miyzaAnaAni qisoTN ; and, agreeably with the usage of the Kur, xxi. 48, mawaAziynu qisoTN . (M.) -A3- A portion, share, or lot; (S, M, Msb, K;) of a thing; (K;) and pertaining to a person: (TA:) pl. A^aqosaATN . (Msb.) You say, waf~aAhu qisoTahu He gave him in full his portion, share, or lot. (TA.) And A^axa*a kul~N mina Al$~urakaA='i qisoTahu Every one of the partners took his portion, or share. (TA.) ― -b2- A portion, or piece. (So accord. to an explanation of the pl., A^aqosaATN , in the TA.) ― -b3- The means of subsistence: (K:) or the portion thereof which is the share of every created being. (TA.) yaxofiDu AlqisoTa wayarofaEuhu , said of God, in a trad., has been explained as meaning He maketh the portion of the means of subsistence which is the share of any created being little, and maketh it much. (TA.) [See, below, another meaning which is assigned to it in this instance; and see also art. xfD .] ― -b4- A quantity, (K, TA,) of water only; or any quantity, of water and of other things. (TA.) ― -b5- A measure with which corn is measured, (S, Mgh, K,) which holds (K) half of a SaAE ; (S, Mgh, K;) six thereof making a faroqa : (S:) accord. to Mbr, four hundred and eighty-one dirhems. (TA.) Sometimes it is used for performing the ablution termed wuDuwo' : and hence it is said in a trad., A_in~a Aln~isaA='a mino A^asofahi Als~ufahaA='i A_il~aA SaAHibapa AlqisoTi waAls~iraAji ; (K;) the qisoT being here the vessel in which the wDw' is performed; (TA;) the meaning app. being, [ Women are of the most lightwitted of the lightwitted, ] except she who serves her husband, and assists him to perform the wDw' , [so I render tuwaD~iy^uhu ,] and takes care of the vessel which he uses for that purpose, and stands at his head with the lamp: (K:) or who performs his affairs with respect to his wDw' and his lamp. (Nh.) ― -b6- A [ mug of the kind called ] kuwz ; (M, K;) so called by the people of the great towns: (M:) now applied to one with which olive-oil is measured. (TA.) ― -b7- A balance, or weighing-instrument. (K.) Some say that this is its meaning in the phrase mentioned above, yaxofiDu AlqisoTa wayarofaEuhu He depresseth the balance, and raiseth it: alluding to the means of subsistence which He decrees. (TA.)
